II. Concerning the other clause: How does this salvation happen?

It happens in this way: I will pour out of my spirit.

This is a wondrous voice, and above all human comprehension, God will save, not by law, but by imparting Himself, I will pour out, He says, of My Spirit, of my substance. Wherever the substance of God is, there is the knowledge of God, the love of God, and eternal life. What greater thing can God give than that which He imparts to us of His spirit, of His substance? Just as Peter says, that we become partakers of the nature of God.

Would that we might recognize and ask for such a great gift, so that, confirmed by this spirit, we might glorify God in confession and in our whole life. But because the gifts of God, as it is said: To him who has, it shall be given. Therefore, we do not understand the magnitude of this divine gift, the Holy Spirit, poured out upon us, because we do not exercise it, we do not bring forth this gift, but we shake it off, we grieve the Holy Spirit.

These are great sins in the world, which, however, reason does not judge or discern.

Let the learned consider this word, My, when it is said: I will pour out of my spirit. For first, it signifies that the spirit is a person consubstantial with God. Then it teaches that God so restores us, by imparting something of His substance. But where the substance of God is, there is light, that is, the true knowledge of God, the true love of God, and eternal life. All these things are far above the grasp of reason, above the justice of the law, and human wisdom. They will be able to be understood, however, if we exercise the gift in daily confession and invocation.

III. And your sons shall prophesy.

He adds signs and testimonies, and the principal works of the Holy Spirit. The first is to prophesy, that is, to rightly understand and declare the Gospel, because the Gospel is the doctrine concerning the will of God toward us, which human reason does not perceive without the Holy Spirit, just as Paul says: The natural man does not perceive the things that are of God. Just as we also see what the wise men of the world do, some of whom want to appear to understand the Gospel, when they certainly do not understand. Origen, Jerome, and many others did not understand the knowledge of faith. These sayings of Paul: The law works wrath, Being justified by faith we have peace, they did not understand to such a degree that they even thought them absurd and improper. So now many theologians do not understand these sayings, even when they imitate the words. But who understands? Truly those who call upon the Lord, who have faith, upon whom the Holy Spirit has been poured out. These prophesy, rightly understand, rightly declare, confess, glorify God, preserve for God the purity of the word, and defend the glory of God.

All these things the word 'prophesy' comprehends; these are pleasing forms of worship to God, as it is written: Praise the Lord, O ye children, etc.

Let us perform these forms of worship, let us be such prophets, true interpreters and confessors. Let us learn, therefore, how many things He proposes in these sermons, concerning true invocation, faith, IIII. He adds other signs to the sign of the Holy Spirit, namely prophecy. Your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.

I have said that prophecy signifies primarily the understanding and true exposition of the word of God, because the word of God contains wisdom concerning the will of God toward us, placed entirely outside the grasp of human reason.

This gift is necessary for the Church, of which Paul speaks much in 1 Corinthians 4: And it is a great light, shining more in some, less in others; at one time there are more in the Church endowed with this gift, at another time fewer.

Just as in the time of Samuel there were more in Israel who thought rightly than in the time of Eli, when, as the text says, the word of the Lord was rare. In the time of the Apostles there were more who rightly understood the Gospel than afterwards under the Papacy, even though there were very many priests, monks, and theologians.

Now God has again stirred up this light a little, and He must be prayed to that He may preserve it, and we must be warned not to extinguish it ourselves with new sophistry and human wisdom, and become such prophets as Saul was, of whom it was said: Is Saul also among the prophets?

So now of many who corrupt the Gospel with new sophistry, seeking reconciliations of doctrines that conform to human wisdom—ambiguous, flexible, and disguised—it can be said: Are these also among the prophets?

When hearts are idle or occupied with human desires, they begin to loathe the word of God; afterwards, in order to seek peace and leisure, they accommodate themselves to the judgments of the impious and allow true doctrine to be depraved.

Thus the devil returns to the swept house.

These great evils must be prudently avoided, but the world is insane with its desires and does not understand these sins.

Therefore the Holy Spirit warns and reproves us through the Gospel, shows these snares, and commands us to watch and beware. And so much for prophecy.

Moreover, Joel adds other testimonies of the Holy Spirit: Old men shall have dreams, and young men shall have visions.

By these words he does not only understand predictions about future things, as Joseph and Daniel were seers.

And Paul also had a vision, as he says in Acts chapter 16. But he generally embraces all the gifts which Paul lists in 1

Corinthians 12. For he wishes to say in general that it will come to pass that the Holy Spirit will declare Himself through many gifts: prophecy, predictions of future things, and the science of governance.

As here, when he speaks of old men, he understands governors; these will have divine impulses, they will govern polities divinely, or great ecclesiastical or political affairs.

Just as sometimes some prince has wisdom or a pious counselor, or a city a pious senator. And do not think that mention is made here of vulgar dreams, but other appellations follow in the text.

By all these he signifies various gifts necessary for the Church and for governance, which, although they are all miraculous and signal works of God, yet some are perceived more than others; as when Peter healed the lame man, or when he was led out of prison, that is called a miracle, and it is made much of because it strikes the eyes, although he had many greater miracles, such as that he was assiduously defended against the devil and against tyrants.

Likewise, that he remained in the purity of doctrine, that his sermons were effective, that his governance was happy. These are great and true miracles, to which are also added sometimes other rare works, which strike the eyes more.

Thus, therefore, let this passage be understood generally concerning all the gifts of the Holy Spirit in the Church.

And let the pious, who are in governance—whether of the Church, or political, or princes and their counselors, and senators of cities—remember what is said here about old men: Old men shall have the gift of the Holy Spirit.

This passage warns governors that they should know that human wisdom is not sufficient for doing great things, neither in ecclesiastical affairs nor in others, but there is need of the Holy Spirit, the governor and guide, and they should pray with David that God may arise to the judgment which He has commanded, that is, to the kingdom.

Psalm 7 and 71: Arise, O God, judge the earth. V. Thus far it has been briefly said concerning the gifts and testimonies of the Holy Spirit, which were added to the promise of the Gospel concerning salvation promised through the Messiah; however, the text adds something about the time of the Messiah, and about the signs preceding the glorious the coming of the Messiah, which it is also profitable to contemplate, so that carnal security may be corrected. The prophets sometimes speak simultaneously of both comings of Christ, just as here Joel speaks of the revelation of the Gospel, and immediately adds the glorious coming of Christ in the final judgment. Let one part of the prophecy be understood of the first coming, and another of the second. For what he says concerning the signs: "I will show wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke; the sun shall be turned into darkness," etc. Although these things can also be accommodated to the time of Christ’s passion, they nevertheless describe the whole time after the revelation of the Gospel up to the judgment—namely, the destruction of the entire Jewish nation, the changes of kingdoms, and public calamities, which will be more savage at the end, just as Christ forewarns in Matt. 28 and Luke 21, as we see change now impending over all kingdoms.

And it has been predicted by name concerning Gog and Magog, that is, concerning the Turks, that they are to devastate a great part of the Church with arms. It has also been predicted concerning the Antichrist or pseudoprophet, that is, the Pope, who will sit in the temple of God, that is, in the Church itself, and will rage with deceit and force. Let us consider these evils, and let us fortify ourselves more with faith, and let us pray to God that He may preserve us, because in Luke, when the same things are predicted: "There will be distress of nations," yet the same consolation is added: "Your redemption draws near."

Likewise: "Watch and pray, that you may be able to escape these things." Certainly, the dangers of the times exhort us to prayer, and warn us that that day is pressing on, in which all the impious together with the devils will be cast into eternal punishments, and the Son of God will glorify His Church.

Let us set this judgment before us, and let us know that it is not far off. Gog and Magog have truly reached the highest pinnacle, and the Antichrist is already being revealed.

These are the signs of the last time, concerning which it was predicted that impiety would then increase. Therefore, let us be vigilant and cautious, lest we fall away from the true doctrine; let us fear and invoke God, that He may rule us. Let us not offend Him with our ingratitude and the baseness of our morals. This admonition is necessary when one speaks of the signs of the last time.

The second part of Peter’s sermon.

"Men of Israel, hear these words."

In the former part of the sermon, it was spoken concerning the benefits of the New Testament themselves, concerning salvation, and the gift of the Holy Spirit, which is the earnest of new and eternal justice and life. Now follows the second part, concerning the cause or author of these benefits, namely, concerning the Messiah.

And it must be diligently considered that this sermon concerning the Messiah who suffered, was resurrected, glorified, and reigns, is opposed to the carnal imaginations of the Jews concerning a worldly kingdom of the Messiah, as if Peter were saying: You expect a Messiah and deliverer who, having driven out the Romans, would grant you the empire of the world. Behold, the Messiah has now come; He reigns otherwise than you think. He was made a victim for the sins of the human race, when He was put to death by you. Then, having been resurrected, God subjected all things to Him.

Know that this Jesus, whom you crucified, is the Messiah and Savior. But as we now have two principal questions with the Jews: the one, whether it behooved Christ to suffer and not to have a worldly empire, but a heavenly one.

The other, whether the Messiah has come, and whether this is the very Jesus whom we preach to have been crucified and resurrected. Thus Peter handles two things: that this very Jesus is the Messiah, and that after His killing, He was resurrected and reigns.

Concerning the first question.

Whether this is the Messiah? That this is the very Messiah, he proves thus: Because God has testified with great signs and miracles that He was sent divinely.

The second testimony is that the Scriptures testify that the Messiah must be resurrected. This one came back to life from death: therefore, this is the Messiah.

He proves the major premise from the Psalm: "Thou wilt not leave my soul in hell, neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption." These things are said concerning the Messiah, because it is certain that David is dead and has not yet been resurrected, but that he prophesied concerning the Messiah. For because God had promised David that one from his loins would have an eternal kingdom, he reasoned from thence that He must necessarily be resurrected according to the flesh.

Since, therefore, the Scripture testifies that the Messiah would be resurrected, and this one has been resurrected: therefore, it is certain that this is the Messiah, and we are witnesses of His resurrection. Concerning the second.

What kind of kingdom the Messiah has? That it is a heavenly kingdom, and that it behooved Christ to suffer, these very Psalms prove: "Preserve me, O Lord, for it is not well with me because of Thee." And the Psalm: "The Lord said," proves the same, that the Messiah would have a perpetual kingdom and divine power to abolish death and sin, and to give righteousness and eternal life. Therefore he says here: Exalted by God, He poured out the Holy Spirit. Such will be the kingdom, namely, liberation from sin and eternal death, the gift of righteousness and eternal life.

The third part is about application, but before application is the doctrine of sin and the preaching of repentance. See, however, that sin accuses, namely, that they did not know the Son of God, but rather crucified Him.

Sins. The people despised the signs of God and manifest miracles, did not believe the Prophets or the words of Christ, and killed Christ. Reason does not judge these sins, and yet we are all guilty. At this time, how horribly is the word of God contradicted? The saints are killed, and many consent, even if they do not kill with their own hands. Let all these know that they are guilty in this way, just as Peter says here: But they are liberated by believing in the name of Jesus.

Psalm 16.: Preserve me, O God. The argument of the Psalm is recited at the beginning, that the Psalm is principally a prophecy about Christ who was to suffer and be resurrected, and there is inserted a distinction between the true Church and the synagogue that persecutes Christ, under the title of the Church of God.

But someone might say, why does he speak in the first person, "Preserve me," as if David were speaking about himself? I answer, he speaks particularly about Christ, and the words are to be understood in such a way that Christ Himself is speaking, just as in Psalm 22.: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" And Psalm 50.: "Waiting I have waited," etc. And yet in Christ he also embraces the members afterwards, whom He knows must be resurrected on account of Christ, who rises first, so that He may be the author of resurrection and eternal life for all members.

Therefore, just as it is said of Christ that He would not remain in death, but would rise again by divine power, so it is signified concerning all members that their bodies are to live again. Thus in other Psalms, when it is prophesied principally about Christ, yet because of the effect which pertains to the members, the Psalms are also accommodated to the members, but nevertheless it must be prudently considered what is attributed properly to Christ alone, as in this Psalm concerning the merit and the calling of the passion of the Son of God, that He is the victim and sacrifice for others, which is not said of the afflictions of the saints, which even if they become sacrifices on account of faith in Christ, that is, worship acceptable to God, yet they do not merit for themselves or others the remission of sins. Likewise, these words are said of Christ alone: "You will not give your holy one to see corruption," as Peter explains here: His flesh did not see corruption, like David, whose sepulcher is still among us.

The Psalm has most useful doctrine. It is a testimony about the resurrection, and it ought to confirm us ourselves in the petition and expectation of eternal life.

It also teaches the distinction of the Church, which is the true Church, and confirms us, lest we be moved by the appearance and authority of the false Church. It teaches also that we should take care to be members of the true Church, and that we should flee the false Church, and not make reconciliations with it, which confirm their abuses.

"I will not receive," he says, "their libations, nor will I take their names upon my lips." Here Christ rejects all the Masses of the impious, and all their worship; He condemns their Church, He says that He does not wish to name it, that is, He does not wish to call it His Church, He does not wish to pray for it.

Nothing can be said that is sadder and more horrible. Therefore let us be cautious, lest we establish their impieties.

Finally, the whole Psalm is as it were a promise that God wishes to hear the members of His Church and to liberate them from eternal death. Thus we also recite this Psalm, and we glue ourselves as members to the head, Christ, who is the firstborn from the dead.

There are, moreover, four members of the Psalm. 1. The petition of Christ that He be preserved, with the exposition of the Passion. 2. The application of the Passion, and the repudiation of the false worship of the impious assembly. 3. The narration concerning the resurrection. 4. The end of the resurrection, that the Church gathered together may truly acknowledge God and celebrate Him in eternal life.

The first verse is the invocation and proposition seeking liberation, and it adds the cause: Because I hope in you, and I call upon you as my God. For this is what it signifies when it says: I said to the Lord, You are my God, that is, I invoke you alone, and I acknowledge you to be omnipotent, a liberator from death, and indeed propitious to me, willing to hear, and to save those who flee for refuge to you; this honor you wish to be given to yourself, that you are willing to save, according to your promises, those who flee for refuge to you.

The complaint and narrative of the passion, "My good is not on account of you," or, "It is not well for me on account of you," that is, I am in afflictions, and I even seem deserted by you, just as he cries out in the Psalm: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" But it is clearer as he says: I am afflicted for Thy sake, according to that: For Thy sake we are killed all the day long. In this verse, therefore, it is described what is the cause of Christ's passion.

For Thy sake I suffer, that is, for Thy secret counsel concerning the restoration of the human race, because Thou didst will that I become a victim. To this Thy will I submit, and I endure horrible punishments, not for any sins of my own. Wherefore, since Thou art my God, and Thou willest to save me, and to gather unto Thee an eternal Church, do not allow me to succumb in these miseries, but confirm and sustain, and deliver me.

To the saints who are in the earth, as if he were saying, To these pertains this my passion, and this is an application for the Church, just as Christ Himself before the passion applied it with His own words: I pray for them, not for them only, but for all who are to believe through their word. Father, sanctify them in truth, Thy word is truth. O sweet consolation, here the Son of God shows Himself to be our high priest, and intercessor before God. Thus he applies it here: My passion serves the saints and those to be honored on earth, to them it is to be profitable for salvation, who are saints, that is, dedicated to God, invoking God, acknowledging Him, worshipping Him. These are they who embrace my Gospel, these I judge to be saints and glorious, for these I offer myself, just as elsewhere he says: I sanctify myself for them, to these I apply my sacrifice, these I love and embrace, and for these I pray. Thus here the word 'Saints' must be explained.

And this is the very article in the creed: I believe in the holy catholic Church, that is, dedicated to God, truly acknowledging, worshipping, and celebrating God, in the faith and confession of the Son of God. This is also to be honored and glorious, because God in turn affects it with honor, bestows glory upon it, namely the Holy Spirit, and through the Holy Spirit, light, righteousness, and eternal life. Short is the verse, but a most beautiful description of the Church: and hence follows the antithesis, which he soon adds. Others are not saints, that is, they are not dedicated to God, not acknowledging God, not worshipping, nor are they to be honored, that is, they lack the glory of God, they are not adorned by God with light, wisdom, righteousness, eternal life.

Their idols are multiplied, after which they hasten. He said that he suffered for the true Church. This he now distinguishes from the impious, who do not want to know the true God, and persecute Christ and the Father. He therefore provides the distinction between the false and the true Church. But just as in the description of the true Church he named two goods, holiness and glory: so in the description of the false Church he names a double evil. The evil of guilt, that is, sins, and the evil of punishment, namely, rejection and damnation. The sins are, the false Church devises idols for itself, nay, it invents many idols, it seeks another God, and to this it hastens, in this it trusts, this it celebrates. But what is it to worship an idol, or another God? Idolatry is manifold. First are the idolaters, who imagine that to be God which is not God, just as the Heathens [did with] their statues, Jove, Mars, Juno, so also the Papists think the saints to be gods, they invoke them as if they were omnipotent, as if they saw the motions of all hearts. This is still manifest idolatry: and to this degree belong the Atheists or blasphemous Epicureans, who think that there is absolutely no God, or say that He does not care for human affairs, such as are very many Pontiffs and Canons, and other Epicureans, who think the Gospel to be a fable. Also pertaining here are those who deny that Christ is God, as the Jews and Arians deny that the Son of God, crucified and resurrected, is God. All these do not worship and invoke the true God, nay, they have no God, because they do not know nor invoke this sole and unique God, who is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom He said: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased, Hear Him. Thus He wills to be acknowledged and invoked, as He Himself revealed, that He is the Father of this Son, who is His co-eternal image, and that for His sake He wills to receive those who believe and invoke Him, and to give eternal life. As it is said in John 17: This is eternal life, that they may know Thee the only true God, and Jesus whom Thou hast sent, to be Christ. The second degree is more obscure, but related to the former.

Idolatry is to worship God without His word, by devised proper cults, and to trust in these cults, that for their sake God might hear and do good. Just as the Jews of old devised various cults, and had trust in these cults: so now the Papists worship God with the cult of the Mass, with vows, with Monasticism. These things, the Mass, Monasticism, are true idols, because it is written: In vain do they worship me with the commandments of men. Likewise, the honor which is due to Christ, namely, trust in the mediator, is transferred to the Mass, to vows, to dead saints, and similar things. Jeremiah 7 preaches about such cults: This is the nation that did not hear the voice of the Lord their God, nor receive discipline, faith has perished, and it has been taken away from their mouth, they dedicated the high places of Tophet. He says that they built shrines everywhere, and instituted cults without the command of God, just as then they even sacrificed and killed their children.

And just as other sins against the second table remain in the world, so much more do sins against the first table remain in all ages, in all times. For the devil tries most of all to turn men away from God, by false opinions and cults.

The Synagogue in the time of Christ did not have statues, and yet it was idolatrous; it denied that Christ was the Son of God, and with false confidence kept ceremonies, partly handed down in the law, partly devised by men. These cults of theirs were idols, in which they trusted, ignorant of the Gospel, of Christ, and of true invocation, which is made by trust in the mercy promised on account of Christ.

Now at this time, idolatry is much greater; the Papists persecute the Gospel and the voice of Christ, they deny that Christ is the mediator, and they have invented for themselves their own false cults: the Mass, monasticism, satisfaction, the invocation of saints. They preach that all these things are righteousness, merits for the remission of sins, and they apply them to others.

These are idolatrous, because they are insulting to Christ; likewise, they are received without the word of God. Also, the trust that is owed to God is placed in these things.

Therefore these are truly idols, of which he says here: They hasten after these things, signifying that there is a great multitude, great gatherings, a great and ardent zeal for impious and idolatrous cults in the world, as we see even now. How great is the number of Masses, how great the monasticisms, how varied the cults of the Saints? How great is the veneration of such things, at what great expense do Masses, monasteries, and temples stand.

In sum, the Papists worship their God Maozim with gold and silver, as Daniel says. The other part follows, concerning punishment.

Neither will I receive their libations of blood.

Nor will I be mindful of their names with my lips.

This is the horrible rejection of all idolaters who persecute Christ, whoever they are, Jews or Papists. He openly denies that they are the Church of God, denies that they have sacrifices, denies that Christ wishes to pray for them, he rejects and condemns that whole idolatrous troop, but the world does not understand this condemnation, indeed, because Pontiffs, Bishops, Priests, Monks, Kings, and Princes grant themselves the title of Church: likewise, because Bishops boast of ordinary succession, the world venerates them, and thinks they are the true Church, when it is a persecutor of Christ and idolatrous.

What must be said against this?

First, the conscience must be confirmed, so that we are not moved by title, authority, or multitude, so that we do not think those gatherings of Bishops are the Church, or because of them fall away from the word of God, but let us know that there is another true Church of the saints, namely, those who embrace the word of God and teach rightly. Let us know that we are members of this true Church, even if we are cast out beyond those congregations of Pontiffs and Bishops, just as Christ says: They will cast you out of the synagogues.

It is difficult to sustain this title, that we are not members of the Church, but let us oppose these consolations. Here Christ says that persecutors are not the Church.

And Paul says: If an angel from heaven should preach another Gospel, let him be anathema. Here Paul consoles us excellently, and recounts this voice of the Psalm: I will not be mindful of them.

For when he calls them anathemas, he signifies that the persecutors of Christ are rejected and condemned by God. Therefore they are not the Church.

Secondly, you should learn that all their cults, Masses, monasticisms, satisfactions, cults of the saints, are condemned cults, and are to be fled. You will not leave me in hell.

The third part of the Psalm is a narration concerning liberation from death and resurrection.

You will not give your holy one to see corruption, that is, not even my flesh will be destroyed, but you show me the paths of life, that is, you make alive, and you resurrect from death, even the body.

But here that which is said specifically of Christ: I will not see corruption. For the bodies of the other saints, even if they do not remain in perpetual corruption, but will be resurrected on account of Christ, nevertheless they are first dissipated into the air, as it is said: We shall all be changed.

But the flesh of Christ, even if it rested in the sepulcher, nevertheless could not be corrupted, because not even in death did the divine nature depart from his body, wherefore it was necessary that it be resurrected immediately incorrupt, or whole, so that he might live again entirely, even in body, which nevertheless had to be pierced on the cross, and expire, and be buried, so that it might be known that he was truly dead. Thus Peter explains these words: Whom God raised up, having loosed the pains of death, according to which it was impossible for him to be held by it.

The remaining verses of the Psalm preach again about the end and the effect. Therefore I endure passion and death, so that, having been resurrected, I may gather an eternal Church, which may enjoy your perpetual sight and company, with most abundant joy and eternal gladness.

The last part of Peter’s sermon is the application of the benefit of Christ. But first he accuses the sins of the hearers, and preaches about repentance. Afterwards he adds about the remission of sins, he says that this happens to believers by faith on account of Christ, and that at the same time the Holy Spirit is given, and that these benefits are applied to us in such a way if we, hearing the voice of the Gospel about Christ, believe, and are baptized in the name of Christ.

On the Lord’s Supper, 1.

1 Cor. 11. I received from the Lord that which I also delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was betrayed, took bread, and giving thanks, he broke it, and said: Take and eat, this is my body, which will be delivered for you: do this in my remembrance.

Likewise also the cup, after he had supped, saying: This cup is the new testament in my blood. Do this as often as you drink in my remembrance. For as often as you shall eat this bread, and drink the cup, you shall announce the death of the Lord until he comes. Therefore whoever shall eat this bread, and drink the cup of the Lord unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of the bread, and drink of the cup. For he who eats and drinks unworthily, eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the body of the Lord. Therefore among you many are weak and feeble and many sleep. But if we would judge ourselves, we would not surely be judged. But while we are judged, we are chastened by the Lord, that we may not be condemned with this world.

It is a grave warning, in which Paul says that the abuse of the sacrament is punished in a twofold way, by the wrath of God and by bodily punishments. For thus he says: He shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. Likewise: He eats judgment to himself.

He brings upon himself a double punishment by eating, namely, eternal, and the calamities of this life. Therefore, he says, among you many are sick, and many die.

There were not yet the greatest abuses. They were not yet as great as they are now. Impious, impure mass-priests celebrate Masses, sell them, take away part of the sacrament from the people, they do not teach about the pious use. The people approach, ignorant of what the sacrament is to be used for, they have heard nothing about the doctrine of faith, they think that by this work they merit the remission of sins. A part of the sacrament is carried around, it is looked at, and adored, and indulgences are given to those watching, so that the vain confidence of watching is confirmed, that it is a meritorious work etc.

These and many other horrible abuses, by which this sacrament is profaned in the last age of the world, deserve no light punishments, wars, dissensions and other public calamities. I believe also that the Turkish successes are especially permitted by God, on account of the manifold profanation of this sacrament, which the pious have always deplored in the Church.

They say that St. Anthony had a vision about the last time of the Church, where among other things there is an image, that he saw pigs standing at the altars, and celebrating Masses. Does not the thing itself correspond to this vision? The last age of the world has Bishops, Canons, Mass-priests, Monks, who have turned the Mass into gain, and serve their belly like pigs, they celebrate for the sake of the belly and wealth.

It is said also that a form of Christ appeared to St. Bridget, lacerated with scourges and dripping with blood; terrified, Bridget asked, what this form signified? The vision replied, that Christ is thus lacerated by the abuse of Masses. However these stories may be, they signify that the saints deplored the abuse of the sacrament, even if perhaps they signified this covertly by such stories, and it was not permitted to them to say openly what they desired.

I have prefaced these things, so that there may be thought about the true use of the sacrament and abuses may be fled. But only that which is delivered in the word of God is called the true use. Abuse is every pomp outside the word of God.

I. I will say therefore first a few things about the true use of the Sacrament. Many have civil and human opinions about the sacraments, such as Baptism and the Lord’s Supper, they think these rites were instituted only so that they might distinguish before men those who are called Christians from Jews and other nations, just as cowls distinguish Monks from others, or they think the Lord’s Supper is a sign of mutual benevolence, because banquets among all nations are signs of friendship.

These are human thoughts, which do not judge rightly about the sacraments. II. Papists have another imagination, that they are works through which we merit for ourselves and others the remission of sins.

This opinion is also ethnic; thus the Heathens felt about their ceremonies. III. Who is therefore the true use? I will say briefly: Sacraments are signs, not only distinguishing Christians before men, but much more signs of the will of God towards us, namely, of promised grace. God from the beginning, when he gave the promise to Abraham, added a sign. Thus when

nions, thinking these rites to be instituted only so that they might distinguish before men those who are called Christians from Jews and other nations, just as cowls distinguish Monks from others, or they think the Lord's Supper is a sign of mutual benevolence, because banquets among all nations are signs of friendship. These are human thoughts, which do not judge rightly concerning the sacraments.

II. Papists have another imagination, that they are works through which we merit for ourselves and others the remission of sins. This opinion is also ethnic; the Heathens felt this way about their own ceremonies.

III. What then is the true use? I shall say briefly: Sacraments are signs, not only distinguishing Christians before men, but much more signs of the will of God toward us, namely, of promised grace.

God from the beginning, when He gave the promise to Abraham, added a sign. Thus when He gave the word to Moses, He added certain signs; thus when He spread the Gospel among the nations, He added signs, Baptism and the Lord's Supper: because the will of God receiving us cannot be known except through His word and the signs handed down by Him. For He wishes to add signs to the word, so that the word may be more illustrious.

And the word and the sacrament signify the same thing, as Augustine says: A sacrament is a visible word, that is, the same thing is signified by voice and by gesture. The voice is perceived by the ears, the gesture by the eyes. As in Baptism, by words the remission of sins is given, by gesture the washing is done. Thus concerning the Lord's Supper, by words we are admonished that Christ suffered for us, that His blood was shed for us. The gesture likewise admonishes that we are made members of the body of Christ, and that the blood is given to us, by which we have been washed.

IIII. How then is it to be used? As Christ teaches: Take, eat, drink, do this in remembrance of me. Nor is it to be thought that it is only a civil spectacle, nor is it to be thought that by this work you merit the remission of sins, but you ought to know that it is a thing proposed, which may admonish you of the promise of the Gospel and the passion of Christ, and that by faith you receive remission on account of Christ, not on account of this your taking; but this taking is a testimony that Christ wishes His benefit to be applied to you and to each individual. When you take, therefore, you shall take, thinking: Behold, the benefit of Christ pertains to you. This ceremony testifies to this, in which He applies Himself to you.

V. Those, therefore, are fit for this Sacrament who perform repentance (as is said here: If we judged ourselves, we would not be judged by the Lord) and, performing repentance, believe that they are forgiven on account of Christ. This faith is stirred up when we think of this testimony, that Christ wishes His benefit to be applied to each individual.

Great, therefore, is the consolation in this taking. You should know that the taking was instituted so that faith might be stirred up, and that we individually might believe that the benefit of Christ pertains to ourselves.

This, therefore, is the true use, when, performing repentance, we take it with this faith, and we console ourselves, and in turn give thanks to God for the given Son, for the given salvation.

This is the remembrance of which Christ speaks: Do this in remembrance of me.

For remembrance signifies not only the thought of history, but faith and thanksgiving. Faith receives the benefit; thanksgiving in turn proclaims God. And always with this ceremony, preaching ought to have been done. Thus also the ancient Church kept this custom, which had no private Masses.

I have explained the true use, namely, the taking by one who performs repentance and believes that sins are remitted to him on account of Christ, and by this taking admonishes himself that the Gospel pertains to individuals. In this true use we know the sacrament to be, and the body and blood of Christ to be given.

Concerning another use without taking, namely, concerning carrying it about, the scripture says nothing: but there ought to be certainty in the sacraments. Therefore let us learn to use the sacrament rightly, and in the true use to exercise faith, and let us flee other abuses outside the word of God: and let us not doubt, God will punish these huge abuses of this sacrament. And I fear the Turk is a scourge especially for punishing these abuses. But let us pray to God that He may mitigate the punishments on account of His May He spare us for His praise, in the Church and in the instruction of youth, just as He spared the Ninevites. But let us also perform penance, as the Ninevites did. May God, for the sake of His Son our Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on us and give us His Holy Spirit.

Latin:

Evangelium in die omnium Sanctorum.

Matth. 5. Videns Iesus turbas ascendit in montem, et cum sedisset, accesserunt ad eum discipuli.

eius, et aperiens os suum, docebat eos, dicens: Beati pauperes spiritu, quoniam ipsorum est regnum coelorum. Beati mites, quoniam ipsi haereditabunt terram. Beati qui lugent, quoniam ipsi consolabuntur. Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt iusticiam, quoniam ipsi saturabuntur. Beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur. Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt. Beati pacifici, quoniam ipsi filii Dei vocabuntur. Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter iusticiam, quoniam ipsorum est regnum coelorum. Beati estis, cum exprobraverint vobis homines, et persecuti vos fuerint, et dixerint omne malum verbum adversus vos mentientes, propter me. Gaudete et exultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in coelis. Sic enim persecuti sunt Prophetas qui fuerunt ante vos.

Tres sunt loci.

I. Doctrina generalis est, contra opiniones de scandalo crucis. II. Et sunt adiectae promissiones bonorum operum, interpretantes legem. III. Et simul traditur doctrina de fide exercenda in his operibus.

De primo.

Duplices sunt promissiones. Aliae legales, quae habent conditionem operum, et sunt additae bonis operibus, seu meritis, ut: Qui dederit uni ex minimis potum aquae, non perdet mercedem suam. Et hic: Beati mites, Beati pauperes spiritu etc.

Sed cum legi nemo satisfaciat, hic quaerendum est, quomodo bona opera placeant Deo, et quomodo hae promissiones fiant ratae. Ideo respondemus, sicut alias saepe dictum est: Lex sine Christo non prodest, sicut autem valet lex, sic et valent legales promissiones, cum prius apprehensa est promissio gratiae donatae propter Christum. Itaque cum fide iusti sumus, deinde placet Deo incoata obedientia, et meretur praemia, ac promissiones tunc ratae sunt, quia illa obedientia dicitur esse quaedam legis impletio.

Est igitur alia promissio propria Evangelii, gratuita, videlicet reconciliationis et iusticiae imputandae propter Christum. Haec promissio semper praelucere debet omnibus operibus et promissionibus, quia per Filium habemus accessum ad patrem. Haec ideo praefati sumus, ut sciatur, quomodo hae promissiones legales valeant et ratae sint, iuxta illud: Per fidem stabilimus legem.

Hinc explicari etiam obiectio potest. Cum hic dicat, homines beatos esse mansuetudine, cur alibi dicitis, sola fide iustificari homines? Respondeo: Haec non pugnant. Oportet primum homines fieri iustos seu acceptos Deo, fide, gratis propter Christum, postea sunt etiam beati, id est, habentes dona et praemia a Deo, propter caeteras virtutes. Haec sine sophistica hoc modo explicata facile intelligi possunt. Discamus igitur tradi hic promissiones legales seu bonorum operum, quae sic accipiendae sunt, ut semper praeluceat promissio evangelica gratiae Christi.

De secundo. Promissiones hoc loco propositae dissentiunt a iudicio rationis, et sunt expositio legis Mosaicae: lex dicit, bonis bene fore. At hic dicit Christus, iustos futuros in paupertate, luctu, persecutione. Sed respondet Christus, differri praemia praecipua, etsi in hac vita etiam conservari Ecclesiam oportet mirabilibus beneficiis Dei.

Iustis bene sit. Abel est iustus, Ergo Abelo bene sit. Respondeo primum ad minorem: Abel est iustus imputatione, et habet incoatam obedientiam, sed quia in eo adhuc haeret peccatum, manet mors, et haec natura vitiosa est subiecta cruci. Ideo differuntur praemia ad consummatam iusticiam.

Deinde respondeas ad maiorem: Iustis bene sit, iuxta consilium Dei, et post hanc vitam. Nam Deus, ut servet Ecclesiam, etiam in hac vita impertit ingentia dona, sed inter mirabilia certamina, sicut servavit Ecclesiam in diluvio, in Aegypto, in captivitate Babylonica, et martyrum temporibus. Teneamus igitur hanc interpretatione legis, quam hic Christus tradit, cum praemia pollicetur, et testatur partim in hac vita dari, partim post hanc vitam.

De tertio.

Sed hoc praecipue discendum est in his contentionibus, quomodo fides in his promissionibus exercenda sit. Laetamus fidem, et maxime fugimus exercitia fidei. Christus praedicit Ecclesiam fore in aerumnis, quia in his vult exerceri fidem. Quomodo? Octo modis.

Primo, agnoscendo gratiam promissam propter Christum. Secundo, invocando Deum. Tertio, impellendo ad bona opera, ut retineatur beneficium Dei. Quarto, ad petendum et expectandum auxilium, adversus diabolum, adversus hostes, adversus imbecillitatem propriam. Quinto, ad expectandam compensationem seu praemia. Sexto, ad petendum auxilium in tolerantia. Septimo, ad ostendendam gratitudinem, et exempla, ut propagetur doctrina, et ornetur gloria Dei. Octavo, ut his exercitiis agitatae et excuscitatae fides, crescat, et crescant caetera dona.

Exemplum, Paulus in afflictionibus primum cogitabat, an placeret Deo, quia afflictiones et adversi casus videntur esse signa irae Dei. Excitat igitur fidem, et sentit se propter Christum placere, et confugit ad Deum. Secundo invocat. Tertio, agnoscens misericordiam Dei erga se, studet retinere beneficium, et cavet, ne amittat iusticiam. Quarto fide petit et expectat liberationem in afflictionibus et auxilium adversus diabolum. Quinto, expectat praemia, et intuens fide in finem promissum, perfert praesentes aerumnas. Sexto, fide petit auxilium et robur spiritus, ut possit praestare patientiam, etiam si mors oppetenda sit. Septimo, statuit haec officia necessaria esse ad ostendendam gratitudinem, ad propagationem Evangelii, agnoscit Deum, mirabili consilio, sic velle abolere peccatum in carne nostra, et Ecclesiam mirabili modo glorificare. Octavo, dat operam ut crescat fides, et caetera dona. Sic dives credens invocat Deum, studet retinere iusticiam, Deo obtemperat in officio liberalitatis, expectat vicissim auxilium a Deo in suis aerumnis, et expectat compensationem seu conservationem facultatum, ostendit gratitudinem suo exemplo, cupit augeri dona, augeri fidem. Sed quia pauci credunt, pauci expectant conservationem facultatum: ideo animi sunt angustiores et illiberales. Haec generalia semper de promissionibus legalibus tenenda sunt, ut meminerimus et in his promissionibus praemiorum exercendam esse fidem.

Beati pauperes spiritu.

Non vult deseri facultates sine vocatione, non approbat Monachatum, iuxta illud: Frustra colunt me mandatis hominum, sed concionatur Christus de vera inopia piorum et fugientium impios quaestus, sive inopia sit fortuita, sive acciderit propter professionem Evangelii. Hos inopes omnes consolatur, et testatur inopiam non esse signum irae Dei et maledictionem, imo pollicetur praemia. Estque opposita sententia legi, et imperiis mundi. Lex docet detrimenta facultatum esse poenas peccatorum et maledictionem: hic Christus docet pios, aliud esse iudicium de cruce secundum Evangelium. Nam afflictiones piis non sunt signa irae, sed fiunt exercitia fidei, sicut ubique clamat Evangelium, Ecclesiam subiectam esse cruci. In durissimis afflictionibus summa lumina Ecclesiae fuerunt, Christus, Iohannes Baptista, Ieremias, Abel etc. Item imperia mundi dicuntur florere, cum habent opes, sic de Ecclesia et Pontifices sentiunt. At Christus hic testatur Ecclesiam potius florere in paupertate, ne desperemus propter inopiam. Addit autem: Pauperes spiritu, id est, spirituali obedientia, patienter ferentes paupertatem, seu parati ad eam ferendam, si fuerint excussi ex facultatibus, sicut Abraham alias habebat facultates, alias vagabatur inops sine certis sedibus.

Beati lugentes.

Et hic loquitur de veris doloribus piorum, sive propter professionem accidant, sive a poenis aut morsibus diaboli oriantur, ut cum David pulsus in exilium agnovit culpam, et sensit se puniri. In talibus aerumnis clamitat conscientia, nos a Deo proiectos vel desertos esse. Sed vox Evangelii diversum docet: Sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus. Item: Multae tribulationes iustorum, et hic promittitur consolatio, cum in hac vita, tum post hanc vitam, sicut docet totus Psalmus 4.: Scitote quoniam mirificat Dominus sanctum suum, et exaudit me cum clamo ad eum. Item 33.: Pauper clamavit, et Dominus exaudivit eum.

Beati mites.

Consolatur oppressos, qui non habent vindicem et defensorem, et docet privatam vindictam Deo commendandam esse, sicut Ioseph, Israëlitae in Aegypto, David sub Saule, pii sub Antiocho,

Ecclesia sub Diocletiano, erant sine defensione. Clarius autem intelligitur hic locus, considerata antithesi. Tyranni existimant imperia retineri, et augeri acerbitate vindictae. Econtra, Evangelium docet, ut in causa iusta simus constantes, nec tamen quaeramus privatam vindictam, sed exitus Deo commendemus. Et cum ex officio exercenda est vindicta, mitigemus eam, sicut exempla David, totam hanc doctrinam pingunt. Nunquam voluit Saulem interficere, deinde regnans, necessariam vindictam, tamen saepe temperavit misericordia, pepercit Semei.

Huc pertinent multa in Psalmis, ut Psalm. 36.: Saevientes exterminabuntur, sustinentes autem Dominum haereditabunt terram. Pharao deletus est, vicit Israël. Apostoli interfecti sunt, mansit tamen Ecclesia deletis tyrannis. Promittitur igitur hic versiculus oppressis, et vindice carentibus, ac non cupidis privatae vindictae, conservationem etiam in terra.

Quanquam autem haec proprie scribuntur propter Ecclesiam, tamen ut res sit magis perspicua, etiam politica exempla consideremus. In politica iustitia, clementia principibus, et mansuetudo privatis utilis est. Econtra, saevitia multis exitio fuit, non solum monstrosis tyrannis, qui etiam aliis sceleribus polluti erant, ut Phalaridi, Dionysio, Neroni, sed etiam alioqui mediocribus, ut Pertinaci, Aureliano. Et saepe videmus, privatas offensiones magnas patientia sanari. Hanc lenitatem maxime flagitat Christus, quia in Ecclesia incidunt periculosae offensiones, ideo toties dicit: Remittite, et remittetur vobis. Et Christus lavans pedes Apostolis, vult nos sanare offensiones omni genere officii, ideo dicit: Exemplum dedi vobis. Et Petrus inquit: Dilectio tegit peccata. Hae sententiae omnes huc transferantur, Et quia in periculis famae, aut rerum, si desit vindex, timemus nos et nostra peritura esse, ideo hic promittitur conservatio, cum ait: Possidebunt terram, sicut Israël in Aegypto conservabatur, etiamsi mandatum erat ut infantes interficerentur.

Beati qui sitiunt et esuriunt iusticiam.

Sitire iusticiam est, vero dolore et zelo affici, ut propagetur gloria Dei, ut iusta sit gubernatio, et scandala, et mala exempla tollantur. Est autem haec particula quasi declaratio quaedam superioris. Antea dixit salutarem esse clementiam, nunc addit hanc clementiam non debere esse dissolutionem seu ignaviam. Accedat zelus, sit vigilans, intentus, acer, unusquisque in suo officio. Estque opposita sententia Epicureis, qui nihil curant qualiacunque vitia, seu religionum, seu alia, ut nunc rident nos Epicurei, cum de idololatria aut de libidinibus querimur. Hanc ignaviam detestatur Christus, et praecipit zelum, ac addit promissionem. Nam impii dicunt pios frustra moliri emendationem. Christus econtra promittit labores non fore inanes, saturabuntur, inquit. Item, hi sitientes intelligantur non Cynici, aliena vitia tantum reprehendentes, ad sua conniventes, sed sese quoque emendantes, iuxta illud: Iustus primum accusator est sui, postea occurrit alteri.

Beati misericordes. Promittitur merces beneficiis, qui defendunt aut adiuvant afflictos, ut qui tegunt eos, qui propter professionem Evangelii affliguntur, iuxta Psalmum: Beatus qui intelligit super egenum et pauperem etc.

Beati mundo corde, id est, casto, sicut ad Ebraeos dicitur: Sectamini sanctificationem, id est, castitatem, sine qua nemo Deum videbit.

Et usitata poena est libidinum coecitas, ut Rom. 1. et Ephes. 4. dicitur.

Beati pacifici, id est, recte diiudicantes dogmata, recte sanantes iniustas discordias Ecclesiae, vel regnorum, cedentes aliis bona conscientia, propter pacem. Continetur autem hic maxima pars Decalogi. Nam ad primum praeceptum pertinent hae virtutes, Veritas et fortitudo in confessione, de qua dicit: Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur. Item: Fides expectans has promissiones et retinens veritatem, propter has promissiones. Item: Patientia in quibuscunque aerumnis. Nam hae virtutes sunt cultus, de quibus concionatur primum praeceptum. Ad secundam tabulam pertinent mansuetudo in mitiganda vindicta, beneficentia, castitas, caritas vel aequitas in facienda pace. Ad primum praeceptum pertinet sitire iusticiam, id est, zelus etc.

De dicto: Non veni solvere legem.

Lex moralis est aeterna et immutabilis sententia in mente divina, quae est regula iusticiae, praecipiens quales omnes creaturas intelligentes baptistae secedunt in angulos, fingunt sibi speculationes, nolunt hac vita civili vivere, His modis putant se accipere Spiritum sanctum, sicut et Monachi, et idololatrae Papistae iactitant se consequi Spiritum sanctum per suas ludicras ceremonias, Missas et opera traditionum.

Sed nos discamus dari Spiritum sanctum per verbum Dei, quandocunque nos eius cogitatione consolamur, audientes, vel legentes, vel cogitantes verbum Dei, et invocamus Deum, ac credimus nobis ignosci propter Christum, et nos iuvari. Haec fiunt in vera poenitentia, et quotidiana invocatione omnium qui agunt poenitentiam, et non perseverant in delictis contra conscientiam.

Dixi de prima parte, scilicet, de promissione.

Nunc dicam de secunda, quid agat Spiritus sanctus. Hic Christus facit antithesin.

Non relinquam vos orphanos. Brevis est oratio, sed est vera imago Ecclesiae coram mundo, et sicut nos ipsi plerumque iudicamus, quando sentimus onus aerumnarum nostrarum.

Vide an non sumus orphani?

Mundus nos persequitur, sumus coetus exiguus, dissipatus, male cohaerens. Non habemus humanum principem, regem, pontificem. Ridiculum est Papae et regibus, quando nos vocamus Ecclesiam.

Deinde singuli suas miserias considerent. Nonne sumus orphani, sine defensore, sine certis auxiliis?

Et praesertim tunc intelligeremus nos esse orphanos, si potentiam diaboli aliquo modo cerneremus. Ergo adversus tantos hostes promittit Christus Spiritum sanctum, ait: Non relinquam vos orphanos, sed ego sum pontifex vester, Rogabo patrem.

Crede, non frustra orat Filius, impetrat nobis a patre auxilium. Quod?

Spiritum paracletum, qui in nobis lucet, dat consilium, erigit animum, incoat vitam aeternam in nobis, sicut hic dicitur: Ut maneat vobiscum semper. Ut autem de his beneficiis cogitare possimus, et nos ipsos excitare, proponamus nobis dulcissimum dictum ex Zacharia, ubi scriptum est: Effundam super domum David Spiritum gratiae et precum.

Haec vox omnia complectitur, et docet quae sint bona opera, qui sint summi et veri cultus Ecclesiae.

Omnes gentes, etiam barbarae, habent cultus Dei externos, honesta opera. Sed hi nondum sunt, quibus proprie colitur et apprehenditur Deus, sola Ecclesia habet veros cultus, quos praestat, cum accipit spiritum gratiae et precum. Quid significant haec verba?

Spiritus gratiae significat Spiritu sancto nos iuvari, ut statuamus nos esse in gratia Dei, certo placere Deo, nobis peccata esse remissa propter Christum.

Haec fides in omni afflictione agnoscit Deum adesse opitulatorem, esse propicium, non esse deserturum orphanos. Hac fide Spiritus sanctus est παράκλητος, consolator et vivificator. Sequitur altera particula, Spiritum precum.

Cum simus orphani in mundo, opus est nobis defensore et auxiliatore Deo.

Ideo excitantur corda Spiritu sancto, ut invocent Deum, sicut et Paulus inquit: Spiritus adiuvat nos, ut clamemus Abba pater. Ideo Ecclesia est onerata ingentibus periculis et aerumnis, ut hanc invocationem exerceamus, fide clamemus ad Deum, expectemus auxilium.

Nec putes haec tantum magnifica verba esse. Pii credentes experiuntur vere adesse Deum opitulatorem et auxiliatorem, et res magnae et magna miracula sic fiunt in mundo.

Sic servatur tua familia contra diabolum. Sic servantur regna, ut Ezechias et Esaias precibus pellebant Assyrios. Alia miracula, ut Moisi, magis cernuntur oculis, quia Deus vult extare illustria quaedam testimonia.

Sed tamen Ecclesia semper habet sua miracula, quae fiunt in invocatione, ut Moises, ut Elias in sua vocatione gubernabantur Spiritu sancto, et res magnas et illustres gerebant. Ita petamus nos gubernari Spiritu sancto, et sciamus veram esse Christi vocem: Dabit vobis Spiritum paracletum.

Sciamus dari nobis Spiritum sanctum, exaudiri nostras preces, iuvari nos in omnibus periculis publicis et privatis, res magnae et magna miracula sic fiunt in mundo, etiam si mundus non cernit: quia bellum inter Christum et diabolum mirabili modo geritur, per vasa infirma in Ecclesia, quae Christus tamen efficit potentia divina per Spiritum sanctum. Memento ergo hanc vocem: Effundam spiritum gratiae et precum.

Excites te fide, ut credas te propter Christum esse in gratia, Petito Spiritum sanctum auxiliatorem, invoca Deum in omnibus negotiis, ut experiaris hunc opitulatorem. Nunc etiam oremus pro Ecclesia, ut retineamus Spiritum veritatis, quia diabolus callidissime struit insidias veritati.

Conatur nova sophistica obruere Evangelium, et mundus delectatur his mendaciis et praestigiis, quia nec Spiritum sanctum novit, neque Christum. Sed pii, qui norunt Christum, et petunt spiritum veritatis, toto pectore adversentur talibus imposturis. Deus tamen servabit Ecclesiam, depellet Turcas, propter Ecclesiam, non propter impios et idololatras. Haec breviter hoc die monenda sunt, ut haec monita Christi accipiant pii, et una invocemus Deum propter Filium, et petamus Spiritum sanctum, sicut promisit: Pater meus coelestis dabit Spiritum sanctum petentibus.

Concio Petri, Actorum 2.

Stans autem Petrus cum undecim, elevavit vocem suam, et locutus est eis: Viri Iudaei, et qui habitatis Hierusalem universi, hoc vobis notum sit, et auribus percipite verba mea. Non enim sicut vos existimatis hi ebrii sunt, cum sit hora diei tertia. Sed hoc est, quod dictum est per Prophetam Ioël: Et erit in novissimis diebus, dicit Dominus, Effundam de spiritu meo super omnem carnem. Et prophetabunt filii vestri et filiae vestrae, et iuvenes vestri visiones videbunt, et seniores vestri somnia somniabunt. Et quidem super servos meos et ancillas meas in diebus illis effundam de spiritu meo, et prophetabunt, et dabo prodigia in coelo sursum, et signa in terra deorsum, sanguinem et ignem, et vaporem fumi. Sol convertetur in tenebras, et Luna in sanguinem, antequum veniat dies Domini magnus et manifestus. Et erit: Omnis quicunque invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit.

Viri Israëlitae, audite verba haec, Iesum Nazarenum virum approbatum a Deo in vobis, virtutibus, et prodigiis et signis, quae fecit Deus per illum in medio vestri, sicut scitis, hunc definitio consilio, et praesentia Dei traditum per manus iniquorum affigentes interemistis. Quem Deus suscitavit, solutis doloribus inferni, iuxta quod impossibile erat teneri illum ab eo. David enim dicit in eum: Providebam Dominum in conspectu meo semper, quoniam a dextris est mihi, ne commovear. Propter hoc laetatum est cor meum, et exultavit lingua mea, insuper et caro mea requiescet in spe. Quoniam non derelinques animam meam in inferno, nec dabis sanctum tuum videre corruptionem. Notus fecisti mihi vias vitae, replebis me iucunditate cum facie tua. Viri fratres, liceat audenter dicere ad vos de patriarcha David, quoniam et defunctus est, et sepultus est, et sepulcrum eius est apud nos usque in hodiernum diem. Propheta igitur cum esset, et sciret, quia iureiurando iurasset illi Deus, de fructu lumborum eius sedere super sedem eius, praevidens locutus est de resurrectione Christi, quod neque derelictus est in inferno, neque caro eius vidit corruptionem. Hunc Iesum resuscitavit Deus, cuius omnes testes sumus. Dextera igitur Dei exaltatus, et promissione Spiritus sancti accepta a patre, effudit hoc donum, quod vos videtis et auditis.

Concio Petri tota continet tres praecipuas partes.

Prima est dictum Ioëlis, continens promissionem Spiritus sancti, et salutis aeternae propriam novi Testamenti. Primum igitur describuntur beneficia novi Testamenti.

Secunda pars est, Concio de morte et resurrectione Messiae, qui est causa beneficiorum novi Testamenti. Estque hic locus testimonium, quod hic Iesus sit Messias, quia resurrexit a mortuis.

Tertia pars, de applicatione, quomodo haec beneficia novi Testamenti, parta per Messiam consequamur, videlicet: Agite poenitentiam, et baptizetur unusquisque in nomine Christi, ad remissionem peccatorum, et accipite donum Spiritus sancti. Longa concio est, et locupletissima, quae non potest paucis tota enarrari.

Prodest autem tiles locos saepe meditari ad alendam cognitionem beneficiorum Christi, et confirmandam fidem, et al excitandam gratiarum actionem, et dilectionem erga Deum. Ideo primum breviter de prima parte concionis Petri dicamus, videlicet, de gratia novi Testamenti, et de donatione Spiritus sancti.

Duo dicit Propheta: Omnis qui invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit. Item, de donatione Spiritus sancti: Effundam de spiritu meo. Utraque sententia est opposita legi. Lex docet et postulat multa, sed non salvat, imo accusat, ut docet Paulus: Lex iram operatur. Sed alia est novi Testamenti praedicatio, quae promittit salutem, et quidem promittit omnibus, sed invocantibus. Quid est promittere salutem? Promittere liberationem a peccato, ab ira Dei, a morte aeterna, donationem vitae aeternae.

Haec adfert novum Testamentum, non propter legem, sed tantum invocanti. Ideo enim dicit: Invocans, ut discernat cultus, quasi dicat: Non quaeretur tunc iste cultus legis, sed alius cultus, scilicet, invocatio sola, quae est vox fidei, credentis et accipientis promissionem, et clamantis: Abba pater. Ideo hoc dictum dulcescet animo, cum cogitabimus promissionem esse universalem, et ad nos ipsos pertinere. Et per invocationem intelligimus fidem, excludentem propria merita, et tantum nitentem Domino, qui iam se patefecit. Oportet enim discerni invocationem a cultu legis. Nam et haec ipsa vox: Omnis qui invocat nomen Domini, salvabitur, est abrogatio legis.

Hic admoneatur auditor, ut diligenter sibi inculcet hanc particulam: Omnis qui invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit, sciat esse summam Evangelii, et intelligat invocationem non more legis, id est, non sic cogitet, invocans salvatur, scilicet si dignus erit, si satis habebit operum etc. sed invocans, id est, non fugiens Deum, sed credens ei propter Messiam missum a patre coelesti.

II. De altera particula: Quomodo fit haec salvatio?

Fit hoc modo: Effundam de spiritu meo.

Haec est mira vox, et supra omnem humanum captum, Deus salvabit, non lege, sed impertiens seipsum, Effundam, inquit, de Meo Spiritu, de mea substantia, Ubicunque est substantia Dei, ibi est noticia Dei, dilectio Dei, vita aeterna. Quid potest Deus dare maius, quam quod impertit nobis de suo spiritu, de sua substantia? sicut Petrus inquit, nos fieri participes naturae Dei.

Utinam tantum donum agnosceremus ac peteremus, ut hoc spiritu confirmati, glorificaremus Deum in confessione, et in tota vita. Sed quia dona Dei, sicut dicitur: Habenti dabitur. Ideo magnitudinem huius doni divini, Spiritus sancti, in nos effusi, non intelligimus, quia non exercemus, non proferimus hoc donum, sed excutimus, contristamus Spiritum sanctum.

Haec sunt magna peccata in mundo, quae tamen ratio non iudicat aut cernit.

Eruditi considerent hoc verbum, Meo, cum dicitur: Effundam de spiritu meo. Primum enim significat spiritum esse personam consubstantialem Deo. Deinde docet, quod Deus ita nos restituat, aliquid suae substantiae impertiens. Ubi autem est substantia Dei, ibi est lux, id est, noticia vera Dei, vera dilectio Dei, et vita aeterna. Haec omnia sunt longe supra captum rationes, supra iusticiam legis, et humanam sapientiam. Intelligi autem poterunt, si exercebimus donum, in confessione et invocatione quotidiana.

III. Et prophetabunt filii vestri.

Addit signa et testimonia, et praecipua opera Spiritus sancti. Primum est, prophetare, id est, recte intelligere et enarrare Evangelium, quia Evangelium est doctrina de voluntate Dei erga nos, quam humana ratio non percipit sine Spiritu sancto, sic ut Paulus inquit: Animalis homo non percipit ea quae Dei sunt. Sicut etiam videmus, quid agant sapientes mundi, quorum aliqui volunt videri intelligere Evangelium, cum certe non intelligant. Origenes, Hieronymus et alii multi non intellexerunt noticiam fidei. Haec dicta Pauli: Lex iram operatur, Iustificati fide pacem habemus, adeo non intellexerunt, ut etiam absurda et impropria esse putaverint. Ita nunc multi Theologi haec dicta non intelligunt, etiam cum verba imitantur. Sed qui intelligunt? Vere invocantes Dominum, qui habent fidem, in quos effusus est Spiritus sanctus. Hi prophetant, recte intelligunt, recte enarrant, confitentur, glorificant Deum, conservant Deo puritatem verbi, et defendunt gloriam Dei.

Haec omnia comprehendit verbum, Prophetare, hi sunt grati cultus Deo, sicut scriptum est: Laudate pueri Dominum etc.

Hos cultus praestemus, Tales prophetae simus, veri interpretes et confessores. Discamus ergo, quantas res his concionibus proponat, de vera invocatione, fide, IIII. Addit signo Spiritus sancti, scilicet prophetiae, alia signa. Senes vestri somnia somniabunt, et iuvenes vestri visiones videbunt.

Dixi prophetiam praecipue significare intellectum et enarrationem veram verbi Dei, quia verbum Dei continet sapientiam de voluntate Dei erga nos, prorsus positam extra captum humanae rationis.

Hoc donum necessarium est Ecclesiae, de quo Paulus 1. Corinth. 4. multa loquitur: Et magna lux est, in aliis magis, in aliis minus fulgens, alio tempore plures in Ecclesia, alio tempore pauciores sunt hoc praediti dono.

Sicut tempore Samuelis plures erant in Israël recte sentientes, quam tempore Eli, cum esset, ut dicit textus, sermo Domini rarus. Tempore Apostolorum plures erant recte intelligentes Evangelium, quam postea sub Papatu, etiamsi plurimum fuerit sacerdotum, Monachorum, Theologorum.

Nunc Deus iterum aliquantulum exuscitavit hanc lucem, et orandus est, ut conservet, et nos monendi sumus, ne ipsi eam extinguamus nova sophistica et humana sapientia, et fiamus prophetae tales, qualis erat Saul, de quo dictum est: Nunquid et Saul inter Prophetas?

Ita nunc de multis, qui nova sophistica corrumpunt Evangelium, quaerunt reconciliationes dogmatum congruentes ad sapientiam humanam, ambiguas, flexibiles et fucatas, dici potest: Nunquid et hi inter Prophetas?

Quando pectora sunt ociosa aut occupata humanis cupiditatibus, incipiunt fastidire verbum Dei, postea, ut quaerant pacem et ocium, accommodant se iudiciis impiorum, et sinunt depravari veram doctrinam.

Ita redit diabolus ad domum purgatam.

Haec magna mala prudenter cavenda sunt, sed mundus insanit suis cupiditatibus, et haec peccata non intelligit.

Ideo Spiritus sanctus nos admonet et arguit per Evangelium, monstrat has insidias, et iubet ut vigilemus et caveamus, Et tantum de prophetia.

Addit autem Ioël alia testimonia Spiritus sancti: Senes somnia habebunt, et iuvenes habebunt visiones.

His verbis non tantum vaticinia de rebus futuris intelligit, sicut Ioseph, Daniel fuerunt vates.

Et Paulus habuit visionem, ut dicit in Actis cap. 16. Sed generaliter omnia dona complectitur, quae Paulus recenset 1.

Corinth. 12. Vult enim in genere dicere, futurum esse, ut Spiritus sanctus declaret se multis donis, prophetia, vaticiniis rerum futurarum, scientia gubernationis.

Ut hic cum de senibus loquitur, intelligit gubernatores, hi habebunt divinos motus, divinitus regent politias, vel magna negocia ecclesiastica, aut politica.

Sicut interdum princeps aliquis habet sapientiam aut pium consiliarium, aut civitas pium senatorem. Nec putes hic fieri mentionem de vulgaribus somniis, sed sequuntur in textu et aliae appellationes.

His omnibus varia dona significat Ecclesiae et gubernationi necessaria, quae etsi omnia sunt miraculosa, et Dei insignia opera, tamen alia aliis magis cernuntur, ut cum Petrus sanaret claudum, vel cum educeretur ex carcere, id vocatur miraculum, Et magni fit, quia incurrit in oculos, cum alia haberet multo maiora miracula, ut, quod assidue defendebatur contra diabolum et contra tyrannos.

Item, quod permansit in doctrinae puritate, quod eius conciones erant efficaces, quod eius gubernatio fuit felix. Haec sunt magna et vera miracula, ad quae accedunt etiam interdum alia rara opera, quae magis incurrunt in oculos.

Sic ergo intelligatur hic locus de omnibus donis Spiritus sancti in Ecclesia generaliter.

Et meminerint pii, qui sunt in gubernatione, vel Ecclesiae, vel politica, vel principes ac eorum consiliarii, et senatores civitatum, quod hic dicitur de senibus: Senes habebunt donum Spiritus sancti.

Hic locus admonet gubernatores, ut sciant humanam sapientiam non sufficere magnis rebus agendis, nec in negotiis ecclesiasticis, nec in aliis, sed opus est Spiritu sancto, gubernatore et duce, et orent cum Davide, ut surgat Deus ad iudicium quod mandavit, id est, ad regnum.

Psalm. 7. et 71.: Surge Deus, indica terram. V. Hactenus breviter dictum est de donis et testimoniis Spiritus sancti, quae addita sunt promissioni Evangelii de salvatione promissa per Messiam, addit autem textus aliquid de tempore Messiae, et de signis praecedentibus gloriosum adventum Messiae, quem etiam prodest cogitare, ut securitas carnalis corrigatur. Prophetae interdum simul loquuntur de utroque adventu Christi, ut hic Ioël loquitur de revelatione Evangelii, et statim adiungit gloriosum adventum Christi in novissimo iudicio. Pars prophetiae intelligatur de primo adventu, pars de secundo. Nam quae de signis dicit: Mittam sanguinem, ignem, Sol mutabitur etc. Etsi haec etiam possunt accommodari ad tempus passionis Christi, tamen describunt totum tempus post Evangelii revelationem usque ad iudicium, videlicet excidium totius Iudaicae gentis, mutationes regnorum, et calamitates publicas, quae erunt saeviores in fine, sicut praemonet Christus Matth. 28. et Luc. 21. ut videmus iam omnibus regnis impendere mutationem.

Et praedictum est nominatim de Gog et Magog, id est, de Turcis, quod sint vastaturi armis magnam partem Ecclesiae. Praedictum est et de Antichristo seu pseudopropheta, id est, Papa, qui sedebit in templo Dei, id est, in ipsa Ecclesia, et grassabitur dolo et vi. Haec mala consideremus, et fide nos magis muniamus, et oremus Deum, ut nos servet, quia in Luca, cum eadem praedicuntur: Erit pressura gentium, tamen additur consolatio eadem: Prope est redemtio vestra.

Item: Vigilate et orate, ut possitis haec effugere. Certe pericula temporum hortantur nos ad precationem, et monent instare illum diem, quo omnes impii cum diabolis in aeternas poenas abiicientur, et Filius Dei glorificabit Ecclesiam suam.

Hoc iudicium nobis proponamus, et sciamus non procul abesse. Gog et Magog vere pervenit in summum fastigium, et Antichristus iam revelatur.

Haec sunt signa ultimi temporis, de quo praedictum est, fore, ut crescat tunc impietas. Ideo simus vigilantes et cauti, ne deficiamus a vera doctrina, timeamus et invocemus Deum, ut nos regat, Non offendamus eum nostra ingratitudine, et turpitudine morum. Haec admonitio necessaria est, quando de signis postremi temporis dicitur.

Secunda pars concionis Petri.

Viri Israëlitae audite verba haec.

In priore parte Concionis dictum est, de ipsis novi Testamenti beneficiis, de salvatione, et de donatione Spiritus sancti, qui est arrhabo novae et aeternae iusticiae et vitae. Nunc sequitur pars secunda, de causa seu autore horum beneficiorum, scilicet, de Messia.

Et diligenter considerandum est, hanc concionem de Messia passo, resuscitato, glorificato et regnante, opponi carnalibus imaginationibus Iudaeoram, de regno mundano Messiae, quasi dicat Petrus: Vos expectatis Messiam et liberatorem, qui pulsis Romanis, tribuat vobis imperium mundi, Ecce iam venit Messias, aliter regnat, quam vos putatis. Factus est victima pro peccatis generis humani, cum a vobis interfectus est. Deinde resuscitato Deus omnia subiecit.

Hunc Iesum quem vos crucifixistis, scitote Messiam et salvatorem esse. Ut autem nunc cum Iudaeis duae nobis praecipuae sunt quaestiones. Altera an Christum oportuerit pati, et non habere mundanum imperium, sed coeleste.

Altera, an venerit Messias, et sitne hic ipse Iesus, quem nos praedicamus, crucifixum et resuscitatum esse. Ita duas res agit Petrus, Hunc ipsum Iesum esse Messiam, et quod post interfectionem resuscitatus, regnet.

De prima quaestione.

An hic sit Messias? Quod autem hic sit ipse Messias, probat sic: Quia Deus magnis signis et miraculis testatus est, hunc divinitus missum esse.

Secundum testimonium, quia scripturae testantur, Messiam resuscitandum esse. Hic revixit ex morte: ergo hic est Messias.

Maiorem probat ex Psalmo: Non relinques animam meam in inferno, nec dabis sanctum tuum videre corruptionem. Haec sunt dicta de Messia, quia certum est Davidem esse mortuum, et nondum resurrexisse, sed vaticinatum esse de Messia. Quia enim Deus promiserat Davidi quendam de lumbis ipsius habiturum regnum aeternum, inde ratiocinatus est, necessario resurrecturum esse illum secundum carnem.

Cum igitur testetur scriptura Messiam resurrecturum esse, et hic resurrexerit: ergo hunc Messiam esse certum est, et nos sumus testes resurrectionis ipsius. De secundo.

Quale sit regnum Messiae? Quod sit regnum coeleste, et quod oportuerit Christum pati, hi ipsi Psalmi probant: Conserva me Domine, quia mihi non bene est propter te. Et Psalmus: Dixit Dominus, idem probat, Messiam habiturum regnum perpetuum, et potentiam divinam ad abolendam mortem et peccatum, et ad dandam iusticiam et vitam aeternam. Ideo hic dicit: Exaltatus a Deo, Effudit Spiritum sanctum. Tale regnum erit, scilicet liberatio a peccato et morte aeterna, donatio iusticiae et vitae aeternae.

Tertia pars est, de applicatione, sed ante applicationem est doctrina de peccato, et praedicatio poenitentiae. Vide autem, quod peccatum accuset, scilicet, quod non noverint Filium Dei, imo crucifixerint ipsum.

Peccata. Populus contemsit signa Dei et manifesta miracula, non credidit Prophetis aut verbis Christi, interfecit Christum. Haec peccata non iudicat ratio, et tamen omnes sumus rei. Iam hoc tempore quam horribiliter contradicitur verbo Dei? Interficiuntur sancti, et multi consentiunt, etsi manu non interficiunt. Hi omnes sciant se sic reos esse, sicut hic Petrus dicit: Sed liberantur per nomen Iesu credentes.

Psalm. 16.: Conserva me. Deus. Argumentum Psalmi initio recitetur, Psalmum principaliter esse vaticinium de Christo passuro et resuscitando, et est insertum discrimen verae Ecclesiae, et synagogae persequentis Christum, titulo Ecclesiae Dei.

Sed dicat aliquis, quare loquitur in prima persona, Conserva me, quasi de se ipso David loqueretur? Respondeo, peculiariter loquitur de Christo, et verba sic intelligenda sunt, quod Christus ipse loquatur, sicut et Psal. 22.: Deus Deus meus, quare me dereliquisti? Et Psal. 50.: Expectans expectavi etc. Et tamen in Christo etiam postea membra complectitur, quae scit propter Christum resuscitanda esse, qui resurgit primus, ut sit autor resurrectionis et vitae aeternae omnib. membris.

Quare sicut de Christo dicitur, eum non mansurum in morte, sed resurrecturum esse divina potentia, ita significatur de omnibus membris, quod eorum corpora sint revictura. Ita in aliis Psalmis, cum principaliter vaticinetur de Christo, tamen propter effectum, qui ad membra pertinet, Psalmi etiam ad membra accommodantur, sed tamen prudenter considerandum est, quae proprie Christo soli tribuantur, ut in hoc Psalmo de merito et appellatione passionis Filii Dei, quod sit victima et sacrificium pro aliis, quod de sanctorum afflictionibus non dicitur, quae etsi fiunt sacrificia propter Christum fide, id est, cultus Deo accepti, tamen non merentur ipsis aut aliis remissionem peccatorum. Item de Christo solo etiam haec verba dicuntur: Non dabis sanctum tuum videre corruptionem, ut hic Petrus exponit: Caro eius non vidit corruptionem, ut David, cuius sepulcrum adhuc apud nos est.

Habet Psalmus utilissimam doctrinam. Est testimonium de resurrectione, et nos ipsos confirmare debet, in petitione et expectatione vitae aeternae.

Item discrimen Ecclesiae docet, quae sit vera Ecclesia, et confirmat nos, ne moveamur specie et autoritate falsae Ecclesiae. Docet item, ut curemus esse membra verae Ecclesiae, et fugiamus falsam Ecclesiam, non faciamus cum ea conciliationes, quae eorum abusus confirmant.

Non recipiam, inquit, libationes eorum, nec sumam nomina eorum in labiis meis. Hic Christus reiicit omnes Missas impiorum, et omnes cultus, damnat eorum Ecclesiam, dicit se nolle eam nominare, id est, nolle vocare eam Ecclesiam suam, nolle pro ea orare.

Nihil potest tristius et horribilius dici. Ideo simus cauti, ne stabiliamus eorum impietates.

Postremo, totus Psalmus est tanquam promissio, quod Deus velit membra Ecclesiae suae exaudire et liberare a morte aeterna. Ita nos quoque recitemus hunc Psalmum, et adglutinemus nos tanquam membra capiti Christo, qui est primogenitus ex mortuis.

Sunt autem quatuor membra Psalmi. 1. Petitio Christi ut servetur, cum expositione Passionis. 2. Applicatio passionis, et repudiatio falsorum cultuum impii coetus. 3. Narratio de resurrectione. 4. Finis resurrectionis, ut Ecclesia collecta, vere agnoscat Deum, et celebret in vita aeterna.

Primus versus est, invocatio et propositio petens liberationem, et addit causam: Quia spero in te, et te Deum meum invoco. Nam hoc significat, quod ait: Dixi Domino, Deus meus es tu, id est, te unum invoco, et statuo esse omnipotentem, liberatorem ex morte, et quidem propitium mihi, volentem exaudire, et salvare confugientes ad te, Hunc tibi honorem tribui vis, quod velis salvare, iuxta tuas promissiones, confugientes ad te.

Querela et narratio passionis, Bonum meum non propter te, seu, non mihi bene propter te, id est, sum in afflictionibus, et videor etiam a te desertus, sicut clamitat in Psalmo: Deus Deus meus, quare me dereliquisti? Sed clarius est quod dicit: Affligor propter Te, iuxta illud: Propter te mactamur tota die.

Describitur ergo hoc versu, quae sit causa passionis Christi. Propter te patior, id est, propter tuum arcanum consilium de restituendo genere humano, quod voluisti me fieri victimam. Huic tuae voluntati obtempero, et sustineo horrendas poenas, non propter aliqua mea delicta. Quare cum sis Deus meus, et velis me servare, et colligere tibi aliquam Ecclesiam aeternam, ne sinas me in his aerumnis succumbere, sed confirma et sustenta, et libera me.

Sanctis qui sunt in terra, quasi dicat, Ad hos pertinet haec mea passio, Estque haec applicatio pro Ecclesia, sicut Christus ipse ante passionem suis verbis applicavit: Rogo pro eis, non pro eis tantum, sed pro omnibus qui credituri sunt per verbum eorum. Pater sanctifica eos in veritate, sermo tuus est veritas. O dulcem consolationem, hic ostendit Filius Dei se esse pontificem nostrum, et interpellatorem apud Deum. Ita hic applicat: Mea passio servit sanctis et honorandis in terra, his est profutura ad salutem, qui sunt sancti, id est, Deo dicati, Deum invocantes, agnoscentes, colentes, Hi sunt, qui meum Evangelium amplectuntur, hos iudico sanctos et gloriosos, pro his me offero, sicut alias inquit: Ego pro eis sanctifico meipsum, his applico meum sacrificium, hos amo et complector, et pro his rogo. Ita hic declarandum est vocabulum, Sancti.

Estque hic ipse articulus in symbolo: Credo Ecclesiam catholicam sanctam, id est, dicatam Deo, vere agnoscentem, colentem et celebrantem Deum, in fide et confessione Filii Dei. Haec etiam est honoranda et gloriosa, quia Deus vicissim eam honore afficit, tribuit ei gloriam, scilicet Spiritum sanctum, et per Spiritum sanctum lucem, iusticiam et vitam sempiternam. Brevis est versiculus, sed pulcerrima descriptio Ecclesiae: et hinc sequitur antithesis, quam mox adiungit. Alii non sunt sancti, id est, non sunt dicati Deo, non agnoscentes Deum, non colentes, nec sunt honorandi, id est, carent gloria Dei, non sunt ornati a Deo luce, sapientia, iusticia, vita aeterna.

Multiplicata sunt idola illorum, post quae festinant. Dixit se passum esse pro vera Ecclesia. Hanc nunc discernit ab impiis, qui nolunt verum Deum cognoscere, et persequuntur Christum et patrem. Tradit igitur discrimen falsae et verae Ecclesiae. Sicut autem in descriptione verae Ecclesiae duo bona nominavit, sanctitatem et gloriam: ita in descriptione falsae Ecclesiae nominat duplex malum. Malum culpae, id est, peccata, et malum poenae, videlicet, reiectionem et damnationem.
