Peccata sunt, falsa Ecclesia excogitat sibi idola, imo multa idola comminiscitur, quaerit alium Deum, et ad hunc festinat, huic confidit, hunc celebrat. Quid est autem idolum colere, aut alium Deum? Multiplex est idololatria. Primum sunt idololatrae, qui hoc fingunt esse Deum, quod non est Deus, sicut Ethnici statuas suas, Iovem, Martem, Iunonem, sic etiam Papistae sanctos putant esse Deos, invocant eos tanquam sint omnipotentes, tanquam videant motus omnium cordium. Haec adhuc est manifesta idololatria: et ad hunc gradum pertinent Athei seu Epicurei blasphemi, qui sentiunt prorsus nihil esse Deum, aut non curare humana dicunt, quales sunt plurimi Pontifices et Canonici, et alii Epicurei, qui cogitant Evangelium esse fabulam. Pertinent etiam huc, qui negant Christum esse Deum, ut Iudaei et Ariani negant Filium Dei crucifixum et resuscitatum, esse Deum. Hi omnes non colunt et invocant verum Deum, imo nullum Deum habent, quia hunc solum et unicum Deum non norunt nec invocant, qui est pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, de quo dixit: Hic est Filius meus dilectus, quo delector, Hunc audite. Sic vult agnosci et invocari, sicut se ipse patefecit, quod sit pater huius Filii, qui est eius coaeterna imago, et quod propter hunc velit credentes et invocantes recipere, et dare vitam aeternam. Sicut Iohan. 17. dicitur: Haec est vita aeterna, ut cognoscant te solum esse verum Deum, et quem misisti Iesum, esse Christum.

Secundus gradus est obscurior, sed superiori cognatus. Idololatria est colere Deum sine verbo ipsius, excogitatis propriis cultibus, et confidere his cultibus, quod propter eos Deus exaudiat et benefaciat. Sicut olim Iudaei excogitabant varios cultus, et fiduciam horum cultuum habebant: ita nunc Papistae colunt Deum, cultu Missae, votis, Monachatu. Hae res, Missa, Monachatus, sunt vera idola, quia scriptum est: Frustra colunt me mandatis hominum. Item, honos qui debetur Christo, scilicet, fiducia mediatoris, transfertur in Missam, in vota, in mortuos sanctos, et similes res. De talibus cultibus concionatur Ieremias 7.: Haec est gens quae non audivit vocem Domini Dei sui, neque recepit disciplinam, periit fides, et ablata est de ore eorum, dedicaverunt excelsa Tophet. Dicit sacella passim condidisse, instituisse cultus sine mandato Dei, sicut tunc etiam liberos immolabant et interficiebant.

Et sicut in mundo manent alia peccata contra secundam tabulam, ita multo magis manent omnibus aetatibus, omnibus temporibus peccata contra primam tabulam. Nam diabolus maxime conatur homines avertere a Deo, falsis opinionibus et cultibus.

Synagoga tempore Christi non habebat statuas, et tamen erat idololatrica, negabat Christum esse Filium Dei, et falsa fiducia servabat ceremonias, partim traditas in lege, partim excogitatas ab hominibus. Hi cultus eorum erant idola, quibus confidebant ignorantes Evangelium, Christum et veram invocationem, quae fit fiducia misericordiae promissae propter Christum.

Iam hoc tempore multo maior est idololatria, Papistae persequuntur Evangelium et vocem Christi, negant Christum esse mediatorem, et finxerunt sibi suos cultus falsos, Missam, Monachatus, satisfactionem, invocationem sanctorum. Haec omnia praedicant esse iusticiam, merita remissionis peccatorum, et applicant aliis.

Haec sunt idololatrica, quia sunt contumeliosa in Christum, item, sunt recepta sine verbo Dei. Item fiducia quae Deo debetur, collocatur in has res.

Ideo haec vere sunt idola, de quibus hic dicit: Post haec festinant, significans magnam esse multitudinem, magnos concursus, magnum et ardens studium impiorum et idololatricorum cultuum in mundo, ut nunc etiam videmus. Quantum est Missarum, quantum Monachatuum, quam varii cultus Sanctorum? quanta est veneratio talium rerum, quantis sumtibus Missae, monasteria et templa constant.

In summa, Papistae colunt Deum suum Maozim auro et argento, sicut Daniel inquit. Sequitur altera pars de poena.

Nec recipiam libationes eorum de sanguine.

Nec memor ero nominum eorum labiis meis.

Haec est horribilis reiectio omnium idololatrarum persequentium Christum, quicunque sunt, Iudaei aut Papistae. Aperte negat eos esse Ecclesiam Dei, negat eos habere sacrificia, negat Christus se velle pro illis orare, reiicit et damnat totum illud agmen idololatricum, sed mundus non intelligit hanc damnationem, imo quia Pontifices, Episcopi, Sacerdotes, Monachi, Reges, Principes tribuunt sibi titulum Ecclesiae: item, quia gloriantur Episcopi de ordinaria successione, hos veneratur, putat esse veram Ecclesiam, cum sit persecutrix Christi et idololatrica.

Quid contra haec dicendum est?

Primum conscientia confirmanda est, ne moveamur titulo, autoritate, multitudine, ut illos coetus Episcoporum putemus esse Ecclesiam, aut propter eos deficiamus a verbo Dei, sed sciamus aliam esse Ecclesiam veram sanctorum, scilicet, qui verbum Dei amplectuntur, et recte docent. Huius verae Ecclesiae nos membra esse sciamus, etiam si sumus abiecti extra illas congregationes Pontificum et Episcoporum, sicut Christus inquit: Eiicient vos extra synagogas.

Difficile est sustinere hunc titulum, quod non simus membra Ecclesiae, sed opponamus has consolationes. Hic dicit Christus, persecutores non esse Ecclesiam.

Et Paulus inquit: Si angelus de coelo aliud Evangelium praedicet, anathema sit. Hic Paulus egregie nos consolatur, et enarrat hanc vocem Psalmi: Non ero memor eorum.

Cum enim vocat anathemata, significat persecutores Christi, reiectos et damnatos esse a Deo. Ergo non sunt Ecclesia.

Secundo discas, omnes eorum cultus, Missas, Monachatus, satisfactiones, cultus sanctorum, esse damnatos cultus, et fugiendos. Non relinques me in inferno.

Tertia pars Psalmi est enarratio de liberatione ex morte, et resurrectione.

Non dabis sanctum tuum videre corruptionem, id est, ne quidem caro mea delebitur, sed ostendis mihi vias vitae, id est, vivificas, et resuscitas ex morte, etiam corpus.

Sed hic de Christo peculiariter dicitur illud: Non videbo corruptionem. Nam reliquorum sanctorum corpora, etiamsi non manent in perpetua corruptione, sed propter Christum resuscitabuntur, tamen prius dissipantur in aerem, sicut dicitur: Omnes immutabimur.

Sed Christi caro, etiamsi in sepulcro quieverit, tamen non potuit corrumpi, quia ne in morte quidem divina natura a corpore eius discessit, quare oportuit statim incorruptum, seu integrum resuscitari, ut revivisceret totus, etiam corpore, quod tamen transfodi in cruce, et expirare, ac sepeliri oportuit, ut sciretur vere mortuum. Sic Petrus haec verba enarrat: Quem Deus suscitavit, solutis doloribus mortis, iuxta quod impossibile erat teneri eum ab illa.

Reliqui versus Psalmi de fine et effectu rursus concionantur. Ideo sustineo passionem et mortem, ut resuscitatus colligam aeternam Ecclesiam, quae fruatur perpetuo conspectu et consuetudine tua, cum uberrima laetitia et aeterno gaudio.

Ultima pars concionis Petri est applicatio beneficii Christi. Sed prius accusat auditorum peccata, et concionatur de poenitentia. Postea addit de remissione peccatorum, hanc dicit fide propter Christum contingere credentibus, et simul donari Spiritum sanctum, et haec beneficia ita nobis applicari, si audientes Evangelii vocem de Christo, credamus, et baptizemur in nomine Christi.

De Coena Domini, 1.

Corinth. 11. Ego accepi a Domino, quod et tradidi vobis, quoniam Dominus Iesus in qua nocte tradebatur, accepit panem, et gratias agens, fregit, et dixit: Accipite et manducate, hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis tradetur: hoc facite in meam commemorationem.

Similiter et calicem, postquam coenavit, dicens: Hic calix novum testamentum est in meo sanguine. Hoc facite quotiescunque bibetis in meam commemorationem. Quotiescunque enim manducabitis panem hunc, et calicem bibetis, mortem Domini annunciabitis donec veniat. Itaque quicunque manducaverit panem hunc, et biberit calicem Domini indigne, reus erit corporis et sanguinis Domini. Probet autem seipsum homo, et sic de pane edat, et de calice bibat. Qui enim manducat et bibit indigne, iudicium sibi manducat et bibit, non diiudicans corpus Domini. Ideo inter vos multi infirmi et imbecilles et dormiunt multi. Quod si nosipsos diiudicaremus, non utique diiudicaremur. Dum iudicamur autem, a Domino corripimur, ut non cum hoc mundo damnemur.

Gravis comminatio est, in qua Paulus dupliciter puniri ait abusum sacramenti, ira Dei et corporalibus poenis. Sic enim ait: Reus erit corporis et sanguinis Domini. Item: Iudicium sibi manducat.

Accersit sibi poenam manducando duplicem, scilicet perpetuam, et calamitates huius vitae. Ideo, inquit, inter vos multi sunt aegroti, et multi moriuntur.

Erant adhuc non maximi abusus, Nondum tanti erant, quanti nunc sunt. Sacrificuli impii, impuri, celebrant Missas, vendunt, partem sacramenti populo adimunt, non docent de pio usu. Populus accedit, ignarus ad quid sit utendum sacramento, nihil audivit de doctrina fidei, putat hoc opere se mereri remissionem peccatorum. Circumgestatur pars sacramenti, spectatur, et adoratur, et dantur indulgentiae spectantibus, ut confirmetur vana fiducia spectationis, quod sit opus meritorium etc.

Hi et alii multi abusus horrendi, quibus prophanatur hoc sacramentum postrema mundi aetate, non leves poenas merentur, bella, dissidia et alias publicas calamitates. Credo etiam Turcicos successus praecipue permitti a Deo, propter huius sacramenti prophanationem multiplicem, quam semper pii in Ecclesia deploraverunt.

Dicunt S. Antonium habuisse visionem de postremo tempore Ecclesiae, ubi inter caetera est imago, quod viderit stantes porcos ad aras, et celebrare Missas. An non respondet res ipsa huic visioni? Postrema aetas mundi habet Episcopos, Canonicos, Sacrificulos, Monachos, qui Missam in quaestum contulerunt, et ut porci ventri serviunt, propter ventrem et opes celebrant.

Dicitur et S. Brigittae species Christi apparuisse, flagris lacerati et cruore stillantis, exterrita Brigitta, interrogavit, quid significaret haec species? respondit visio, Christum sic lacerari abusu Missarum. Hae historiae quoquo modo se habent, tamen significant sanctos deplorasse abusum sacramenti, etiamsi fortassis tecte hoc significarunt talibus historiis, et non licuit eis aperte dicere quod cupiebant.

Haec sum praefatus, ut cogitetur de vero usu sacramenti et fugiantur abusus. Vocatur autem verus usus tantum is, qui est in verbo Dei traditus. Abusus est omnis pompa extra verbum Dei.

I. Dicam igitur primum pauca de vero usu Sacramenti. Multi de sacramentis, ut de Baptismo et Coena Domini habent civiles et humanas opiniones, cogitant hos ritus institutos esse, tantum ut coram hominibus discernant eos qui vocantur Christiani a Iudaeis et aliis gentibus, sicut cuculli discernunt Monachos a caeteris, aut putant coenam Domini esse signum mutuae benevolentiae, quia convivia apud omnes gentes sunt signa amicitiae.

Hae sunt humanae cogitationes, quae non recte de sacramentis iudicant. II. Papistae aliam habent imaginationem, quod sint opera per quae meremur nobis et aliis remissionem peccatorum.

Haec opinio etiam est ethnica, sic de ceremoniis suis sentiebant Ethnici. III. Quis est igitur verus usus? Dicam breviter: Sacramenta sunt signa, non tantum discernentia Christianos coram hominibus, sed multo magis signa voluntatis Dei erga nos, videlicet, promissae gratiae. Deus ab initio, cum dedit promissionem Abrahae, addidit signum. Sic cum

niones, cogitant hos ritus institutos esse, tantum ut coram hominibus discernant eos qui vocantur Christiani a Iudaeis et aliis gentibus, sicut cuculli discernuunt Monachos a caeteris, aut putant coenam Domini esse signum mutuae benevolentiae, quia convivia apud omnes gentes sunt signa amicitiae. Hae sunt humanae cogitationes, quae non recte de sacramentis iudicant.

II. Papistae aliam habent imaginationem, quod sint opera per quae meremur nobis et aliis remissionem peccatorum. Haec opinio etiam est ethnica, sic de ceremoniis suis sentiebant Ethnici.

III. Quis est igitur verus usus? Dicam breviter: Sacramenta sunt signa, non tantum discernentia Christianos coram hominibus, sed multo magis signa voluntatis Dei erga nos, videlicet, promissae gratiae.

Deus ab initio, cum dedit promissionem Abrahae, addidit signum. Sic cum dedit verbum Mosi, addidit signa quaedam, sic cum Evangelium sparsit inter gentes, addidit signa, Baptismum et Coenam Domini: quia voluntas Dei recipientis nos, non potest cognosci, nisi per suum verbum, et signa ab ipso tradita. Vult enim addere signa verbo, ut verbum sit illustrius.

Et rem eandem significant verbum et sacramentum, sicut Augustinus inquit: Sacramentum est verbum visibile, id est, res eadem significatur voce, et gestu. Vox auribus, gestus oculis percipitur. Ut in Baptismo, verbis datur remissio peccatorum, gestu fit ablutio. Sic de coena Domini, verbis admonemur Christum pro nobis esse passum, ipsius sanguinem pro nobis fusum. Gestus idem admonet, nos fieri membra corporis Christi, et nobis dari sanguinem, quo abluti sumus.

IIII. Quomodo igitur utendum est? Sicut docet Christus: Accipite, manducate, bibite, facite ad mei recordationem. Nec est cogitandum, quod sit tantum civile spectaculum, nec cogitandum est, quod hoc opere merearis remissionem peccatorum, sed scire debes, quod sit res proposita, quae admoneat te de promissione Evangelii, et passione Christi, et quod fide propter Christum accipias remissionem, non propter hanc tuam sumtionem, sed haec sumtio est testimonium, quod Christus velit tibi et singulis applicari suum beneficium. Cum sumis, ideo sumes, cogites: Ecce ad te pertinet beneficium Christi. Id testatur hac ceremonia, in qua se tibi applicat.

V. Illi igitur sunt idonei ad hoc Sacramentum, qui agunt poenitentiam (sicut hic dicitur: Si nos iudicaremus, non iudicaremur a Domino) et agentes poenitentiam, credunt sibi ignosci propter Christum. Haec fides exuscitatur, cum hoc testimonium cogitamus, quod velit Christus singulis applicari suum beneficium.

Magna igitur consolatio est in hac sumtione. Scias sumtionem institutam esse, ut fides excitetur, et singuli credamus ad nos ipsos pertinere beneficium Christi.

Hic est igitur verus usus, cum agentes poenitentiam hac fide sumimus, et nos consolamur, ac rursus gratias agimus Deo pro donato Filio, pro data salute.

Haec est recordatio, de qua Christus dicit: Facite ad mei recordationem.

Significat enim recordatio, non historiae tantum cogitationem, sed fidem et gratiarum actionem, Fides accipit beneficium, Gratiarum actio vicissim praedicat Deum. Et semper cum hac ceremonia debebat fieri praedicatio. Sic etiam vetus Ecclesia hunc morem servabat, quae nullas habuit privatas Missas.

Exposui verum usum, scilicet, sumtionem agentis poenitentiam, et credentis sibi remitti peccata propter Christum, et hac sumtione se admonentis, quod Evangelium ad singulos pertineat. In hoc vero usu scimus sacramentum esse, et dari corpus et sanguinem Christi.

De alio usu sine sumtione, scilicet de circumgestatione, nihil dicit scriptura: debet autem in sacramentis esse certitudo. Ideo discamus recte uti sacramento, et in vero usu exercere fidem, et alios abusus extra verbum fugiamus: nec dubitemus, Deus puniet hos ingentes abusus huius sacramenti. Et timeo Turcam esse flagellum praecipue ad hos abusus puniendos. Sed nos oremus Deum, ut mitiget poenas propter suam Ecclesiam et institutionem puericiae, ad suam laudem parcat nobis, sicut Ninivitis pepercit. Sed nos etiam agamus poenitentiam, ut Ninivitae. Deus propter Filium suum Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum misereatur nostri, et det nobis Spiritum sanctum suum.

## 5:4 Sermons on Matthew
Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the earth.

Meek, that is, not greedy for vengeance, nor harming others out of a desire for private vengeance, just as very many most pernicious wars are stirred up on account of the desire for vengeance. On the contrary, David is gentle or meek, that is, not greedy for vengeance, since he could often have killed Saul, and, speaking civilly, he would have had the right to kill the enemy, yet he never wished to kill him, lest, clearly, he be the author of a new example or scandal of seizing dominion among the people of God, if a private person or subject were said to have killed the ordinary king. Thus the example of Joseph, the most meek Patriarch, also depicts this whole doctrine.

But since the desire for vengeance is a most sharp impulse and a huge fire in the minds of men, we must resist this affection with greater contention, fortified by the word and divine aid, according to the command of Paul, Rom. 12: Do not avenge yourselves. And private vengeance is severely prohibited.

Therefore it is manifest that individuals, as often as they are inflamed with anger, burning with hatreds and malevolence unjustly, like Cain, ought to lay aside these affections clinging against their conscience, and not give way to anger and the desire for vengeance, according to the maxim which exists in the Epistle of John: He who pursues his brother with hatred is a murderer. Furthermore, even when you are justly angry, provoked by true causes, you still ought to restrain the private desire for vengeance. Because God has ordained an order, that there be laws, judges, and governments or magistrates; to these he has subjected the human race, and to these he wishes you to flee, to seek defense, protection, and the execution of punishments, and in the meantime to yield vengeance to God, to the laws, and to the judges with a true spirit, and not to nourish private hatred.

Therefore, a promise is added, which consoles those unjustly oppressed: Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the earth. Which promise is indeed understood more clearly when the antithesis is considered, for it is opposed to human judgments. Kings, Princes, and private persons or men of lower orders think that they will obtain power, empires, dignities, that they will have successes, glory, and increments of fortune, if they appear formidable by the bitterness of vengeance, if they press and trample upon others. But on the contrary, Christ promises to those who do not indulge in private vengeance preservation even on earth, so that when tyrants are destroyed, they may finally be the ones to rule.

Examples: as David is raised to the pinnacle of the kingdom, however atrociously Saul and the other impious enemies raged. Jacob is preserved and covered divinely, even though he is forced for some time to flee the cruelty of his brother Esau. Joseph becomes lord of all his brothers, the event responding to his dreams, which his brothers strove to hinder with all their might. Indeed, he is set over and commands even his master and his master's wife, who had seen to it that he was thrown into prison. David remains lord, and retains the royal place above all Princes and nobles of the kingdom, although most of those conspiring strove to snatch the kingdom away by force.

Latin:

Beati mites, quia possidebunt terram.

Mites, id est, non cupidi vindictae, nec laedentes alios cupiditate privatae vindictae, sicut plurima perniciosissima bella moventur propter cupiditatem vindictae. E contrario David est mansuetus seu mitis, id est, non cupidus vindictae, cum saepe posset Saulem interficere, et civiliter loquendo, haberet ius interimendi hostem, tamen nunquam voluit occidere, ne videlicet auctor esset novi exempli seu scandali rapiendae dominationis in populo Dei, si privatus vel subditus diceretur interfecisse regem ordinarium. Sic exemplum Iosephi mitissimi Patriarchae etiam pingit hanc totam doctrinam.

Cum autem acerrimus impetus et ingens incendium sit in animis hominum cupiditas vindictae, eo maiore contentione huic affectui repugnemus, muniti verbo et auxilio divino, iuxta praeceptum Pauli Rom. 12.: Non vindicantes vosmetipsi. Estque vindicta privata severe prohibita.

Ergo manifestum est singulos quotiescunque incenduntur ira, ardento odiis et malevolentia iniuste, sicut Cain, debere hos affectus contra conscientiam haerentes deponere, nec irae et cupiditati vindictae morem gerere, secundum gnomen quae extat in Iohannis Epistola: Qui odio persequitur fratrem suum, est homicida. Praeterea, etiam cum veris causis lacessitus iuste irasceris, tamen debes cohibere privatam cupiditatem vindictae. Quia Deus sanxit ordinem, ut sint leges, iudices et regimina seu magistratus, his subiecit genus humanum, ad hos vult confugere, petere defensionem, praesidium et executionem poenarum, ac interim te Deo, legibus ac iudicibus vero animo cedere vindictam, nec alere privatum odium.

Adiungitur itaque promissio, quae consolatur iniuste oppressos: Beati mites, quia possidebunt terram. Quae quidem promissio clarius intelligitur considerata antithesi, est enim opposita humanis iudiciis. Reges, Principes et privati seu inferiorum ordinum homines cogitant, se consecuturos potentiam, imperia, dignitates, habituros successus, gloriam, et incrementa fortunarum, si formidabiles videantur acerbitate vindictae, si premant et conculcent alios. At contra Christus promittit non indulgentibus privatae vindictae conservationem etiam in terra, ita ut deletis tyrannis illi tandem sint dominaturi.

Exempla, ut David evehitur ad fastigium regni, quantumvis atrociter saeviente Saule et caeteris hostibus impiis. Iacob servatur et tegitur divinitus, etiamsi cogitur aliquandiu fugere saevitiam fratris Esau. Ioseph fit dominus omnium suorum fratrum, respondente eventu suis somniis, quem fratres moliebantur omnibus viribus impedire. Imo praeficitur ac imperat etiam hero suo et herili coniugi, qui curaverunt eum conici in carcerem. David manet dominus, et retinet regium locum supra omnes Principes ac proceres regni, quamvis plerique conspirantes conarentur vi oppresso regnum eripere.

## 5:6 Sermons on Matthew
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied.

To hunger and thirst for righteousness is to be truly affected by grief and to be anguished on account of one's own infirmity, uncleanness, stains, lapses, and sins, and by faith to seek from God remission, consolation, and salutary amendment, as David, Manasseh, Peter, the thief on the cross, after they were dismayed by the recognition of the wrath of God against their sins, and amending themselves, truly hunger and thirst for righteousness, they experience abundant and effective consolation, just as these sayings promise: He has filled the hungry with good things, and the rich he has sent away empty.

Also Isaiah 66: Where will the Lord dwell? In a contrite and troubled spirit.

Then these also hunger and thirst for righteousness, who are truly tormented by grief and zeal on account of the confusion of heavenly doctrine in the Church, on account of the weakening of the truth and impious corruptions, because they see very many teaching perversely, confirming and establishing idols, inventing new errors, etc., and praying with groans that God may aid the propagation of His truth and heal the wounds of the Church, which has been extricated from errors.

Thus John the Evangelist at that time endured sharp pains when Hebion and Cherinthus spread an impious and blasphemous dogma, detracting from the divine nature of Christ. But Irenaeus writes of Polycarp that he was accustomed often to deplore with true groans that, not long before he had heard the horrendous blasphemies of Marcion, he had been called by God from the course of this life. Whoever, therefore, with a true movement of the heart cry out to God, groaning and mourning, so that the truth may not be weakened and oppressed, their prayers are by no means in vain.

Thus Daniel, with a great movement, prays for the restoration of the Church and the rebuilding of the temple of Jerusalem. And in Ezekiel 9, God forbids the angel from killing those who groan on account of the idols and abominations in Judah. Likewise, 3 Kings 19, a most beautiful example of true and ardent zeal is proposed in Elijah, hungering and thirsting for righteousness, when, groaning with most bitter complaints, he cries out: I have been very zealous for the Lord God of hosts, because the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, have thrown down thine altars, and have slain thy prophets with the sword, and I alone am left, and they seek my life to take it away.

Latin:

Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt iusticiam, quia saturabuntur.

Esurire et sitire iusticiam, est vero dolore affici et angi propter propriam infirmitatem, immunditiem, labes, lapsus atque peccata, et fide a Deo petere remissionem, consolationem ac salutarem emendationem, ut David, Manasse, Petrus, latro in cruce, postquam consternati agnitione irae Dei adversus sua peccata, et sese emendantes, vere esuriunt ac sitiunt iusticiam, experiuntur uberem et efficacem consolationem, quemadmodum pollicentur haec dicta: Esurientes implevit bonis, ac divites dimisit inanes.

Item Esaiae 66.: Ubi habitabit Dominus? In spiritu contrito et tribulato.

Deinde hi quoque esuriunt et sitiunt iusticiam, qui vero dolore et zelo excruciantur propter confusionem doctrinae coelestis in Ecclesia, propter veritatis labefactationem et impias corruptelas, quia vident plurimos perverse docere, confirmare et stabilire idola, comminisci novos errores etc. ac gementes orant, ut Deus adiuvet propagationem suae veritatis, et sanet vulnera Ecclesiae extricatae ex erroribus.

Sic Iohannes Evangelista tunc sustinuit acres dolores, cum Hebion et Cherinthus impium et blasphemum dogma sparserunt, detrahentes Christo divinam naturam. At de Polycarpo scribit Irenaeus, solitum saepe veris gemitibus deplorare, quod non multo ante, quam horrendas blasphemias Marcionis audivisset, a Deo ex huius vitae curriculo evocatus esset. Quicunque igitur vero motu cordis clamant ad Deum, gementes ac moerentes, ne labefactetur et opprimatur veritas, illorum preces nequaquam sunt irritae.

Ita Daniel ingenti motu precatur de restituenda Ecclesia et instauratione templi Ierosolymitani. Et Ezechiel. 9. vetat Deus ab angelo occidie eos, qui gemunt propter idola et abominationes in Iuda. Item 3. Reg. 19. proponitur exemplum pulcerrimum veri et ardentis zeli in Elia esuriente et sitiente iusticiam, quando gemens acerbissimis querelis clamitat: Zelo zelatus sum pro Domino Deo exercituum, quia dereliquerunt pactum tuum filii Israël, altaria tua destruxerunt, et Prophetas tuos occiderunt gladio, et solus relictus sum ego, cuius animam quaerunt ut auferant.

## 5:7 Sermons on Matthew
Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy. What does mercy differ from justice?

The justice of a judge is to punish according to the laws all who have offended, and indeed to execute the penalties for individual crimes according to the norm established by the laws. Thus God most severely, without any mitigation, punishes the devils according to this immutable order of severe justice.

Mercy, however, is a virtue which is affected by grief at another's unjust calamity, and helps those who are unjustly oppressed as much as it can; or even in a just calamity, it grieves for the lot of those who, although they have deserved punishment, yet were not the leaders and authors of the crimes, but were deceived, having fallen through error or weakness, and it strives to alleviate the miseries of such people for a probable reason. Thus God is merciful in receiving our first parents, Adam and Eve, whose fall, although it was most sad, yet they themselves did not, with proud contempt of God, knowingly and blasphemously pour out false persuasion to others, as the instigators of the devil, burning with horrible hatred of God. Therefore, God distinguishes by this distinction between fallen men and devils, because He exercises and executes severe justice rigidly without any mitigation against the blasphemous devils. But with an ineffable temperament and wonderful coupling of justice and mercy, He so spares men that He both declares His wrath in punishments and exercises mercy in the mitigation of punishments.

Let us know that this virtue has also been commanded and enjoined upon us: Be merciful, as your Father also is merciful.

First, we ought to be affected by the sense of the calamity of the innocent, just as at this very time very many innocent and pious men with miserable families wander, cast out from their little nests, to whom we ought to bring aid, to do good, and to alleviate miseries, each according to our means and vocation.

Secondly, we ought also to forgive the guilty, so that we remit something of the highest law and mitigate a just calamity, wherever the reason of duty and public office does not command us to execute punishments severely.

For the name of mercy is by no means to be attributed to excessive indulgence that confirms atrocious sins, as if a judge or some magistrate should wish to connive at enormous crimes, to spare murderers, thieves, and other such highwaymen, who, in the hope of impunity, proceed to disturb the common society.

Let the lightning of the divine voice from Deuteronomy be opposed to this: Thou shalt not spare him.

Mercy, however, has probable causes for clemency and the mitigation of punishment; it forgives those who have been deceived or seduced, and for whom there is not a vain hope of amendment.

But indulgence or leniency that connives at crimes is a confirmation of wickedness, murders, and other turpitudes.

Furthermore, to this mercy, which is attributed either to the guilty or to the innocent, as was said a little before, the Lord added a most ample and sweetest promise: Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy. Many sayings confirm the same, as Psalm 41: Blessed is he that considereth the poor and needy; in the evil day the Lord will deliver him, the Lord will preserve him and give him life, and will make him blessed on the earth, and will not deliver him into the will of his enemies; the Lord will help him upon his bed of sorrow.

You, O God, drive away all his diseases, and relieve all his pains. Likewise, Prov.

19: He who has pity on the poor, lends to the Lord, and He will repay him in return. And later, chapter 28: He who gives to the poor will not lack, but he who turns away his eyes will be stripped of his fortunes.

The Lord looked to the same thing when He says thus in Matthew 25: Come, you blessed of my Father, and possess the inheritance of the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry, and you gave me food, etc.

Likewise, 3 Kings 17. The most beautiful example of the widow of Zarephath is magnificently preached, to whom the reward of the mercy which she showed to the Prophet is returned in abundance, and God adorned not only her and her son with most generous rewards, but without doubt the whole town felt the rich fruit and compensation of her good deed.

Exception. But here it is necessary to know that mercy is to be exercised only toward those toward whom the heavenly and merciful Father was and still is, such as toward the unjustly oppressed, or even toward the guilty and those who have deserved ill, yet by no means toward blasphemers, nor toward the instigators and authors of crimes, such as are the devils and all persistent idolaters, blasphemers, and heretics, nor toward able-bodied beggars, impudent swindlers, greedy vagabonds, and impostors, such as wander about everywhere today.

We must not be moved or affected by the calamities of such people, nor help or do good to them, just as the following testimonies clearly command, 2 John 1: If anyone comes to you and does not bring this doctrine, do not receive him into your house, nor say greeting to him; for he who says to him, 'Greetings,' shares in his evil works.

Likewise, 2 Thess. 3: If anyone will not work, neither let him eat. For we have heard, etc.

Prov. 5: Do not give your honor to strangers, and your years to the cruel one. Luke 9: Be merciful, just as your heavenly Father is, etc.

He does not exercise mercy toward devils, persistent heretics, and blasphemers.

Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God. This particle speaks of chastity, Blessed are those who have a pure heart.

And here let us attentively and seriously consider all the precepts concerning chastity, so often repeated by God.

Let us also propose to ourselves the horrible examples of punishments.

Latin:

Beati misericordes, quia misericordiam consequentur.

Quid differt misericordia a iusticia? Iusticia iudicis est iuxta leges punire omnes qui deliquerunt, et quidem singulorum delictorum poenas exequi iuxta normam legibus constitutam. Ita Deus asperrime sine ulla mitigatione punit diabolos iuxta hunc immotum ordinem severae iusticiae.

Misericordia vero virtus est, quae afficitur dolore in aliena calamitate iniusta, et opitulatur iniuste oppressis, quantum potest: aut etiam in calamitate iusta dolet vicem eorum, qui etsi poenas meriti sunt, tamen non fuerunt duces et auctores scelerum, sed errore aut imbecillitate lapsi deceptive sunt, ac propter probabilem rationem talibus lenire miserias studet. Sic Deus est misericors in recipiendis primis parentibus Adamo et Eva, quorum lapsus etsi tristissimus fuit, tamen ipsi non superbo contemptu Dei scientes et blasphemi offuderunt aliis falsam persuasionem, ut impulsores diaboli ardentes horribili odio Dei. Propterea Deus hac distinctione discernit homines lapsos et diabolos, quod rigide sine ulla mitigatione severam iusticiam exercet et exequitur adversus blasphemos diabolos. At inenarrabili temperamento mirandaque copulatione iusticiae et misericordiae sic parcit hominibus, ut et iram declaret in poenis, et mitigatione poenarum misericordiam exerceat.

Hanc virtutem sciamus nobis quoque mandatam et praeceptam esse: Estote misericordes, sicut et Pater vester misericors est.

Primum debemus affici sensu calamitatis innocentum, sicut hoc ipso tempore plurimi homines innocentes ac pii cum miseris familiis vagantur eiecti ex suis nidulis, quibus opem ferre, benefacere ac miserias lenire singuli pro facultatibus et vocatione debemus.

Secundo, sontibus etiam debemus ignoscere, sic ut remittamus aliquid de summo iure, et mitigemus iustam calamitatem, ubicunque ratio muneris et officii publici non iubet severe poenas exequi.

Nam indulgentiae nimiae confirmanti atrocia peccata nequaquam misericordiae appellatio tribuenda est, ut si iudex aut magistratus aliquis velit connivere ad enormia delicta, parcere homicidis, furibus, et aliis id genus grassatoribus, impunitatis spe pergentibus turbare communem societatem.

Huic opponatur fulmen vocis divinae ex Deuteronomio: Non parces ei.

Misericordia vero probabiles habet causas clementiae et mitigatione poenae, ignoscit iis, qui decepti seu seducti sunt, et quibus non vana spes est emendationis.

Sed indulgentia seu lenitas connivens ad delicta, est confirmatio scelerum, caedium et aliarum turpitudinum.

Porro huic misericordiae, quae tribuitur vel sontibus vel innocentibus, quemadmodum paulo ante dictum est, Dominus addidit amplissimam et dulcissimam promissionem: Beati misericordes, quia misericordiam consequentur. Idem confirmant plurima dicta, ut Psalm. 41.: Beatus qui intelligit super egenum et pauperem, in die mala liberabit eum Dominus, Dominus servabit eum et vivificabit, et beatum faciet in terra, nec tradet eum voluntati inimicorum suorum, Dominus opitulabitur ei decumbenti.

Tu Deus depellis omnes eius morbos, et universos dolores levas. Item, Proverb. 19.: Qui miseretur inopis, mutuo dat Domino, is vicissim illi benefaciet. Et postea 28. cap.: Qui dat pauperi, non indigebit, qui vero avertit oculos suos, excutietur ex fortunis.

Eodem respexit Dominus, cum sic inquit Matthaei. 25.: Venite benedicti patris mei, ac possidete haereditatem regni vobis parati inde usque a conditione mundi.

Esurivi enim, et dedistis mihi cibos etc. Item tertio Regum 17.

Magnifice praedicatur pulcherrimum exemplum viduae Sareptanae, cui cumulate redditur merces misericordiae, quam Prophetae praestitit, nec solum ipsam et filium largissimis praemiis ornavit Deus, sed haud dubie totum oppidum sensit eius beneficii uberem fructum ac compensationem.

Exceptio.

At hic oportet scire, tantum erga illos exercendam esse misericordiam, erga quos pater coelestis et misericors fuit et adhuc est, ut erga iniuste oppressos, aut etiam erga sontes et male meritos, nequaquam tamen blasphemos, nec impulsores et autores scelerum tales, quales sunt diaboli et omnes pertinaces idolatrae, blasphemi et haeretici, nec erga validos mendicantes, impudentes stelliones, petaces errones ac impostores, quales passim hodie vagantur.

Talium calamitatibus non debemus moveri vel affici, nec ipsis subvenire vel benefacere, sicut sequentia testimonia clare praecipiunt, 2. Iohan. 1.: Si quis venit ad vos, et hanc doctrinam non affert, non recipite illum in aedes, nec salutem illi dicite, Qui enim dicit illi, Salve, communicat operibus eius malis.

Item 2. Thes. 3.: Si quis non vult laborare, non manducet.

Audivimus enim etc.

Proverb. 5.: Ne des alienis honorem tuum, et annos tuos crudeli.

Lucae 9.: Estote misericordes, sicut pater vester coelestis etc.

Is non exercet misericordiam erga diabolos, pertinaces haereticos et blasphemos.

## 5:8 Sermons on Matthew
What is chastity?

First, therefore, you should know that chastity is a virtue which avoids all commixtions and effusions of seed prohibited by the law of God, such as fornications, adulteries, incestuous habits, etc.

And let there be added to the consideration of these prohibitions the threats of most sad punishments, and let us not doubt that God is horribly angered by wandering lusts, and that the atrocious violation of this precept is punished with atrocious punishments in this mortal life, and then after this life with everlasting torments universally in all who do not do penance.

For in Leviticus 18, God says: All who have committed abominations of this kind, the land shall vomit out. Likewise, Hebrews 12: God will judge fornicators and adulterers.

Likewise, 1 Corinth. 6: Do not err, fornicators, adulterers, shall not possess the kingdom of God.

And therefore God sanctioned chastity so severely, so that it might be a distinguished and conspicuous virtue, discerning God from the devils and other unclean natures.

Here also propose to yourselves examples of horrible punishments.

Sodom burned because of incestuous lusts. And God Himself affirms that the Canaanites were destroyed because of incestuous lusts. Afterward, almost the entire tribe of Benjamin was destroyed because of the ravished wife of the Levite, Judges 20.

So that twenty-five thousand of the most wicked men were killed.

Likewise, David's adultery brought great calamities upon him and his kingdom.

Furthermore, let each one think and recall to memory ancient and recent histories, in which they will discern examples of punishments wandering through all nations in all times, but the chief and saddest punishment of impurity is that of which Paul says: That lusts are punished with blindness, according to the words of Paul, in Romans 1 and Ephesians 4.

Therefore, the sight and consideration of punishments should arouse and increase in us the fear of God.

But the sweet and ample promises should bend our minds to the love of chastity, just as it is added here: For they shall see God, that is, security, blindness, and fury accompany lusts, just as the citizens in Sodom, blinded and mad, brought destruction upon themselves.

Likewise, as Solomon, for the sake of the women he loved, fell into idolatry.

How many Kings and even Princes, outstanding in talent, authority, wisdom, and learning, do we read of

 disturbed in health and mind by shameful loves. Concerning whom Solomon says in Proverbs 6: The Lord abominates him who sows discord among brothers.

Numbers 25. Israel was staying in Shittim, and the people began to commit fornication with the daughters of Moab, who called them to their sacrifices. And they, eating and drinking, worshipped their idols, and Israel was initiated, that is, clung to Baal Peor.

In our own memory, the Bishop of Trier, and likewise the Margrave of Baden, was killed in his very bedchamber by a certain cobbler. Likewise, the Bishop of Worms, Dalburgius, excellent in erudition, and the Chancellor of Heidelberg, while entering a brothel at night, fell by accident into a wine cellar and perished miserably.

On the contrary: God adorns and accumulates the chaste with great light, wisdom, and excellence of gifts, as the example of Joseph testifies, concerning whose increase of gifts the text speaks: They shall see God. Likewise, to the Hebrews 12: Pursue sanctification, without which no one shall see God.

Latin:

Beati mundo corde, quia Deum videbunt.

Haec particula loquitur de castitate, Beati habentes cor castum.

Et hic attente ac serio cogitemus omnia praecepta de castitate, toties a Deo repetita.

Horribilia etiam poenarum exempla nobis proponamus. Quid est castitas? Primum igitur scias, castitatem esse virtutem, quae vitat omnes commixtiones et effusiones seminis prohibitas lege Dei, ut scortationes, adulteria, incestas consuetudines etc. Et adiungantur ad considerationem harum prohibitionum comminationes poenarum tristissimarum, nec dubitemus Deum horribiliter irasci vagis libidinibus, et atrocem violationem huius praecepti puniri cum atrocibus poenis in hac mortali vita, tum post hanc vitam sempiternis suppliciis universaliter in omnibus non agentibus poenitentiam.

Nam Levitici 18. dicit Deus: Omnes qui fecerint abominationes huiusmodi, terra evomet.

Item Ebraeos 12.: Scortatores et adulteros iudicabit Deus.

Item, 1. Corinth. 6.: Nolite errare, scortatores, adulteri, non possidebunt regnum Dei.

Ac ideo tam severe Deus sanxit castitatem, ut esset insignis et conspicua virtus, discernens Deum a diabolis et aliis immundis naturis.

Hic etiam vobis horribilium poenarum exempla proponite.

Sodoma conflagrarunt propter incestas libidines. Ac Deus ipse Cananaeos affirmat propter incestas libidines deletos esse.

Postea fere tota tribus Beniamin deleta est propter stupratam Levitae uxorem, Iudicum 20. Ita, ut interficerent viginti quinque millia hominum hellicosissimorum.

Item Davidis adulterium magnas ipsi et regno calamitates attulit.

Porro singuli cogitent ac memoria repetant historias veteres atque recentes, in quibus exempla cernent poenarum, per omnes gentes omnibus temporibus vagantium, sed praecipua et tristissima poena impuritatis est, de qua Paulus inquit: Coecitate puniri libidines, iuxta Pauli dicta, ad Romanis 1. et Ephesios 4.

Itaque conspectus et consideratio poenarum exuscitet et augeat in nobis timorem Dei. Promissiones vero dulces et amplae flectant animos ad amorem castitatis, sicut et hic additur: Quia Deum videbunt, hoc est, securitas, coecitas et furor comitantur libidines, quemadmodum cives ...in Sodomis excoecati et amentes accersebant sibi exitium.

Item, ut Salomon in gratiam mulierum quas amabat, ruit in idolatriam.

Quam multos praestantes ingeniis, autoritate, sapientia, eruditione Reges etiam atque Principes, legimus obscoenis amoribus de sanitate ac mente deturbant. De quibus Salomon Proverb. 6.: Eum qui serit discordias inter fratres abominatur Dominus.

Numeri 25. Commorabatur Israël in Setim, et coepit fornicari populus cum filiabus Moab, quae vocabant eos ad sacrificia sua. At illi comedentes ac bibentes adorabant idola earum, et initiatus est, seu, adhaesit Israël Baal Peor.

Sic nostra memoria Episcopus Trevirensis, idemque Marchio Badensis in ipso thalamo interfectus est a sutore quodam. Item Episcopus Wormatiensis, Dalburgius excellens eruditione, et Cancellarius Edelbergae, dum noctu ingreditur aedes meretricias, casu delapsus in cellam vinariam, misere periit.

E contrario: magna luce, sapientia, donorumque praestantia Deus ornat et cumulat castos, ut exemplum Iosephi testatur, de quibus donorum incrementis loquitur textus: Deum videbunt. Item, ad Ebraeos 12.: Sectamini sanctificationem, sine qua Deum nemo videbit.

## 5:9 Sermons on Matthew
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.

There are three kinds of men in every government.

The first kind is of the slothful, who are negligent and cease in their duty. Such was Sardanapalus in political government: in ecclesiastical government, Pope Leo, not caring for just and unjust things, nor performing their duty even moderately, but idle gluttons. The Prophets cry out against such, as Ezekiel 34: Woe to the shepherds who fed themselves; you ate the milk and covered yourselves with the wool, but you did not feed my flock. Likewise, Jeremiah chapter 48: Cursed is he who does the work of the Lord negligently. Likewise, Isaiah 5: Woe to you who rise early to pursue drunkenness, and drink until evening, so that you burn with wine, with the harp, lyre, timbrel, flute, and wine at your feasts, and you do not regard the work of the Lord, nor the works of his hands, that is, you do not consider the divine order.

The second kind is not slothful, but malevolent, envious, restless, pugnacious, armed with impudence and sophistry, which, through pride, ambition, envy, quarrelsomeness, or curiosity, and meddlesomeness, excites only contentions and discord. And such are many in all governments, as Marius and Catiline in Rome, and Arius, Eck, and Canisius in the Church, who seek only dissensions, distractions, and horrible tumults. Concerning whom Solomon says in Proverbs 6: The Lord abominates him who sows discord among brothers.

The third kind is the peaceful. And the peaceful are those who diligently perform the necessary labors proper to their own vocation, not greedy for quarrels, not seeking after contests, nor grasping at unjust discords, with gentleness [ἐπιεικείᾳ] and mildness tolerating the weaker members, judging dogmas in an orderly and correct manner, settling controversies in an orderly, gentle, and kind way, correcting the errors of those who can be healed, and not perplexingly involving or insidiously perverting business with calumnious sentences when called to judgment. They are not slothful, not malevolent, not seeking unnecessary quarrels, not meddlesome, not cruel to the weak, not rebuking with bitterness without order, not exercising cruelty upon those who can be healed, nor wishing to win with bitter, scurrilous, and contumelious words, especially not before they have been lovingly and orderly admonished or chastised.

Thus were the peacemakers in political government Scipio and Augustus, understanding and sedulously and faithfully performing the chief duties of their own office, which are just and necessary. And in the Church or ministry, Paul and other faithful teachers, as Jeremiah and the other Prophets.

Nor should the Sophists be considered peaceful, who with ambiguous words and double-talk wish to moderate and reconcile the controversies of religions, as the Synod of Sirmium did, which hoped that by this counsel the distinct Churches could be joined again if the word ὁμοούσιον [consubstantial] were removed from the Nicene Creed and the general word ὅμοιον [similar] were inserted. For this ambiguous formula, like a buskin fitting either foot, by no means removed the dissension, but increased the discords. Our age has seen not a few examples of such counsels and subversions, alas, as when the Augsburg Sphinx, which is called the INTERIM, was brought forth.

Opposed to the peacemakers in political government are tyrants, and in the Church, calumniators, devils, and sycophants. Tyrants seek and incite wars without just and necessary causes, just as at this very time the Roman Pontiff moves wars and excites tumults against an emperor who is desirous of peace and public tranquility. Likewise, such is the Turkish tyrant, etc.

Calumniators and sycophants seek logomachies or cavils and plausible sophisms to elude the simple truth, or to cunningly to deprave the counsels and deeds of others, as when the Papists clamor that we think and speak too little honorably of the saints, nay, that we confirm profanity and contempt for piety, under this pretext, that we do not approve of the invocation of dead men etc. Yet we speak of the saints and of divine actions or works in the hearts of the saints much more rightly, honorably, and splendidly than they do. Likewise, when we are burdened before foreign kings with this most impudent calumny, or rather manifest lie, that we loosen the bonds of marriage, discipline, etc. And there is no end or limit to the false accusations, sophistic depravations, and most poisonous calumnies.

Just as the text of Proverbs 6 says: God abominates those who sow and excite discord: so the Lord says here, as it were from the opposite, blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God, because the closest society and union with God is that for which Christ the Lord prays in John 17: That they may be one in us, as the Father in me, and I in the Father.

But the only-begotten Son of God is Son by nature, or by birth. We, however, are made sons by adoption, that is, as sons and heirs we are received into grace through faith in Christ, or the trust of this only-begotten Son given to us. But afterwards, when we are peacemakers, we are named children of God in this sense, as salutary organs through which God effects and promotes peace, as when teachers in the Church, by the ministry of the Apostle Paul writing to the Galatians, are brought back into concord and pious agreement. Or, when John the Evangelist, joining the churches in Asia, makes them consenting and concordant against Hebion and Cerinthus, so that henceforth the orthodox teachers confess and teach with one voice and sentiment that both natures are and remain in Christ, namely, the divine and the human.

Such peacemakers are children of God, in this understanding, that in them and through them He is efficacious. And let no alien interpretation be attached to these words: For they shall be called children of God, as if Paul or John become children of God through this their ministry of pacification, when they were already received into grace and made children by faith, but let it be understood that, having already received the remission of sins, when they are authors and promoters of peace and pious concord in their function and ministry, then they are also children of God, as salutary organs or instruments through which God effects and restores peace in the Churches. In this way, Emperor Constantine is a peacemaker, when, as if by throwing reins upon him, he restrains and coerces Licinius, so that he may not continue to exercise cruelty against the Christians. Likewise, afterwards, when he takes care in the Nicene Synod, having judged ecclesiastical controversies, that discords be healed and concord in doctrine be restored. For he is truly an organ of God in this office or duty of pacification, even though he was previously received into grace and is righteous before God by faith or trust in the Mediator.

For this text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God, speaks of the functions and ministries which follow in the righteous and pleasing, who have already been converted to God and justified or reconciled by faith apprehending Christ, the only-begotten Son of God. Such are named children of God in this place, that is, salutary organs of God. Which is a huge divine benefit and a singular honor.

Latin:

Beati pacifici, quia filii Dei vocabuntur.

Tria genera hominum sunt in omni gubernatione.

Primum genus est ignavorum, qui sunt negligentes, et cessant in officio suo. Qualis in regimine politico fuit Sardanapalus: in regimine ecclesiastico Leo Papa, non curantes iusta et iniusta, nec facientes mediocriter officium, sed ociosi helluones. De talibus clamitant Prophetae, ut Ezechiel 34.: Vae pastoribus qui pascebant semetipsos, lac comedebatis et lanis operiebamini, gregem vero meum non pascebatis. Item Ieremias cap. 48.: Maledictus qui facit opus Domini negligenter. Item Esaiae 5.: Vae qui surgitis mane ad ebrietatem sectandam, et potandum usque ad vesperam, ut vino aestuetis, cithara, lyra, tympanum, tibia, et vinum in conviviis vestris, et opus Domini non respicitis, nec opera manuum eius, id est, ordinem divinum consideratis.

Secundum genus est non ignavum, sed malevolum, lividum, inquietum, pugnax, armatum impudentia et sophistica, quod superbia, ambitione, invidentia, rixositate, aut curiositate, ac polypragmosyne tantum contentiones et discordias excitat. Et tales multi sunt in omnibus regiminibus, ut Romae Marius, Catilina, in Ecclesia Arius, Eccius, Canysius, qui tantum dissidia, distractiones et horribiles tumultus quaerunt. De quibus Salomon Proverb. 6.: Eum qui serit discordias inter fratres abominatur Dominus.

Tertium genus est pacificum. Suntque pacifici, diligenter facientes labores necessarios et proprios suae vocationi, non cupidi rixarum, non appetentes certaminum, nec captantes iniustas discordias, ἐπιεικείᾳ, et lenitate tolerantes infirmiora membra, ordine et recte diiudicantes dogmata, ordine, leniter ac benigne diremtis controversiis, corrigentes errata sanabilium, nec perplexe involventes aut insidiose depravantes negocia sententiis calumniosis vocati ad diiudicationem. Non ignavi, non malevoli, non quaerentes, non necessarias rixas, non polypragmonici, non saevi in imbecilles, non obiurgantes cum acerbitate sine ordine, non exercentes saeviciam in sanabiles, nec acerbe, scurriliter et contumeliose dictis volentes vincere, praesertim non prius amanter et ordine admonitos seu castigatos.

Ita fuerunt pacifici in gubernatione politica Scipio et Augustus, intelligentes ac sedulo fideliterque facientes proprii muneris officia praecipua, iusta et necessaria. Et in Ecclesia seu ministerio Paulus et alii fideles doctores, ut Ieremias et caeteri Prophetae.

Nec existimentur esse pacifici Sophistae, qui verbis ambiguis et flexiloquis conciliationibus moderari atque concordare volunt religionum controversias, ut fecit Synodus Syrmiensis, quae distinctas Ecclesias hoc consilio speravit rursus coniungi posse, si ex Symbolo Niceno eximeretur vox ὁμοούσιον et generale verbum ὅμοιον insereretur. Nam haec ambigua formula, et velut utrique pedi conveniens cothurnus, nequaquam sustulit dissidium, sed auxit discordias. Talium consiliorum et evertuum non pauca, proh dolor, aetas nostra vidit exempla, ut cum Sphynx Augustana, quae nominatur INTERIM, prolata est.

Pacificis opponuntur in regimine politico tyranni, in Ecclesia calumniatores, diaboli, sycophantae. Tyranni quaerunt et concitant bella sine causis iustis et necessariis, sicut hoc ipso tempore Romanus Pontifex movet bella, et tumultus excitat adversus imperatorem cupidum pacis et publicae tranquillitatis. Item qualis est Turcicus tyrannus, etc.

Calumniatores et sycophantae quaerunt logomachias seu cavillationes et sophismata plausibilia ad eludendam veritatem simplicem, aut ad veteratorie depravanda aliorum consilia et facta, ut cum Papistae clamitant, nos parum honorifice de sanctis et sentire et loqui, imo profanitatem et contemtum pietatis confirmare, hoc praetextu, quod non approbamus invocationem mortuorum hominum etc. Cum tamen de sanctis et actionibus seu operibus divinis in sanctorum cordibus multo loquamur rectius, honorificentius ac splendidius quam ipsi. Item, cum apud exteros reges praegravamur hac impudentissima calumnia, seu verius manifesto mendacio, quod laxemus vincula coniugii, disciplinae etc. Nec est finis aut modus falsarum criminationum, sophisticarum depravationum et venenatissimarum calumniarum.

Quemadmodum igitur textus Proverb. 6. inquit: Deum abominari serentes et excitantes discordias: ita Dominus hic dicit tanquam e regione, pacifici sunt filii Dei, quia proxima societas et copulatio cum Deo est illa, de qua precatur Christus Dominus Iohan. 17.: Ut sint unum in nobis, sicut pater in me, et ego in patre.

At Filius Dei unigenitus, est natura, seu, nativitate filius. Nos vero filii efficimur adoptione, hoc est, tanquam filii et haeredes in gratiam recipimur per fidem in Christum, seu fiducia huius unigeniti Filii nobis donati. Sed postea cum pacifici sumus, in hanc sententiam nominamur filii Dei, ut organa salutaria, per quae Deus efficit, et promovet pacem, ut, cum doctores in Ecclesia, ministerio Pauli Apostoli scribentis ad Galatas, reducuntur in concordiam et piam consensionem. Aut, cum Iohannes Evangelista Ecclesias in Asia coniungens consentientes efficit ac concordes adversus Hebionem et Cerinthum ita, ut deinceps doctores orthodoxi una voce ac sententia confiteantur, atque doceant in Christo utramque naturam esse et manere, divinam scilicet et humanam.

Huiusmodi pacificatores sunt filii Dei, hoc intellectu, quod in eis et per eos est efficax. Nec affingatur aliena interpretatio his verbis: Quia filii Dei vocabuntur, perinde ac si Paulus aut Iohannes fiant filii Dei per hoc suum ministerium pacificationis, cum prius in gratiam recepti ac filii factis sint fide, sed intelligantur, accepta iam remissione peccatorum, cum in sua functione ac ministerio pacis et concordiae piae sunt autores atque promotores, tunc etiam esse filii Dei, ut organa seu instrumenta salutaria, per quae Deus efficit, et restituit pacem in Ecclesiis. Ad hunc modum Constantinus imperator est pacificus, cum velut iniectis frenis reprimit atque coërcet Licinium, ne pergat exercere saevitiam adversus Christianos. Item, postea quando curat in Synodo Nicena, diiudicatis controversiis ecclesiasticis, sanari discordias et concordiam in doctrina restitui. Est enim vere Dei organum in hoc officio seu munere pacificationis, tametsi prius in gratiam receptus et coram Deo iustus sit fide seu fiducia mediatoris.

Nam hic textus: Beati pacifici, quia filii Dei vocabuntur, loquitur de functionibus et ministeriis, quae sequuntur in iustis ac placentibus, qui iam ad Deum conversi, et fide apprehendente Christum unigenitum Dei Filium iustificati seu reconciliati sunt. Tales hoc loco nominantur filii Dei, id est, organa Dei salutaria. Quod est ingens beneficium divinum et singulare decus.

## 5:10 Sermons on Matthew
Blessed are those who suffer persecution for righteousness' sake.

On the scandal of the cross.

First, it must be said that it is certain that the entire wisdom of human reason is harshly offended, perturbed, and stupefied, contemplating this eternal spectacle, namely, that the Church appears as a congregation burdened with miseries, dissipated and trampled or oppressed, and especially that the chief lights and excellent members of the Church are cruelly killed as if rejected by God, and as expiatory sacrifices or execrable scapegoats, like Abel, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Christ, Peter, John the Baptist.

Against this scandal, it is necessary that we be rightly forewarned and forearmed. And let us know entirely that only in the word of God propagated through the Fathers, Prophets, Christ, and the Apostles are the true causes shown why the Church is more harshly pressed and is subject to the cross in this mortal life, but the judgment of human reason protests, and in this way argues: It is fitting for the righteous to fare well, we are righteous, therefore we ought to be without calamities, to flourish, to enjoy wealth, glory, tranquility, etc. But the doctrine of the Gospel, which is the wisdom proper to the Church, provides the declaration.

And first it answers the major premise or the saying of the law, It ought to fare well with the righteous. That is true, namely, if the remnants of sin do not cling to the righteous, if they are entirely liberated from sin. But the voice of the Gospel reveals complete liberation, teaching that the righteous, however much they are afflicted in this life, will afterwards possess eternal goods, and will enjoy perpetual joy then, when they have been liberated from all sin, not only by imputation and initiation, but by the consummation of newness. Then he responds to the minor premise: We are righteous, namely, by faith, by imputation or righteousness imputed by God on account of the Son, and by the initiation of new purity, which indeed initiated newness is still squalid and has much infirmity, so that at the same time great filth still clings to the converted, so that the remnants of sin truly remain, sad doubts, likewise many wandering flames of desires, or manifold vicious inclinations in this unclean and miserable nature, until this carnal mass immersed in sin is utterly abolished and destroyed by bodily death.

Let these things be said at the beginning concerning the scandal of the cross, because human reason is offended by these most sad spectacles, looking at the mass of miseries by which the Church is exercised and burdened.

Furthermore, it must be known that there are four kinds of afflictions.

The first and most common kind of calamities is the punishment of certain and peculiar transgressions, such as the prison or captivity of Manasseh. Likewise, the spectacles of public punishments, when murderers are afflicted with the ultimate penalty. This text does not speak of this kind of chastisements: Blessed are those who suffer persecution for righteousness' sake, but beforehand the Lord proposed consolation to those sustaining these works of divine righteousness: Blessed are those who mourn, etc.

The second kind of calamities is exercise or probation, as when Joseph, innocent, is unjustly cast into prison on account of his continence. The third kind is Martyrdom, or the testimony of doctrine, as when Peter, Paul, John the Baptist, etc., are killed solely on account of the confession of true doctrine. Christ speaks here of both kinds of afflictions, namely, probation and martyrdom, because he wishes even holy men and those pleasing to himself to acknowledge that the remnants of sin still cling to them, and that this whole corrupted nature must be destroyed on account of sin.

Furthermore, the death and afflictions of the saints are testimonies of the future judgment; they testify that another life and another judgment remain after this life. For when God has shown beforehand by manifest and illustrious testimonies that Paul is pleasing to him and is his concern, whom he nevertheless allows to be killed afterwards most indignantly by a most base tyrant, he signifies that another judgment will follow, in which he will show that he approves of Paul, not Nero. Likewise, the punishments of the saints in confession are testimonies concerning doctrine; they confirm that it is true and not a fabricated doctrine, and that the saints, preferring the truth of life, truly and seriously feel as they teach, and do not, like hypocrites, carry around a fictitious or fabulous doctrine for the sake of their own advantage.

The fourth kind of calamities is λύτρον [ransom], that is, compensation or price for our sins, satisfying the righteousness of God to appease his wrath. But it is the obedience of Christ alone in all his afflictions and death. Let these four kinds, distinguished by their appellations, be diligently considered, and let not the chastisements of Manasseh be confused with the miseries of Joseph, yet let us know that divine consolations are offered and proposed to both of these.

For to Manasseh is granted the remission of sins on account of the mediator Christ, to whom, as one flees with true faith, punishments are mitigated. Thus Joseph is pardoned, and his natural infirmity and uncleanness are remitted on account of the same Son of God, the propitiator, and the cross or calamity is mitigated and finally removed. But from the miseries of Joseph, these final causes follow, that testimonies of doctrine and of the life to come may be brought forth.

Latin:

Beati qui patiuntur persecutionem propter iusticiam.

De scandalo crucis.

Primo dicendum est, quod constet universam sapientiam rationis humanae duriter offendi, perturbari et obstupefieri, intuentem hanc aeternam speciem, videlicet, quod Ecclesia videtur miseriis oneratus, dissipatus et conculcatus seu oppressus coetus, ac praesertim quod praecipua lumina et excellentia membra Ecclesiae crudeliter interficiuntur tanquam a Deo reiecta, et piacula seu catharmata execranda, ut Abel, Esaias, Ieremias, Christus, Petrus, Iohannes Baptista.

Adversus hoc scandalum necesse est nos recte praemonitos et praemunitos esse. Ac omnino sciamus tantum in verbo Dei propagato per Patres, Prophetas, Christum et Apostolos monstrari veras causas, quare durius prematur, et in hac mortali vita subiecta cruci sit Ecclesia, sed iudicium rationis humanae reclamat, et hoc modo disputat: Iustis congruit bene esse, Nos sumus iusti, Ergo debebamus esse sine calamitatibus, florere, frui opibus, gloria, tranquillitate etc. Verum doctrina Evangelii, quae est sapientia Ecclesiae propria, declarationem tradit.

Ac primum respondet ad maiorem seu dictum legis, Iustis debet bene esse. Id verum est, scilicet, si non haereant in iustis peccati reliquiae, si sint prorsus a peccato liberati. Sed vox Evangelii revelat integram liberationem, docens iustos, quantumvis afflictos in hac vita, postea habituros aeterna bona, et fruituros perpetua laetitia tunc, cum liberati fuerint a toto peccato, non tantum imputatione et incoatione, sed consummatione novitatis. Deinde respondet ad minorem: Nos sumus iusti, scilicet, per fidem, imputatione seu iusticia a Deo imputata propter Filium, et incoatione novae puritatis, quae quidem incoata novitas adhuc squalida plurimum habet infirmitatis, ita ut simul adhuc magnae sordes haereant in conversis, ut vere manent reliquiae peccati, tristes dubitationes, item multae errantes flammae cupiditatum, seu inclinationes viciosae multiplices in hac immunda et misera natura, donec haec massa carnalis mersa in peccatum prorsus aboleatur ac destruatur morte corporali.

Haec initio dicta sint de scandalo crucis, quod offenditur humana ratio his tristissimis spectaculis, intuens molem aerumnarum, quibus exercetur et oneratur Ecclesia.

Porro sciendum est quatuor esse genera afflictionum.

Primum et communissimum genus calamitatum est, poena certorum et peculiarium delictorum, ut carcer seu captivitas Manassae. Item spectacula publicarum poenarum, cum ultimo supplicio afficiuntur homicidae. De hoc genere castigationum non loquitur iste textus: Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter iusticiam, sed antea consolationem proposuit Dominus haec opera iusticae divinae sustinentihus: Beati qui lugent etc.

Secundum genus calamitatum est exercitium seu probatio, ut cum Ioseph innocens propter continentiam iniuste coniicitur in carcerem. Tertium genus est Martyrium, seu testimonium doctrinae, ut cum Petrus, Paulus, Iohannes Baptista etc. tantum propter confessionem verae doctrinae interficiuntur. De utroque genere afflictionum, videlicet, probatione et martyrio loquitur hic Christus, Quia vult etiam sanctos homines ac ipsi placentes agnoscere, quod adhuc haereant in ipsis reliquiae peccati, et quod haec corrupta natura universa propter peccatum destruenda sit.

Praeterea mors et afflictiones sanctorum sunt testimonia de secuturo iudicio, testantur restare aliam vitam et aliud iudicium post hanc vitam. Cum enim Deus ostenderit antea manifestis et illustribus testimoniis, Paulum sibi placere et curae esse, quem tamen sinat a turpissimo tyranno indignissime postea interfici, significat, secuturum aliud iudicium, in quo ostendet se approbare Paulum, non Neronem. Item, supplicia sanctorum in confessione sunt testimonia de doctrina, confirmant veram esse, et non commentitiam doctrinam, et quod sancti anteferentes veritatem vitae vere ac serio sic sentiant, sicut docent, nec ut hypocritae circumferant fictam aut fabulosam doctrinam, sui commodi causa.

Quartum genus calamitatum est λύτρον, id est, compensatio seu precium pro nostris peccatis, satisfaciens iusticiae Dei ad placandam iram. Est autem solius Christi obedientia in omnibus ipsius afflictionibus et morte. Haec quatuor genera distincta appellationibus diligenter considerentur, nec confundantur castigationes Manassae, cum aerumnis Iosephi, attamen utrique horum divinas consolationes offerri atque proponi sciamus.

Etenim donatur Manassae remissio peccatorum propter mediatorem Christum, ad quem vera fide confugienti poenae mitigantur. Ita Ioseph condonatur atque remittitur naturalis infirmitas et immundities propter eundem Filium Dei propiciatorem, et mitigatur ac tollitur tandem crux seu calamitas. Sed a Iosephi aerumnas accedunt hae causae finales, ut edantur testimonia doctrinae, et secuturae vitae.

## 5:13 Sermons on Matthew
You are the salt of the earth.

At the beginning, he warns about the ministry, by which it is necessary that there be some who teach.

And in another place he expressly institutes teachers, namely when he sends the Apostles, Matthew 10. Likewise John 18: As the Father has sent me, so I also send you. And he commands all who teach that they should be like salt, that they should rebuke sins, and show the true worship of God. And he adds a threat: If the salt has become insipid, it will be poured out and trampled underfoot, as it is said in Hosea: Because you have rejected knowledge, I will reject you, that you may not serve as a priest. This threat is always observed in the human race.

When teachers become negligent and omit their duty, then afterwards some calamity follows, in which they perish, just as the Canons, Monks, and other Papists will be destroyed, because they neglected and corrupted the ministry.

Latin:

Vos estis sal terrae.

Initio monet de ministerio, quo oporteat esse aliquos qui doceant.

Et in alio loco expresse instituit doctores, scilicet cum mittit Apostolos Matthaei 10. Item Iohan. 18.: Sicut misit me pater, sic et ego mitto vos. Et praecipit omnibus qui docent, ut sint sicut sal, arguant peccata, et ostendant veros cultus Dei. Et addit comminationem: Si sal fuerit insipidum, effundetur et conculcabitur, sicut in Hosea dicitur: Quia scientiam repulisti, repellam te, ne sacerdotio fungaris.

Haec comminatio semper in genere humano servatur. Quando doctores fiunt negligentes, et omittunt officium, tunc postea sequitur aliqua calamitas, in qua pereunt, sicut Canonici, Monachi et alii Papistae delebuntur, quia neglexerunt et corruperunt ministerium.

## 5:14 Sermons on Matthew
He repeats the same admonition: You are the light of the world. And let this be the duty of teachers, that they show the true doctrine concerning God, etc.

Latin:

Repetit eandem admonitionem: Vos estis lux mundi. Et sit hoc officium docentium, ut ostendant veram doctrinam de Deo etc.

## 5:17 Sermons on Matthew
Do not think that I have come to abolish the law.

Here he begins the sermon concerning the law, which it appears he has often repeated, because it is an interpretation of the law, which ought to be known in the Church.

But first here, as we often do, and as it is often necessary to be done, the hearers must be warned that the law is one thing, and the Gospel is another. This distinction must be most well-known.

What is the law? I answer briefly for the boys: It is the Decalogue. It is, moreover, the doctrine handed down by God, prescribing what kind of people we ought to be, and what we ought to do and omit, and demanding perfect obedience, and condemning all who do not provide perfect obedience, namely testifying by divine authority that such people are guilty of the wrath of God and eternal death, and are punished in many ways in this life and after this life.

This doctrine, which is the law, is not the doctrine concerning the remission of sins. And Christ is not a legislator.

Because the law was implanted in us immediately at creation, and afterwards repeatedly and often reiterated, and promulgated in the mountain of Sinai by a manifest testimony. And horrible punishments in life testify that the law is valid, and that God is the guardian of the law, and executes punishments, just as he says: God is a consuming fire.

And let us not think that the law of God can be removed just as a picture is removed from a wall, or just as human statutes can be removed, like a beer tax, or a commandment about clothing. But the law is the horrible sentence of God against sin, which He himself, because He is just, executes.

And He only spares those fleeing to the Son, but nevertheless He imposed punishments upon the Son, so that divine justice might be satisfied. These general things concerning the law must often be thought upon, and it is necessary that these be known.

The Gospel, however, is the preaching of repentance and the promise, in which, on account of the Son of God, the remission of sins, the imputation of righteousness, the Holy Spirit, and eternal life are freely given to us, through faith in Christ alone, not on account of the law and not on account of our merits. This promise is the medicine that heals wounds, that is, the condemnation and punishments which are imposed upon us by the voice of the law.

And God revealed this medicine in the promise immediately, when He received Adam and Eve, who had also fallen into condemnation and just punishments, but the Son of God interceded for them. And thus, on account of the Son, they were received, and the promise was issued: The seed of the woman shall crush the head of the serpent. Therefore, our Lord Jesus Christ is the one who merits this promise, and the pledge and the preacher, by whose blood the promise was sealed.

But when the people had heard that they were to be freed by the Messiah from condemnation, which is the punishment that the law imposes, they also heard that there would be an end to the Levitical ceremonies; they understood the doctrine concerning liberty carnally, as if license were now granted for all desires, just as many, twenty years ago, having heard the preaching of Christian liberty, wanted to be free from all laws, from rents, and from discipline. To this foolish opinion, Christ first opposes here a most grave sentence concerning the law: I have not come to abolish the law, but to fulfill it.

Objection. But let someone say: If Christ is not a legislator, why does he preach the law?

I answer. It is true that Christ is not a legislator, because the law was previously given and known, but he came principally on account of the promise.

But nevertheless, because it must be known in the Church what sin is, it is necessary for the voice of the Decalogue to sound in the Church, which is the eternal sentence of God, and it spares no men, except those fleeing to the Son of God, as I said before. Medicine cannot be known unless the disease is known first.

Thus, the magnitude of mercy and the remission of sins cannot be understood unless sin is understood in some way. How can you bind a wound if you do not know where or what kind of wound it is?

Therefore, the Decalogue is always recited in the Church as well, as Paul says: Through the law comes the knowledge of sin. And because the Pharisees had interpreted the law wrongly, and valued their own traditions more than the law of God, just as the Papists and Monks do among us. Therefore Christ, as a faithful teacher, often repeated the Decalogue, and censured and abolished false interpretations, just as in our time the Lord Doctor Martin has abolished such Pharisaical interpretations in his preaching of the Decalogue. Meanwhile, however, you should know that the proper promise of the Gospel is one thing, and that Christ has other principal offices, namely, to sound the voice of the Gospel, and to become a victim, and to give the remission of sins, righteousness, and eternal life. Now look at the words. I have not come to abolish the law. To abolish signifies to delete, weg thun, and to blot out. He affirms clearly, therefore, that he does not wish to abolish the law, namely the Decalogue. For the Decalogue is that part of the law which is the foundation of other laws, and it is a perpetual sentence, and it pertains to the whole human race, not only to the Jewish people. But why is the Decalogue not abolished? Because it is not merely a picture in books or on walls, but it is the very wisdom and will of God, which is eternal, just as God himself is. Therefore, just as the wisdom and will of God cannot be abolished, so the law cannot be abolished, as we see punishments remain in us ourselves, because the law, that is, the just will of God, imposes them. He says, therefore: I have not come to abolish the law, but to fulfill it. These words are full of the greatest wisdom, and ought to be most well-known to all, and are to be thought upon often, so that little by little we may learn to understand them more and more. But in order that we may explain these words in some way according to our infirmity, it must be known that Christ fulfills the law in four ways. First, by the perfection of his own obedience, because Christ alone perfectly performs the law. Second, by paying the penalties for us. Third, by effecting the law in us, giving the Holy Spirit, and regenerating us, and restoring eternal life to us, so that the law may thus be fulfilled in us, because it is necessary that our wills correspond with the wisdom and will of God. Fourth, because he himself also teaches and illustrates it, and testifies that obedience is necessary.

Latin:

Ne putate, quod venerim solvere legem.

Hic incipit concionem de lege, quam apparet ab eo saepe repetitam esse, quia est interpretatio legis, quam in Ecclesia notam esse oportet.

Primum autem hic, ut saepe facimus, et saepe fieri necesse est, moneri auditores oportet, aliud esse legem, et aliud Evangelium. Hoc discrimen notissimum esse oportet.

Quid est lex? Respondeo pro pueris breviter: Est Decalogus. Est autem doctrina a Deo tradita praecipiens quales nos esse oportet, et quae facere et omittere oportet, et postulans perfectam obedientiam, et damnans omnes, qui non praestant perfectam obedientiam, videlicet testificans autoritate divina, quod tales rei sint irae Dei et mortis aeternae, et multipliciter puniantur in hac vita et post hanc vitam.

Haec doctrina, quae est lex, non est doctrina de remissione peccatorum. Et Christus non est legislator.

Quia lex statim in creatione nobis insita est, et postea subinde et saepe repetita, et in monte Sinai manifesto testimonio promulgata. Et poenae horrendae in vita testantur, legem esse ratam, et Deum esse custodem legis, et poenas exequi, sicut inquit: Deus est ignis consumens.

Et non putemus, legem Dei ita tolli posse, sicut tabula a pariete amovetur, vel sicut statuta humana tolli possunt, Wie ein Biersteuer, oder ein Gebot von Kleidern. Sed lex est sententia Dei horrenda adversus peccatum, quam ipse, quia est iustus, exequitur.

Et tantum parcit confugientibus ad Filium, sed tamen Filio imposuit poenas, ut iusticiae divinae satisfieret. Haec generalia de lege saepe cogitanda sunt, et sciri haec necesse est.

Evangelium vero est praedicatio poenitentiae et promissio, in qua propter Filium Dei gratis dantur nobis certo remissio peccatorum, imputatio iusticiae, Spiritus sanctus, et vita aeterna, per solam fidem in Christum, non propter legem et non propter nostra merita. Haec promissio est medicina, quae sanat vulnera, id est, damnationem et poenas, quae voce legis nobis imponuntur.

Et hanc medicinam in promissione statim Deus revelavit, quando recipit Adam et Hevam, qui etiam ceciderant in damnationem et poenas iustas, sed Filius Dei pro eis deprecatus est. Et ita propter Filium recepti sunt, et edita est promissio: Semen mulieris conculcabit caput serpentis. Est ergo huius promissionis promeritor, et pignus et praedicator, Dominus noster Iesus Christus, cuius sanguine promissio obsignata est.
