Here he simultaneously promises the preservation of the ministry, and of the Church, and lodgings, but with tribulation; that is, he promises the defense which he himself will bestow, even if kings and princes persecute the Church.

Be prudent as serpents, and simple as doves.

Here begins the doctrine concerning persecution.

Previously he gave express commands, sent them, ordered them to teach, and said what they ought to teach, namely the Gospel, and said they would have provisions and defense, even if they have no money in their belts, and have no weapons, garrisons, or armies.

Now follows an express prediction concerning enemies.

But there is a need for us to be forewarned in the New Testament concerning enemies, and concerning the mode of defense, because after the Law was given, and the polity of Moses was established, the people knew they had a certain seat of the kingdom, and defenders, leaders, and kings, such as Joshua, Gideon, Samuel, David, Jehoshaphat, and always thereafter some such, and they had a certain kingdom.

But what is similar in the Church? There is no certain seat, no certain kingdom, no certain defense. Therefore it is necessary for the Apostles and all of us to be forewarned, especially since the Apostles held this opinion, that the Messiah was to have an earthly kingdom.

But first he sets forth a marvelous saying.

Be prudent as serpents, and simple as doves.

Concerning doves, it is easier to understand what he means.

Doves are without gall, [German: have no gall], that is, they have no anger and hatred, and desire for vengeance. Thus we ought to be without private anger, without hatreds, without desire for vengeance.

Here let it be considered how great movements in empires arise from private hatreds.

Pompey and Julius overturn the Roman empire on account of private hatred, etc.

Thus Arius stirs up his heresy with a desire for vengeance, because he was not made a Bishop.

Thus we have seen Carlstadt stir up tumults out of hatred for Luther, etc.

And many such things happen in this time.

These things are prohibited, when he says: Be simple as doves, that is, without private hatreds, without envy, without desire for vengeance.

There are also other good properties of doves, which fit here.

Doves often give birth, and diligently cherish their chicks, and do not know adultery, and do not depart from their places.

Such is a good preacher; he teaches many.

He does not teach adulterous doctrine. He does not wander through various sects, etc.

Be prudent as serpents.

This is said to be the nature of the serpent, when it fights with other serpents, or enemies, then it especially labors with the strength of its head, but so that it may not be harmed, it diligently and artfully surrounds it with the coils of its neck, and takes care that its head is not harmed.

Thus a Christian preacher labors with his head, that is, with doctrine, and surrounds his head, that is, he takes care that he does not lose the doctrine.

Serpents do not lose their life, even if other parts of the body are dissected.

Thus the Church and the soul do not perish, even if limbs and faculties perish, provided the doctrine is safe.

Likewise, the serpent knows him by whom it is harmed, even if it is in a great crowd of men, and it attacks him, not others.

Thus a preacher ought to know the enemies, the foes of the Gospel, and repress them, not irritate others.

Likewise, the serpent knows its remedies; in old age it purges its eyes with fennel, and from this men learned that fennel is beneficial for the eyes.

Thus a preacher ought to know the remedies for the eyes, the word of God, and ought to look far ahead, lest he receive evil dogmas.

There follows an express forewarning concerning persecution.

Beware of men, they will hand you over, etc.

And the same forewarning concerning persecution is often repeated.

Brother will hand over brother, father his son.

You will be hated by all on account of my name.

Certainly these things are hard.

Consolation.

After this forewarning follows consolation, which is also often repeated.

Do not be anxious about what you are to say.

Latin:

Caput X.

Et vocans duodecim discipulos suos, etc. Hic et post resurrectionem describitur vocatio Apostolorum, quia Deus vult nos certos esse de doctrina, vult nos scire per quos et quomodo propagata sit, sicut inde usque ab initio vocavit Prophetas, et diximus saepe alias, quid sint Prophetae, Apostoli, Pastores et Doctores.

Et primum bene notandum est, quod scriptum est, Lucae 6. quod tota nocte ante hanc electionem Apostolorum Christus manserit in monte, in precatione.

Iam cogitemus, quantum opus esse ipse Dominus iudicaverit, mittere certos doctores, petivit ab aeterno Patre, ut ipse eos gubernet, sicut etiam in agone suo precatur: Sanctifica eos in veritate, sermo tuus est veritas etc. Sic nos petamus dari idoneos ministros.

II. Consideremus autem ingentia beneficia Dei, et agamus Deo gratias.

Deus dupliciter vocat Ministros, immediate, et mediate.

Immediate Prophetas et Apostolos, et addit eis testimonia, ut simus certi.

Mediate per Ecclesiam alios Pastores et Doctores, qui debent doctrinam traditam per Prophetas et Apostolos sine ulla mutatione tradere.

In utraque vocatione Filius Dei est efficax, ut ad Ephesios 4. dicitur, et Rom. 1.: Evangelium est potentia Dei ad salutem omni credenti.

III. Postquam eos vocavit et addidit potestatem faciendi miracula, ut doctrina habeat testimonia, tradidit etiam mandata, ubi et quid debeant docere.

Non inter gentes, quia Deus prius voluit colligere Ecclesiam in Israël. Postea tamen inter gentes post triennium, interea tamen etiam multi ex gentibus conversi sunt.

Quid debebant docere? Sicut alibi dicit: Agite poenitentiam et credite Evangelio, et hic inquit: Venit regnum coelorum? Regnum promissum propter Filium Dei, in quo delebitur peccatum et mors, et restituetur iustitia et vita aeterna. Hoc regnum in hac vita inchoatur praedicatione Evangelii, poenitentia et fide, post resurrectionem erit consummata iustitia et vita aeterna, in qua Deus erit omnia in omnibus, et erimus sine peccato et morte.

Sic alibi dicit: Ite praedicantes poenitentiam et remissionem in nomine meo.

IV. De defensione. Quando aliquid novi instituitur, quando legati mittuntur, necesse est eos habere viaticum et defensionem. Et in toto orbe velle mutationem facere per Apostolos, et quidem florente imperio Romano, videtur res impossibilis esse. Ideo prius hic confirmat Apostolos Christus, promittit eis defensionem et viaticum, sicut alibi inquit: Ego ero vobiscum usque ad consummationem seculi. Item, Iohann. 15.: Ego elegi vos, ut eatis et fructum feratis, et fructus vester maneat. Et hic inquit: Mitto vos sicut oves in medio luporum, sed omnes capilli capitis vestri numerati sunt.

Ac primum de viatico dicit: Non possidete aurum in zonis, neque calceos etc.

Hic aliqui fanatici homines disputaverunt, Pastores et alios concionatores nihil debere habere proprium, et faciunt singularem cultum Dei ex non habendo proprium.

Christus non hoc dicit, quod non liceat habere, sed loquitur de facto, quod ita fit. Non habent pii doctores divitias et defensionem. Et addit consolationem, ne relinquant officium, propterea quod non habent defensionem et divitias, et promittit se curaturum, ut tamen habeant hospitia et victum. spitia et victum.

Talis est Ecclesia, ubicunque est in mundo, habet hospitium, quod Deus protegit, et non habet humanam defensionem. Ideo dicitur in Esaia: Dabo vobis doctorem et panem et aquam, cum tribulatione. Hic simul promittit conservationem ministerii, et Ecclesiae, et hospitia, sed cum tribulatione, id est, promittit defensionem, quam ipse tribuet, etiamsi reges et principes persequuntur Ecclesiam.

Sitis prudentes sicut serpentes, et simplices sicut columbae.

Hic incipit doctrina de persecutione.

Prius dedit mandata expressa, misit eos, iussit docere, et dixit, quid debeant docere, scilicet Evangelium, et dixit eos habituros esse viaticum et defensionem, etiamsi non habeant aes in zonis, et non habeant arma et praesidia et exercitus.

Nunc sequitur expressa praedictio de hostibus.

Ideo autem opus est praemoneri nos in novo Testamento de hostibus, et de modo defensionis, quia postquam Lex est data, et constituta politia Moisi, scivit populus se habere certam sedem regni, et defensores duces et reges, ut Iosue, Gedeon, Samuelem, Davidem, Iosaphat, et semper deinceps aliquos tales, et habuerunt certum regnum.

Quid autem simile est in Ecclesia? Non est certa sedes, non certum regnum, nulla certa defensio. Ideo necesse est Apostolos et nos omnes praemoneri, praesertim cum Apostoli haberent hanc opinionem, quod Messias esset habiturus mundanum regnum.

Primum autem ponit mirabile dictum.

Estote prudentes sicut serpentes, et simplices sicut columbae.

De columbis facilius est intelligere quid velit.

Columbae sunt sine felle, haben keine Gallen, id est, non habent iras et odia, et cupiditatem vindictae. Sic nos debemus esse sine privata ira, sine odiis, sine cupiditate vindictae.

Hic consideretur quanti motus in imperiis oriantur ex privatis odiis.

Pompeius et Iulius evertunt imperium Romanum propter privatum odium etc.

Sic Arius movet suam haeresin cupiditate vindictae, quia non est factus Episcopus.

Sic nos vidimus Carolostadium movere tumultus odio Lutheri etc.

Et multa hoc tempore fiunt talia.

Haec prohibentur, cum ait: Estote simplices sicut columbae, id est, sine privatis odiis, sine invidentia, sine cupiditate vindictae.

Sunt et aliae proprietates bonae columbarum, quae huc congruunt.

Columbae saepe pariunt, et diligenter fovent pullos, et non norunt adulteria, et non discedunt ex suis locis.

Talis est bonus concionator, multos docet.

Non docet adulterinam doctrinam. Non vagatur per varias sectas, etc.

Estote prudentes sicut serpentes.

Dicitur haec natura esse serpentis, quando pugnat cum aliis serpentibus, vel hostibus, tunc praecipue laborat viribus capitis, sed ne laedatur, diligenter et arte circumdat gyris colli, et curat, ne laedatur caput.

Sic Christianus concionator laborat capite, id est, doctrina, et circumdat caput, id est, cavet, ne amittat doctrinam.

Serpentes non amittunt vitam, etiamsi aliae partes corporis sint dissectae.

Sic Ecclesia et anima non perit, etiamsi membra et facultates pereunt, modo doctrina sit salva.

Item, serpens novit eum a quo est laesus, etiamsi est in magna turba hominum, et hunc petit, non alios.

Sic debet concionator nosse inimicos, hostes Evangelii, et hos reprimere, non irritare alios.

Item, serpens novit remedia sua, in senecta purgat oculos faeniculo, et inde didicerunt homines faeniculum prodesse oculis.

Sic debet concionator nosse remedia oculorum, verbum Dei, et debet procul prospicere, ne mala dogmata recipiat.

Sequitur praemonitio expressa de persecutione.

Cavete ab hominibus, tradent vos, etc.

Et saepe repetita est eadem praemonitio de persecutione.

Tradet frater fratrem, pater filium.

Eritis odio omnibus propter nomen meum.

Certe haec dura sunt.

Consolatio.

Post hanc praemonitionem sequitur consolatio, quae etiam saepe repetita est.

Non sitis soliciti, quid sitis dicturi.

## 10:20 Sermons on Matthew
It is not you who speak, but the spirit of your Father speaking in you. Do not fear those who kill the body. Two sparrows are sold for a penny. All the hairs of your head are numbered. All these sayings are most sweet promises, which affirm that God is certainly present in the Church, and helps his own in confession and in teaching. Let these consolations be in sight.

There is also a general testimony that God cares for us: Two sparrows are sold for a penny, and one does not fall upon the earth without your Father; you are better than many sparrows. To this are added other promises, in the last chapter of Matthew. I am with you, even to the consummation of the age. Isaiah 51. I have put my words in your mouth, and I will protect you with the shadow of my hand, that you may plant the heavens. Declare it. Isaiah 46. Even in old age I will carry you, etc. Isaiah 40. As a shepherd carries lambs recently born, so I will carry you. Such promises ought to be known to us all, so that we may know that God will preserve the Church, and we may ask that he be present with us and protect us; therefore these promises have been repeated so often, so that faith may be confirmed, and we may know for certain that the Church will remain, and with this faith we may labor, and ask for help, defense, and all things necessary from God.

He repeats the command concerning confession, and the promise: Whoever will confess me before men, I will confess him before my heavenly Father, and whoever will deny me, I will deny him.

Let these sayings confirm us against the judgments of the wise, who cry out: Why do you stir up dissensions? Why are you the cause of discord? Let us answer: It is an immutable command that one must confess.

Do not think that I have come to bring peace. It is a prediction that the cross follows the preaching of the Gospel and confession, and that the Church is subject to the cross.

This is often predicted, as in Genesis 3. Because if men were not forewarned, reason would judge those to be cast off by God who are so horribly killed by tyrants.

I will put enmities between the seed of the woman and the serpent, etc. Item: Whoever wishes to follow me, let him take up his cross and follow me. Item 2 Timothy 3. All who wish to live piously in Christ will suffer persecution.

Let a declaration be added.

Latin:

Non vos estis, qui loquimini, sed spiritus patris vestri loquens in vobis. Non timete eos, qui occidunt corpus. Duo passeres asse veneunt. Omnes capilli capitis vestri numerati sunt. Omnia haec dicta sunt dulcissimae promissiones, qui affirmant, quod certo Deus adsit in Ecclesia, et iuvet suos in confessione, et in docendo. Hae consolationes sint in conspectu.

Est et generale testimonium, quod Deus curet nos: Duo passeres asse veneunt, et unus non cadit super terram sine patre vestro, vos multis passeribus meliores estis. Huc addantur aliae promissiones, Matthaei ultimo. Ego vobiscum sum, usque ad consummationem seculi. Esaiae 51. Posui verba mea in ore tuo, et umbra manus meae protegam te, ut plantes coelos. Declara. Esaiae 46. Etiam in senecta ego gestabo vos, etc. Esaiae 40. Sicut pastor gestat agnos recens editos, sic ego gestabo vos. Tales promissiones debent nobis omnibus notae esse, ut sciamus Deum servaturum esse Ecclesiam, et petamus, ut nobis adsit, et nos protegat, ideo istae promissiones toties repetitae sunt, ut fides confirmetur, et sciamus certo mansuram esse Ecclesiam, et hac fide laboremus, et petamus auxilium, defensionem et omnia necessaria a Deo.

Repetit mandatum de confessione, et promissionem: Qui confitebitur me coram hominibus, confitebor eum coram patre meo coelesti, et qui negaverit me, negabo eum.

Haec dicta confirment nos contra iudicia sapientum, qui clamant: Cur movetis dissensiones? Cur estis causae discordiae? Respondeamus: Est mandatum immutabile, quod oportet confiteri.

Non putate, quod venerim mittere pacem. Praedictio est, quod crux sequatur praedicationem Evangelii et confessionem, et quod Ecclesia sit subiecta cruci.

Hoc saepe praedicitur, ut Genes. 3. Quia si homines non essent praemoniti, ratio iudicaret istos a Deo abiectos esse, qui tam horribiliter interficiuntur a tyrannis.

Ponam inimicitias inter semen mulieris et serpentem etc. Item: Qui vult me sequi, tollat crucem suam et sequatur me. Item 2. Timoth. 3. Omnes qui pie volunt vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur.

Addatur declaratio.

## 10:34 Sermons on Matthew
I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.

I came to separate a man from his father, etc. Here the heathens and the wise argue thus. That which is the cause of discord is evil. The Gospel is the cause of discord. Therefore the Gospel is evil.

I answer. The Gospel is not the cause of discord, but the evil will of men opposing God. The whole creation ought to obey God, and it is to be lamented that men do not wish to accept the offered medicine and salvation, etc.

But because evil men do not obey God, they themselves are the cause of discord. Truly it is a sad sermon that a daughter should be at variance with her mother, etc. Added is a consolation and a promise of receiving life: Whoever loses his soul for my sake will find it.

Second part.

Whoever receives you, receives me. Command concerning listening to ministers.

And this includes that God wills to be effective through the ministry. As the Father sent me, so I send you. This is a necessary consolation, that God wills to be certainly effective through the voice of the ministers of the Gospel.

Romans 1. The Gospel is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes. Romans 10. How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the Gospel of peace.

Let a declaration be added. These sayings are commands concerning the ministry of the Gospel, not concerning the traditions of Bishops outside the Gospel. They do not establish kingdoms outside the Gospel, but they command that Christ be obeyed, that the word of God be heard.

As Psalm 2: Kiss the Son. The command is immutable, that we should hear the Gospel.

Third part. A promise added concerning the rewards of those who receive teachers, who aid the propagation of the doctrine, who aid teachers and learners.

He who receives a Prophet because of his doctrine shall receive the reward of a Prophet. He who shall have given a drink of water etc. Amen I say to you etc. The Lord swears that He will give a reward to such as aid the propagation of the Gospel.

Therefore let us not doubt that God will protect the Church and the hospices of the Church. And examples are recited.

The widow of Sarepta is fed, and the Son is raised. The hostess of Elisha is saved, and the Son is resurrected. God does good to the midwives in Egypt. The friend of Jeremiah is saved in the court of Zedekiah during the destruction of the city of Jerusalem. And in this our time you see that God has mitigated punishments for princes who have provided hospitality to the Gospel.

Latin:

Non veni mittere pacem, sed gladium.

Veni separare hominem a patre, etc. Hic Ethnici et sapientes sic argumentantur. Hoc quod est causa discordiae, est malum. Evangelium est causa discordiae. Ergo Evangelium est malum.

Respondeo. Evangelium non est causa discordiae, sed mala voluntas hominum adversantium Deo. Tota creatura debet obedire Deo, et est dolendum, quod homines non volunt accipere oblatam medicinam et salutem, etc.

Sed quia homines mali non obediunt Deo, ipsi sunt causa discordiae. Profecto tristis concio est, quod filia a matre sit dissensura, etc. Addita est consolatio et promissio recipiendae vitae: Qui perdit animam suam propter me, inveniet eam.

Secunda pars.

Qui vos recipit, me recipit. Mandatum de audiendis ministris.

Et hoc complectitur, quod Deus velit esse efficax per ministerium. Sicut Pater me misit, sic ego mitto vos. Haec est necessaria consolatio, quod velit esse certo efficax Deus per vocem ministrorum Evangelii.

Rom. 1. Evangelium est potentia Dei ad salutem omni credenti. Rom. 10. Quam speciosi pedes Evangelizantium pacem.

Addatur declaratio. Haec dicta sunt mandata de ministerio Evangelii, non de traditionibus Episcoporum extra Evangelium. Non constituunt regna extra Evangelium, sed praecipiunt, ut Christo obediatur, ut verbum Dei audiatur.

Ut Psalm. 2.: Osculamini filium. Mandatum est immutabile, ut audiamus Evangelium.

Tertia pars. Promissio addita de praemiis eorum, qui recipiunt docentes, qui iuvant propagationem doctrinae, qui iuvant docentes et discentes.

Qui recipit Prophetam propter doctrinam, mercedem Prophetae accipiet. Qui dederit potum aquae etc. Amen dico vobis etc. Dominus iurat se daturum mercedem talibus, qui iuvant Evangelii propagationem.

Ideo non dubitemus, quin Deus sit protecturus Ecclesiam et hospitia Ecclesiae. Et exempla recitentur.

Vidua Sareptana alitur, et excitatur Filius. Hospita Elisaei servatur, et resuscitatur Filius. Deus benefacit obstetricibus in Aegypto. Ieremiae amicus in aula Sedechiae servatur in excidio urbis Ierosolymae. Et hoc nostro tempore videtis, quod Deus mitigavit poenas principibus, qui Evangelio hospitium praebuerunt.

## 11:1 Sermons on Matthew: Argument
Chapter XI.

John sends his disciples to inquire, not because he himself doubts, but so that the disciples may hear from Christ Himself that no other Messiah is to be expected, and so that they themselves may be confirmed by the miracles they see. This is the sum of this embassy.

II. The reason for the disciples' doubting was this, because in the people there was this common persuasion that the Messiah would restore a political kingdom, and would have armies, and, having subdued the nations, would occupy provinces, just as the Monarchs, Cyrus, Alexander, and others did. Since, therefore, they saw that this Jesus was only a poor preacher, they were moved by this appearance to doubt whether this was the Messiah.

III. But Christ answers this reason for doubting, and teaches what the future kingdom of the Messiah will be, when He says: The Gospel is preached to the poor. Item: Blessed is he who shall not have been offended in me, that is, the kingdom of the Messiah will not be political, instructed with riches, an army, and similar to the empires of the world: but it will be such as you see, the preaching of the Gospel, by which the Messiah will be effective, will gather an eternal Church by the voice of the Gospel from all nations, and through the Gospel will give remission of sins, and the Son Himself will vivify those who believe and do penance, and will give them the spirit and eternal life. Therefore the Messiah is promised, not that He might constitute an empire of the world.

Christ later declares this answer more fully, where He says: From the days of John the Baptist the kingdom of heaven breaks forth by force, [dringet mit gewalt erfür]. Item: The Law and the Prophets until John, that is, you have a foolish imagination that the Law of Moses is still to reign among the nations, and that the whole world is to be a Jewish polity. Cast away this error, the end of this polity is now here, another kingdom comes, namely the kingdom of heaven, and it comes by force.

These words are not to be understood as if Christ occupies empires by force, like Alexander. But the divine power breaks forth against the furies of Devils and tyrants, and proceeds even against the will of Devils and tyrants. And the violent take it by force, that is, not the timid, not those fleeing dangers, but the constant, and those preferring the glory of God and the confession of their life to all pleasures.

Here let a declaration of the saying be made: The Law until John, and let it be said that many seek subtle expositions, but we wish to be content with this simpler one, because Christ speaks of the end of the polity. He speaks, therefore, here of the Law, in so far as it is political, namely of ceremonies and forensic matters, [vom Kirchen gepreng, vnd von Bürgerlicher regierung], and also of the moral Law, in so far as it is external discipline, restraining civilly. And let the distinction of the three parts of the law be recited to the people in a crude way, as it is in the Megalburg examination.

Another sermon.

Christ gives testimony to John, that he is a constant teacher, and a witness of Christ. And He says that he is not like the courtiers, who flatter their masters, etc. Afterwards, he is commemorated in the description of his office.

What was the Prophet among the people? Preaching about Christ, and ruling some political counsels, and retaining the law of Moses. Therefore John says: I am not a Prophet. And Christ says: More than a Prophet. Because he both points to the present Christ, and begins the new Church, baptizes, receives Gentiles and Jews; it was not granted to other Prophets to institute a new rite.

Therefore he says: No one greater has arisen, namely, in office. Because no one's office is greater than John's, after Christ.

Therefore Christ excepts himself, when he says: He who is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater, that is, Christ, who is most humbled before all men, he is greater than John. He baptizes with the Holy Spirit, he is the redeemer and savior, just as John says: From his fullness we have all received.

Latin:

Caput XI.

Iohannes mittit discipulos suos, ut interrogent, non quod ipse dubitet, sed ut discipuli ex ipso Christo audiant, quod non alius Messias exspectandus sit, et ut ipsi coram visis miraculis confirmentur. Haec est summa huius legationis.

II. Ratio autem dubitandi discipulis fuit haec, quia in populo fuit haec vulgaris persuasio, Messiam instauraturum esse regnum politicum, et habiturum exercitus, ac domitis gentibus occupaturum esse provincias, sicut fecerunt Monarchae, Cyrus, Alexander et alii. Cum igitur viderent hunc Iesum tantum esse pauperem concionatorem, hac specie humi movebantur, ut dubitarent, an hic esset Messias.

III. Respondet autem Christus ad hanc rationem dubitandi, et docet, quale sit regnum Messiae futurum, cum ait: Pauperibus Evangelizatur. Item: Beatus, qui non offensus fuerit in me, id est, regnum Messiae non erit politicum, instructum divitiis, exercitu, et simile imperiis mundi: sed erit tale, quale videtis, praedicatio Evangelii, qua Messias erit efficax, colliget aeternam Ecclesiam voce Evangelii ex omnibus gentibus, et per Evangelium dabit remissionem peccatorum, et ipse filius vivificabit credentes et agentes poenitentiam, et dabit eis spiritum et vitam aeternam. Ideo est promissus Messias, non ut constituat imperium mundi.

Hanc responsionem Christus postea magis declarat, ubi dicit: A diebus Iohannis Baptistae regnum coelorum vi erumpit, dringet mit gewalt erfür. Item: Lex et Prophetae usque ad Iohannem, id est, vos habetis stultam imaginationem, iam legem Mosi inter gentes regnaturam esse, et totum mundum fore Iudaicam politiam. Hunc errorem abiicite, finis iam est huius politiae, aliud regnum venit, scilicet regnum coelorum, et venit vi.

Haec verba non sic intelligantur, quod Christus vi occupet imperia, sicut Alexander. Sed potentia divina erumpit contra furores Diabolorum et tyrannorum, procedit etiam nolentibus Diabolis et tyrannis. Et violenti rapiunt, scilicet, non timidi, non fugientes pericula, sed constantes, et anteferentes gloriam Dei et confessionem suae vitae et omnibus voluptatibus.

Hic fiat declaratio dicti: Lex usque ad Iohannem, et dicatur, quod multi quaerant subtiles expositiones, sed nos velimus esse contenti hac simpliciore, quia Christus loquitur de fine politiae. Loquitur ergo hic de Lege, in quantum est politica, scilicet de ceremoniis et forensibus, vom Kirchen gepreng, vnd von Bürgerlicher regierung, etiam de Lege morali, in quantum est externa disciplina, coërcens civiliter. Et recitetur populo crasse distinctio trium partium legis, ut est in examine Megalburgensi.

Alia concio.

Christus dat testimonium Iohanni, quod sit constans doctor, et testis de Christo. Et dicit eum non esse similem aulicis, qui assentantur dominis, etc. Postea commemoratur in descriptione officii ipsius.

Quid fuit Propheta in populo? praedicens de Christo, et regens aliqua consilia politica, et retinens legem Moisi. Ideo Iohannes ait: Non sum Propheta. Et Christus ait: Plus quam Propheta. Quia et praesentem Christum monstrat, et inchoat novam Ecclesiam, baptizat, recipit gentes et Iudaeos, aliis Prophetis non fuit concessum instituere novum ritum.

Ideo dicit: Non surrexit maior, scilicet, in officio. Quia nullius officium est maius, quam Iohannis, post Christum.

Ideo Christus sese excipit, cum ait: Qui minimus est in regno coelorum, est maior, id est, Christus, qui est maxime humiliatus prae omnibus hominibus, hic est maior Iohanne. Hic baptizat Spiritu sancto, est redemtor et salvator, sicut Iohannes inquit: Ex eius plenitudine omnes accepimus.

## 11:2-7 Third Sunday
Third Sunday

of Advent. Gospel

Matthew 11. When John had heard in prison the works of Christ, having sent two of his disciples, he said to him: Are you he who is to come, or do we expect another? And Jesus answering said to them: Go and report to John those things which you hear and see: The blind receive sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor receive the joyful message of the Gospel. And blessed is he who has not been offended in me. And as they were going, Jesus began to say to the crowds concerning John: What did you go out into the desert to see?

A reed shaken by the wind? Come, what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft garments? Behold, those who wear soft things are in the houses of kings. But, what did you go out to see? A Prophet? Truly I say to you, and more excellent than a Prophet.

For this is he of whom it is written: Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.

There are five topics. I. The testimony of doctrine. II. Concerning the scandal of the Cross, and the appearance of Christ and the Church. III. Concerning the office and constancy of the Preacher. IV. Concerning the office of John, and the collation of John and Christ.

V. Concerning the distinction between the Old and New Testament. The Law and the Prophets until John.

Concerning the first. Perpetual miracles of the whole Church are to be observed. And although some unusual things happened among the nations, yet the resurrection of the dead was never performed outside the Church. Item, ethnic miracles were never universal preservations, such as the preservation of Noah, or the leading out of Egypt, or the perpetual preservation of the Church amidst such great storms.

Therefore Christ alleges miracles, so that he might confirm the listeners, and because the Prophets had predicted that the Messiah would perform these miracles, he admonishes them to recognize the Messiah, and to know that the time is now at hand, of which the Prophets spoke. On the second. Blessed is he who shall not have been scandalized in me. The weak appearance of Christ offends all wise men. And the Jews had a far different imagination concerning the kingdom of the Messiah. Therefore, He warns us not to be offended by this weak appearance, and teaches us to oppose true testimonies, namely, those of the word and of miracles.

There is also a similar appearance of the Church, which is weak, miserable, and scattered. Therefore, He says here: It is preached to the poor, signifying what kind of thing the Church is. He also recounts this among the miracles, that the Church is such a gathering. For the Prophets also placed these things among the signs and miracles of the Messiah, and Mary says: He has exalted the humble.

For it is a great miracle that God gathers the Church from the miserable, the abject, and the believers, and opposes this to the power of the devil and the world, and glorifies it with great works, and preserves it. As the Psalm says: God makes His holy one wonderful. Meanwhile, monarchs and the powerful perish. Furthermore, the believers themselves understand this to be a singular and admirable work of God, that God hears, regards, and vivifies the afflicted, which is taught in the Church alone, and is unknown to all men and all nations who are ignorant of the Gospel.

On the third.

John's constancy is adorned with an excellent encomium, which He wishes to be an example for those teaching in the Church. On the contrary, the wisdom of courts is to incline oneself to the more fortunate side of the ship. And it happens in all ages that courts have wanted to temper religions to their own utilities, and light-minded people are found who serve the desires of Princes. But Christ exhorts all teachers to imitate the constancy of John.

On the fourth.

Concerning the office of John, and the comparison with Christ, There has not arisen a greater, namely, in office. For although the Prophets were political governors, and purifiers of the Church, and teachers of the Gospel, yet they did not begin the whole ministry of the New Testament, namely, the preaching of the Gospel and Baptism; they did not show the present Christ, they did not begin the universal calling of the Gentiles. But what Christ adds, He who is lesser in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he, I understand this statement concerning the person of Christ, who calls Himself lesser, because in truth Christ overcomes all angels and men by the true humility of His heart. For since He perfectly knows the Father, He most perfectly attributes to Him the highest honor, and casts Himself further below Him than any angels or men.

I also believe that because of such great humility He was despised by the proud angels, and that the angels fell because of this sin. Then in the passion, Christ was in truth also depressed below all men, as Esaias says: We saw Him despised, and the last of men. Item: I am a worm, and not a man. Let us consider this humility of Christ, and let us learn to depress our pride, our admiration of ourselves, our confidence in ourselves, our contempt for others, our impatience, our security, our desire for vengeance, and similar affections which arise from pride, just as He Himself says: Learn from me, for I am meek and humble of heart.

But Christ says that He is greater, namely in person and office, because Christ is not only a teacher, like John, but He is Himself the redeemer, the sanctifier, the vivifier, by whose trust we receive the remission of sins, the Holy Spirit, and eternal life. Therefore John says: I baptize with water, that is, by ministry: Christ will baptize with the Holy Spirit, that is, He will give the remission of sins, the Holy Spirit, and eternal life.

On the fifth.

The Law and the Prophets until John, that is, the polity of Moses and the ceremonies end in John, and let this statement be held as a rule, confirming the abrogation of the polity of Moses and the ceremonies; afterwards follows the spiritual ministry of the Gospel, which John begins, he argues against sins, and preaches the remission of sins on account of the Lamb of God, etc. If anyone objects, If the law is until John, is it therefore not to be preached afterwards? I answer briefly to the antecedent: The statement speaks of the polity of Moses, and not of the spiritual ministry, which is for all times, until eternal life.

For the voice of God remains, arguing against sins, which is the eternal law, and the voice of the Gospel concerning the remission of sins is added. The kingdom of heaven is invaded by force, and the violent take it by force, that is, not the slothful, not the timid, not those yielding to the threats or terrors of the devil. For the kingdom of heaven cannot be obtained without true struggles, both public and private.

Adolescents

let them struggle with their own desires, let them know that some contention is necessary for taming desires. Let the old struggle with the persecutors of the Gospel, with infidelity, and other bites of the devil; this is what the text teaches, the violent take it by force, namely, by struggling and fighting against the devil.

Latin:

Dominica III.

Adventus. Evangelium

Matth. 11. Cum audisset Ioannes in carcere facta Christi, missis duobus discipulis suis, dixit illi: Tu es ille qui venturus est, an alterum expectamus? Et respondens Iesus dixit illis: Íte et renunciate Ioanni ea, quae auditis et videtis: Coeci visum recipiunt, et claudi ambulant, Leprosi mundantur, et surdi audiunt, Mortui excitantur, et pauperes laetum accipiunt Evangelii nuncium. Et beatus est quisquis non fuerit offensus in me. Euntibus autem illis, coepit Iesus dicere turbis de Ioanne: Quid existis in desertum ut videretis?

Num arundinem, quae agitatur a vento? Age, quid existis ut videritis? Num hominem mollibus vestibus amictum? Ecce qui mollia gestant in domibus regum sunt. At, quid existis videre? Num Prophetam? Certe dico vobis, et excellentiorem Propheta.

Hic est enim de quo scriptum est: Ecce ego mitto nuncium meum ante faciem tuam, qui praeparaturus est viam tuam ante te.

Quinque sunt loci. I. Testimonium doctrinae. II. De scandalo Crucis, et specie Christi et Ecclesiae. III. De officio et constantia Concionatoris. IV. De officio Iohannis, et collatione Iohannis et Christi.

V. De discrimine Veteris ac Novi Testamenti. Lex et Prophetae usque ad Ioannem.

De primo. Miracula perpetua totius Ecclesiae intuenda sunt. Et quanquam apud gentes acciderunt interdum quaedam inusitata, tamen nunquam extra Ecclesiam facta est resuscitatio mortuorum. Item miracula ethnica nunquam fuerunt servationes universales, sicut servatio Nohae, aut eductio ex Aegypto, aut perpetua conservatio Ecclesiae inter tantas procellas.

Allegat igitur Christus miracula, ut confirmaret auditores, Et quia Prophetae praedixerant, Messiam haec miracula facturum esse, admonet ut agnoscant Messiam, et sciant tempus iam adesse, de quo dixerunt Prophetae. De secundo. Beatus qui in me non fuerit scandalizatus, Offendit omnes sapientes infirma species Christi. Et Iudaei longe aliam imaginationem de regno Messiae habebant. Ideo admonet nos, ne offendamur hac infirma specie, et docet opponere vera testimonia, scilicet verbi et miraculorum.

Est et similis Ecclesiae species, quae est infirma, aerumnosa, dissipata. Ideo hic dicit: Pauperibus evangelizatur, significans qualis sit Ecclesia. Recenset autem et hoc inter miracula, quod Ecclesia sit talis coetus. Nam et Prophetae inter signa Messiae et miracula haec posuerunt, et Maria inquit: Exaltavit humiles.

Magnum enim miraculum est, quod colligit Deus Ecclesiam ex miseris, abiectis, credentibus, et hanc opponit potentiae diaboli et mundi, et glorificat eam magnis operibus, et conservat. Sicut Psalmus inquit: Mirificat Deus sanctum suum. Interim vero pereunt monarchae et potentes. Praeterea ipsi credentes intelligunt hoc esse singulare et admirandum opus Dei, quod Deus exaudit, respicit, vivificat afflictos, quod in sola Ecclesia docetur, et omnibus hominibus, et omnibus gentibus ignotum est, ignaris Evangelii.

De tertio.

Constantia Iohannis ornatur egregio encomio, quam vult exemplo esse docentibus in Ecclesia. Econtra aularum sapientia est, inflectere se ad navis latus felicius. Et omnibus aetatibus accidit, ut aulae voluerint attemperari religiones ad suas utilitates, et inveniuntur levia ingenia, quae serviunt Principum cupiditatibus. Sed hortatur omnes doctores Christus, ut Ioannis constantiam imitentur.

De quarto.

De officio Ioannis, et collatione Christi, Non surrexit maior, scilicet in officio. Etsi enim Prophetae fuerunt gubernatores politici, et repurgatores Ecclesiae, et doctores Evangelii, tamen non incoaverunt totum ministerium novi Testamenti, videlicet, praedicationem Evangelii et Baptismum, non ostenderunt praesentem Christum, non incoaverunt universalem vocationem gentium. Quod autem addit Christus, Qui minor est in regno coelorum, maior est eo, hoc dictum de persona Christi intelligo, qui vocat sese minorem, quia revera Christus vera cordis humilitate vincit omnes angelos et homines, Cum enim perfecte norit patrem, perfectissime tribuit ei summum honorem, et se infra eum abiicit longius, quam ulli angeli aut homines.

Arbitror etiam propter tantam humilitatem a superbis angelis despectum fuisse, et hoc peccato lapsos esse angelos. Deinde in passione, Christus revera etiam depressus est infra omnes homines, sicut Esaias inquit: Vidimus eum despectum, et novissimum virorum. Item: Ego sum vermis, et non homo. Hanc humilitatem Christi consideremus, et discamus deprimere superbiam nostram, admirationem nostri, fiduciam nostri, contemptum aliorum, impatientiam, securitatem, cupiditatem vindictae, et similes affectus, qui oriuntur a superbia, sicut ipse dicit: Discite a me, quia mitis sum, et humilis corde.

Dicit autem Christus se maiorem esse, scilicet persona et officio, quia Christus non est tantum doctor, sicut Ioannes, sed ipse redemptor, sanctificator, vivificator, cuius fiducia accipimus remissionem peccatorum, Spiritum sanctum, et vitam aeternam. Ideo ait Ioannes: Ego baptizo aqua, id est, ministerio: Christus baptizabit Spiritu sancto, id est, dabit remissionem peccatorum, Spiritum sanctum, et vitam aeternam.

De quinto.

Lex et Prophetae usque ad Ioannem, id est, politia Moisi et ceremoniae desinunt in Ioanne, et hoc dictum tanquam regula teneatur, confirmans abrogationem politiae Moisi et ceremoniarum, postea sequitur ministerium spirituale Evangelii, quod Ioannes incoat, arguit peccata, et praedicat remissionem peccatorum propter agnum Dei etc. Si quis obiiciat, Si lex usque ad Iohannem, ergo postea non est praedicanda? respondeo breviter ad antecedens: Dictum loquitur de politia Moisi, et non de ministerio spirituali, quod est omnium temporum, usque ad vitam aeternam.

Manet enim vox Dei, arguens peccata, quae est aeterna lex, et additur vox Evangelii de remissione peccatorum. Regnum coelorum vi invaditur, et violenti rapiunt illud, id est, non ignavi, non timidi, non cedentes minis, aut terroribus diaboli. Non enim potest regnum coelorum obtineri, sine vers certaminibus, publicis et privatis.

Adolescentes

dimicent cum suis cupiditatibus, sciant esse opus aliqua contentione ad domandas cupiditates. Seues dimicent cum persecutoribus Evangelii, cum infidelitate, et aliis morsibus diaboli, hoc docet lictum, violenti rapiunt, scilicet certantes et praeliantes adversus diabolum.

## 11:17 Sermons on Matthew
We have piped to you and you have not danced.

This whole following part is a complaint about the contempt of the Gospel in the world. And it is a sad threatening of punishments: Woe to Chorazin, woe to Capernaum. We have piped to you, that is, we have preached the Gospel and the promises. We have mourned, that is, we have preached the law and the punishments, and you have cared for neither.

To this add the saying in Luke: The servant who knows the will of the Lord, and does not do it, shall receive many stripes.

We ourselves must also fear, for few are amended, and many take more license for themselves under the pretext of Evangelical liberty. Therefore this will happen, which the Lord said about the fig tree, Luke 13.

The Lord grants time, so that more may be converted, but when too few are converted, then at last he destroys whole kingdoms, and whole nations, just as he destroyed Sodom.

Now there are small chastisements in Germany, so that we may be warned to be more ardent in conversion, invocation, and all exercises of piety. But because too few are amended, and very many become more furious, therefore punishments increase, just as this year many cities perished by fires, as in war, Schweinfurt, Culmbach, Newstadt. Also outside of war, Lauben, Goldberg, etc. And some time later the Turks will come, and will devastate all Germany, just as they have already burned Novum Solium, Newen Solen. And the Isennacensian monk Johannes Hilten predicted that the Turks in the year 1600 would be masters of Italy and Germany.

Question.

I know it is objected here by some: Why do you speak of punishments, when nevertheless we ought to love God freely? Also, should not repentance begin from the love of justice, and not from the fear of punishment?

Response. God punishes for this reason, that his wrath may be recognized, and he wants his wrath to be understood and feared.

On the contrary, he promises and gives good things for this reason, that his goodness and mercy may be recognized; he wants both to be known, wrath and mercy, therefore he wants punishments and benefits to be preached, and he himself does both, he punishes and delivers, therefore it is necessary that these be preached.

He does not want us to be iron-hearted, so that we are not moved by punishments. Indeed, he censures this hardness, as when he says in Isaiah chapter 48: I know that you are hard, your forehead is bronze.

Also Isaiah 28 he rebukes the hard: You think you have a covenant with death, you imagine in your security that no evil will happen, but I will punish you. And therefore I punish, so that some may be converted, because vexation gives understanding, etc.

Let us therefore each consider our own and public punishments, and let us rouse ourselves to repentance, like the prodigal son, and then let us progress, let us fear the wrath of God and God himself. Again, let us also recognize the mercy of God and his good things, and let us ask and expect good things from God, let us praise his mercy, and let us love him, just as he himself teaches us, saying that he does an alien work, so that he may do his own, that is, he says he punishes and mortifies, so that he may again vivify, and give good things.

Latin:

Cecinimus vobis et non saltastis.

Tota haec sequens pars est querela de contemtu Evangelii in mundo. Et est tristis comminatio poenarum: Vae Corazin, vae Capernaum. Cecinimus vobis, id est, praedicavimus Evangelium et promissiones. Ploravimus, id est, praedicavimus legem et poenas, et neutrum curastis.

Huc addatur dictum in Luca: Servus qui scit voluntatem Domini, et non facit, accipiet plures plagas.

Metuendum est et nobis ipsis, pauci emendantur, et multi praetextu Evangelicae libertatis plus sibi licentiae sumunt. Ideo fiet hoc, quod dixit Dominus de ficu, Lucae 13.

Dominus concedit tempus, ut plures convertantur, sed quando nimis pauci convertuntur, tunc tandem delet tota regna, et totas gentes, sicut delevit Sodoma.

Nunc sunt parvae castigationes in Germania, ut moniti simus ardentiores in conversione, invocatione, et omnibus exercitiis pietatis. Sed quia nimis pauci emendantur, et plurimi fiunt furiosiores, ideo crescunt poenae, sicut hoc anno urbes multae incendiis perierunt, ut in bello, Schweinfurt, Culmbach, Newstadt. Item extra bellum, Lauben, Goldberg, etc. Et aliquanto post venient Turci, et totam Germaniam vastabunt, sicut iam combusserunt Novum Solium, Newen Solen. Et Monachus Isennacensis Iohannes Hilten praedixit, Turcos anno 1600. fore dominos Italiae et Germaniae.

Quaestio.

Scio hic obiici ab aliquibus: Cur dicis de poenis, cum tamen debeamus Deum gratis diligere? Item poenitentia debet inchoari ab amore iustitiae, et non a timore poenae? Responsio.

Deus ideo punit, ut ira ipsius agnoscatur, et vult iram intelligi et metui.

Econtra ideo promittit et dat bona, ut eius bonitas et misericordia agnoscatur, vult utrumque cognosci, iram et misericordiam, ideo vult praedicari poenas et beneficia, et ipse utrumque facit, punit et liberat, ergo necesse est haec praedicari.

Non vult nos esse ferreos, ut non moveamur poenis. Imo hanc duritiem taxat, ut cum apud Esaiam dicit capite 48.: Scio quod durus es, frons tua aenea est.

Item Esaiae 28. obiurgat duros: Cogitatis vos habere foedus cum morte, fingitis securi nihil fore mali, ego vero puniam vos. Et ideo puniam, ut aliqui convertantur, quia vexatio dat intellectum, etc.

Reputemus ergo singuli nostras poenas proprias et publicas, et nos ad poenitentiam exsuscitemus, sicut filius prodigus, et deinde proficiamus, timeamus iram Dei et ipsum Deum. Rursus etiam agnoscamus misericordiam Dei et bona, et petamus et exspectemus a Deo bona, laudemus eius misericordiam, et ipsum diligamus, sicut ipse nos docet, dicens se facere alienum opus, ut faciat proprium, id est, dicit se punire et mortificare, ut rursus vivificet, et det bona.

## 11:25 Sermons on Matthew
I confess to you, Father.

There are three members of this most beautiful and sweetest sermon of Christ.

I. The first is the thanksgiving of Christ, by which he gives thanks to the eternal Father, because he gathers some Church, and at the same time teaches what kind he gathers.

II. The second member is, who Christ himself is, and why he was sent, and what is the manner of gathering the Church.

III. The member is the command, that we recognize this son, and flee to him, and a promise is added, which is the sum of the Gospel: I will refresh you. Also: You will find rest for your souls, etc.

On the first member.

Just as here Christ gives thanks to the eternal Father for this immense benefit, that he gathers the Church, so let us know that he has always prayed for the human race, and prays, that the Church may be gathered and preserved, just as it is said in Psalm 2: Ask to me, and I will give you the nations.

And John 17, long and express is the prayer: I pray not for them only, but for all who will believe through their word.

Item, 1 John 3.

Here let us learn these wonderful counsels, that the human race was not created in vain, but that God through mercy gathers from it an eternal Church, but with the Son interceding.

And these things must always be joined: prayer and thanksgiving for the thing obtained. It is altogether wicked to ask for many things, and to receive them, and afterwards to be ungrateful.

Let us consider, however, what gratitude is. It is composed of two virtues: it is truth, which confesses from whom the benefit was received, and it is justice, binding itself in turn to certain duties.

Gratitude holds within itself the two highest virtues, Truth and Justice. Truth is that it confesses from whom the gift comes. Furthermore, it is Justice, that it binds itself, in return, to certain friendly services.

Thus here Christ confesses that the gathering of the Church is a benefit of the eternal Father, and attributes to the Father this praise of mercy, that from Him is this huge good, that He wills to gather an eternal Church, to which He communicates Himself in all eternity. These great things we also must think upon, and together with Christ give thanks, and pray that the Church may be gathered among us as the Psalm commands: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem.

Item, it is said there: For my brethren's sake I have prayed for thee. This our supreme Priest Christ does especially, but we also ought to do this, just as the daily prayer teaches: Thy kingdom come.

Then consider what kind of Church he says is gathered here: Thou hast hidden these things from the wise, and hast revealed them unto babes.

Here we learn that the Church is a congregation of babes and miserable ones; few wise, few powerful embrace the Gospel, as 1 Corinthians 1 and following is said. Let us hold these testimonies, that we may confirm ourselves against this scandal, by which human minds are greatly tormented, because they see the Church to be such a torn and weak body, gathered from the poor, and dispersed without empires.

Think how beautiful the assembly was at Rome, the Senate of Augustus, with Augustus presiding. What were they compared to these, miserable men in Judea, like worms, Zacharias, Simeon, Anna, Joseph, Elizabeth, Mary? etc. By this scandal men are certainly moved, but let us know it was predicted that such is the Church, a congregation of the weak and poor, and let us believe the word of God, whether the powerful and wise believe, or do not believe.

It is written: The powerful shall suffer torments powerfully.

On the second member. I. What Christ is, and why He was sent, and on the manner of gathering the Church. II. Here Christ openly names Himself the Son of God, just as He often does elsewhere.

And He adds that this is such a Son, who perfectly knows the Father, and who shows the Father to others. This is the sublime doctrine concerning the Son.

No creature perfectly knows the eternal Father. Therefore this Son is above creatures. And no creature could have seen this counsel, that the human race was to be redeemed in this way, namely by the Son assuming human nature.

But only the Son brings forth this decree, as John 1 is said: The Son who is in the bosom of the Father, He has declared Him to us. And therefore He is called the Word of the eternal Father, because He is that person who immediately addresses the Church and brings forth the Gospel from the secret counsel of the divinity, from then even from the beginning, when He addresses Eve.

Genesis 3. Here at the same time you learn the manner of gathering the Church, namely through the Word.

No one knows the Father, except to whom the Son reveals Him. Therefore it is necessary to hear the Gospel, and the Son Himself is effective with the Gospel, and nowhere is there a Church where the voice of the Gospel is not. The hearers of Mahomet and the Pope, and of sects fighting against the Gospel, are outside the Church of God.

To this pertains the command: Hear Him.

And in Psalm 2: Kiss the Son. And in Deuteronomy: I will raise up a Prophet from among thy brethren. Whoever will not hear, I will be the avenger.

And consider well. The Son reveals the Father in two ways, namely both by the voice of the Gospel, and by illuminating hearts then, when He is effective through the Gospel, because He is together with the Gospel.

When you believe in true consolation, then the Son is truly present, and shows you the mercy of the Father, and is effective, and at the same time pours the Holy Spirit into your heart: He gives gifts to men, Ephesians 4.

When He was speaking to Eve, He was speaking simultaneously outside and inside; with an external voice, He moved and comforted her heart. Thus you may learn to recognize Christ, and know that He is truly effective with the Ministry. He by His own person gathers and sustains the Church, just as He says: No one shall snatch my sheep from my hands. Therefore, the command follows immediately: Come to me. Come to me all you who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you.

Before, He said who Christ is, and how the Church is gathered. Now He adds the command that we should flee to Him. This doctrine ought to be most well-known to all, and it is most frequently repeated, namely, that it is an eternal and immutable command, and that it is universal—it is a command for all—that we should be converted to God, and hear this Son, and believe in Him, and receive consolation from Him, and find rest in Him—that we in this Lord Christ seek certain comfort, and remain by it, and thus be at peace, and know that this is the only comfort before God, and no other, and thus expect grace and salvation through Him alone.

You hear this summary of the Gospel often, and it has been repeated often, as in Psalm 2: Kiss the Son. And the Father Himself says from heaven: Hear Him, Matthew 17.

And He Himself repeats the same thing so many times in John 6: This is the will of the Father, who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son, and believes in Him, may have eternal life. And let us learn this doctrine in true conversion and invocation; there it can be learned.

Those who are secure and persevere in wickedness against their conscience do not understand nor do they care.

Nor is there need for a long declaration; the words are manifest by themselves to those who are in sorrows and seek this consolation.

Concerning the universal particle.

Note, however, diligently, that He says "all," and here the admonition that we often cite must be repeated.

There are two temptations in true sorrows.

The first is concerning dignity. We always think this: I know God is good and merciful, but toward the righteous, and those who do not have such many and such great sins as I do. This is the voice of the law in the minds of all men; because of this temptation, men flee from God, and do not approach Him, and do not dare to call upon Him. This flight, this fidgeting and fleeing before God, is a great sin, even if men do not consider it, and do not think that this flight is a great sin, etc.

But against this temptation, we must oppose the voice of the Gospel, which says "freely," that is, without our own merit, but because of the merit of Christ. And the merit of Christ must be valued more than the whole kingdom of sin; therefore it is said: Grace abounds over the transgression.

Let us not say like Cain: My iniquity is greater than can be forgiven.

Let us therefore hold to this consolation against the first temptation, and let us be mindful of the saying: The blood of Christ has purified us from all sins.

II. The second temptation is concerning particularity, whether all those who have refuge in Christ are accepted, because we think thus: Perhaps God has a register of some whom He wills to make saved; whoever does not stand in that same register will not be saved, whether he has good or evil works, whether he seeks Christ or

not. This temptation is also common, and many a man thinks thus: David had greater sin than Ahithophel, and yet Ahithophel is cast away, but David is saved. How can I now know whether I also belong in God's register?

Against this evil temptation, this consolation must be opposed, that both preachings are universal; it embraces all, the preaching of repentance, and the promise of grace. And thus Christ speaks in this passage, Matthew 11: Come to me all.

Item: Everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved, Acts 2, Romans 10. Item: He has concluded all under sin, that He might have mercy on all.

Romans 11, Galatians 3.

Item: He has placed upon Him the iniquity of us all, Isaiah 53.

In this, you also ought to include yourself, and not think that you do not belong therein.

You ought not to seek another register of God than this one, which He has revealed to you in His Word. You ought to judge according to His revealed Word, and not seek other registers.

This rule you ought to learn well, that your heart and thoughts look upon the revealed Word, to learn the will of God, and not to ascend into Heaven by other ways. Therefore it is said beforehand, This Son has God sent, and spoken, This one you should hear. Whoever now comforts himself with such sayings, he belongs certainly to the number of those whom God will hear and accept. This teaching you should consider often and with great earnestness among yourselves. And this teaching is beautifully depicted in the Canaanite woman, where Christ speaks to her harshly, as if she did not belong in the number of the Holy ones, and were rejected like a dog; she does not let herself be rejected, but speaks with great wisdom and courtesy, The little dogs also eat with the little children, the crumbs that fall under the table, etc.

Latin:

Confiteor tibi Pater.

Tria membra sunt huius pulcherrimae et dulcissimae concionis Christi.

I. Primum est gratiarum actio Christi, qua agit gratias aeterno patri, quod aliquam colligat Ecclesiam, et simul docet, qualem colligat.

II. Secundum membrum est, quis sit ipse Christus, et quare missus sit, et quis sit modus colligendae Ecclesiae.

III. Membrum est mandatum, ut hunc filium agnoscamus, et ad eum confugiamus, et addita est promissio, quae summa Evangelii: Ego reficiam vos. Item: Invenietis requiem animabus vestris, etc.

De primo membro.

Sicut hic Christus agit gratias aeterno patri, pro hoc immenso beneficio, quod colligit Ecclesiam, ita sciamus eum semper precatum esse pro genere humano, et precari, ut Ecclesia colligatur et servetur, sicut Psalm. 2. dicitur: Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes.

Et Iohann. 17. longa et expressa est precatio: Oro non pro eis tantum, sed pro omnibus credituris per verbum eorum.

Item, 1.

Iohannis 3. Hic discamus haec miranda consilia, quod genus humanum non sit frustra conditum, sed quod Deus per misericordiam inde colligat aeternam Ecclesiam, sed intercedente filio.

Et haec semper debent coniungi: precatio et gratiarum actio pro re impetrata. Est omnino iniquum, multa petere, et accipere, et postea ingratum esse.

Cogitemus autem, quid sit gratitudo. Est composita ex duabus virtutibus: est veritas, quae fatetur unde sit acceptum beneficium, et est iustitia obligans se vicissim ad aliqua officia.

Danckbarkeit fast in sich zwo die höchsten tugenden, Warheit vnd Gerechtigkeit. Warheit ist sie darin, das sie bekent, von wem die gabe herkomet, Darnach weiter ist sie Gerechtigkeit, das sie sich verplicht, dagegen auch zu etlichen freundlichen diensten.

Ita hic Christus fatetur, quod collectio Ecclesiae sit beneficium aeterni patris, et tribuit patri hanc laudem misericordiae, quod ab ipso sit hoc ingens bonum, quod velit colligere aeternam Ecclesiam, cui se communicet in tota aeternitate. Has tantas res debemus et nos cogitare, et simul cum Christo gratias agere, et precari, ut colligatur Ecclesia inter nos sicut Psalmus praecipit: Rogate pacem Ierusalem.

Item ibi dicitur: Propter fratres meos rogavi pro te. Hoc praecipue facit Christus noster summus Sacerdos, sed nos quoque hoc facere debemus, sicut et precatio quotidiana docet: Adveniat regnum tuum.

Deinde cogita, qualem hic dicat colligi Ecclesiam: Abscondisti a sapientibus, et revelasti ea parvulis.

Hic discimus quod Ecclesia sit congregatio parvulorum et miserorum, pauci sapientes, pauci potentes amplectuntur Evangelium, ut 1. Corinth. 1. et deinceps dicitur. Haec testimonia teneamus, ut nos confirmemus contra hoc scandalum, quo valde excruciantur humanae mentes, quod vident Ecclesiam esse tam lacerum et imbecille corpus, collectum ex pauperibus, et dispersum sine imperiis.

Cogita, quam pulcer consessus fuerit Romae, Senatus Augusti, Augusto praesidente. Quid erant collati ad hos, miseri homines in Iudaea, tanquam vermiculi, Zacharias, Simeon, Anna, Ioseph, Elizabeth, Maria? etc. Hoc scandalo certe moventur homines, sed sciamus praedictum esse, quod talis sit Ecclesia, congregatio imbecillium et pauperum, et credamus verbo Dei, sive potentes et sapientes credant, sive non credant.

Scriptum est: Potentes potenter tormenta patientur. De secundo membro.

I. Quid sit Christus, et quare missus sit, et de modo colligendae Ecclesiae. II. Hic Christus aperte nominat se filium Dei, sicut et alias saepe.

Et addit, talem hunc esse filium, qui perfecte noverit patrem, et qui ostendat aliis patrem. Haec est sublimis doctrina de filio.

Nulla creatura perfecte novit aeternum patrem. Ergo hic filius est supra creaturas. Et nulla creatura potuisset videre hoc consilium, quod genus humanum esset hoc modo redimendum, scilicet filio assumente humanam naturam.

Sed solus filius hoc decretum profert, ut Iohann. 1. dicitur: Filius qui est in sinu patris, ipse enarravit nobis. Ideoque dicitur Verbum aeterni patris, quia est illa persona, quae immediate Ecclesiam alloquitur et profert Evangelium ex arcano consilio divinitatis, inde usque ab initio, quando Hevam alloquitur.

Genes. 3. Hic simul discis modum colligendae Ecclesiae, scilicet per Verbum.

Nemo novit patrem, nisi cui Filius revelat. Ergo necesse est audire Evangelium, et ipse filius cum Evangelio est efficax, et nusquam est Ecclesia, ubi non est vox Evangelii. Auditores Mahometi et Papae, et sectarum pugnantium cum Evangelio, sunt extra Ecclesiam Dei.

Huc pertinet mandatum: Hunc audite.

Et in Psalmo 2. Osculamini filium. Et in Deuteron. Suscitabo Prophetam de fratribus tuis. Qui non audierit, ego ultor ero.

Et bene consideres. Filius revelat patrem dupliciter, scilicet et voce Evangelii, et illuminans corda tunc, quando per Evangelium est efficax, quia simul est cum Evangelio.

Quando in vera consolatione credis, tunc filius vere adest, et tibi ostendit misericordiam patris, et est efficax, et simul effundit Spiritum sanctum in cor tuum: Ipse dat dona hominibus, Ephes. 4.

Quando ad Hevam loquebatur, simul foris et intus loquebatur, cum voce externa, movebat et consolabatur cor eius. Ita discatis agnoscere Christum, et sciatis cum Ministerio vere efficacem esse. Ipse sua persona colligit et sustentat Ecclesiam, sicut ait: Nemo rapiet oves meas ex manibus meis. Ideo mox sequitur mandatum: Venite ad me. Venite ad me omnes, qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos.

Antea dixit, quis sit Christus, et quomodo colligatur Ecclesia. Nunc addit mandatum, ut confugiamus ad ipsum. Haec doctrina omnibus debet esse notissima, et est saepissime repetita, scilicet, quod sit mandatum aeternum et immutabile, et quod sit universale, das allen geboten ist, ut convertamur ad Deum, et hunc filium audiamus, et credamus ei, et consolationem ab eo accipiamus, et acquiescamus in eo, das wir in diesem HErrn Christo, den gewissen trost suchen, vnd dabey bleiben, vnd also zu frieden sein, vnd wissen, das dieser der einige trost ist bey Gott, vnd kein anderer, vnd also durch in allein gnad vnd seligkeit erwarten. Hanc summam Evangelii saepe auditis, et saepe repetita est, ut Psalmo 2.: Osculamini filium.

Et pater ipse de coelo inquit: Hunc audite, Matthaei 17.

Et ipse toties idem repetit Iohann. 6.: Haec est voluntas Patris, qui misit me, ut omnis qui videt filium, et credit in eum, habeat vitam aeternam. Et hanc doctrinam discamus in vera conversione et invocatione, ibi disci possunt.

Securi et perseverantes in sceleribus contra conscientiam, non intelligunt neque curant.

Nec opus est longa declaratione, verba per sese sunt manifesta, his qui sunt in doloribus, et hanc consolationem quaerunt.

De particula universali.

Nota autem diligenter, quod dicit omnes, et hic repetenda est admonitio quam saepe citamus.

Duae sunt tentationes in veris doloribus.

Prior est de dignitate. Semper hoc cogitamus: Scio Deum esse bonum et misericordem, sed erga iustos, et non habentes tam multa et tam magna peccata, sicut ego. Haec est vox legis in omnium hominum animis, propter hanc tentationem fugiunt homines Deum, et non accedunt ad eum, non audent invocare. Haec fuga, dieses zappeln, vnd vor Gott fliehen, sind grosse sünd, etsi homines non considerant, et non cogitant hanc fugam esse magna peccata, etc.

Sed huic tentationi debemus opponere vocem Evangelii, quae dicit gratis, id est, one vnfern verdienst, sed propter meritum Christi. Et meritum Christi pluris faciendum est quam totum regnum peccati, ideo dictum est: Gratia exuberat supra delictum.

Non dicamus sicut Cain: Maior est iniquitas mea, quam ut remitti possit.

Teneamus igitur hanc consolationem contra primam tentationem, et simus memores dicti: Sanguis Christi purificavit nos ab omnibus peccatis.

II. Altera tentatio est de particularitate, ob auch alle die zu Christo zuflucht haben, angenomen werden, quia sic cogitamus: Vielleicht hat Gott ein Register etlicher, die er wölle selig machen, wer nicht im selbigen Register stehet, der wird nicht selig, er hab gute oder böse werck, er suche Christum oder nicht.

Diese anfechtung ist auch gemein, vnd dencket mancher also, Dauid hat grösser Sünd, denn Achitophel, vnd ist dennoch Achitophel verworffen, Aber Dauid ist selig, Wie kan ich nu wissen, ob ich auch in Gottes Register gehöre?

Contra hanc malam tentationem, haec consolatio opponenda est, quod utraque praedicatio est universalis, begreifft alle, die Buspredig, vnd die verheissung der gnaden, Vnd also spricht Christus in diesem Spruch, Matthaei 11.: Venite ad me omnes.

Item: Omuis qui invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit, Actor. 2. Rom. 10.

Item: Conclusit omnes sub peccatum, ut omnium misereatur. Rom. 11. Gal. 3.

Item: Posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum, Esaiae 33.

In diesem alle soltu dich auch einschliessen, vnd nicht gedencken, das du nicht darein gehörest.

Du solt nicht ein ander Register Gottes suchen, denn dieses, das dir in seinem Wort geoffenbart hat. Du solt richten nach seinem geoffenbarten Wort, vnd nicht andere Register suchen.

Diese Regel soltu wol lernen, das dein Herz vnd Gedancken, das geoffenbarte Wort anschauen, da Gottes willen lernen, vnd nicht durch andere weg in Himel steigen. Darümb ist zuuor gesagt, Diesen Son hat Gott gesand, vnd gesprochen, Diesen solt jr hören. Wer sich nu tröst mit solchen Sprüchen, der gehört gewisslich in die zal derselbigen, die Gott wil erhören vnd annemen. Diese Lere solt jr bey euch offt vnd mit grossem ernst betrachten. Vnd ist diese Lere lieblich furgemalet im Cananeischen Frewlein, da Christus sie hart anspricht, gleich als gehöre sie nicht in der Heiligen zal, vnd sey verworffen wie ein Hund, lesst sie sich nicht verwerffen, sondern spricht mit grosser Weisheit vnd höffligkeit, Die Hündlin essen auch mit den Kindlin, die brösamlin, die vnter den Tisch fallen, etc.

## 11:28 Sermons on Matthew
I have said these things concerning the saying: Come unto me all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

And remember well this whole consolation. And it is certain that by this saying many have been saved at all times. Thus Duke Frederick, Elector of Saxony, and many others have assiduously repeated this saying in their agony. Learn from me, for I am meek and lowly in heart. Take my yoke upon you.

He said before why the Son was sent, and a promise was added, and it is a command that all should believe in the Son and flee to him. Now he adds the doctrine concerning the cross, because it is necessary for us in the Church to know that the Church, by the singular counsel of God, is subjected to the cross, and it is necessary to know the causes revealed by God, why He wills the Church to be subjected to the cross. For unless we are forewarned, men are moved by this argument of reason: Great prosperity, glory, opulence, peace, are gifts of God. Therefore where those goods are, they rather seem to be the people of God. But we see the Turks and others ruling, and the Church being miserable and afflicted. Therefore it is not to be thought that this miserable assembly is the people of God, or that it pleases God. Men's minds are greatly moved by this argument, and many fall away from God because of the splendor of empires. Therefore Scripture often repeats this doctrine concerning the cross, affirms that the Church is subjected to the cross, and explains the causes, and at the same time adds consolations, that God in this life nevertheless brings us aid, and miraculously preserves the Church, and that after this life the Church shall have eternal joy, wisdom, justice, and that God then wills to be all in all.

1 Cor. 15. This doctrine is repeated in Psalm 37. Do not fret, and often elsewhere: and Christ says elsewhere: If anyone wishes to follow me, let him take up his cross. And Paul says: It is necessary for all to be made like the Son of God, Rom. 8. Thus he commands in this place, that we take up his yoke, that is, the confession of the doctrine, which always brings the cross into the world.

This is the simplest explanation. But see how he speaks. The world judges the cross to be most bitter; the Lord teaches the contrary: My yoke is sweet. Let these opposites be considered. It is true that to the body the cross is bitter, as to be killed, to be burned, are bitter to the body. But when hearts are raised by faith, within there is consolation and joy in God, just as Lawrence felt consolation when he was burned on the gridiron, as it was said: I am with him in tribulation. Item: Your sorrow shall be turned into joy. Item: He who loses his field etc. shall receive a hundredfold in this life, and eternal life afterwards. Both are promised, consolation in this life, but yet with tribulation, and afterwards eternal life.

This whole sermon is then understood when we are afflicted and seek consolation. But secure and profane men deride this sermon, so I speak of it more briefly. But after he spoke of the cross, he proposes himself as an example: Learn from me, for I am meek and lowly in heart. Here first this reminder is necessary. Christ is to be acknowledged in two ways, first as savior and cause of salvation, secondly, as an example. First, he is the cause of salvation, as redeemer by his merit, also by his effect, because he himself quickens us by the Gospel and the Holy Spirit. This is the principal acknowledgment of Christ, in which we distinguish him from all the Saints.

Secondly, however, Christ also wants himself to be considered as an example, as Paul also in chapter 2 to the Philippians proposes Christ as an example. Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ, who when he was in the form of God etc.

And Peter 1 Peter 4: Communicate in the sufferings of Christ.

He names here two virtues, which ought to be in governors and teachers, and especially here Christ preaches to governors and teachers.

And these virtues are better understood when the opposite vices are considered. Two virtues are named, Gentleness and Humility.

Against these contend Vengefulness and Pride. Vengefulness is when one has anger against another, and seeks thereafter unfair means to suppress the same, and to bring to nothing.

As, Saul wanted to exterminate David, Cain kills Abel, Pompey wanted to exterminate Julius, etc. These are very common in the greatest part of men, but especially among princes and teachers, who stir up one another, and burn full of vengefulness against God's commandment, who wills that we do not seek vengeance in a disorderly way.

Often it also happens in our time, that someone has moved a false dogma out of hatred for another, Carolostadius out of hatred for Luther, and Osiander etc. It is therefore gentleness, not to have unjust hatreds, and not to seek vengeance in a disorderly way.

Gentleness is this virtue, not to bear unjust hatred, also not to seek vengeance in a disorderly way, and to moderate and keep within the anger according to God's will. Pride contends against humility, and is the well from which flow vengefulness and much vice, as Sirach says: Pride is the beginning of all sin.

And pride is namely to live in security without the fear of God, and not to recognize one's own weakness, and therefore to esteem oneself great, and to want to have honor above others, and to want to exalt oneself outside of one's calling, and to murmur against God and men who hinder such things. As an example, Saul is insane with pride, and esteems himself great, and cannot endure that David also has honor beside him, and does not consider that his and David's good fortune was God's gift, etc.

Now let everyone consider what damage these two little weeds do in all government, Pride and Vengefulness, etc. On the other hand, Humility is to recognize one's own weakness in the fear of God, and not to esteem oneself great, and not to step outside of one's calling.

WORKS. VOL. XIV. Humility is to fear God, and by the recognition of one's own infirmity and the will of God, not to seek greater things than one's calling, and with trust in God to serve one's own calling, and not to despise others, but to judge in such a way that others also are instruments of God, through whom God can do more good.

Latin:

Haec dixi de dicto: Venite ad me omnes, qui laboratis et onerati estis, ego reficiam vos.

Et bene mementote hanc totam consolationem. Et certum est hoc dicto multos omni tempore servatos esse. Sic Dux Fridericus Elector Saxoniae et alii multi assidue in agone repetiverunt hoc dictum. Discite a me, quia mitis sum et humilis corde. Tollite iugum meum super vos.

Prius dixit, quare Filius missus sit, et addita est promissio, et mandatum est, ut omnes credant filio, et ad eum confugiant. Nunc addit doctrinam de cruce, quia nos in Ecclesia necesse est scire, quod Ecclesia singulari consilio Dei subiecta sit cruci, et oportet scire causas a Deo revelatas, quare velit Ecclesiam subiectam esse cruci. Nisi enim simus praemoniti, moventur homines hoc rationis argumento: Magna prosperitas, gloria, opulentia, pax, sunt Dei dona. Ergo ubi sunt illa bona, illi potius videntur esse populus Dei. Videmus autem Turcos et alios dominari, et Ecclesiam esse miseram, et adflictam. Ideo non cogitandum est, hunc coetum miserum esse populum Dei, aut placere Deo. Valde moventur hominum animi hoc argumento, et multi deficiunt a Deo propter splendorem imperiorum. Ideo saepe scriptura repetit hanc doctrinam de cruce, adfirmat Ecclesiam subiectam esse cruci, et exponit causas, et simul addit consolationes, quod Deus in hac vita tamen nobis etiam opem ferat, et mirabiliter servet Ecclesiam, et quod post hanc vitam Ecclesia sit habitura aeternam laetitiam, sapientiam, iustitiam, et quod Deus tunc velit esse omnia in omnibus.

1. Corinth. 15. Haec doctrina repetita est in Psalmo 37. Noli aemulari, et saepe alias: et Christus alibi inquit: Si quis vult me sequi, tollat crucem suam. Et Paulus inquit: Oportet omnes fieri similes filii Dei, Rom. 8. Sic praecipit hoc loco, ut tollamus iugum ipsius, id est, doctrinae confessionem, quae semper adfert in mundo crucem.

Haec est simplicissima enarratio. Sed vide quomodo loquatur. Mundus iudicat crucem esse amarissimam. Dominus contrarium docet: Iugum meum suave est. Haec contraria considerentur. Verum est, corpori crucem amaram esse, ut interfici, comburi, sunt amara corpori. Sed cum corda sunt erecta fide, intus est consolatio et laetitia in Deo, sicut Laurentius consolationem sentit, cum uritur in craticula, sicut dictum est: Cum ipso sum in tribulatione. Item: Tristitia vestra vertetur in gaudium. Item: Qui perdet agrum etc. recipiet centuplum in hac vita, et vitam aeternam postea. Utrumque promittitur, consolatio in hac vita, sed tamen cum tribulatione, et postea vita aeterna.

Haec tota concio tunc intelligitur, quando adfligimur, et quaerimus consolationem. Sed securi et profani homines derident hanc concionem, ita brevius de ea dico. Postquam autem de cruce dixit, sese proponit tanquam exemplum: Discite a me, quia mitis sum et humilis corde. Hic primum haec commonefactio necessaria est. Christus dupliciter agnoscendus est, primum ut salvator et causa salutis, secundo, ut exemplum. Primum, causa salutis est, ut redemtor suo merito, item effectione, quia ipse vivificat nos Evangelio et Spiritu sancto. Haec est principalis agnitio Christi, in qua discernimus eum ab omnibus Sanctis.

Secundo vult tamen Christus etiam se considerari ut exemplum, ut et Paulus ad Philippenses capite 2. proponit Christum ut exemplum. Hoc sentite in vobis, quod et in Christo, qui cum esset in forma Dei etc.

Et Petrus 1.

Petri 4.: Communicate passionibus Christi. Nominat autem hic duas virtutes, quas in gubernatoribus et doctoribus esse oportet, et praecipue hic Christus concionatur gubernatoribus et doctoribus.

Et virtutes hae melius intelligentur, consideratis oppositis vitiis. Duae virtutes nominantur, Sanfftmütigkeit vnd Demuth.

Wider diese streiten Rachgyrigkeit vnd Hoffart. Rachgyrigkeit ist, so einer ein zorn wider einen hat, vnd sucht darnach vnbilliche mittel, denselbigen nider zu drücken, vnd zu nichten zu machen.

Als, Saul wilden Dauid ausrotten, Cain tödtet den Abel, Pompeius wil den Iulium ausrotten, etc. Haec sunt usitatissima in maxima parte hominum, sed praecipue inter principes et doctores, die wehen einander, vnd brinnen voll Rachgyrigkeit wider Gottes gebot, der wil, das wir nicht rach vnordentlich suchen.

Saepe etiam accidit nostro tempore, ut aliquis moverit falsum dogma odio alterius, Carolostadius odio Lutheri, et Osiander etc. Est igitur mansuetudo, non habere iniusta odia, et non quaerere vindictam vnordentlich.

Sanfftmütigkeit ist diese Tugend, nicht vnrechten hass tragen, auch nicht vnordentlich Rach suchen, vnd den zorn nach Gottes willen messigen vnd innen halten. Hoffart streit wider Demuth, vnd ist der Brun, daraus fliessen rachgyrigkeit vnd viel vntugend, wie Syrach spricht: Hoffart ist der anfang aller Sünd.

Vnd ist nemlich Hoffart, one Gottes forcht in sicherheit leben, vnd eigene schwacheit nicht erkennen, vnd darumb sich selb gros achten, vnd ehre vber andere haben wöllen, vnd sich ausser seinem beruff wöllen erhöhen, vnd murren wider Gott vnd Menschen die solchs vorhindern. Als exempel, Saul ist vnsinnig von hoffart, vnd acht sich selb gros, vnd kan nicht leiden, das Dauid neben im auch ehre habe, vnd betrachtet nicht, das seine vnd Dauids glück, Gottes gabe war, etc.

Nu betrachte ein jeglicher, was schaden in aller regierung diese zwey kreutlein thun, Hoffart vnd Rachgyrigkeit, etc. Dagegen ist Demuth, in Gottes forchteigene schwacheit erkennen, vnd sich nicht gros achten, vnd nicht ausser seinen beruff treten.
