OPER. VOL. XIV. Humilitas est, timere Deum, et agnitione propriae infirmitatis et voluntatis Dei, maiora vocatione non appetere, et fiducia Dei suae vocationi servire, nec alios despicere, sed ita iudicare, quod et alii sint organa Dei, per quos Deus plura bona facere possit.

## 12:1 Sermons on Matthew: Argument
Chapter XII.

The first history contains: I. The doctrine concerning the reprehension of human traditions, which were valued more than the law of God, as in the custom of the recent time, it was a greater sin to eat meat on the sixth day than to lie in wait for another's spouse.

II. The distinction concerning works. Moral duties are to be preferred to ceremonial ones.

And here is treated the most learned sentence of Hosea: I desire mercy, and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. It was without doubt a general sentence, delivered against superstition. Because it is most common for men, having lost the light of faith, to embrace ceremonies, nay, human traditions, and to place in these the whole worship of God.

Opposed to this error is this sentence, which commands concerning true worship, the knowledge of God, and mercy. The knowledge of God is the true fear of God, and true faith.

To know that God truly is angry at sin, and truly forgives for the sake of the Son, hears, etc. Mercy is the love of the neighbor, etc.

These are better than ceremonies, and much better than human traditions. This understanding God wills to exist in the Church, and concerning this matter 28 years ago struggles were stirred up.

It is more the commandment of God to be a husband than to be celibate, according to human tradition. The Lord is the son of man even of the Sabbath.

The simplest sentence is that the Messiah is above the law. He reprehends, however, the foolish opinion of the Pharisees, who neither understood the observation of the Sabbath correctly, nor knew the Messiah, but thought that in the time of the Messiah the ceremonies of Moses would remain, and that this is the righteousness which the Messiah was to bring, nor did they understand the righteousness of faith. There was a great heap of these errors; he refutes this whole heap with this saying, as if he were saying: You blind men, you neither understand the law, nor do you know the Messiah; you think this observation of ceremony is righteousness, and you dream that the Messiah will bring nothing else but such an observation of the law.

Indeed, the law concerning the Sabbath was given for another reason, namely, that it might be a day destined for the ministry of the doctrine of the law and of the promises. But the Messiah brings eternal righteousness and life, not these ceremonies, the end of which will be in eternal life, where there will be a true Sabbath in the constant sight of God.

As Isaiah says: There shall be a Sabbath from Sabbath. Stretch out your hand.

The second disputation, which follows immediately, is a repetition and example of the same doctrine concerning the Sabbath.

Here Christ refutes the wrong understanding of the Sabbath, and afterwards performs a work which is truly a work of the Sabbath, because it is a testimony of doctrine.

Here, therefore, let it be briefly said again why the Sabbath was instituted. It is mentioned by name concerning sanctification: Sanctify the holy. It does not say: Be idle. But on that day you should perform holy works, that is, properly devote that day to the ministry of doctrine, let the teachers teach, let the people listen, let all gather to learn and for public preaching. This is the sum of the commandment, and this is the end.

Christ, therefore, now truly sanctifies the Sabbath, teaches, and provides testimonies of doctrine. But blind superstition imagines that idleness is worship, just as traditions were established then, and the Jews still have traditions. On the Sabbath they lead Christians about, who cook, who pick mucus from lamps, etc. Thus also the Papists have instituted feast days, but let us learn the true understanding of the Sabbath.

Jesus looked around in anger. Here let us learn that not all anger is sin.

Because God so created angels and men that they have appetites, good desires and inclinations, love, fear, hope, dread, anger, joy. These were created thus, but after the fall they became disordered. But yet in the saints they are restrained and drawn back to order.

Thus Abraham loves his wife and children, and does rightly. But David loves another man's wife, and does not do rightly, because he departs from order. But that order is just which agrees with the law of God.

Thus in Christ the motions are ordered. Anger is good, which is sorrow for the glory of God, and where there is not such anger, which is called zeal, there is a cold love of God, and a heart that is too sluggish. Just as a brave soldier does not fight without anger: so a brave and sharp teacher cannot but be angry at lies.

This anger is commanded in the first commandment: You shall love the Lord your God. Likewise it is praised in the Psalm: The zeal of your house has eaten me up. Let these brief remarks suffice concerning the affections.

The place of Isaiah XXII.

Matthew cites a place from Isaiah, which contains most sweet doctrine and consolations.

I. He teaches what kind of kingdom the Messiah's will be.

II. That he will receive all sinners who are doing penance, and who flee to him, even if they are weak in gifts and virtues, and are miserable.

And thus he begins: First he names the Messiah: Behold my servant, whom I have chosen, in whom my soul is well pleased. When he names this Messiah the chosen servant, he distinguishes him from other servants, such as Abraham, David, the Prophets, and others. And he signifies that this one is peculiarly promised, for whose sake the others are pleasing.

Therefore he describes him thus, that his soul is delighted in this servant, as it is said in Matthew 17: This is my beloved son. In whom I have my delight and joy.

And this description in Isaiah is to be diligently considered and thought upon, agreeing with the heavenly voice? In whom I am well pleased, so that from there we may learn that this son is primarily loved by God, and for his sake others are received, not that others are loved without him.

And it is added in the text, what kind of kingdom will be theirs. Concerning the kingdom of this son.

He will not be an earthly king, therefore it is said: I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles, that is, he shall rule by the preaching of the Gospel, and by giving the Holy Spirit. He shall not cry out. That is, he shall not have royal pomp, nor will he show partiality.

This is a sweet consolation, that he receives all who flee to him, without partiality, that is, He is the same toward all equally, He punishes sin in all, and condemns all who do not flee to him, be they wise, mighty, or of great virtue as they wish. Conversely, he also receives equally all who flee to him, whether they have great virtue or not, whether they are small or great, weak or mighty. And this must be well impressed upon the heart, that God is impartial, that he is without partiality, just as Paul says: God is rich unto all who call upon him.

Latin:

Caput XII.

Prima historia continet: I. Doctrinam de reprehensione humanarum traditionum, quae pluris fiebant quam lex Dei, ut in consuetudine proximi temporis, maius peccatum fuit carnes die sexto edere, quam alterius coniugi insidiari.

II. Discrimen de operibus. Moralia anteferantur ceremonialibus.

Et hic tractetur eruditissima sententia Oseae: Misericordiam volo, non sacrificium, et agnitionem Dei plus quam holocausta. Fuit haud dubie generalis sententia, tradita contra superstitionem. Quia usitatissimum est homines amissa luce fidei, amplecti ceremonias, imo traditiones humanas, et in his collocare totum cultum Dei.

Huic errori opposita est haec sententia, quae praecipit de veris cultibus, agnitione Dei, et de misericordia. Agnitione Dei est verus timor Dei, et vera fides.

Nosse quod Deus vere irascatur peccato, et vere remittat propter filium, exaudiat etc. Misericordia est dilectio proximi etc.

Haec potiora sunt ceremoniis, et multo potiora traditionibus humanis. Hunc intellectum vult Deus in Ecclesia extare, et de hac re ante annos 28. mota sunt certamina.

Potius est mandatum Dei, esse maritum, quam esse coelibem, iuxta traditionem humanam. Dominus est filius hominis etiam Sabbati.

Simplicissima sententia est, quod Messias sit supra legem. Reprehendit autem stultam opinionem Pharisaeorum, qui nec observationem Sabbati recte intelligebant, nec norant Messiam, sed putabant tempore Messiae mansuras esse ceremonias Moisi, et has esse iustitiam, quam Messias allaturus esset, nec intelligebant iustitiam fidei. Horum errorum magnus erat cumulus, hunc totum cumulum reprehendit hoc dicto, quasi dicat: Vos coeci, nec legem intelligitis, nec nostis Messiam, putatis hanc observationem ceremoniae esse iustitiam, et somniatis Messiam nihil aliud allaturum esse, nisi talem legis observationem.

Imo propter aliam causam lex de Sabbato tradita est, scilicet, ut sit dies destinatus ministerio doctrinae legis et promissionum. Messias vero adfert aeternam iustitiam et vitam, non has ceremonias, quarum finis erit in vita aeterna, ubi erit verum Sabbatum in adsiduo conspectu Dei.

Sicut Esaias inquit: Erit Sabbatum ex Sabbato. Extende manum.

Secunda disputatio, quae proxime sequitur, est eiusdem doctrinae de Sabbato repetitio et exemplum.

Hic Christus reprehendit malum intellectum Sabbati, et postea facit opus, quod vere est opus Sabbati, quia est testimonium doctrinae.

Hic igitur breviter rursus dicatur, quare Sabbatum est institutum. Nominatim dicitur de sanctificatione: Sanctum sanctifica. Non dicit: Sis otiosus. Sed in eo die facias opera sancta, id est, proprie tribuas eum diem ministerio doctrinae, doctores doceant, populus audiat, omnes conveniant ad discendum et ad publicam praedicationem. Haec est summa mandati, et hic finis est.

Christus igitur iam vere sanctificat Sabbatum, docet, et edit testimonia doctrinae. Sed coeca superstitio fingit otium esse cultum, sicut et tunc traditiones conditae sunt, et adhuc Iudaei traditiones habent. In Sabbato conducunt Christianos, qui coquant, qui decerpant mucos a lychnis etc. Sic et Papistae festos dies instituerunt, sed nos discamus verum intellectum Sabbati.

Iesus iratus circumspexit. Hic discamus non omnem iram peccatum esse.

Quia Deus sic condidit angelos et homines, ut habeant appetitiones, gute begirden und neigung, lieb, furcht, hoffnung, schrecken, zorn, freud. Haec sic condita sunt, sed post lapsum fiunt inordinata. Sed tamen in sanctis frenantur et ad ordinem retrahuntur.

Sic Abraham diligit uxorem et filios, et recte facit. Sed David diligit alienam, et non recte facit, quia discedit ab ordine. Est autem ille ordo iustus, qui congruit cum lege Dei.

Sic in Christo sunt ordinati motus. Ira est bona, quae est dolor pro gloria Dei, et ubi non est talis ira, quae vocatur zelus, ibi frigidus amor Dei est, et nimis pigrum pectus. Sicut fortis miles non pugnat sine ira: sic fortis et acer doctor non potest non irasci mendaciis.

Haec ira praecipitur in primo praecepto: Diligas Dominum Deum tuum. Item laudatur in Psalmo: Zelus domus tuae comedit me. Haec brevia sufficiant de affectibus.

Locus Esaiae XXII.

Citat Matthaeus locum Esaiae, qui continet doctrinam et consolationes dulcissimas.

I. Docet quale regnum Messiae futurum sit.

II. Quod recepturus sit omnes peccatores agentes poenitentiam, et ad eum confugientes, etiam si sint imbecilles in donis et virtutibus, et sint aerumnosi.

Et sic orditur: Primum nominat Messiam: Ecce servus meus, quem elegi, in quo complacitum est mihi. Quando nominat hunc Messiam servum electum, discernit eum ab aliis servis, ut ab Abraham, Davide, Prophetis et aliis. Et significat hunc peculiariter promissum, propter quem caeteri placent.

Ideo sic eum describit, quod anima eius delectetur hoc servo, sicut dicitur Matth. 17: Hic est filius meus dilectus.

Daran ich mein wonn vnd freud habe. Et diligenter consideranda et cogitanda est haec descriptio in Esaia, congruens cum voce coelesti?

In quo mihi complacitum est, ut inde discamus hunc filium principaliter diligia Deo, et propter eum caeteros recipi, non diligi alios sine eo. Et additur in textu, quale sit regnum eis futurum.

De regno huius filii. Non erit rex mundanus, ideo dicitur: Dedi spiritum meum super eum: iudicium gentibus proferet, id est, reget praedicatione Evangelii, et dando spiritum sanctum. Non clamabit. Id est, non habebit pompam regiam, nec personam accipiet.

Haec est dulcis consolatio, quod omnes recipiat confugientes ad ipsum, sine acceptatione personarum, id est, Er ist gleich gegen allen gleichen, Er strafft Sünd in allen, vnd verdampt alle die nicht zu jm fliehen, sie sind weiß, mechtig, großer tugend wie sie wollen. Dagegen nimpt er auch an zu gleich alle die zu jm fliehen, sie haben große tugend oder nicht, sie sind klein oder groß, schwach oder mechtig. Et hoc bene inculcandum est cordi, quod Deus sit aequalis, quod sit sine acceptatione personarum, sicut Paulus inquit: Dives Deus in omnes, qui invocant eum.

## 12:20 Sermons on Matthew
A bruised reed he shall not break, and smoking flax he shall not extinguish.

Here he says clearly that he receives the infirm and the terrified, just as Isaiah also teaches elsewhere, where he says that God dwells in the terrified and the afflicted.

Both must be learned: that God condemns carnal security and demands contrition, that is, repentance or conversion, just as he condemns the secure Pharaoh, the secure Pharisees, who were opposing Christ.

The second thing that is learned is this: just as he condemns the secure, so he truly wishes to receive the terrified, if they flee to him.

Therefore he says: Smoking flax. Let there not be absolutely no heat or fire in the flax, but let there be something, that is, let there be an acknowledgment of the Son of God, and a petition that he may receive us, that he may heal us, etc.

Example. What is David in exile and in flight? Is he not then truly a bruised reed, is he not the most miserable of all men, and horribly prostrated? And he is flax, not indeed now having a beautiful light, as before when he flourished in glory and victories, but he is smoking flax; he still has some fire, he does not rage against God, he does not despair, but he still approaches God and asks that he be received and saved.

Compare this example to this text. And let each one most diligently fix these words in their hearts: A bruised reed he shall not break, and smoking flax he shall not extinguish: In his name the Gentiles shall hope.

Here he teaches about the manner, how this Messiah is going to save others. The Gentiles shall hope, that is, they shall embrace this Lord by faith and hope, and thus they shall be saved by faith and hope.

In his name, that is, in the acknowledgment or invocation of him. Just as it is said elsewhere in Isaiah: His knowledge shall justify many.

It is necessary that the benefits given through this Son—the remission of sins, reconciliation, righteousness, the Holy Spirit, and eternal life—be preached, acknowledged, and grasped by faith.

The text follows: But the Pharisees hearing it said.

Against these manifest testimonies of God concerning the Son, the Pharisees furiously cry out that he casts out demons by Beelzebub. This is a sad evil, that even among the people of God there are such blasphemers. These men saw the dead raised, and they saw other manifest miracles, and they had the scriptures testifying about this Messiah, that he was to come at that time, that he was not to have an earthly kingdom, that he was to preach and perform miracles, and to suffer.

Against these testimonies of scripture and the corresponding miracles, they nevertheless, demented by their own opinions about an earthly kingdom, fight most audaciously and condemn this Messiah. Let us not, therefore, now marvel at the obstinacy and fury of those who now persecute the Gospel.

Latin:

Calamum quassatum non confringet, et linum fumigans non extinguet.

Hic clare dicit, quod recipiat infirmos et perterrefactos, sicut Esaias etiam alibi docet, ubi ait, quod Deus habitet in perterrefactis et adflictis.

Utrumque discendum est, quod Deus damnet securitatem carnalem, et postulet contritionem, id est, poenitentiam seu conversionem, ut, damnat securum Pharaonem, securos Pharisaeos, qui Christo adversabantur.

Secundum est, quod discitur. Sicut damnat securos, ita vere vult recipere perterrefactos, si ad ipsum confugiunt.

Ideo dicit: Linum fumigans. Non sit prorsus nihil caloris seu ignis in lino, sed sit aliquid, id est, sit agnitio filii Dei, et petitio, ut recipiat nos, ut sanet nos etc.

Exemplum. Quid est David in exilio et in fuga? Nonne tunc vere est calamus quassatus, est omnium hominum miserrimus, et horribiliter prostratus? Et est linum, non quidem iam habens pulcram lucem, ut antea, cum floreret gloria et victoriis, sed est linum fumigans, aliquid adhuc ignis habet, non irascitur Deo, non desperat, sed adhuc accedit ad Deum, et petit, ut recipiatur et servetur.

Hoc exemplum conferte ad hunc textum. Et haec verba diligentissime singuli infigant cordibus: Calamum quassatum non confringet, et linum fumigans non extinguet: In nomine eius gentes sperabunt.

Hic docet de modo, quomodo hic Messias sit alios salvaturus. Gentes sperabunt, id est, fide et spe amplectentur hunc Dominum, et ita erunt salvi fide et spe.

In nomine eius, id est, in agnitione vel invocatione eius. Sicut in Esaia alibi dicitur: Notitia eius iustificabit multos.

Oportet praedicari, agnosci, fide adprehendi beneficia per hunc filium data, remissionem peccatorum, reconciliationem, iustitiam, Spiritum sanctum, et vitam aeternam.

Sequitur textus: Pharisaei autem audientes dixerunt.

Contra haec manifesta testimonia Dei de filio, furenter clamitant Pharisaei, quod eiiciat Daemones, in Beelzebub. Hoc est triste malum, quod etiam in populo Dei sunt tales blasphemi. Isti viderunt resuscitari mortuos, et viderunt alia manifesta miracula, et habebant scripturas testificantes de hoc Messia, quod eo tempore fuerit venturus, quod non fuerit habiturus imperium mundanum, quod fuerit praedicaturus et facturus miracula, et passurus.

Adversus haec testimonia scripturae et miracula congruentia, tamen ipsi dementati suis opinionibus de regno mundano, audacissime pugnant, et hunc Messiam damnant. Non igitur iam miremur pertinaciam et furorem nunc persequentium Evangelium.

## 12:22 Sermons on Matthew
Then there was brought to him one possessed by a demon.

Again he shows the testimony of the doctrine, and let it be said briefly here concerning the miracles of the common doctrine:

I. That they are testimonies of the doctrine.

II. That they are testimonies that this Jesus is the Messiah.

III. That they are examples of promises and application.

A new and great struggle follows.

The impious cry out against these manifest works of God, that demons are cast out through imposture by the Devils.

Christ refutes them, and here he delivers a most serious doctrine concerning three matters. I.

First, concerning the distinction of miracles, which are true and which are false.

II. Concerning neutrals, who do not wish to be in the confession of the Gospel, or do not wish to be associates of the cross, and pretend to be in doubt, and to await the judgment of a synod. The mediators who do not want to be on either side.

III. Concerning the openly blasphemous.

Concerning the first article.

One may ask about the distinction of miracles, since even the Heathens have miracles, which are true, which are false? Likewise: We have seen many miracles performed in the invocation of saints.

Concerning these I answer. Miracles are distinguished in three ways. First, by substance.

Because some are inimitable by the Devil, such as the resurrection of the dead, stopping the sun, etc. These manifestly testify that the one performing them is from God, and that they are done by divine power alone.

And the Church has had many such things from the very beginning, which are to be considered, so that they confirm us that the doctrine of the Church is true.

The Heathens also had miracles, such as, King Tarquin cut a stone with a knife.

Aspasia had a dream that she should anoint her face with roses plucked from the crown of Venus. And thus she was cured, when physicians had despaired of the healing of the ulcers on her face.

Many such things have been done in the worship of Saints, and the Devil can easily do such things. But he cannot raise the dead, etc.

Second difference. Miracles, which are performed by God, are not joined with any manifestly impious command, nor do they manifestly establish an impious cult, as when Heathen prophets predicted some event, they ordered human sacrifices to be slaughtered.

Or they established manifest idolatry and lusts, such as the miracles of Bacchus. Such are not the miracles of the Son of God; they command nothing that conflicts with the commands of God.

And although miracles move the minds of men greatly, yet God ordered them to be compared to the law. If they conflict with the law of God and the express word, then God orders them to be rejected.

Thus the specters of the dead, when they asked for Masses or such things, are to be rejected, because the Devil through these frauds seeks the confirmation of Idols. As I know an honest matron, who was pregnant when her husband died; her husband came to her sitting at the hearth before supper, and the husband was accompanied by a tall monk.

There the husband ordered his wife to be of a tranquil mind, because it was going well with him, but he ordered certain debts to be paid, and three Masses to be celebrated. And afterwards, departing, he gave his hand to his wife, and burned it, so that it became entirely black like coal.

Thus the Devil so vexed the pious matron, to whom it was also afterwards commanded not to believe this specter, but to judge that it had been Demons. And scripture clearly says: Not from the dead [seek] the truth.

Third difference is. True miracles are performed to establish the true recognition of the Son of God, and are performed in the name of the Son of God, and openly curse the Devil, and drive out Devils unwilling and resisting.

But false miracles are performed without mention of the Son of God, and they do not curse the Devils, nor do they always drive them out. These rules about miracles are contained here, when Christ says that he fights with the Devils.

The Devil does not destroy his own kingdom himself. But the Son of God destroys the kingdom of the Devil.

True miracles are performed, not for the confirmation of false doctrine, like the diabolical ones, but are performed with the preaching of true doctrine. Thus he says: I perform miracles, which the Devil cannot imitate, and I expel him resisting, and I do it to establish true doctrine.

Therefore know that my miracles are true. After it has been spoken about the doctrine of miracles, now let consolation also be added.

Peter says: The Devil goes about, seeking whom he may devour. Therefore he always lies in wait for us.

Therefore let us learn here that the Son of God is our guardian, and let us ask that he may drive away the Devils, as it was said: The Son of God came, that he might destroy the works of the Devil.

Concerning neutrals and concerning the blasphemous.

Many think it is wisdom to be silent now, or to conduct themselves as neutrals. But Christ here condemns them: He who does not gather with me, scatters.

Likewise in another place he commands confession: He who confesses me before men, I will confess him before my heavenly father. Therefore let neutrals know, that it is not enough to be silent, but that confession is necessary.

Concerning the blasphemous.

Here the text clearly distinguishes blasphemies from other sins.

Threefold are the sins. First, there are infirmities clinging to the saints, which are evil affections, evil inclination, which the saints resist, and do not indulge against their conscience.

These are to be acknowledged, And they are in every saints in this life [there are] many such things: but yet they do not extinguish faith, as it is said in Rom. 7 and 8: There is no condemnation in those who are in Christ, etc.

Secondly, there are lapses against conscience, as when ...David became an adulterer, and Peter denied that he knew Christ. These things are such that they do not stand together with faith, and if anyone persists in them, he is condemned to eternal punishments: but if he is converted, he is received again, according to that: I live, I do not desire the death of the sinner, but that he be converted and live.

And these sins are offenses against the second table, or they are against the first out of ignorance or out of infirmity, as the Gentiles worshipped Idols against the first table out of ignorance. Peter lapsed out of infirmity. But blasphemies are sins against the first table, when men, knowing and willing, condemn and persecute the acknowledged truth, as the stubborn Epicureans, likewise stubborn Idolaters, as now the Papists, who knowingly defend Idols, and against conscience say that Idols are God, that their Saints are to be invoked, as if they were God, and kill men who do not want to approve of this.

This description is clear enough.

But you say: Why, he says, is it not forgiven? I answer. He says so, and let us not doubt that it is true.

The sentence of God has already been passed upon all blasphemers. Meanwhile, however, we ought to preach repentance to all. And if any are converted, these, however, were not blasphemers against conscience, but sinned either out of ignorance or out of infirmity. Thus Christ and the Apostles preach to the Jews, many of whom were persecuting the Gospel, but out of error or infirmity, who were afterwards converted. Many, however, being openly blasphemous, were not converted.

Latin:

Tunc oblatus est ei Daemonium habens.

Rursus ostendit testimonium doctrinae, et dicatur breviter hic de miraculis communis doctrina:

I. Quod sint testimonia doctrinae.

II. Quod sint testimonia, quod hic Iesus sit Messias.

III. Quod sint exempla promissionum et applicationis.

Sequitur novum et magnum certamen.

Impii contra haec manifesta opera Dei clamant, eiici daemonia per imposturam a Diabolis.

Christus refutat eos, et hic tradit gravissimam doctrinam de tribus materiis. I.

Primum de discrimine miraculorum, quae sint vera, quae sint falsa.

II. De neutralibus, qui nolunt esse in confessione Evangelii, aut nolunt esse socii crucis, et simulant se dubitare, et exspectare iudicium synodi. Die Mitler die keins teils sein wollen.

III. De aperte blasphemis.

De primo articulo.

De discrimine miraculorum quaeri potest, cum etiam Ethnici habeant miracula, quae sint vera, quae falsa? Item: Vidimus multa miracula facta in invocatione sanctorum.

De his respondeo. Tribus modis discernuntur miracula. Primo substantia.

Quia quaedam sunt inimitabilia Diabolis, ut resuscitatio mortuorum, sistere solem etc. Haec manifeste testantur, quod faciens sit a Deo, et quod fiant sola divina potentia.

Et talia habuit Ecclesia inde usque a principio multa, quae cogitanda sunt, ut confirment nos, quod doctrina Ecclesiae vera sit.

Ethnici etiam habuerunt miracula, ut, rex Tarquinius secuit lapidem cultro.

Aspasia habuit somnium, ut ungeret se in facie rosis detractis a corona Veneris. Et ita curata est, cum medici curationem ulcerum in facie desperassent.

Talia multa facta sunt in cultu Sanctorum, et Diabolus facile potest talia facere. Sed mortuos resuscitare non potest, etc.

Secunda differentia. Miracula, quae fiunt a Deo, non sunt coniuncta cum aliquo mandato manifeste impio, nec stabiliunt manifeste cultum impium, ut quando Ethnici vates praedixerunt aliquem eventum, iusserunt mactari humanas hostias.

Vel stabilierunt manifestam idololatriam et libidines, ut Bacchi miracula. Talia non sunt miracula filii Dei, nihil praecipiunt, quod pugnet cum mandatis Dei.

Et quanquam miracula multum movent animos hominum, tamen Deus iussit ea conferri ad legem. Si pugnant cum lege Dei et expresso verbo, tunc iubet Deus ea reiici.

Sic spectra mortuorum, quando petiverunt Missas vel talia, reiicienda sunt, quia Diabolus per has fraudes quaerit confirmationem Idolorum. Ut ego scio honestam matronam, quae mortuo viro erat gravida, venit ad eam maritus sedentem ad focum ante coenam, et marito comes erat longus monachus.

Ibi maritus iussit uxorem tranquillo animo esse, quia secum bene ageretur, sed iubebat quaedam debita solvi, et tres Missas celebrari. Et postea abiens dedit uxori manum, et ussit eam, ut tota fieret atra sicut carbo.

Sic tantum vexavit Diabolus piam matronam, cui etiam postea mandatum est, ne huic spectro crederet, sed iudicaret fuisse Daemones. Et scriptura clare dicit: Non a mortuis veritatem.

Tertia differentia est. Vera miracula fiunt ad stabiliendam agnitionem veram filii Dei, et fiunt in nomine filii Dei, et aperte maledicunt Diabolo, et pellunt Diabolos invitos et repugnantes.

Sed falsa miracula fiunt sine mentione filii Dei, et non maledicunt Diabolis, nec semper eos pellunt. Hae regulae de miraculis hic continentur, quando Christus dicit, pugnare se cum Diabolis.

Diabolus non destruit ipse suum regnum. Sed filius Dei destruit regnum Diaboli.

Miracula vera fiunt, non ad confirmationem falsae doctrinae, ut diabolica, sed fiunt cum praedicatione verae doctrinae. Sic inquit: Ego facio miracula, quae non potest imitari Diabolus, et expello eum repugnantem, et facio ad stabiliendam veram doctrinam.

Ergo scitote mea miracula vera esse. Postquam de doctrina miraculorum dictum est, iam etiam addatur consolatio.

Petrus inquit: Diabolus circumit, quaerens quem devoret. Ergo semper insidiatur nobis.

Ideo hic discamus filium Dei custodem nostrum esse, et petamus, ut depellat Diabolos, sicut dictum est: Filius Dei venit, ut destruat opera Diaboli.

De neutralibus et de blasphemis.

Multi putant sapientiam esse iam tacere, aut gerere se neutrales. Sed Christus hic damnat eos: Qui non congregat mecum, dissipat.

Item alio loco praecipit confessionem: Qui confitetur me coram hominibus, confitebor eum coram patre meo coelesti. Ideo neutrales sciant, non satis esse tacere, sed necessariam esse confessionem.

De blasphemis.

Hic clare discernit textus blasphemias ab aliis peccatis.

Triplicia sunt peccata. Primo, sunt infirmitates haerentes in sanctis, quae sunt mali adfectus, bose neigung, quibus repugnant sancti, et non indulgent contra conscientiam.

Haec agnoscenda sunt, Et sunt omnibus sanctis in hac vita multa talia: sed tamen non exstinguunt fidem, ut Rom. 7. et 8. dicitur: Nulla est damnatio in his, qui sunt in Christo etc.

Secundo sunt lapsus contra conscientiam, ut quando David factus est adulter, et Petrus negavit se nosse Christum. Haec talia sunt, ut non stent simul cum fide, et si quis in eis perseverat, damnatur aeternis poenis: sed si convertitur, rursus recipitur, iuxta illud: Vivo ego, nolo mortem peccatoris, sed ut convertatur et vivat.

Et haec peccata sunt delicta contra secundam tabulam, vel sunt contra primam ex ignorantia vel ex infirmitate, ut Ethnici coluerunt Idola contra primam tabulam ex ignorantia. Petrus est lapsus ex infirmitate. Sed blasphemiae sunt peccata contra primam tabulam, cum homines scientes et volentes agnitam veritatem damnant et persequuntur, ut pertinaces Epicurei, item pertinaces Idololatrae, ut nunc Papistae, qui scientes defendunt Idola, et contra conscientiam dicunt Idola Deum esse, suos Sanctos invocandos esse, tanquam Deum, et occidunt homines, qui nolunt id adprobare.

Haec descriptio satis clara est.

Sed dicis: Quare inquit, non remitti? Respondeo. Sic dicit, et verum esse non dubitemus.

Sententia Dei iam lata est super omnes blasphemos. Interea tamen nos debemus omnibus praedicare poenitentiam. Et si qui convertuntur, hi tamen non fuerunt blasphemi contra conscientiam, sed vel ex ignorantia vel ex infirmitate peccaverunt. Sic Christus et Apostoli praedicant Iudaeis, quorum multi persequebantur Evangelium, sed errore vel infirmitate, qui postea convertebantur. Multi autem aperte blasphemi, non convertebantur.

## 12:38 Sermons on Matthew
Master, we wish to see a sign from you.

Summary.

First, one must inquire about the doctrine, and see whether it agrees with the scriptures previously handed down. Afterwards, one must judge concerning the signs.

That we ought to follow this rule now, there is no doubt. And all who heard the doctrine of Christ at that time, in the time of Christ and the Apostles, ought also to have seen whether it agreed with the Prophetic [doctrine]. But they, having omitted the collation of the doctrine, demand signs, and although many signs were being done, yet they did not want to believe, because they held in their mind a contrary opinion about the Messiah, fighting against the Prophetic description. They wanted such a Messiah who would enrich them, and heap them with wealth and pleasures. They also sought such signs, that, having expelled the Romans, he would hand over the empire to them.

There are, therefore, two gross sins of the Jews.

First, that they neglect the Prophetic doctrine.

Second, that they seek signs, such as pleased them, and did not want to be moved by the signs which had been done before, and were being done daily.

But God does not want us to propose to Him the manner and form of signs, as if someone now were to say: I do not want to believe, unless God does this sign, that He gives me the Turkish kingdom.

Such imaginations are impious, and are to tempt God, because we ought to seek just things, not those prohibited by God. But to seek foreign things is prohibited by God. Likewise, to seek things that are not necessary, but curious.

Therefore John says: Whatever you have asked according to His will, that is, things not prohibited, and not sought out of curiosity, but out of necessity, here God helps. Because He is a helper, in opportunity, that is, in true necessity, not in illicit or curious desires.

But the whole petition of the Jews is a desire for a kingdom, and a curiosity for unnecessary things.

Just as all men always seek many such things.

These things concerning the sin of the Jews are to be well considered, so that we may learn these two things.

First, to judge doctrine from the collation of Scripture.

Second, that we may learn that it is not to be sought that God should indulge our desires or our curiosity, but that necessary things are to be sought.

Christ's Response. Because of these sins, Christ rebukes the Jews, and answers harshly. He calls them an adulterous and wicked generation, that is, a generation that does not keep faith to God, but falls away from God, just as an adulteress from her husband, and only wantonly plays with the glory of the title, that it is the people of God. Just as now the Pope and the Cardinals are truly adulterers, they have fallen away from God, and only wantonly play with the glory of the title of the Church.

Then he responds concerning signs. He does not say that he will give no signs. Rather, he promises the greatest sign of all concerning the resurrection and the destruction of this people. He signifies this when he says: The sign of the Prophet Jonah shall be given to them. They shall have a sign, just as Nineveh did then. I shall revive after death, just as Jonah did, etc. Then this people, because of their unbelief, will be destroyed, etc.

But why does he say: No other sign shall be given? Why does he say this, when he has performed many other greater signs?

I respond. First, there can be an easy answer: that this is the principal sign and the greatest of all, the resurrection from death, and this especially confirms all believers, because this sign clearly shows the omnipotence of Christ. Likewise, it initiates eternal life before the Church, which existed then, before Mary and the Apostles, etc.

But there is also another answer as to why he says: No other sign shall be given, namely, although I do many things, yet no other sign will pertain to these unbelievers, except the sign of Jonah, that is, except the destruction of this kingdom, which will be a testimony that I have not been a False Prophet.

Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, because he preached, and he alleged as testimony of his calling his deliverance from the whale. And the preaching was effective; this too is a sign.

Likewise, he threatened them with destruction. And although the destruction was delayed because of their repentance, yet after some years, when idolatry was resumed, Nineveh perished, 60 years after Jonah.

The history of Jonah contains an image of the preaching, passion, and resurrection of Christ.

Apply it. And let a useful admonition be added, that because of repentance God even revokes his own predictions, and does not carry them out. Just as Jeremiah 38 says to Zedekiah: If you repent, Jerusalem will not be captured.

Latin:

Magister, volumus a te signum videre.

Summa.

Primum quaerendum est de doctrina, et videndum an consentiat cum scripturis antea traditis. Postea iudicandum est de signis.

Hanc regulam nos nunc oportere sequi non dubium est. Et debebant tunc quoque tempore Christi et Apostolorum videre omnes, qui audiebant doctrinam Christi, an congrueret cum Prophetica. Sed ipsi omissa collatione doctrinae postulant signa, et quanquam fiebant multa signa, tamen credere nolebant, quia tenebant in mente contrariam opinionem de Messia, pugnantem cum Prophetica descriptione. Talem Messiam volebant, qui eos ditaret, et opibus et voluptatibus eos cumularet. Talia etiam signa petebant, ut expulsis Romanis traderet ipsis imperium.

Duo sunt igitur crassa peccata Iudaeorum.

Primum, quod doctrinam Propheticam negligunt.

Secundum, quod petunt signa, qualia ipsis placebant, et non volebant moveri signis, quae antea facta erant, et quotidie fiebant.

Non vult autem Deus nos sibi modum et formam signorum proponere, ut si quis nunc dicat: Nolo credere, nisi Deus hoc signum faciat, ut mihi det regnum Turcicum.

Tales imaginationes sunt impiae, et sunt tentare Deum, quia nos debemus petere iusta, non prohibita a Deo. Petere autem res alienas, est prohibitum a Deo. Item petere non necessaria, sed curiosa.

Ideo inquit Iohannes: Quidquid petiveritis secundum voluntatem eius, id est, res non prohibitas, et non curiositate petitas, sed ex necessitate, hic Deus opitulatur. Quia est adiutor, in opportunitate, id est, in vera necessitate, non cupiditatibus illicitis, aut curiosis.

Tota autem petitio Iudaeorum est cupiditas regni, et non necessariarum rerum curiositas.

Sicut semper multa talia omnes homines petunt.

Haec de peccato Iudaeorum bene consideranda sunt, ut haec duo discamus.

Primum, iudicare doctrinam ex collatione Scripturae.

Secundum, ut discamus, non esse petendum, ut cupiditatibus aut curiositati nostrae Deus morem gerat, sed necessaria petenda esse.

Responsis Christi. Propter haec peccata obiurgat Christus Iudaeos, et duriter respondet. Nominat eos genus adulterum et pravum, id est, genus quod non servat Deo fidem, sed deficit a Deo, sicut adultera a viro, et tantum petulanter ludit gloria tituli, quod sit populus Dei. Sicut nunc Papa et Cardinales vere sunt adulteri, defecerunt a Deo, et tantum ludunt petulanter gloria tituli Ecclesiae.

Deinde de signis respondet. Non dicit se nulla signa daturum esse. Imo promittit signum omnium summum de resurrectione et excidio huius populi. Hoc significat, cum ait: Dabitur eis signum Ionae Prophetae. Habebunt signum, sicut tunc Ninive. Ego post mortem reviviscam, sicut Ionas, etc. Deinde hic populus propter incredulitatem delebitur, etc.

Sed quare dicit: Non dabitur aliud signum? Cur sic dicit, cum multa alia signa maiora fecerit?

Respondeo. Prima potest esse facilis responsio, quod hoc sit principale signum et omnium summum, resurrectio ex morte, et hoc praecipue confirmat omnes credentes, quia hoc signum manifeste ostendit omnipotentiam Christi. Item inchoat vitam aeternam coram Ecclesia, quae tunc fuit, coram Maria et Apostolis, etc.

Sed est et altera responsio, quare dicat: Non aliud signum dabitur, scilicet, quanquam multa facio, tamen non aliud pertinebit ad istos incredulos, nisi signum Ionae, id est, nisi deletio huius regni, quae erit testimonium, quod non fuerim Pseudopropheta.

Ionas fuit signum Ninivitis, quia praedicavit, et allegavit testimonium vocationis suae liberationem ex coeto. Et praedicatio fuit efficax, hoc quoque est signum.

Item, minatus est eis exitium. Et quanquam dilatum est excidium propter poenitentiam, tamen post aliquot annos recepta Idololatria, periit Ninive, 60. annis post Ionam.

Historia Ionae continet imaginem praedicationis, passionis, et resurrectionis Christi.

Adplicate. Et adijciatur utilis admonitio, quod propter poenitentiam Deus etiam suas proprias praedicationes revocat, et non exsequitur. Sicut Ieremias 38. dicit ad Sedechiam: Si egeris poenitentiam, non capietur Ierusalem.

## 12:41 Sermons on Matthew
The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment. The Queen of the South shall rise, etc.

The threat is taken from examples. Others performed repentance who did not see such great miracles, nor did they have such great revelation. You do not perform repentance, when you hear the Son of God himself, when you see constant miracles. Therefore, great punishments hang over you, as we see.

Germany has had great gifts, great light, greater than before, as it is necessary to admit. It began to abuse those gifts for luxury, for pride, for gluttony, and for other vices.

Therefore, such a great punishment has followed, as has never been in Germany.

Latin:

Viri Ninivitae surgent in iudicio. Regina Austri surget, etc.

Comminatio est ab exemplis sumta. Alii egerunt poenitentiam, qui non viderunt tanta miracula, nec tantam revelationem habuerunt. Vos non agitis poenitentiam, cum audiatis ipsum filium Dei, cum videatis assidua miracula. Ergo magnae vobis poenae impendent, sicut videmus.

Germania habuit magna dona, magnam lucem, maiorem, quam antea, ut fateri necesse est. Coepit abuti illis donis ad luxum, ad superbiam, ad crapulam, et ad alia vitia.

Ideo tanta poena secuta est, quanta etiam nunquam fuit in Germania.

## 12:42 Sermons on Matthew
There are three kinds of hearers.

I. The first are those who do not perform repentance at all, who are persecutors and enemies.

II. The second are others, who begin to perform repentance, but return to their former vices.

III. The third are the few who perform repentance, and persevere in faith and fear.

Here he speaks of the second kind. And it is a terrible sermon: The last things become worse than the first.

Just as happened to Jerusalem after the crucifixion of Christ, all of Judea was full of impiety, seditions, murders, and all horrible evils. And such are already the beginnings among us, which I wish God would amend. For certainly great and horrible and unheard-of evils will follow, unless God by his mercy mitigates the punishments.

The Cause.

But what is the cause of such great evils after the preaching has been heard? Idleness and security in those who began to perform repentance, and afterwards become more negligent and secure, seeking pleasures, wealth, power. When the Devil sees this idleness and this security, he breaks in as if through an opened gate.

Concerning this security, it is often said elsewhere, as in Matt. 24: Watch, for you do not know at what hour the Lord is to come. Likewise, in the parable of the fig tree, which is rooted out when it does not bear fruit after cultivation, etc.

And Jeremiah: They did not know how to blush, but if now these great calamities do not make us more modest, then truly much sadder punishments will come. There will be new civil wars, the Turks will come, and they will reduce this most beautiful part of the whole human race, namely the Churches in Germany, into desolation and solitude, just as Asia and Greece are now solitudes.

There is no need for a more subtle explanation in this text. But there is a need for consideration of the wrath of God and the examples, and for such hearts of the hearers, that they may tremble and be moved by such a terrible threat, and perform repentance, and cry out to God, that He may mitigate the punishments.

While He was still speaking. Since He answers so harshly those who are calling out about His mother and brothers, it is sufficiently apparent that He was burning with great anger at that time, when He gave that former terrible sermon. And in this anger He answers more harshly.

But the doctrine is useful, that He calls all those His brothers and members who hear the word of God and obey the word of God. And those who are not such, even if they were brothers by nature, this would profit them nothing.

Let us hold onto this consolation, and let us often think of these two things: The first concerning anger against sin, that it is so great that it could not be taken away except through the Son of God.

The second concerning mercy. It is very necessary to love the human race from God, because He gave His Son to us, and willed that He assume human nature, so that we might know that the human race is truly loved by Him, since He is our brother, and bone of our bones.

But therefore it was necessary for the Son of God to assume human nature, because it was necessary for a man to sustain the punishment for the human race. And yet no one was an equal price, and no one could have sustained the punishment unless He were at the same time God. These things must be thought of often, so that we may rouse ourselves to repentance, and so that consolation may kindle invocation.

Latin:

Tria sunt genera auditorum.

I. Primum sunt prorsus non agentes poenitentiam, qui sunt persecutores et hostes.

II. Secundo sunt alii, qui incipiunt agere poenitentiam, sed redeunt ad priora vitia.

III. Tertio sunt pauci agentes poenitentiam, et perseverantes in fide et timore.

Hic dicit de secundo genere. Et est terribilis concio: Fiunt novissima peiora prioribus.

Sicut accidit Ierosolymae post crucifixionem Christi, tota Iudaea fuit plena impietatis, seditionum, caedium et omnium horribilium malorum. Et talia sunt iam principia apud nos, quae utinam Deus emendet. Quia certe magna et horribilia et inaudita mala sequentur, nisi Deus sua misericordia poenas mitigabit.

Causa.

Sed quae causa est tantorum malorum post auditam praedicationem? Otium et securitas in his, qui coeperunt agere poenitentiam, et postea fiunt negligentiores et securi, quaerunt voluptates, opes, potentiam. Hoc otium et hanc securitatem cum videt Diabolus, irrumpit tanquam per portam patefactam.

De hac securitate saepe alias dicitur, ut Matth. 24.: Vigilate, quia nescitis qua hora venturus sit Dominus. Item, in parabola de ficu, quae eradicatur, cum post culturam non fert fructum etc.

Et Ieremias: Erubescere nescierunt, sed si nunc hae tantae calamitates non faciunt nos modestiores, tunc profecto multo tristiores poenae venient. Erunt nova bella intestina, venient Turci, et hanc pulcherrimam partem totius generis humani, videlicet Ecclesias in Germania, redigent in vastitatem et solitudinem, sicut Asia, sicut Graecia nunc sunt solitudines.

Non opus est in hoc textu alia declaratione subtiliore. Sed opus est consideratione irae Dei et exemplorum, et talibus auditorum cordibus, quae expavescant et moveantur tam terribili comminatione, et agant poenitentiam, et clament ad Deum, ut poenas mitiget.

Adhuc eo loquente. Cum tam duriter respondeat interpellantibus de matre et fratribus, satis adparet magna eum ira tunc flagrasse, cum illam priorem terribilem concionem habuit. Et in ista ira durius respondet.

Sed doctrina utilis est, quod ipse fratres et membra sua esse dicit omnes, qui audiunt verbum Dei, et verbo Dei obediunt. Et qui non sunt tales, etiamsi essent natura fratres, hoc nihil eis prodesset.

Hanc consolationem teneamus, et saepe cogitemus haec duo: Alterum de ira adversus peccatum, quod tanta sit, ut non potuerit tolli, nisi per filium Dei.

Alterum de misericordia. Necesse est valde diligit genus humanum a Deo, quod filium suum nobis donavit, et hunc voluit assumere naturam humanam, ut sciremus vere diligit ab eo genus humanum, cum sit frater noster, et os ex ossibus nostris.

Ideo autem oportuit filium Dei adsumere humanam naturam, quia oportuit hominem sustinere poenam pro genere humano. Et tamen nemo erat aequale pretium, et nemo potuisset sustinere poenam, nisi simul esset Deus. Haec saepe cogitanda sunt, ut nos ad poenitentiam exsuscitemus, et ut consolatio accendat invocationem.

## 12:43 Sermons on Matthew
When the unclean spirit has gone out.

Latin:

Cum autem immundus spiritus exierit.

## 13:1 Sermons on Matthew: Argument
Chapter XIII. Concerning the Church.

There follow many images of the Church, in which necessary doctrine and consolation are proposed.

But first it must be known why Christ said this. Because the Jews hoped that the kingdom of Christ would be a worldly empire. He, on the contrary, here and often elsewhere teaches that His Church is not a worldly empire.

We also have always thought and do think that there will be beautiful empires and a splendid political state. But the outcome does not agree with this imagination.

Let us learn, therefore, that empires are one thing, the Church another, and because of the mutation of empires, let us not lose eternal things.

God variously transfers kingdoms, on account of the sins of princes and the people. But meanwhile the Church remains wherever the voice of the Gospel sounds correctly.

Therefore, this doctrine is to be taken from this similitude.

I. That empires are one thing, the Church another.

II. That the Church is gathered through the word of God, and that God is effective through this voice of the ministers.

What the Church of God is.

But an optimal and true definition can be taken from this text, which all Christians ought to know. The Church is the assembly of those who embrace the Gospel, and who use the Sacraments according to the institution of the Gospel, in which assembly God is effective through the ministry of the Gospel, and regenerates many to eternal life, even if there are many in the same assembly in this life who are not reborn, but yet are consenting to the doctrine.

It is necessary that this definition be known, so that we may know what the Church is and where it is, because it is necessary for men to understand the article of faith: I believe there is a Catholic Church, and it is necessary for individuals to know whether they are members of the Church, and why they are members of the Church, because the saying is true: Outside the Church of God there is no salvation.

Learn, therefore, that these three things are necessary for this, that a man may be a member of the Church, namely: to embrace the doctrine of the Gospel, to use the Sacraments according to the institution, and to obey the ministry in those things which properly pertain to the ministry. If a man finds these in his mind and will, he is certainly a member of the Church.

And when he truly performs repentance and believes in the Gospel, he is a living member, and God hears him, and is effective in him.

Furthermore, no similarity is required in human laws, such as in the eating of meats, or similar indifferent things, as Paul clearly says: Let no one judge you in food and in drink.

Likewise, no one is a member of the Church of God who pertinaciously defends a heretical article, or a law commanding a work against divine mandates, as the Synod now hands down articles that are manifestly heretical, because it is necessary to always doubt about the remission of sins.

Likewise, that human satisfaction for sins is necessary.

Likewise, those laws are impious which prohibit marriage. Those who stubbornly defend such things openly fight against the word of God; therefore, they are not members of the Church of God.

But you should look to the true and fundamental causes that make one a member of the Church, and know for certain that you are a member of the Church of God when you find those causes in your mind and will, as I have said: the reception and confession of pure doctrine, the legitimate use of the Sacraments, and obedience toward the ministry in those things that pertain to the ministry.

If you find these in your mind and will, know that you are a member of the true Church, and call upon God with this faith; and if you have faith and a good conscience, know that your invocation is truly heard.

This is the kingdom of the Messiah, and this is the assembly that is born, with this farmer sowing.

This is the highest consolation: to know that even when empires are falling, the Church is something else, and we are heard by God, and we shall have another, eternal kingdom.

Furthermore, this parable also conveys this consolation; it consoles us against the multitude of the impious.

The Church is not therefore non-existent, even if many are impious, enemies of the truth, or Apostates, etc.

Conclusion.

Let us learn this summary from this text, and let us most diligently instruct ourselves about the Church, so that we may know what it is and where it is.

And let us not think that the Church is invisible.

Indeed, you and I and all who confess the true doctrine are the Church, which is perceived by the eyes and heard by the ears, just as it is written: Their sound has gone out into all the earth.

And let us strive to be in this true Church; let us flee the impious assembly, just as Paul says: If anyone teaches another Gospel, let him be anathema.

Conversely, God will hear us, just as it is written: Wherever two or three shall be in my name, that is, truly acknowledging and calling upon me, I am in their midst.

Thus the Church is described, and in this saying: If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him, and make our dwelling with him, that is, if anyone is a guardian of true doctrine.

If anyone embraces true doctrine, this person is truly a member of the Church and a temple of God.

This is the summary of this first similitude.

Next, we shall speak of the parts.

I. On the smallness of the true Church.

With many listening, and not persecuting, yet few are the good soil.

II. On the blinding of the impious.

Seeing, they may not see.

This is the punishment of those who despise, just as Sodom became blinder, having despised Shem, who was in the vicinity and often preached there, and likewise Lot.

Differences of men in the Church.

The first degree of seed sown along the path.

These are the wise, from whom the word of God is shaken away, not because of common infirmities, persecution, pleasures, riches, or poverty.

These do not move the wise to such an extent, but there is a singular evil, which is described here, that the word is snatched away from them by the Devil; they become Epicureans, just as the leading men are now almost everywhere, but especially in Italy.

When they think about religion for a long time, they eventually lose it entirely, because their reason is offended that certain things are handed down in the Gospel that are incomprehensible.

Likewise, they see the smallness of the Church, its infirmity, the power of the Turks, of empires, etc.

Second degree: upon the rocks.

These are fervent at the beginning, but later depart in persecution, like the Apostles when Christ was being crucified.

Third degree: among the thorns.

Those who, through idleness, avarice, and ambition, become more negligent, just as all the Lutheran cities are properly depicted here.

God gave peace, He gave other goods, and therefore ambition, pomp, and avarice grew among the people and the teachers.

If you wish to know what the status of our cities is everywhere, look at this description, and carefully weigh the word 'choked'.

Courts are choked by courtly cares about their pomp, their revenues, and buildings.

Teachers are choked by idleness, avarice, and ambition, and the people as well.

Thus the Gospel is gradually extinguished, and from such beginnings follows blindness and contempt.

Afterward come punishments, Turks, and other evils.

Fourth degree: of the seed sown in good soil.

The pious bearing fruit with patience.

He adds a mark that distinguishes them from the former.

Where there is patience, there is persecution, danger, invocation, the exercise of faith, there is no place for idleness, none for avarice, none for ambition. Thus the Church endures, thus the Gospel is preserved in such exercises, just as in Babylon there was greater glory for the afflicted Church, of Daniel and others, who did not want to worship the statue, than there had been before in the idleness of Jerusalem.

They conclude with an exhortation, that we fear the punishments placed here: Seeing they may not see, etc. To everyone who has, it will be given, etc.

This sentence is a useful consolation for the infirm and for beginners, who nevertheless are not slothful, and have a desire to learn and to progress in life and doctrine. And on the contrary, there is a sad threat against the contemners of doctrine and persecutors. Even that which they have, will be taken away.

Let the application be made.

Many men are anxious and think: I feel my own infirmity, I do not have such virtues as I ought to have, I do not know if I please God, and they fall into great doubt, which hinders the invocation of some. And some from this temptation rush into despair, or into contempt of God.

Here let us be vigilant, and let us fortify ourselves against this temptation, and let this most firm rule be held: As I live, I do not desire the death of the sinner, but that he be converted and live. If you have some contrition and do not retain sins against your conscience, then it is a divine command that you believe that your sins are remitted to you on account of our Lord Jesus Christ, and that you then please God, not on account of your own purity, but on account of the intercessor, the Son of God. And after you are such, now know that you are in this number, of whom it is said: To him who has, it will be given. You have the beginnings of faith, therefore ask for increase, then God will without doubt hear you and help you.

This is a doctrine very useful for consolation against the sight of our infirmity. The same is taught in this saying: It is God who works in you, both to will and to perform, so that some good things may be done that are pleasing to Him. That is, Do not despair on account of your infirmity, just as now certainly the appearance of our Churches is very infirm, many think it will be that shortly the whole doctrine of the Gospel will be destroyed, just as recently the Bishop of Lebus said, as I hear: That around Pentecost there will be no Lutheran in these lands.

But nevertheless God has promised us help, even if we are infirm, God will be present nevertheless, and will help us, so that we may progress, and will preserve the light of doctrine. Such is also in Mark he who says: I believe Lord, but help my unbelief. You have the beginnings, if you are not a contemner of God, and you are anxious, and you desire to progress. Since you have these beginnings, know that you certainly please God, and invoke Him, that He may increase your strength, according to the promise: How much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask. To those who ask He says, not to the swine who contemn, not to the wolves who persecute, but to you who ask, crying out with that one in Mark: I believe Lord, but bring aid to my weakness.

Consider this consolation in this text well. For it profits individuals and the community. God does not want to neglect you, just as was said above: A smoldering flax He will not extinguish. So also our whole Church, groaning and crying out, although it is already afflicted, He wants to preserve etc.

On the contrary, Epicureans and persecutors, who now do not want to hear the Gospel, will lose the whole light of doctrine, and will quickly fall away, even if it will be necessary for us to endure the cross for some time. Nevertheless God will preserve us and will deliver us and will console us.

Another parable.

Latin:

Caput XIII. De Ecclesia.

Sequuntur multae imagines Ecclesiae, in quibus doctrina et consolatio necessaria proposita est.

Primum autem sciendum est, quare haec Christus dixerit. Quia Iudaei sperabant regnum Christi fore imperium mundanum. Ipse contra hic et saepe alias docet, Ecclesiam suam non esse imperium mundanum.

Nos quoque semper cogitavimus et cogitamus fore pulcra imperia, et statum politicum speciosum. Sed eventus non congruit cum hac imaginatione.

Discamus igitur aliud esse imperia, aliud Ecclesiam, et propter mutationem imperiorum, non amittamus aeterna.

Deus varie transfert regna, propter peccata principum et populi. Sed interea manet Ecclesia ubicunque recte sonat vox Evangelii.

Doctrina igitur ex hac similitudine sumenda est haec.

I. Quod aliud sint imperia, aliud Ecclesia.

II. Quod Ecclesia per verbum Dei colligatur, et quod Deus per hanc vocem ministrorum sit efficax.

Quid sit Ecclesia Dei.

Sumi autem potest optima et vera definitio ex hoc textu, quam omnes Christiani scire debent. Ecclesia est coetus amplectentium Evangelium, et utentium Sacramentis iuxta institutionem Evangelii, in quo coetu Deus est efficax per ministerium Evangelii, et multos regenerat ad vitam aeternam, etsi multi sunt in eodem coetu in hac vita, qui non sunt renati, sed tamen de doctrina consentientes.

Hanc definitionem sciri necesse est, ut quae sit Ecclesia, et ubi sit, sciamus, quia oportet homines intelligere articulum fidei: Credo esse Ecclesiam Catholicam, et oportet singulos scire, an sint membra Ecclesiae, et cur sint membra Ecclesiae, quia verum est dictum: Extra Ecclesiam Dei non est salus.

Discatis ergo haec tria necessaria esse ad hoc, ut homo sit membrum Ecclesiae, videlicet, amplecti Evangelii doctrinam, uti Sacramentis iuxta institutionem, obedire ministerio, in his, quae proprie ad ministerium pertinent. Haec si invenit homo in sua mente et voluntate, certo est membrum Ecclesiae.

Et cum vere agit poenitentiam et credit Evangelio, est vivum membrum, et Deus eum exaudit, et est in eo efficax.

Caeterum non requiritur similitudo in legibus humanis, ut in esu carnium, aut similibus mediis rebus, ut Paulus clare dicit: Nemo vos iudicet in cibo et in potu.

Item, nemo est membrum Ecclesiae Dei, qui pertinaciter defendit articulum haereticum, aut legem praecipientem opus contra mandata divina, ut Synodus nunc tradit articulos manifeste haereticos, quod oporteat semper dubitare de remissione peccatorum.

Item, quod satisfactio humana pro peccatis necessaria sit.

Item leges impiae sunt, quae prohibent coniugium. Talia pertinaciter defendentes manifeste pugnant cum verbo Dei, ideo non sunt membra Ecclesiae Dei.

Sed tu videas veras et fundamentales causas, quae faciunt membrum Ecclesiae, et certo scias, te esse membrum Ecclesiae Dei, cum illas causas in tua mente et voluntate invenies, ut dixi, doctrinae purae receptionem et confessionem, usum legitimum Sacramentorum, et obedientiam erga ministerium in his, quae ad ministerium pertinent.

Haec si invenis in tua mente et voluntate, scito te esse membrum verae Ecclesiae, et Deum hac fide invocato, et si habes fidem et bonam conscientiam, scias vere exaudiri tuam invocationem.

Hoc est regnum Messiae, et hic est coetus, qui nascitur, seminante hoc agricola.

Haec est summa consolatio, scire etiam ruentibus imperiis, tamen aliud esse Ecclesiam, et nos a Deo exaudiri, et habituros aliud regnum aeternum.

Deinde et hanc consolationem haec parabola tradit, consolatur nos contra multitudinem impiorum.

Non ideo nulla est Ecclesia, etiamsi multi sunt impii, hostes veritatis, aut Apostatae, etc.

Conclusio.

Hanc summam discamus ex hoc textu, et diligentissime nos ipsos erudiamus de Ecclesia, ut sciamus quae sit et ubi sit.

Et non cogitemus Ecclesiam esse invisibilem.

Imo tu et ego et omnes veram doctrinam confitentes sunt Ecclesia, quae oculis cernitur, et auribus auditur, sicut scriptum est: In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum.

Et studeamus esse in hac vera Ecclesia, fugiamus impium coetum, sicut Paulus inquit: Si quis aliud Evangelium docet, anathema sit.

Econtra nos exaudiet Deus, sicut scriptum est: Ubicunque erunt duo aut tres in nomine meo, id est, me vere agnoscentes et invocantes, in medio eorum sum.

Sic describitur Ecclesia, et in hoc dicto: Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit, et Pater meus diliget eum, et veniemus ad eum, et mansionem apud eum faciemus, id est, si quis est custos verae doctrinae.

Si quis veram doctrinam amplectitur, hic est vere membrum Ecclesiae, et templum Dei.

Haec est summa huius primae similitudinis.

Proxime de partibus dicetur.

I. De parvitate Ecclesiae verae.

Multis audientibus, et non persequentibus, tamen pauci sunt bona terra.

II. De excoecatione impiorum.

Videntes non videant.

Haec est poena contemnentium, sicut Sodoma facta est coecior, contemto Sem, qui erat in vicinia, et ibi saepe praedicavit, item Loth.

Differentiae hominum in Ecclesia.

Primus gradus seminis secus viam iacti.

Hi sunt sapientes, quibus excutitur verbum Dei non propter vulgares infirmitates, persecutionem, voluptates, divitias, paupertatem.

Hae non movent sapientes usque adeo, sed est singulare malum, quod hic describitur, quod per Diabolum eripitur eis verbum, fiunt Epicurei, sicut iam praecipui homines fere ubique, sed maxime in Italia.

Quando diu cogitant de religione, tandem eam prorsus amittunt, quia ratio offenditur, quod quaedam traduntur in Evangelio incomprehensibilia.

Item vident Ecclesiae parvitatem, infirmitatem, potentiam Turcorum, imperiorum, etc.

Secundus gradus: supra saxa.

Hi sunt principio ferventes, postea in persecutione discedentes, Apostolici cum crucifigeretur Christus.

Tertius gradus, inter spinas.

Qui otio, avaritia, ambitione fiunt negligentiores, sicut proprie hic depinguntur omnes Lutheranae civitates.

Deus dedit pacem, dedit alia bona, ideo crevit ambitio, pompa, avaritia, in populo et doctoribus.

Si vis scire qualis sit status nostrarum civitatum ubique, vide hanc descriptionem, et bene expende verbum suffocantur.

Aulae suffocantur curis aulicis de sua pompa, de suis reditibus, aedificiis.

Doctores suffocantur otio, avaritia, ambitione, populus etiam.

Ita exstinguitur Evangelium paulatim, et ex talibus initiis sequitur coecitas et contemtus.

Postea veniunt poenae, Turci et alia mala.

Quartus gradus, de semine iacto in bonam terram.

Pii facientes fructum cum patientia.

Addit notam, quae discernit eos a superioribus.

Ubi est patientia, ibi est persecutio, periculum, invocatio, exercitium fidei, non est otio locus, non avaritiae, non ambitioni. Sic durat Ecclesia, sic conservatur Evangelium in talibus exercitiis, ut in Babylone erat maior gloria Ecclesiae adflictae, Danielis et aliorum, qui nolebant adorare statuam, antea fuerat in otio Ierosolymis.

Concluduntur cum adhortatione, ut metuamus poenas hic positas: Videntes non videant, etc. Omni habenti dabitur, etc.

Haec sententia est utilis consolatio pro infirmis et incipientibus, qui tamen non sunt ignavi, et habent studium discendi et proficiendi in vita et doctrina. Et econtra est tristis comminatio adversus contemtores doctrinae et persecutores. Etiam id quod habent, auferetur.

Fiat adplicatio.

Multi homines anguntur et cogitant: Ego sentio meam infirmitatem, non habeo tantas virtutes, quantas habere debebam, nescio an Deo placeam, et incidunt in magnam dubitationem, quae impedit aliquorum invocationem. Et aliqui ex hac tentatione ruunt in desperationem, vel in contemtum Dei.

Hic simus vigilantes, et muniamus nos contra hanc tentationem, et teneatur haec regula firmissima: Vivo ego, nolo mortem peccatoris, sed ut convertatur et vivat. Si habes aliquam contritionem et non retines peccata contra conscientiam, tunc mandatum divinum est, ut tibi credas remitti peccata propter Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, et quod tunc placeas Deo, non propter tuam munditiem, sed propter intercessorem filium Dei. Et postquam es talis, iam scito te in hoc numero esse, de quo dicitur: Habenti dabitur. Tu habes initia fidei, ergo pete incrementum, tunc Deus haud dubie te exaudiet et iuvabit.

Haec est doctrina valde utilis ad consolationem contra conspectum nostrae infirmitatis. Idem docetur in hoc dicto: Deus est qui facit, ut velitis, et ut perficiatis, ut aliqua bona fiant ipsi grata. Id est, Ne desperes propter tuam infirmitatem, sicut iam certe species Ecclesiarum nostrarum valde est infirma, multi putant fore, ut paulo post deleatur tota doctrina Evangelii, sicut nuper dixit Episcopus Lebusianus, ut audio: Circa Pentecosten nullum fore Lutheranum in his terris.

Sed tamen Deus promisit nobis auxilium, etiamsi sumus infirmi, Deus aderit tamen, et iuvabit nos, ut proficiamus, et servabit lucem doctrinae. Talis est et in Marco ille qui dicit: Credo Domine, sed adiuva incredulitatem meam. Habes initia, si non es contemtor Dei, et angeris, et optas proficere. Haec initia cum habeas, scito te certo placere Deo, et eum invoca, ut tibi vires augeat, iuxta promissionem: Quanto magis Pater vester coelestis dabit Spiritum sanctum petentibus. Petentibus dicit, non porcis contemnentibus, non lupis persequentibus, sed tibi petenti, clamanti cum isto apud Marcum: Credo Domine, sed opem fer meae imbecillitati.

Hanc consolationem in hoc textu bene considerate. Prodest enim singulis et in commune. Deus te non vult negligere, sicut supra dictum est: Linum fumigans non exstinguet. Sic etiam nostram totam Ecclesiam gementem et clamantem, quanquam iam est adflicta, vult servare etc.

Econtra Epicurei et persecutores, qui iam nolunt audire Evangelium, amittent totam doctrinae lucem, et cito delabuntur, etiamsi nos aliquamdiu sustinere crucem oportebit. T'amen Deus servabit nos et liberabit et consolabitur nos.

Alia parabola.

## 13:24-30 The 5th Sunday After Epiphany
The 5th Sunday after Epiphany. Gospel of Matthew.

13. Concerning the Tares.

Another parable He proposed to them, saying: The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field. But while men were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went away. But when the herb had sprouted and produced fruit, then the tares also appeared. And the servants of the householder coming, said to him: Lord, did you not sow good seed in your field? From where then does it have tares? But he said: An enemy man has done this. But the servants said to him: Do you want us then to go and gather them? But he said: No, lest perhaps in gathering the tares, you root up the wheat together with them. Let both grow until the harvest, and in the time of the harvest I will say to the reapers: Gather first the tares, and bind them into bundles, that they may be burned, but gather the wheat into my barn.

There is one principal point of this Gospel, that in the Church it is not permitted to remove the disobedient by force and sword, namely, as it pertains to the ministry of the Apostles and the word, that is, to ecclesiastical power, whose proper office it is not to rebuke men by bodily force, but only by the word. For the kingdom of Christ is a spiritual kingdom, which is governed by the word alone, without the sword.

Now here it is asked: Is it therefore not permitted to remove adulterers, murderers, etc.? For thus someone could argue: Tares are not to be removed; adulterers are tares: therefore adulterers are not to be removed. The whole argument must be conceded as it pertains to the ministry of the word, not as it pertains to civil power.

The civil magistrate has the power of removing adulterers, murderers, and similar openly wicked persons. For the magistrate, as Paul says, is he who bears the sword for the terror of the wicked, to punish them. Likewise: The law is set for the unjust, and there are three causes of civil punishments.

The first is the Justice of God. The second, Example. The third, Public peace, as is said more prolixly elsewhere.

Is it permitted for the magistrate to punish heretics? For the magistrate is the guardian of the whole law, that is, not only of the second, but also of the first table, as far as it pertains to external discipline. But the judgment concerning doctrine does not pertain only to the magistrate, but to the whole Church, of which the magistrate is a part. He, therefore, should see to it that he judges with certainty, not as is done now, out of the savagery and cruelty of two or three monks, but according to the opinion of the best and most learned in the Church.

Thus, in the heresy of the Donatists, who imagined a Church in which there were absolutely no vicious people, and contended that Sacraments administered by the wicked were rendered void, the Emperor Constantine committed the judgment to the Roman Bishops, who, having examined the matter, condemned the Donatists, and they were unwilling to abide by this judgment. The Emperor instituted a convention at Arles, where, being present himself, he judged the matter and passed sentence against the Donatists, and so that they might be afflicted with some penalty, he transferred their ecclesiastical goods to the true Church.

Thus, in sum, this Gospel teaches that the Apostles should not, under the pretext of the Gospel, seize the sword and establish a worldly kingdom, which is far different from the kingdom of Christ.

But Paul speaks of their office: Rebuke, argue, with all authority. By which words Paul signifies that ecclesiastical power can command in those things which are of divine law, and that it must necessarily be obeyed. For this is what ἐπιταγή (command) signifies.

Latin:

Dominica V. post Epiphania. Evangelium Matth.

13. De Zizaniis.

Aliam parabolam proposuit eis dicens: Simile est regnum coelorum homini, qui seminavit bonum semen in agro suo. Cum autem dormirent homines, venit inimicus eius, et superseminavit zizania in medio tritici, et abiit. Cum autem germinasset herba, et fructum fecisset, tunc apparuerunt et zizania. Accedentes autem servi patrisfamilias, dixerunt ei: Domine, nonne bonum semen seminasti in agro tuo? unde ergo habet zizania? Ille autem ait: Inimicus homo hoc fecit. Servi autem dixerunt ei: Vis ergo ut euntes colligamus ea? Ille autem ait: Non, ne forte colligentes zizania, eradicetis simul cum eis triticum. Sinite utraque crescere usque ad messem, et in tempore messis dicam messoribus: Colligite primum zizania, et colligate ea in fasciculos, ut comburantur, triticum autem congregate in horreum meum.

Unus est praecipuus locus huius Evangelii, quod in Ecclesia non liceat tollere vi et gladio inobedientes, scilicet quod attinet ad ministerium Apostolorum et verbi, id est, ad potestatem ecclesiasticam, cuius officium proprium est, non vi corporali, sed tantum verbo arguere homines. Nam regnum Christi est regnum spirituale, quod solo verbo, sine gladio regitur.

Iam hic quaeritur: Utrum igitur, non licet tollere adulteros, homicidas? etc. Sic enim aliquis argumentari posset: Zizania non sunt tollenda, Adulteri sunt zizania: ergo adulteri non sunt tollendi. Concedendum est totum argumentum, quod attinet ministerium verbi, non quod ad civilem potestatem.

Magistratus civilis habet potestatem tollendi adulteros, homicidas, et similes palam flagitiosos. Magistratus enim, ut inquit Paulus, est qui fert gladium in terrorem malis, ut puniat eos. Item: Lex est iniustis posita, et poenarum civilium tres sunt causae.

Prima est Iusticia Dei. Secunda, Exemplum. Tertia, Pax publica, ut alias prolixius dicitur.

Licetne magistratui punire haereticos? Magistratus enim est custos totius legis, hoc est, non tantum secundae, verum etiam primae tabulae, quod ad externam disciplinam attinet. Sed iudicium de doctrina non tantum pertinet ad magistratum, sed ad totam Ecclesiam, cuius pars est magistratus. Is igitur viderit, ut certo iudicet, non ut nunc fit, ex duorum aut trium monachorum saevitia et crudelitate, sed ex sententia optimorum et doctissimorum in Ecclesia.

Sic in haeresi Donatistarum, qui fingebant Ecclesiam, in qua prorsus nulli essent viciosi, et contendebant, Sacramenta per malos administrata fieri irrita, Constantinus imperator iudicium commisit Episcopis Romanis, qui cum recognita damnassent Donatistas, neque ii stare hoc iudicio vellent. Imperator Arelati conventum instituit, ubi praesens ipse re diiudicata sententiam tulit contra Donatistas, et ut poena aliqua afficerentur, transtulit bona ipsorum ecclesiastica ad veram Ecclesiam.

Ita in summa hoc Evangelium docet, ne Apostoli praetextu Evangelii arripiant gladium, et constituant regnum mundanum, quod longe aliud est, quam regnum Christi.

Sed de eorum officio loquitur Paulus: Increpa, argue, cum omni imperio. Quibus verbis significat Paulus, potestatem ecclesiasticam posse imperare in iis, quae sunt iuris divini, eique necessario obediendum esse. Id enim significat ἐπιταγή.

## 13:25 Sermons on Matthew
When men were sleeping etc.

In the former parable He said what the Church is like, and He has already planted the Church. Now concerning the planted one He says what temptations it has, and warns that in the Church good and bad are always mixed.

This doctrine is necessary, because it often happens, as in the kingdom of Münster, where they wanted to make a Church in which there would be no sinners. But such people afterwards fall into this, that they receive no one except their own flatterers, and they pretend that these are saints, even though they are the worst scoundrels. Let this doctrine therefore be from this similitude, that in this life, until the resurrection, the Church of God is to remain, and that in it there are always mixed good and bad.

What then do you say about excommunication? Are the bad not to be excommunicated?

I answer: Those who live in manifest sins, if they do not wish to repent, are to be excommunicated.

But besides these, many hypocrites still remain, suffering from various vices, who are to be tolerated, but we must assiduously preach repentance, so that some may be converted.

Why therefore does he say? Let both grow together.

First, he refutes the opinion of the Apostles concerning the worldly kingdom of the Messiah.

For the Apostles hoped that there would be such a beautiful state, with all the wicked destroyed, and only the holy living in this mortal life, etc. He therefore rebukes them, and teaches the Church that the kingdom will not be worldly, and he does not want the Apostles to wield the sword, or to punish sinners with the sword.

But against manifest sins, he teaches excommunication elsewhere.

Yet afterwards many vices remain.

Here let us know that on account of this there is no Church, even if many wicked are mixed with the good.

This doctrine is a useful consolation, because many now also cry out on account of many scandals: If the Lutherans were the Church, there would be no adulterers, drunkards, thieves, etc., among them.

Against this scandal, know that the Church is to be sought where the voice of the Gospel sounds, and nowhere else.

Nor let it deter you, even if not all are converted, etc., because nowhere is there the Church of God, except in the assembly of the called, that is, where the true voice of the Gospel sounds.

Rom. 8: Those whom he chose, these he also called, etc.

Third parable.

The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed.

The sum is of the sermon, and of the similitude, concerning the ministry of the Gospel and its effects.
