First, that God in His immense mercy excites restorers of the doctrine of the Gospel, and indeed wishes to send such ones in the last time.

Secondly, when such are sent, let us learn the Gospel, and among great perils let us confess, because the last time will be similar to the time of Elijah, and also to the time of John.

In the time of Elijah, impious kings reigned, and there were many impious cults in Israel, and pious Prophets were driven out everywhere.

So in the time of John, the Pharisees and Sadducees, Herod and the Romans reigned, and the saints were oppressed, and the Church was small.

Let us look at this appearance, and compare it to the present, and let us console ourselves. Since God there nevertheless, among those greatest crowds of the impious, and under impious Pontiffs and Priests, preserved the remnants of His Church, let us know that it is preserved now also.

Likewise, let us confirm ourselves by the example of the saints. Just as the saints were then forced to dissent from the Pharisees and Sadducees, so now we are forced to dissent.

Lastly, let this example also be considered.

Just as the Jews then hoped that the Messiah would come and would establish a kingdom of the world. And they thought that Elijah would stir up tumults against kings before the Messiah. But it happened far otherwise. John is killed by Herod. Yet the spirit of Elijah is not slothful; it taught saving things, and the doctrine remained, although in various persecutions.

So it happens now in our time. There is no doubt that the voice of the Gospel is that voice of Elijah of the last time, and it will proceed, even if the world opposes it.

On the lunatic.

And when He had come to the crowds, a man approached Him, falling on his knees before Him, saying: Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is a lunatic, and suffers badly.

This history contains three things.

1. An example of the weakness of faith in the Apostles.

2. An example of weak and growing faith in the father.

3. The miracle itself, which confirms faith.

I. Since sin remains in the Saints, let us acknowledge this misery of ours, and let us be humble, in fear.

And indeed the Apostles are harshly rebuked. Let us know that our own security is also rebuked there. Again, let us also hold onto consolation, even if there is sin in us, yet this sin is covered by immense mercy through the Son, as it is written in Psalm 32: Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered, etc.

This doctrine is necessary on both sides, concerning humility and concerning consolation, that we please God by faith.

II. The example of weak and growing faith in the Father teaches also that weak faith is not void, not ineffective. And it is a very sweet consolation and testimony that faith, however weak, pleases God, and that God increases it, that it is effective and obtains its request.

Thus Doctor Caspar Cruciger, already sick, often prayed: I call upon thee, O God, eternal Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the faith of thy Son, although with languid and feeble faith, but yet nevertheless with faith.

III. A miracle confirms faith. Thus let us also believe, and believing we shall obtain.

Faith is excited and confirmed in many ways, generally and specially.

I. Generally, because he who asks for these goods acknowledges that they are not scattered by chance, but are truly given by God, and that even this bodily life is cherished and preserved, so that the Church may exist in this life, offspring may be nourished and instructed, and men may be ruled, according to the saying: Deut. 30: He is thy life, and the length of thy days.

Likewise Acts 17: In him we live, and move, and have our being.

And faith is confirmed when the liberation or mitigation of a calamity shows the presence of God, according to the saying:

Psalm 34: This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him.

Psalm 27: My father and my mother have forsaken me, but the Lord hath taken me up. Psalm 118: The Lord hath chastened me sore, but he hath not given me over unto death. Likewise: I shall not die, but live, etc.

Lam. 3: It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, etc.

II. Then faith is specially exercised and confirmed, because God wills that these bodily goods be reminders of invocation, so that at the same time one may think of the promise of grace. For invocation cannot take place unless this faith shines forth, that God for the sake of the Mediator receives and hears us freely. Therefore, this special faith concerning grace is simultaneously exercised and confirmed.

Concerning the beginnings of faith, and concerning sober prayer.

Latin:

Caput XVII.

Et post dies sex assumsit Iesus Petrum et Iacobum et Iohannem fratrem eius, et duxit illos in montem excelsum.

De revelatione facta in monte, ubi pater dedit testimonium de filio, et mandatum addidit: Hunc audite.

In hac historia continetur amplissima doctrina, sed volumus praecipua membra complecti, et faciam tres locos, seu tres articulos.

Primus, quare Deus ediderit subinde manifesta de se testimonia, per singulares patefactiones.

Secundus, in hac patefactione docet, quis sit hic Iesus, quem Apostoli vident iam in lumine coelesti.

Tertius, mandatum de audiendo hoc filio.

De primo articulo.

Quare testimonia edita sunt?

Etsi tota creatura testimonium est, quod sit Deus, et ratio humana habet naturalem notitiam quandam de Deo: tamen haec tantum est Legis notitia.

Voluit autem Deus edere promissionem Evangelii, quae fuit ignota omnibus creaturis.

Ideo fuit opus singulari patefactione et testimoniis.

II. Praeterea ratio humana ignorat filium Dei, et sine singulari revelatione et certis testimoniis nihil de eo sciret, nec fateretur Deum habere filium, et aberraret a vero Deo.

III. Praeterea levitas rationis humanae finxit sibi Deos alibi alios.

Ideo Deus immensa misericordia se toties patefecit, et addidit certa testimonia, ut eductionem ex Aegypto, resuscitationes mortuorum, et alia miracula, et vult agnosci verum Deum, et vult eum discerni ab omnibus aliis fictitiis diis.

Vult etiam agnosci Filium et Spiritum sanctum, vult sciri promissionem.

Haec saepe cogitanda sunt in ipsa invocatione.

Et quoties invocas, cogita quem Deum invoces, quis sit, et quomodo, et ubi se patefecerit, et quomodo velit invocari, in agnitione et fiducia filii. Et saepe alias dictum est: Quando incipis tuam precationem, cogita vel patefactionem factam in baptismo Christi, vel factam in monte, iuxta hanc historiam, de qua iam dico, et exsuscita te ad has cogitationes: Discerno meam invocationem ab invocatione Ethnica, credo non esse irritos nostros gemitus et vota.

Credo me exaudiri propter filium, quia ideo sunt factae patefactiones, ut sciamus, quis sit verus Deus, et quare exaudiat.

Hic usus harum historiarum commonefacit nos, quare hae mirandae res factae sint, et sciamus factas esse, non tantum propter tunc praesentes, sed universa Ecclesia cogitet se spectatorem esse.

Tu ipse haec cogitans, stas ad Iordanem, vel stas in hoc monte, et oculis et auribus et mente accipis haec manifesta testimonia.

Sic ad usum nostrum transferantur patefactiones omnes, et haec doctrina utilis et necessaria est, et valde confirmat fidem in cordibus, et seiungit nos ab Ethnicis et aliis impiis.

Saepe etiam gratias agimus Deo, quod immensa misericordia se sic patefecerit, et quod filium miserit, quod promissiones dederit, etc.

Haec doctrina de his exercitiis videtur esse parvi momenti, sed profecto est saluberrima, et maxime assuefaciendi sunt pii ad haec exercitia, in quibus et ipsi utilitatem experientur, sentient fidem accendi et confirmari, et vere pasci corda.

Qualis etiam ingratitudo est, cum Deus toties prodierit, et tanta misericordia renovaverit Ecclesiam, et res mirandas fecerit, nolle eas cogitare, aut imaginari, nihil eas pertinere ad nos?

Absit a nobis haec turpis ingratitudo.

Quotidie una pars precationum esse debebat, dicere: Ago tibi gratias vere Deus, omnipotens, aeterne pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, conditor coeli et terrae, et hominum et Ecclesiae tuae, una cum filio tuo Domino nostro Iesu Christo, et Spiritu sancto, quod te immensa misericordia toties patefecisti, et vis agnosci a nobis, et vis nos in vera agnitione tui tibi copulatos esse, et misisti filium, et donas nos Spiritu sancto tuo, ut vera tui agnitio in nobis accendatur.

Oro te propter filium, accende corda nostra Spiritu sancto tuo, ut te vere agnoscamus, vere invocemus, tibi vere obediamus, tibi gratias agamus.

Talia vel similia verba saepe apud nos repetenda erant, quando surgimus, quando imus cubitum, quando accedimus ad operas.

Sed nimis magna profanitas nunc est, non adsuefaciunt se homines ad precationem, ideo poenae mundi non mitigantur.

Hortor autem vos ad tales meditationes et precationes.

Dictum est de primo articulo, quare sint factae patefactiones.

De secundo articulo. Doctrina de Iesu, quis sit.

In omni patefactione proponitur aliqua doctrina, vel promissio, vel consolatio, sicut in Sinai proponitur Lex.

In colloquio cum Abraham traditur promissio: In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes.

Consideremus igitur, quid fiat in hac patefactione.

Doctrina de filio confirmatur, et postea additur mandatum de audiendo filio.

Cogites igitur hoc colloquium Dei, Filii, Moisis, Eliae, esse synodum praecipuam, in qua de summa doctrinae Evangelii tales personae colloquuntur, audientibus et spectantibus omnibus Angelis, et aliquibus Apostolis, quos voluit Deus esse nuntios et testes de hoc colloquio.

Discamus igitur hic articulum tradi, de filio Dei.

Affirmat Deus ipse, hunc Iesum natum ex Maria virgine, esse Messiam promissum, et esse filium aeterni Patris, de quo locutae sint promissiones et Prophetae.

Hanc doctrinam teneamus, et in hac synodo repetitam esse sciamus.

Discamus autem hic totum articulum de filio Dei, quod in Christo sint duae naturae, quod sit factus pro nobis victima, quod Deus mirabili consilio sic et non aliter, voluerit iustitiae suae satisfieri, et placari iram, et quod certo propter hunc filium recipiamur, et quod fide oporteat accipi eius beneficia, etc.

Sunt autem dulcissima verba: Hic est filius meus dilectus, an welchem ich herzliche freud vnd wonne habe.

Testatur hunc filium diligii a se, ut sciamus et eius membra diligii, sicut Paulus inquit ad Ephes. 1.: Dilexit nos in Christo dilecto, etc.

Tertius articulus continet mandatum: Hunc audite.

Haec est vox saepe repetita in Prophetis, Deut. 18.: Suscitabo tibi in medio fratrum tuorum etc. qui non audierit illum, Ego ultor ero.

Item Psalm. 2.: Ego constitui regem meum super montem Sion, praedicare praeceptum etc.

Osculamini filium. Item, Esaiae 16.: Ad annuntiandum misit me etc. Hae et similes prophetiae omnes comprehenduntur in hoc mandato immutabili: Hunc audite.

1. Sciamus ergo necessario discendam esse doctrinam Evangelii, quam tradidit. 2. Sciamus, necessario credendum esse omnibus promissionibus ipsius. 3. Sciamus omnes doctrinas de Deo extra Evangelii doctrinam fugiendas et reiiciendas esse. 4. Sciamus solos illos homines esse Ecclesiam Dei, et membra Ecclesiae Dei, qui amplectuntur hanc de Deo doctrinam. 5. Sciamus nullos homines esse Ecclesiae membra sine hac doctrina, vel pugnantes cum hac doctrina. 6. Sciamus certo nos hanc doctrinam amplectentes, et vera fide inde consolationem petentes, haeredes esse vitae aeternae.

Et has consolationes infigamus animis, ut semper sint in conspectu. Et saepe in nostra invocatione tamquam in hunc montem ascendentes, de hac revelatione cogitemus, ut fides nostra confirmetur, intuens in ipsas patefactiones Dei et earum testimonia, scilicet in eductionem populi ex Aegypto, in resuscitationem mortuorum, et similia miracula. Et hanc doctrinam in quotidiana invocatione exerceamus.

Hic etiam discamus, quid agant Sancti in coelo. Certum est eos, qui sunt in coelo, sollicitos esse pro Ecclesia, et pro ea orare, sicut hic Moises et Elias colloquuntur cum filio Dei, de ipsius passione et resurrectione, et de collectione Ecclesiae, sicut Lucas dicit: Colloquebantur de his, quae eventura erant.

Accedentes discipuli timuerunt valde, et accedens Iesus attigit eos.

Propositio.

In hoc exemplo proponitur doctrina saepe repetita in scripturis, scilicet, quod haec humana natura non potest sustinere Dei conspectum, vel Deum loquentem immediate. Quia natura polluta peccato, metuit et fugit iudicem, sicut in monte Sinai populus Israël expavit, et dixit: Non loquatur nobis Dominus, ne moriamur. Et corda singulorum in pavoribus sentiunt, quam sit horribile iudicium, sicut dicitur: Deus ignis consumens est. Item: Sicut leo contrivit omnia ossa mea. Hanc iram Dei homines securi non considerant. Et dolendum est, tantam esse duritiem humani pectoris, ut non afficiatur cura vel cogitatione irae Dei, quae certissima est, et poenae quotidie sunt in conspectu. Exsuscitemus igitur nos ad considerationem irae Dei ad timorem, cogitatione verbi Dei et poenarum, et certo sciamus, non relinqui peccata impunita. Sicut Iob dicit capite 9.: Verebar in omnibus operibus meis, sciens quod non parcis delinquenti.

Secunda pars.

De Mediatore.

Quia autem magnitudinem irae Dei non potest homo sustinere, ideo intercessit pro nobis Filius Dei, et factus est Mediator, sed tamen ita, ut ipse in sese derivaret praecipuam poenam, et satisfaceret iustitiae Dei. Hoc quia fecit, postea nobis parcitur, quando hunc Filium fide apprehendimus, quando ipse nos contrectat, et dicit: Noli timere.

Sic de hoc tanto beneficio scriptum est in Esaia cap. 53.: Disciplina pacis nostrae super eum, et livore eius sanati sumus. Item: Vere languores nostros ipse tulit, et dolores nostros ipse portavit. Et Esaiae 4. enarratur typus: Sicut in deserto interdiu nubes erat umbraculum tegens populum contra aestum, noctu vero ignis anteibat populum. Ita inquit Esaias, Deum velle Ecclesiae suae dare Messiam, ut sit umbraculum contra aestum. Quando hoc umbraculo tegimur, tunc possumus audire Deum loquentem, quia per hunc audimus simul vocem misericordiae, et iuvamur et donamur Spiritu sancto, sicut Paulus inquit: Spiritus opem fert infirmitati nostrae.

Hae sunt magnae res, quae in Ecclesiae notae esse debent. Agnitio iudicii et irae Dei, et rursus mediator et gratia, fide agnoscenda.

Et utrumque in assidua invocatione cogitandum est. Poenae sunt iam in conspectu, vidimus bella, et sustinemus magnas calamitates propter bellum, paupertatem et multas difficultates. Nunc sequitur turbatio Ecclesiarum. Et post hyemem existimant rursus Hispanicos exercitus et Hussernos in his regionibus fore. Haec omnia sunt horribilia opera irae Dei.

Et Ecclesia nullum habet humanum auxilium.

In his tantis periculis sciamus, tamen nos velut umbraculum per filium tegi, et hac spe eum invocemus, et petamus et certo exspectemus auxilium.

Haec doctrina non nisi in cruce et in tali invocatione discitur, in qua fides et spes vera lucent, et petitur et exspectatur auxilium Dei.

Et tantum de hac parte: Nolite timere.

II. De prohibitione.

Quare prohibet passim narrari hanc visionem, donec facta fuerit resurrectio? Respondeo. Vult nos Deus ordiri doctrinam a verbo, quod tradidit Ecclesiae suae certis testimoniis, et vult disci necessaria. Non vult nos humana curiositate subinde novas visiones quaerere. Sed tamen hanc visionem vult praedicari, sed post resurrectionem, quia vult conspici testimonium convincens homines, ne existimaretur haec visio fabulosa esse. Coniungenda sunt miracula, quae dant testimonium patefactionibus divinis. Et cogitatione patefactionum et miraculorum excitanda et confirmanda est fides, et discernenda vera invocatio ab Ethnica et hypocritica, sicut initio dixi, cogitatione huius patefactionis discendum esse, quem Deum invocemus, et quomodo velit invocari.

Et interrogaverunt eum discipuli, dicentes: Quid ergo Scribae dicunt, quod oporteat prius Eliam venire? At ille respondens, ait eis: Elias quidem venturus est prius, et restituet omnia. Dico autem vobis: Elias iam venit, et non cognoverunt eum, sed fecerunt ei quae voluerunt, etc.

Occasio huius quaestionis haec est. Malachiae ultimo scriptum est: Ecce mittam vobis Eliam. Hinc persuasio recepta est, quod Elias sua persona ante Messiam venturus esset. Sicut et propter dicta Apocalypseos 11. recepta fuit opinio, Eliam sua persona venturum esse ante novissimum diem.

Sed Christus hic interpretatur Malachiam, et affirmat, illum textum de Iohanne intelligendum esse, qui spiritu Eliae concionatur.

Quid nos ex hac historia discere debemus?

Hanc doctrinam inde sumamus.

Primum, quod Deus immensa misericordia excitet instauratores doctrinae Evangelii, et quidem novissimo tempore velit mittere tales.

Secundo, cum tales mittuntur, Evangelium discamus, et inter magna pericula confiteamur, Quia postremum tempus erit simile tempori Eliae, item tempori Iohannis.

Tempore Eliae regnabant impii reges, et erant multi impii cultus in Israël, et Prophetae pii undique pellebantur.

Sic tempore Iohannis regnabant Pharisaei et Sadducaei, Herodes et Romani, et sancti erant oppressi, et Ecclesia erat exigua.

Hanc speciem intuearum, et conferamus ad praesentem, et nos consolemur. Cum Deus ibi tamen, inter illas maximas catervas impiorum, et sub Pontificibus et Sacerdotibus impiis servaverit reliquias Ecclesiae suae, sciamus nunc quoque servari.

Item confirmemus nos exemplo sanctorum. Sicut sancti tunc dissentire cogebantur a Pharisaeis et Sadducaeis, sic nunc cogimur dissentire.

Postremo hoc exemplum etiam consideretur.

Sicut tunc Iudaei sperabant Messiam venturum esse, et regnum mundi constituturum. Et Eliam cogitabant ante Messiam regibus moturum esse tumultus. Sed longe aliter fiebat. Iohannes ab Herode interficitur. Spiritus tamen Eliae non est ignavus, docuit salutaria, et mansit doctrina, quanquam in variis persecutionibus.

Ita fit iam nostro tempore. Non dubium est, quin vox Evangelii sit illa vox Eliae postremi temporis, et processura est, etiamsi mundus adversatur.

De lunatico.

Et cum venisset ad turbas, accessit ad eum homo genibus provolutus ante eum dicens: Domine miserere filio meo, quia lunaticus est, et male patitur.

Haec historia tria continet.

1. Exemplum imbecillitatis fidei in Apostolis.

2. Exemplum infirmae et crescentis fidei in patre.

3. Miraculum ipsum, quod confirmat fidem.

I. Cum in Sanctis maneat peccatum, agnoscamus hanc nostram miseriam, et simus humiles, in timore.

Et quidem duriter obiurgantur Apostoli. Sciamus ibi et nostram securitatem obiurgari. Rursus etiam teneamus consolationem, etiamsi est in nobis peccatum, tamen hoc peccatum immensa misericordia per Filium tegitur, sicut scriptum est Psalm. 32.: Beati quorum remissae sunt iniquitates, et quorum tecta sunt peccata etc.

Haec doctrina necessaria est de utraque parte, de humilitate et de consolatione, quod fide placeamus.

II. Exemplum infirmae et crescentis fidei in Patre, docet etiam infirmam fidem non esse irritam, non inefficacem. Et est valde dulcis consolatio et testimonium quod Deo placeat quamquam infirma fides, et quod Deus augeat eam, quod sit efficax et impetret.

Sic Doctor Caspar Cruciger, iam aegrotus saepe orabat: Invoco te o Deus aeterne Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, in fide filii tui, quamquam languida et imbecilli fide, sed tamen fide.

III. Miraculum confirmat fidem. Sic nos quoque credamus, et credentes impetrabimus.

Fides excitatur et confirmatur multipliciter, generaliter et specialiter.

I. Generaliter, quia petens haec bona, agnoscit, ea non casu spargi, sed vere a Deo dari, foveri et servari etiam hanc corporalem vitam, ut in hac vita Ecclesia esse possit, soboles ali et institui et homines regi possint, iuxta dictum: Deut. 30.: Ipse est vita tua, et longitudo dierum tuorum.

Item Act. 17.: In ipso sumus, vivimus et movemur.

Et confirmatur fides, cum liberatio aut mitigatio calamitatis ostendit praesentiam Dei, iuxta dictum:

Psalm. 34.: Iste pauper clamavit, et Dominus exaudivit eum.

Psalmo 27.: Pater et mater dereliquerunt me, Dominus autem assumsit me. Psalmo 118.: Castigans castigavit me, et morti non tradidit me. Item: Non moriar, sed vivam etc.

Thren. 3.: Misericordiae Domini, quod non consumti sumus etc.

II. Deinde specialiter exercetur et confirmatur fides, quia Deus vult haec corporalia bona commonefactiones esse de invocatione, ut simul de promissione gratiae cogitetur. Non enim potest fieri invocatio, nisi praelucente hac fide, quod Deus nos propter Mediatorem gratis recipiat et exaudiat. Simul igitur haec specialis fides de gratia exercetur et confirmatur.

De initiis fidei, et de oratione sobria.

## 17:18 Sermons on Matthew
Why could we not cast it out?

Here the doctrine concerning the beginnings of faith and its increments is repeated.

First, as I said above, it must be known that many and great infirmities remain in all saints, which we must in some way acknowledge and deplore.

But yet, consolation must also be held, that we are received by faith for the sake of the Mediator, even if we are very weak, as it is said in Rom. 14 concerning the weak: God hath received him. And here the Apostles were righteous and pleased God, and yet the Lord rebukes them because faith was more languid in them.

Therefore, let us first know that there must be beginnings of faith in us, and that we please God by faith, and can obtain many things, even if faith is still small.

Secondly, but yet let us know that faith and other virtues must grow. And it always happens thus: man does not remain at one level, but virtues are always either growing or decreasing. It is universal that they decrease when they are not exercised. Just as all bodies without exercise become sick and rot. Thus faith is extinguished in idleness. Conversely, however, when bodies are exercised, they become more lively. Thus virtues grow by exercises. As it is said in the parable of the merchants: To him that hath shall be given, and from him that hath not, that which he hath shall be taken away.

And Augustine beautifully says: Love merits that love be increased, which is true, because the Lord adorns the faithful merchant more and more.

So it says here: If you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, Amen I say, etc.

of soul and body has been given to us by the Son of God, and we receive the freedom of the soul even in this life. But the body will be free from diseases, death, and all calamities after this life.

Latin:

Quare nos non potuimus eiicere?

Hic repetita est doctrina de initiis fidei, et de incrementis.

Primum, ut supra dixi, sciendum est, manere in omnibus sanctis multas et magnas infirmitates, quas aliquo modo agnoscere et deplorare debemus.

Sed tamen et consolatio tenenda est, quod fide propter Mediatorem recepti simus, etiamsi valde infirmi sumus, ut Rom. 14. dicitur de infirmis: Deus eum recepit. Et hic Apostoli erant iusti et placebant Deo, et tamen obiurgat eos Dominus propterea, quod languidior erat in eis fides.

Primum igitur sciamus, quod oporteat in nobis initia fidei esse, et quod fide placeamus, et multa possimus impetrare, etiamsi adhuc exigua est fides.

Secundo, sed tamen sciamus, fidem et alias virtutes oportere crescere. Et semper ita fit, homo non manet in uno gradu, sed semper aut crescunt virtutes, aut decrescunt. Universale est, quod decrescunt, quando non exercentur. Sicut omnia corpora sine exercitio fiunt aegra et putrescunt. Sic fides in otio exstinguitur. Econtra vero, quando exercentur corpora, fiunt vivaciora. Sic virtutes exercitiis crescunt. Sicut in parabola de negotiantibus dicitur: Habenti dabitur, et a non habente id quod habet, auferetur.

Et Augustinus pulcre dicit: Dilectio meretur augeri dilectionem, quod verum est, quia Dominus fidelem negotiatorem magis magisque ornat.

Ita hic dicit: Si habebis fidem, sicut granum sinapis, Amen dico, etc.

animae et corporis a Filio Dei nobis donata sit, et libertatem animae accipimus etiam in hac vita. Corpus vero erit liberum a morbis, morte, et omnibus calamitatibus post hanc vitam.

## 18:1-5 Michaelmas Day
Gospel for Michaelmas Day, Matthew 18.

At that hour the disciples came to Jesus saying: Who then is greater in the kingdom of heaven? And Jesus calling a little child, set him in the midst of them, and said: Amen I say to you, unless you be converted, and become as little children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven. Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, he is the greater in the kingdom of heaven. And he that shall receive one such little child in my name, receiveth me.

But whosoever shall scandalize one of these little ones, who believe in me, it is better for him that a millstone should be hanged about his neck, and that he should be drowned in the depth of the sea. Woe to the world because of scandals. For it is necessary that scandals come, but nevertheless woe to the man by whom the scandal comes. And if thy hand or thy foot scandalize thee, cut it off, and cast it from thee: it is good for thee to enter into life maimed or weak, rather than having two hands, or two feet, to be cast into everlasting fire. And if thy eye scandalize thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: it is good for thee having one eye to enter into life, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire. See that you despise not one of these little ones. For I say to you, that their angels in heaven always see the face of my father, who is in heaven.

There are seven principal topics.

I. The error or sin of the Apostles contending about primacy.

II. The rebuke of the struggles for the kingdom, which arise either from a false persuasion about the kingdom of Christ, or from ambition.

And from these struggles arise the neglect of doctrine, schisms, heresies, hatreds, wars, and the desolations of Churches. Therefore Christ is so greatly incensed in this place, looking upon the huge and horrible discords about to come into the Church, which are going to dissipate the Churches and cause desolations.

III. What form of government, therefore, does He wish there to be? Will there be no superior power governing? The answer is: Christ wishes the Churches to be governed by His Gospel, and not by human authority, not by the ranks of Bishops.

IIII. Although there is an arithmetic equality of governors in the Church, because Christ does not wish anyone to excel in power, yet there is an inequality of gifts. Thus a geometric proportion is formed, when, namely, those who are excellent in gifts diligently consult for the inferiors, and excel them in authority. And conversely, the inferiors obey and yield to the more excellent ones on account of the word of God.

V. Admonition concerning the avoidance of scandals of doctrine and morals.

VI. Concerning the custody of angels. VII. Concerning infants in the Church, a notable testimony that they are pleasing to God.

Concerning the first.

Let us learn that there are errors and sins even among the saints, just as here the Apostles still imagine that the kingdom of Christ will be a worldly polity, in which, as in a kingdom, there are to be ranks of dissimilar power. There was more evil, if the Apostles even contended with ambition, envy, and emulation, and one preferred himself to another by his own judgment, just as is signified in Luke, chapter 22.

Concerning the second. Christ saw, without doubt, how much evil these opinions about establishing a kingdom in the Church would produce, for from them many things follow: Bishops, armed with power, establish laws, institute cults, ceremonies, such as the Mass and similar things. This is later thought to be the justice of the Gospel, and thus the truth is oppressed. Furthermore, when ambition is added, how many movements arise? Just as Arius grieved that Alexander was preferred to him in the election of a Bishop: and all ages have seen similar examples. Likewise, at Rome, how great were the contentions about the election a thousand years ago? Whence that saying arose: More have arrived at the Episcopate in the manner of Romulus than of Peter. But ambition has produced much more evil among men of genius contending for the praise of doctrine, whence heresies, schisms, and many other pernicious changes have arisen. Just as from the Arian dissension Mahomet arose, and from that followed the devastation of the Churches. Christ, beholding all these things, here preaches so harshly about scandals, and admonishes us that we should wish to be governed by the word, that we should avoid ambitious contentions about doctrine and about the ministry.

Concerning the third. What form of government does He establish here?

The principal answer is in this saying: Whoever receives a child in My name, receives Me. Here He shows that He binds the Church, not to the person of any man, but to His own word. Therefore He says, if another has brought My word, listen. I wish you to be governed by the word, not by the ranks of persons. This is what He means when He says, If anyone has received a child in My name, that is, one bringing My word, and He demands that the Apostles themselves be humble in the manner of infants, who as yet dispute nothing about a kingdom. For the application or comparison is easy and illustrious. For the stronger naturally take to themselves command over the inferior. Therefore, infancy, feeling its weakness, does not yet take to itself command over others, and although perhaps one nature obeys more, another less, yet all infants fear those who are older. The comparison is therefore clear, and it detracts power from the governors of the Church. As infants do not take to themselves command over others, but receive what is dictated by the stronger, so Christ wishes Bishops to carry around the dictates delivered in the Gospel without command. We see, therefore, that this grim domination established in the Church, which indeed also retains and defends unjust laws, impious cults, and tyrannical empires, is displeasing to Christ. And many other huge sins are added. It is a peculiar doctrine of Christians to determine concerning the will of God from His own word, not from our opinions or events. Therefore, so that the authority of the word may be amplified and magnified, Christ leads men away from the sight of persons, and shows the true and only governor, namely, the very voice of the Gospel, just as it is often said elsewhere: Thy word is a lamp to my feet. Likewise: Hear Him, If anyone shall keep My word, he shall not see death. But human reason lightly cares for the word of God, and thinks of the Church as of a human polity, and in all temptations is prone to embrace those things which reason shows. Therefore, Christ here calls us back to the word, and wishes us to remember that the word is the ruler, not persons, not human reason.

Concerning the fourth. Concerning the avoidance of scandals.

A scandal is a false doctrine or a wicked example, which harms others, either because it invites imitation, or because it brings about public punishments, or because it alienates minds from the society of good things, or because it provides an occasion for the wicked to speak ill of God and divine matters.

We make five degrees.

The first is false doctrine. This kind of scandal is most harmful.

The second is a wicked example, which harms by imitation, such as the invocation of Saints. Likewise many other manifest crimes, which invite others to sin, or increase license by example, such as gluttony, whoredoms, etc.

The third degree is not only of manifest crimes, but also of secret ones, which bring about public punishments, wars, seditions, and other evils, which drag along with them manifold sins. It is, however, most miserable to bear the conscience that an infinite multitude perishes on account of our fault. For just as the whole human race perished on account of the sin of Adam and Eve, as huge public punishments followed on account of the adultery of David, on account of the idolatry of Ahaz and Manasseh, so public punishments, arising from the sins of some individuals, always wander through the world.

The fourth degree is a wicked example, which alienates minds from the society of good things, just as the disgraces of teachers or princes alienate minds from the Gospel. The baseness of leaders, such as Antony or Saul, weakens the spirits of armies, because they judge that God will punish the crimes of the leaders. To this also pertains petulance and pertinacity in indifferent matters. Using liberty petulantly before the pious who are not yet instructed alienates them. Conversely, pertinaciously retaining superstitions confirms errors, and wounds the weak minds of other pious people who use liberty, and grieves the Holy Spirit.

And concerning the sons of Eli it is said in 1 Sam. 2: The sin of the young men was great before the Lord, because they caused men to despise the sacrifice of the Lord. Let us remember these sentences, so that we may consider that in individual wicked deeds this sin is added, that the glory of the name of God is harmed. Furthermore, let us remember these most severe threats: Woe to that man by whom the scandal comes. These sayings testify that scandals are most gravely punished, with present and eternal punishments.

Concerning the fifth. Concerning the guardianship of angels.

Here exists a clear testimony that guardian angels are added to the pious. Here similar testimonies are gathered, such as the companion of Elisha seeing himself surrounded by a great army of angels. And here let the antithesis of evil and good angels be considered. To the evil ones two principal vices are attributed, that they are liars, blasphemous against God, and murderers, as the devil showed both in Paradise. For he shakes Eve’s [belief in the] command of God by pouring in another opinion, "You will be like gods," and he dragged the whole human race into eternal death. He still attempts the same; he impels light minds to embrace and sow Epicurean opinions or other false opinions. He attempts to drag into eternal death as many as he can; he is the cause of bodily death and of very many calamities for men, so that through them he may drag weakened souls to despair and eternal death; he impels the impious to all kinds of outrages, lusts, and murders, just as the history of the whole world of all times shows, which commemorates horrible outrages and unjust wars. Against these great evils our leader and liberator is the Son of God, Immanuel, who destroys the works of the devil and sends good angels to the pious to hinder many of the attempts of the wicked.

Concerning the sixth.

Here it must be diligently observed as a testimony that infants inserted into the Church are pleasing to God and are heirs of eternal life. For concerning such it is clearly said: It is not the will of the Father that one of these little ones should perish.

Latin:

Evangelium die Michaelis, Matth. 18. De Angelis.

In illa hora accesserunt discipuli ad Iesum dicentes: Quis ergo maior est in regno coelorum? Et advocans Iesus parvulum, statuit eum in medio eorum, et dixit: Amen dico vobis, nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum coelorum. Quicunque ergo humiliaverit seipsum sicut parvulus iste, hic maior est in regno coelorum. Et qui susceperit unum parvulum talem in nomine meo, me suscipit.

Qui autem scandalizaverit unum de pusillis istis, qui in me credunt, expedit ei, ut suspendatur mola asinaria in collo eius, et demergatur in profundum maris. Vae mundo a scandalis. Necesse est enim ut veniam scandala, veruntamen vae homini per quem scandalum venit. Si autem manus tua vel pes tuus scandalizat te, abscinde eum, et proiice abs te: bonum est tibi ad vitam ingredi claudum vel debilem, quam duas manus, vel duos pedes habentem, mitti in ignem aeternum. Et si oculus tuus scandalizat te, erue eum, et proiice abs te: bonum est tibi cum uno oculo in vitam intrare, quam duos oculos habentem mitti in gehennam ignis. Videte ne contemnatis unum ex his pusillis. Dico enim vobis, quod angeli eorum in coelis semper vident faciem patris mei, qui in coelis est.

Septem sunt praecipui loci.

I. Error seu peccatum Apostolorum contendentium de primatu.

II. Reprehensio certaminum de regno, quae oriuntur vel ex falsa persuasione de regno Christi, vel ex ambitione.

Et ex his certaminibus oriuntur neglectio doctrinae, schismata, haereses, odia, bella, et vastitates Ecclesiarum. Ideo Christus tantopere incandescit in hoc loco, intuens venturas in Ecclesiam ingentes et horribiles discordias, quae dissipaturae sunt Ecclesias et facturae vastitates.

III. Quam igitur vult esse formam regiminis? nullane erit superior potestas gubernans? Responsio, Christus vult regi Ecclesias Evangelio suo, et non autoritate humana, non gradibus Episcoporum.

IIII. Etsi est aequalitas arithmetica gubernatorum in Ecclesia, quia Christus non vult quenquam exellere potestate, tamen est inaequalitas donorum. Ita fit geometrica proportio, cum videlicet excellentes donis, diligenter consulunt inferioribus, et antecellunt eos autoritate. Et econtra, inferiores obtemperant et cedunt excellentioribus propter verbum Dei.

V. Admonitio de cavendis scandalis doctrinae et morum.

VI. De custodia angelorum. VII. De infantibus in Ecclesia insigne testimonium, quod Deo placeant.

De primo.

Discamus in sanctis etiam esse errores et peccata, sicut hic Apostoli adhuc imaginantur, regnum Christi fore mundanam politiam, in qua, ut in regno, sint futuri gradus dissimili potestate. Plus mali fuit, si etiam ambitione, invidia, aemulatione Apostoli certaverunt, et alius alteri se suo iudicio praetulit, sicuti in Luca significatur, capite 22.

De secundo. Vidit haud dubie Christus, quantum mali pariturae essent hae opiniones de constituendo regno in Ecclesia, inde enim multa sequuntur: Episcopi armati potestate, condunt leges, instituunt cultus, ceremonias, ut Missam et similes. Haec postea putatur iusticia Evangelii, ita opprimitur veritas. Praeterea cum accedit ambitio, quanti motus oriuntur? ut Arius praeferri sibi doluit Alexandrum in electione Episcopi: et omnes aetates viderunt similia exempla. Item, Romae quanta fuerunt certamina de electione ante mille annos? Unde vox illa orta est: Plures Romuli more, quam Petri pervenire ad Episcopatum. Sed multo plus mali peperit ambitio ingeniorum de laude doctrinae contendentium, unde sunt ortae haereses, schismata, et multae aliae perniciosae mutationes. Sicut ex Ariana dissensione ortus est Mahomet, inde secuta est vastitas Ecclesiarum. Haec omnia intuens Christus, hic tam duriter concionatur de scandalis, et nos admonet, ut verbo regi velimus, ut caveamus ambitiosa certamina de doctrina, et de ministerio.

De tertio.

Quam constituit hic formam regiminis? Principalis responsio est in hoc dicto: Si quis puerum recipit in nomine Meo, me recipit. Hic ostendit se alligare Ecclesiam, non ad ullius hominis personam, sed ad verbum suum. Ideo inquit, sive alius verbum meum attulerit, audite. Verbo regi vos volo, non gradibus personarum. Hoc vult, cum ait, Si quis puerum receperit in nomine meo, id est, verbum meum afferentem, et postulat ut ipsi Apostoli sint humiles more infantum, nihil adhuc de regno disputantium. Est enim facilis et illustris applicatio seu collatio. Nam fortiora naturaliter sibi sumunt imperium in inferiora. Ideo infantia sentiens imbecillitatem, nondum sumit sibi imperium in alios, etsi fortassis alia natura magis, alia minus obtemperat, tamen omnes infantes metuunt grandiores. Est igitur perspicua collatio, et detrahit potestatem gubernatoribus Ecclesiae. Ut infantes non sumunt sibi imperium in alios, sed accipiunt dictata a fortioribus, sic vult Christus Episcopos sine imperio circumferre dictata in Evangelio tradita. Videmus igitur displicere Christo hanc tetram dominationem in Ecclesia constitutam, quae quidem etiam iniustas leges, impios cultus, tyrannicis imperiis retinet, et defendit. Et accedunt multa alia ingentia peccata. Peculiaris doctrina est Christianorum, de voluntate Dei statuere ex ipsius verbo, non ex opinionibus nostris aut eventibus. Ideo ut verbi autoritas amplificetur et magnifiat, Christus abducit homines a conspectu personarum, et monstrat verum ac solum gubernatorem, scilicet, ipsam vocem Evangelii, sicut alibi saepe dicitur: Lucerna pedibus meis verbum tuum. Item: Hunc audite, Si quis sermonem meum servabit, mortem non videbit. Sed humana ratio leviter curat verbum Dei, et de Ecclesia cogitat sicut de humana politia, et in omnibus tentationibus prona est ad amplectenda ea, quae ratio ostendit. Ideo Christus hic revocat nos ad verbum, et vult nos meminisse, verbum esse rectorem, non personas, non humanam rationem.

De quarte. De cavendis scandalis.

Scandalum est falsa doctrina seu pravum exemplum, quod aliis nocet, vel quia invitat ad imitandum, vel quia accersit poenas publicas, vel quia alienat animos a societate rerum bonarum, vel quia praebet occasionem malis, de Deo et de rebus divinis male loquendi.

Gradus quinque facimus.

Primus, est falsa doctrina. Hoc genus scandali nocentissimum est.

Secundus, pravum exemplum, quod imitatione nocet, ut invocatio Sanctorum. Item multa alia manifesta delicta, quae invitant alios ad peccandum, aut exemplo licentiam augent, ut helluationes, scortationes etc.

Tertius gradus est, non tantum manifestorum scelerum, sed etiam arcanorum, quae accersunt poenas publicas, bella, seditiones, et alia mala, quae secum multiplicia peccata trahunt. Est autem miserrimum sustinere conscientiam, quod propter nostram culpam infinita multitudo pereat. Ut enim propter Adae et Evae delictum totum genus humanum periit, ut propter Davidis adulterium, propter idololatriam Achas, Manassae, secutae sunt ingentes publicae poenae, ita semper in mundo vagantur publicae poenae, ortae ab aliquibus singulorum peccatis.

Quartus gradus est, pravum exemplum, quod alienat animos a societate rerum bonarum, ut dedecora docentium aut principum, alienant animos ab Evangelio. Ducum turpitudines, ut Antonii, Saulis, languefaciunt animos exercituum, quia iudicant Deum puniturum esse scelera ducum. Huc etiam pertinet in mediis factis petulantia et pertinacia. Petulanter utens libertate apud pios nondum institutos, alienat eos. Rursus pertinaciter retinens superstitiones, confirmat errores, et sauciat aliorum piorum, qui libertate utuntur, infirmas mentes, et contristat Spiritum sanctum.

Et de filiis Eli dicitur 1. Reg. 2.: Erat peccatum puerorum grande coram Domino, quia detrahebant homines sacrificio Domini. Has sententias meminerimus, ut cogitemus in singulis pravis factis accedere hoc peccatum, quod laeditur gloria nominis Dei. Praeterea meminerimus has severissimas minas: Vae illi, per quem venit scandalum. Haec dicta testantur gravissime puniri scandala, praesentibus et aeternis poenis.

De quinto. De custodia angelorum.

Extat hic perspicuum testimonium, additos esse custodes angelos piis. Hic colligantur similia testimonia, ut, comes Elisaei videt se stipatum esse magno exercitu angelorum. Et consideretur hic antithesis malorum et bonorum angelorum. Malis duo vitia praecipua tribuuntur, quod sint mendaces, blasphemiae adversus Deum, et homicidae, ut in Paradiso utrunque ostendit diabolus. Excutit enim Evae mandatum Dei offusa alia opinione, Eritis sicut dii, et traxit totum genus humanum in aeternam mortem. Idem adhuc conatur, impellit levia ingenia ad epicureas opiniones, aut alias falsas opiniones amplectendas et serendas. Conatur in aeternam mortem pertrahere, quotquot potest, causa est necis corporalis, et plurimarum calamitatum hominibus, ut per eas pertrahat languefactos animos ad desperationem, et aeternam mortem, impellit impios ad omnis generis flagitia, libidines, et caedes iniustas, sicut historia totius mundi omnium temporum ostendit, quae commemorat horribilia flagitia, iniusta bella. Adversus haec tanta mala dux est nobis liberator filius Dei Emanuel, qui destruit opera diaboli, et mittit piis bonos angelos, ad impediendos multos conatus malorum.

De sexto.

Diligenter hic observandum est testimonium, quod infantes inserti Ecclesiae placeant Deo, et sint haeredes vitae aeternae. De talibus enim clare dicitur: Non est voluntas patris, ut pereat unus de parvulis istis.

## 18:1-10 Michaelmas Day
Gospel for Michaelmas Day, Matthew 18. Concerning Angels.

At that hour the disciples came to Jesus saying: Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven? And Jesus calling a little child, set him in the midst of them, and said: Amen I say to you, unless you be converted, and become as little children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven. Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, he is the greater in the kingdom of heaven. And he that shall receive one such little child in my name, receiveth me. But he that shall scandalize one of these little ones, who believe in me, it is better for him that a millstone should be hanged about his neck, and that he should be drowned in the depth of the sea. Woe to the world because of scandals. For it is necessary that scandals come, but nevertheless woe to the man by whom the scandal cometh. And if thy hand or thy foot scandalize thee, cut it off, and cast it from thee: it is good for thee to enter into life maimed or lame, rather than having two hands or two feet, to be cast into everlasting fire. And if thy eye scandalize thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: it is good for thee with one eye to enter into life, rather than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire. See that you despise not one of these little ones. For I say to you, that their angels in heaven always see the face of my father who is in heaven.

There are seven principal topics.

I. The error or sin of the Apostles contending about primacy.

II. The rebuke of the struggles about the kingdom, which arise either from a false persuasion about the kingdom of Christ, or from ambition.

And from these struggles arise the neglect of doctrine, schisms, heresies, hatreds, wars, and the desolations of Churches. And conversely, the inferiors obey and yield to the more excellent ones on account of the word of God.

V. Admonition concerning the avoiding of scandals of doctrine and morals.

VI. Concerning the guardianship of angels.

VII. Concerning infants in the Church, a notable testimony that they are pleasing to God.

Let us learn that there are errors and sins even in the saints, just as here the Apostles still imagine that the kingdom of Christ will be a worldly polity, in which, as in a kingdom, there are to be ranks of dissimilar power. Christ, beholding all these things, here preaches so harshly about scandals, and warns us that we should wish to be ruled by the word, that we should beware of ambitious contentions about doctrine and about the ministry.

I wish you to be ruled by the word, not by the ranks of persons. Concerning the fifth. Concerning the guardianship of angels.

Here stands a clear testimony that guardian angels are added to the pious.

Here similar testimonies are collected, such as that the companion of Elisha sees himself surrounded by a great army of angels. And let the antithesis of evil and good angels be considered here. Two chief vices are attributed to the evil ones, that they are liars, blasphemers against God, and murderers, as the devil shows both in Paradise.

For he shakes the command of God to Eve by pouring in another opinion, "You shall be as gods," and he dragged the whole human race into eternal death. He still attempts the same; he impels light minds to embrace and sow Epicurean opinions or other false opinions. He attempts to drag into eternal death as many as he can; he is the cause of bodily death and of very many calamities for men, so that through them he may drag weakened souls to despair and eternal death; he impels the impious to all kinds of atrocities, lusts, and unjust slaughters, as the history of the whole world of all times shows, which commemorates horrible atrocities and unjust wars.

Against these such great evils, our leader is the liberator, the Son of God, Emmanuel, who destroys the works of the devil and sends good angels to the pious to hinder many attempts of the wicked.

The fourth degree is a wicked example, which alienates minds from the society of good things, as the indecencies of teachers or princes alienate minds from the Gospel.

The baseness of leaders, such as that of Antony or Saul, weakens the spirits of armies, because they judge that God will punish the crimes of the leaders. To this also pertains petulance and stubbornness in indifferent matters. Using liberty petulantly in the presence of the pious who are not yet instructed alienates them.

Again, stubbornly retaining superstitions confirms errors and wounds the weak minds of other pious people who use liberty, and grieves the Holy Spirit. The fifth degree is that which is also spread among all, because the wicked take a plausible occasion from wicked examples to speak ill of God and divine matters, just as Shimei, because of David's transgression, has such a specious argument by which to persuade that David was not divinely called as king, nor as a Prophet.

For a Prophet is not seen to fall in such a way. Thus Ezekiel says: Because of you, God is afflicted with insult among the nations.

Concerning the sixth.

Here the testimony must be diligently observed that infants inserted into the Church are pleasing to God and are heirs of eternal life.

For concerning such it is clearly said: It is not the will of the Father that one of these little ones should perish.

Latin:

Evangelium die Michaelis, Matth. 18. De Angelis.

In illa hora accesserunt discipuli ad Iesum dicentes: Quis ergo maior est in regno coelorum? Et advocans Iesus parvulum, statuit eum in medio eorum, et dixit: Amen dico vobis, nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum coelorum. Quicunque ergo humiliaverit seipsum sicut parvulus iste, hic maior est in regno coelorum. Et qui susceperit unum parvulum talem in nomine meo, me suscipit. Qui autem scandalizaverit unum de pusillis istis, qui in me credunt, expedit ei, ut suspendatur mola asinaria in collo eius, et demergatur in profundum maris. Vae mundo a scandalis. Necesse est enim ut veniam scandala, veruntamen vae homini per quem scandalum venit. Si autem manus tua vel pes tuus scandalizat te, abscinde eum, et proiice abs te: bonum est tibi ad vitam ingredi claudum vel debilem, quam duas manus, vel duos pedes habentem, mitti in ignem aeternum. Et si oculus tuus scandalizat te, erue eum, et proiice abs te: bonum est tibi cum uno oculo in vitam intrare, quam duos oculos habentem mitti in gehennam ignis. Videte ne contemnatis unum ex his pusillis. Dico enim vobis, quod angeli eorum in coelis semper vident faciem patris mei, qui in coelis est.

Septem sunt praecipui loci.

I. Error seu peccatum Apostolorum contendentium de primatu.

II. Reprehensio certaminum de regno, quae oriuntur vel ex falsa persuasione de regno Christi, vel ex ambitione.

Et ex his certaminibus oriuntur neglectio doctrinae, schismata, haereses, odia, bella, et vastitates Ecclesiarum. Ideo Christus tantopere incandescit in hoc loco, intuens venturas in Ecclesiam ingentes et horribiles discordias, quae dissipaturae sunt Ecclesias et facturae vastitates.

III. Quam igitur vult esse formam regiminis? nullane erit superior potestas gubernans? Responsio, Christus vult regi Ecclesias Evangelio suo, et non autoritate humana, non gradibus Episcoporum.

IIII. Etsi est aequalitas arithmetica gubernatorum in Ecclesia, quia Christus non vult quenquam exellere potestate, tamen est inaequalitas donorum. Ita fit geometrica proportio, cum videlicet excellentes donis, diligenter consulunt inferioribus, et antecellunt eos autoritate. Et econtra, inferiores obtemperant et cedunt excellentioribus propter verbum Dei.

V. Admonitio de cavendis scandalis doctrinae et morum.

VI. De custodia angelorum.

VII. De infantibus in Ecclesia insigne testimonium, quod Deo placeant.

De primo.

Discamus in sanctis etiam esse errores et peccata, sicut hic Apostoli adhuc imaginantur, regnum Christi fore mundanam politiam, in qua, ut in regno, sint futuri gradus dissimili potestate. Plus mali fuit, si etiam ambitione, invidia, aemulatione Apostoli certaverunt, et alius alteri se suo iudicio praetulit, sicuti in Luca significatur, capite 22.

De secundo. Vidit haud dubie Christus, quantum mali pariturae essent hae opiniones de constituendo regno in Ecclesia, inde enim multa sequuntur: Episcopi armati potestate, condunt leges, instituunt cultus, ceremonias, ut Missam et similes. Haec postea putatur iusticia Evangelii, ita opprimitur veritas. Praeterea cum accedit ambitio, quanti motus oriuntur? ut Arius praeferri sibi doluit Alexandrum in electione Episcopi: et omnes aetates viderunt similia exempla. Item, Romae quanta fuerunt certamina de electione ante mille annos? Unde vox illa orta est: Plures Romuli more, quam Petri pervenire ad Episcopatum. Sed multo plus mali peperit ambitio ingeniorum de laude doctrinae contendentium, unde sunt ortae haereses, schismata, et multae aliae perniciosae mutationes. Sicut ex Ariana dissensione ortus est Mahomet, inde secuta est vastitas Ecclesiarum. Haec omnia intuens Christus, hic tam duriter concionatur de scandalis, et nos admonet, ut verbo regi velimus, ut caveamus ambitiosa certamina de doctrina, et de ministerio.

De tertio.

Quam constituit hic formam regiminis? Principalis responsio est in hoc dicto: Si quis puerum recipit in nomine Meo, me recipit. Hic ostendit se alligare Ecclesiam, non ad ullius hominis personam, sed ad verbum suum. Ideo inquit, sive alius verbum meum attulerit, audite. Verbo regi vos volo, non gradibus personarum. Hoc vult, cum ait, Si quis puerum receperit in nomine meo, id est, verbum meum afferentem, et postulat ut ipsi Apostoli sint humiles more infantum, nihil adhuc de regno disputantium. Est enim facilis et illustris applicatio seu collatio. Nam fortiora naturaliter sibi sumunt imperium in inferiora. Ideo infantia sentiens imbecillitatem, nondum sumit sibi imperium in alios, etsi fortassis alia natura magis, alia minus obtemperat, tamen omnes infantes metuunt grandiores. Est igitur perspicua collatio, et detrahit potestatem gubernatoribus Ecclesiae. Ut infantes non sumunt sibi imperium in alios, sed accipiunt dictata a fortioribus, sic vult Christus Episcopos sine imperio circumferre dictata in Evangelio tradita. Videmus igitur displicere Christo hanc tetram dominationem in Ecclesia constitutam, quae quidem etiam iniustas leges, impios cultus, tyrannicis imperiis retinet, et defendit.

Et accedunt multa alia ingentia peccata. Peculiaris doctrina est Christianorum, de voluntate Dei statuere ex ipsius verbo, non ex opinionibus nostris aut eventibus. Ideo ut verbi autoritas amplificetur et magnifiat, Christus abducit homines a conspectu personarum, et monstrat verum ac solum gubernatorem, scilicet, vocem Evangelii, sicut alibi saepe dicitur: Lucerna pedibus meis verbum tuum. Item: Hunc audite, Si quis sermonem meum servabit, mortem non videbit.

Sed humana ratio leviter curat verbum Dei, et de Ecclesia cogitat sicut de humana politia, et in omnibus tentationibus prona est ad amplectenda ea, quae ratio ostendit. Ideo Christus hic revocat nos ad verbum, et vult nos meminisse, verbum esse rectorem, non personas, non humanam rationem.

De quarto. De cavendis scandalis.

Scandalum est falsa doctrina seu pravum exemplum, quod aliis nocet, vel quia invitat ad imitandum, vel quia accersit poenas publicas, vel quia alienat animos a societate rerum bonarum, vel quia praebet occasionem malis, de Deo et de rebus divinis male loquendi.

Gradus quinque facimus. Primus, est falsa doctrina. Hoc genus scandali nocentissimum est.

Secundus, pravum exemplum, quod imitatione nocet, ut invocatio Sanctorum. Item multa alia manifesta delicta, quae invitant alios ad peccandum, aut exemplo licentiam augent, ut helluationes, scortationes etc.

Tertius gradus est, non tantum manifestorum scelerum, sed etiam arcanorum, quae accersunt poenas publicas, bella, seditiones, et alia mala, quae secum multiplicia peccata trahunt.

Est autem miserrimum sustinere conscientiam, quod propter nostram culpam infinita multitudo pereat. Ut enim propter Adae et Evae delictum totum genus humanum periit, ut propter Davidis adulterium, propter idololatriam Achas, Manassae, secutae sunt ingentes publicae poenae, ita semper in mundo vagantur publicae poenae, ortae ab aliquibus singulorum peccatis.

Et de filiis Eli dicitur 1.

Reg. 2.: Erat peccatum puerorum grande coram Domino, quia detrahebant homines sacrificio Domini. Has sententias meminerimus, ut cogitemus in singulis pravis factis accedere hoc peccatum, quod laeditur gloria nominis Dei.

Praeterea meminerimus has severissimas minas: Vae illi, per quem venit scandalum. Haec dicta testantur gravissime puniri scandala, praesentibus et aeternis poenis.

De quinto. De custodia angelorum.

Extat hic perspicuum testimonium, additos esse custodes angelos piis.

Hic colligantur similia testimonia, ut, comes Elisaei videt se stipatum esse magno exercitu angelorum. Et consideretur hic antithesis malorum et bonorum angelorum. Malis duo vitia praecipua tribuuntur, quod sint mendaces, blasphemi adversus Deum, et homicidae, ut in Paradiso utrunque ostendit diabolus.

Excutit enim Evae mandatum Dei offusa alia opinione, Eritis sicut dii, et traxit totum genus humanum in aeternam mortem. Idem adhuc conatur, impellit levia ingenia ad epicureas opiniones, aut alias falsas opiniones amplectendas et serendas. Conatur in aeternam mortem pertrahere, quotquot potest, causa est necis corporalis, et plurimarum calamitatum hominibus, ut per eas pertrahat languefactos animos ad desperationem, et aeternam mortem, impellit impios ad omnis generis flagitia, libidines, et caedes iniustas, sicut historia totius mundi omnium temporum ostendit, quae commemorat horribilia flagitia, iniusta bella.

Adversus haec tanta mala dux est nobis liberator filius Dei Emanuel, qui destruit opera diaboli, et mittit piis bonos angelos, ad impediendos multos conatus malorum.

Quartus gradus est, pravum exemplum, quod alienat animos a societate rerum bonarum, ut decora docentium aut principum, alienant animos ab Evangelio.

Ducum turpitudines, ut Antonii, Saulis, languefaciunt animos exercituum, quia iudicant Deum puniturum esse scelera ducum. Huc etiam pertinet in mediis factis petulantia et pertinacia. Petulanter utens libertate apud pios nondum institutos, alienat eos.

Rursus pertinaciter retinens superstitiones, confirmat errores, et sauciat aliorum piorum, qui libertate utuntur, infirmas mentes, et contristat Spiritum sanctum. Quintus gradus est, qui etiam spargitur in omnes, propterea quod mali de Deo, et de rebus divinis sumunt occasionem probabilem ex pravis exemplis male loquendi, ut Semeias propter Davidis delictum, tam habet speciosum argumentum, quo persuadeat Davidem non esse regem divinitus vocatum, nec Prophetam.

Nam Propheta non videtur ita ruere. Ita Ezechiel dicit: Propter vos contumelia afficitur Deus inter gentes.

De sexto.

Diligenter hic observandum est testimonium, quod infantes inserti Ecclesiae placeant Deo, et sint haeredes vitae aeternae.

De talibus enim clare dicitur: Non est voluntas patris, ut pereat unus de parvulis istis.

## 18:1 Sermons on Matthew: Argument
Chapter XVIII.

At that time the disciples came to Jesus, saying: Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?

This chapter speaks principally of the ministry of the Gospel, and of jurisdiction in the Church, of excommunication and the remission of sins, and the reception of the fallen.

The principle from which he arrives at the ministry of the Gospel is the refutation of the human opinion concerning the polity of the Church. The Apostles imagine that the Church will be a republic similar to a kingdom, or other empires of the world, where there will be future degrees of power and dignity, fortified by authority, wealth, and arms, such as a king, leaders, prefects, and then other degrees. And with this opinion accepted, ambitious struggles arise, just as a certain Pope said, that more have arrived at the Pontificate in the manner of Romulus than in the manner of Peter.

He therefore prohibits in the first part that such an empire be made in the Church as the Papistic one, where the supreme Bishop assumes for himself authority, like a king, above the laws. But he wants the word of God to have supreme authority, whether it be recited by a boy or by the powerful. And it is a commendation of the common ministry of all who teach rightly. God wants his voice to be heard in the whole human race, without respect of persons, whether a Bishop, or a Priest, or a Sexton teaches. He therefore prohibits all struggles of ambition, and prohibits the Papacy from being instituted. And Christ, reciting this sad sermon against ambition and the political opinions of the world, saw in his mind how much evil ambition has brought to all ages, and will bring.

And Jesus calling a little child, set him in the midst of them, and said: Amen I say to you, unless you be converted, etc.

II. This passage is a clear testimony that children are pleasing to God in the Church. By this testimony let us confirm the faith in us concerning our infants.

But he brings forward a child for this reason, that he may teach the disciples and all ministers of the Gospel to be without ambition, like children. He also commands the people to listen equally to all who bring the word of God. And thus he removes political imaginations, and testifies that in the Church there do not reign degrees of men, as in empires, but only the voice of the Gospel, whether someone is called a Bishop or a Priest. And that the Church is there where the voice of the Gospel sounds and is received, whether there are names of dignities there or not.

But on the contrary, the Synagogue and the Pontiffs always contended that the Church was among them, on account of titles and ordinary succession, as they call it.

Utility.

Let us learn therefore: 1) What is the Church? 2) That the ministry is to be venerated, and obeyed. 3) Let us console ourselves against those who cry out that we have defected from the Church, etc.

But whoever shall scandalize one of these little ones who believe in Me, it is better for him that a millstone be hung about his neck, and he be drowned in the depth of the sea. Woe to the world because of scandals.

III. Now follows the doctrine concerning scandal. Here let the division be taken from the commonplaces. One is Pharisaical scandal. Another is given scandal, Ein unrecht vnd schädlich Ergernis, which is false doctrine, or some evil work, the imitation of which harms others. Or it is an indifferent work, not done opportunely, which alienates the wills of the weak from the Gospel. Let the rules therefore be recited, which scandals it is necessary to avoid, and conversely where one must resist the Pharisees, even if they say they are offended.

Latin:

Caput XVIII.

In illo tempore accesserunt discipuli ad Ie- sum, dicentes: Quis maximus est in regno coelorum?

Hoc caput principaliter loquitur de ministe- rio Evangelii, et de iurisdictione in Ecclesia, de excommunicatione et remissione peccatorum, ac receptione lapsorum.

Principium, a quo pervenit ad ministerium Evangelii, est reprehensio humanae opinionis de politia Ecclesiae. Apostoli fingunt Ecclesiam fore rempublicam similem regno, aut aliis mundi imperiis, ubi sint futuri gradus potentiae et digni- tatis, muniti autoritate, opibus et armis, ut rex, duces, praefecti, et deinde alii gradus. Et hac opinione recepta oriuntur ambitiosa certamina, sicut quidam Papa dixit, plures ad Pontificatum pervenisse, more Romuli, quam more Petri.

Prohibet igitur in prima parte, in Ecclesia fieri imperium tale, quale est Papisticum, ubi summus Episcopus sumit sibi autoritatem, sicut rex, supra leges. Sed vult verbum Dei habere summam autoritatem, sive a puero, sive a po- tentibus recitetur. Et est commendatio commu- nis ministerii omnium recte docentium. Deus vult audiri suam vocem in toto genere humano, sine respectu personarum, sive Episcopus, sive Sacerdos, sive Aedituus doceat. Prohibet igitur omnia certamina ambitionum, et prohibet institui Papatum. Et Christus hanc tristem concionem recitans contra ambitionem et politicas opiniones mundi, vidit mente, quantum mali ambitio omni- bus aetatibus attulerit, et allatura sit.

Et advocans Iesus parvulum, statuit eum in medio eorum, et dixit: Amen dico vobis, nisi conversi fueritis, etc.

II. Hic locus perspicuum testimonium est, quod pueri in Ecclesia placeant Deo. Hoc testi- monio confirmemus fidem in nobis de nostris in- fantibus.

Sed ideo adducit puerum, ut doceat disci- pulos et omnes ministros Evangelii, ut sint sine ambitione, ut pueri. Praecipit etiam populo, ut audiant aequaliter omnes, adferentes verbum Dei. Et sic tollit politicas imaginationes, et testatur, quod in Ecclesia non regnent gradus hominum, ut in imperiis, sed sola vox Evangelii, sive ali- quis vocetur Episcopus, sive Sacerdos. Et quod Ecclesia sit ibi, ubi vox Evangelii sonat et reci- pitur, sive sint ibi nomina dignitatum, sive non sint.

At contra semper Synagoga et Pontifices con- tenderunt apud se esse Ecclesiam, propter titulos, et ordinariam successionem, ut vocant.

Utilitas.

Discamus ergo: 1) Quid sit Ecclesia? 2) Quod ministerium sit venerandum, et ei obediendum. 3) Consolemur nos contra illos, qui clamant, nos defecisse ab Ecclesia, etc.

Qui autem scandalizaverit unum de pusillis istis, qui in Me credunt, expedit ei, ut mola asinaria suspendatur in collo eius, et demergatur in profundum maris. Vae mundo a scandalis.

III. Nunc sequitur doctrina de scandalo. Hic sumatur ex locis communibus divisio. Aliud est scandalum Pharisaicum. Aliud datum scandalum, Ein unrecht vnd schädlich Ergernis, quod est falsa doctrina, seu malum aliquod opus, cuius imitatio nocet aliis. Vel est medium opus, non factum opportune, quod alienat voluntates imbecillium ab Evangelio. Recitentur ergo regulae, quae scandala ne- cesse sit vitare, et rursus ubi sit resistendum Pha- risaeis, etiamsi dicunt se offendi.

## 18:13 Sermons on Matthew
A sermon on the ninety-nine sheep.

Let the similitude be recited, as it is placed in the text. And let the narrative be added, which is in chapter 15 of Luke, concerning him who takes the found sheep onto his shoulder etc.

Moreover, the sum of this similitude is the doctrine of repentance. And the consolation showing the will of God, that He ardently wishes to remit sins, provided that we begin to do repentance.

And this image entirely agrees with the oath: As I live, I do not desire the death of the sinner, but that he be converted and live. All these sayings must be diligently and often pondered, so that we may recognize the magnitude of God's love toward us, and invited by such great goodness, may return to repentance: and may confirm our faith with these manifest promises and commands, and in faith may prayer become more ardent. The outcome will show that such prayer is not in vain. But we are cold, and we neither care for repentance, nor stir up faith, nor exercise prayer, because we do not ponder these sweetest sermons and promises, we do not read, we do not hear the Gospel.

Of the parts of repentance.

But what repentance is, and what its parts are, you often hear. You ought to know, however, that the chief parts of repentance are three: contrition, faith, and new obedience. First, let there be some contrition, that is, some dread and fear of the wrath and judgment of God and of punishments, and sorrow that you have offended God.

That such sorrow is necessary, Paul confirms, who says in 2 Corinthians 7: "Godly sorrow produces repentance leading to salvation."

Carnal security is very displeasing to God, just as in Jeremiah chapter 6 He rebukes the people: "They did not know how to blush." Certainly this drunken, secure, and bestial life, thinking nothing of the wrath and judgment of God, does not please God. Therefore, let us ponder the wrath and judgment of God, and let us be terrified. For this reason, God chastises us with so many scourges, so that He may shake that security out of us.

Let the second part be faith.

Because God does not want us to be only in sorrow, but He also wants us to be comforted. And here it must be known that the Monks taught wrongly, who said that men merit the remission of sins on account of sufficient contrition. There can be no sufficient contrition. And that false imagination obscures the glory of Christ and takes away faith. Let us know this for certain, that God wills to remit sins on account of the Son freely, that is, not on account of any merits of ours.

This true and salutary consolation must be held; this is the light of the Gospel, as it is clearly said in Acts 10: "To Him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in Him receives remission of sins through His name." And Romans 3: "We are justified freely, by grace through Christ, by faith, etc."

Third part.

Nor should this faith be idle, but let it kindle prayer, and let us begin to have a good purpose and a good conscience. And let Paul's rule always be before our eyes: "Wage the good warfare, having faith and a good conscience." Let this be the rule of life. And this simple and plain doctrine of repentance can be understood by all the pious.

The dreams of the Monks could not be understood. But we are ungrateful, and it is no wonder that the world is punished, when there is such great light of this doctrine, and few are amended, few care, indeed few learn. Therefore, horrible punishments come. If your brother sins against you, etc.

This sermon of Christ has been wrongly explained as being only about fraternal reconciliation, when it speaks of the ministry and the judgments of the Church, and what the process in the judgments of the Church ought to be. For since in every polity there must be a jurisdiction restraining the contumacious and protecting the obedient, the Apostles could ask: What will happen in our kingdom? If we are not kings, we will not have weapons, how will we coerce or restrain those who do not obey? Christ answers, establishing the order of Ecclesiastical judgment: "If he does not hear you, tell it to the Church. If he does not hear the Church, let him be to you like a Gentile and a tax collector." This punishment is excommunication.

But first, let a distinction be established between political power, secular authority, and Ecclesiastical power, the preaching office. Political power, or the power bearing the sword, is power ordained by God for maintaining discipline and peace. And it restrains the contumacious by corporal force. Here, no admonition precedes. When a crime is manifest, such as theft, or homicide, or adultery, then the magistrate must punish the guilty party, whether the guilty party turns to God or does not turn. And this judgment of the political magistrate is a matter outside the Church. But Ecclesiastical power is power ordained by God for teaching the Gospel and for the administration of the sacraments, and for announcing the remission of sins publicly or privately to those doing repentance, and for punishing the contumacious not by corporal force, but by excommunication.

And this power is commended principally to the Church, that is, to the pastors and the principal persons in the whole body of the Church. Having considered this distinction, let us then know that God wills that there be in the Church judgments concerning manifest offenses against doctrine or morals: and that those guilty of false doctrine, or of evil morals, be excommunicated.

But although such judgments remain in some way, yet it is to be lamented that they are not exercised more severely. But the political power hinders it.

And it must be confessed that Bishops and the Pope have abused this authority. It was the custom to excommunicate men on account of money owed and on account of other business pertaining to the political forum.

This custom was evil. Because the Ecclesiastical power ought to seek amendment in doctrine and morals: it ought not to conduct business immediately pertaining to the political forum.

Secondly, this process is ordered: Before condemnation, an admonition ought to precede, because the Ecclesiastical power seeks amendment. But the political [power] does not seek amendment, but punishment. Thirdly: If the admonition has not profited, having been made by the pastor and other judges ordained in the Church, then one must proceed to punishment.

There were, however, two punishments.

One milder: separation for a time, on account of the hope of amendment. The other harsher: excommunication, which pronounces that the condemned is not a member of the Church, and as long as he remains contumacious, it pronounces that sins are not remitted to him, and that he is guilty of eternal damnation.

This punishment is by no means to be despised. And these judgments have always been in the Church from the beginning.

Let this suffice to have said concerning judgments.

Latin:

Concio de nonaginta novem ovibus.

Recitetur similitudo, sicut in textu ponitur. Et adiungatur narratio, quae est in capite 15. Lucae, de eo qui inventam ovem tollit in hume- rum etc.

Est autem summa huius similitudinis, doctri- na de poenitentia. Et consolatio ostendens vo- luntatem Dei, quod ardenter velit remittere pec- cata, modo ut incipiamus agere poenitentiam.

Et prorsus congruit haec imago cum iura- mento: Vivo ego, nolo mortem peccatoris, sed ut convertatur et vivat. Haec dicta omnia diligenter et saepe cogitanda sunt, ut magnitudinem amoris Dei erga nos agnoscamus, et tanta bonitate invitati, redeamus ad poenitentiam: et fidem confirmemus his manifestis promissionibus et mandatis, et in fide fiat ardentior invocatio. Talem invocationem eventus ostendet non esse inanem. Sed sumus frigidi, nec poenitentiam curamus, nec excitamus fidem, nec exercemus invocationem, quia has dulcissimas conciones et promissiones non cogitamus, non legimus, non audimus Evangelium.

De partibus poenitentiae.

Quid autem sit poenitentia, et quae sint eius partes, saepe auditis. Scire autem debetis, quod praecipuae partes poenitentiae tres sint: contritio, fides, et nova obedientia. Primum sit aliqua contritio, id est, aliquis pavor, et metus irae ac iudicii Dei et poenarum, et dolor, quod Deum offenderis.

Quod autem talis dolor sit necessarius, confirmat Paulus, qui inquit 2. ad Corinth. 7. Tristitia secundum Deum efficit poenitentiam ad salutem.

Valde displicet Deo carnalis securitas, sicut apud Ieremiam cap. 6. obiurgat populum: Erubescere nescierunt. Certe haec ebria, secura et bestialis vita, nihil cogitans de ira et iudicio Dei, non placet Deo. Ideo cogitemus iram et iudicium Dei, et expavescamus. Deus ideo tot flagellis castigat nos, ut nobis illam securitatem excutiat.

Secunda pars sit fides.

Quia non vult Deus nos tantum in dolore esse, sed vult nos etiam consolari. Et hic sciendum est, quod male docuerint Monachi, qui dixerunt, homines propter sufficientem contritionem mereri remissionem peccatorum. Nulla potest esse sufficiens contritio. Et illa falsa imaginatio obscurat gloriam Christi, et tollit fidem. Hoc sciamus certo, quod velit Deus peccata remittere propter filium gratis, id est, non propter ulla nostra merita.

Haec consolatio vera et salutaris tenenda est, haec est lux Evangelii, ut Act. 10. clare dicitur: Huic omnes Prophetae testimonium perhibent, accipere remissionem peccatorum per nomen eius, omnes, qui credunt in eum. Et Roman. 3. Iustificamur autem gratis, per gratiam propter Christum, fide, etc.

Tertia pars.

Nec sit haec fides otiosa, sed accendat invocationem, et incipiamus habere bonum propositum, et bonam conscientiam. Et semper sit nobis regula Pauli in conspectu: Milita bonam militiam, habens fidem et bonam conscientiam. Haec sit regula vitae. Et haec simplex et plana doctrina de poenitentia ab omnibus piis intelligi potest.

Monachorum somnia non potuerunt intelligi. Sed sumus ingrati, et nihil mirum est, puniri mundum, cum lux tanta sit huius doctrinae, et pauci emendentur, pauci curent, imo pauci discant. Ideo veniunt poenae horribiles. Si peccaverit in te frater tuus etc.

Haec concio Christi male enarrata est de sola reconciliatione fraterna, cum de ministerio et iudiciis Ecclesiae loquatur, et qualis esse processus in iudiciis Ecclesiae debeat. Cum enim in omni politia oporteat esse iurisdictionem compescentem contumaces, et tuentem obedientes, quaerere poterant Apostoli: Quid fiet in nostro regno? Si non erimus reges, non habebimus arma, quomodo coërcebimus aut compescemus eos qui non obtemperant? Respondet Christus, sanciens ordinem iudicii Ecclesiastici: Si non audierit te, dic Ecclesiae. Si Ecclesiam non audiet, sit tibi sicut Ethnicus et publicanus. Haec poena est excommunicatio.

Primum autem constituatur discrimen inter potestatem politicam, Weltliche Oberkeit, et inter potestatem Ecclesiasticam, Predigampt. Potestas politica, seu potestas gerens gladium, est potestas a Deo ordinata ad custodiendam disciplinam et pacem. Et coërcet contumaces vi corporali. Hic non praecedit admonitio. Quando delictum est manifestum, ut furtum, vel homicidium, vel adulterium, tunc magistratus debet reum punire, sive reus convertatur ad Deum, sive non convertatur. Et hoc iudicium politici magistratus, est res extra Ecclesiam. Sed Ecclesiastica potestas, est potestas a Deo ordinata, ad docendum Evangelium et ad administrationem sacramentorum, et ad annuntiandum remissionem peccatorum publice vel privatim, agentibus poenitentiam, et ad puniendos contumaces non vi corporali, sed excommunicatione.

Et haec potestas est commendata principaliter Ecclesiae, id est, pastoribus et praecipuis personis in toto corpore Ecclesiae. Hac distinctione considerata, deinde sciamus, Deum velle ut sint in Ecclesia iudicia de manifestis delictis contra doctrinam vel mores: et ut excommunicentur rei falsae doctrinae, vel malorum morum.

Etsi autem utcunque talia iudicia manent, tamen dolendum est, non severius ea exerceri. Sed potestas politica impedit.

Et fatendum est, Episcopos et Papam hac autoritate abusos esse. Fuit consuetudo excommunicare homines propter pecuniam debitam et propter alia negotia, pertinentia ad forum politicum.

Haec consuetudo mala fuit. Quia potestas Ecclesiastica debet quaerere emendationem in doctrina et moribus: non debet agere negotia immediate ad forum politicum pertinentia.

Secundo ordinatur hic processus: Ante condemnationem debet praecedere admonitio, quia potestas Ecclesiastica quaerit emendationem. Sed politica non quaerit emendationem, sed poenam. Tertio: Si admonitio non profuit, facta per pastorem et alios iudices in Ecclesia ordinatos, tunc procedendum est ad poenam.

Fuerunt autem duae poenae.

Una mitior: separatio ad tempus, propter spem emendationis. Altera durior: excommunicatio, quae pronuntiat, condemnatum non esse membrum Ecclesiae, et donec manet contumax, pronuntiat ei non remitti peccata, et eum reum esse aeternae damnationis.

Haec poena nequaquam contemnenda est. Et semper in Ecclesia inde usque ab initio haec iudicia fuerunt.

Haec satis sit dixisse de iudiciis.

## 18:18 Sermons on Matthew
Amen, Amen I say to you: Whatsoever you shall bind upon earth, shall be bound also in heaven, etc.

Afterwards in the text follow general doctrines concerning the remission of sins, and concerning the common congregation of the Church.

Christ expressly gives the command to remit sins, and affirms that the voice of absolution is true in heaven: Whatsoever you shall bind upon earth, shall be bound in heaven.

Item: Whatsoever you shall loose upon earth, shall be loosed in heaven. Here let all the pious learn that the voice of the Gospel is this very voice, announcing that sins are remitted to those doing penance.
