This description, as is evident, signifies that the kingdom of Christ will not be a worldly empire, but a spiritual kingdom, which, although it is begun in this flesh, will nevertheless be more clearly seen and perfected after the resurrection.

And these descriptions are to be referred to the whole kingdom, both that which is begun and that which is to come.

And indeed, it discourses specifically about the death of the Messiah and the manner of liberation.

In the blood of your testament, you will lead forth the prisoners from the pit, that is, the Messiah, by his blood, with which he will confirm the testament and the covenant of eternal life, will lead forth the prisoners from the pit, that is, he will deliver the dead from the captivity of death and sin.

Therefore he says here, He will come poor, that is, not as a worldly victor, but as one about to undergo the cross.

It is profitable, however, to hold these testimonies of the Prophets, not only against the Jews, but also against our own hypocrites, who do not rightly understand the kingdom of Christ, who do not know that the chief benefit is that he blotted out sin by his death, that he was made a victim for us.

They do not know that this must be apprehended by faith, they do not know that by this faith sin and death are conquered, and thus the kingdom of Christ is begun in this life, and at the same time the flesh is subjected to the cross and mortification.

Meanwhile, fanatical men falsely imagine the kingdom of Christ to be either a papal polity or a Cynic polity, such as the Anabaptist one.

Third.

When we say what kind of kingdom Christ’s is, and what his benefits are, it must be added what the proper forms of worship are in that kingdom. These also are proposed in this triumph: the chief one is the true acknowledgment of this savior, and faith, by which we believe that he was made a victim for our sins, etc.

As John says: Everyone who believes in the Son has eternal life.

The second is to celebrate and confess this very doctrine, just as the pious here add auspicious prayers from the Psalms, and confess that this is the Messiah.

Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord: that is, This King sent by God is blessed, that is, he is loved, he is helped by God, he will perform great deeds, he will deliver the people from eternal evils.

Hosanna to the son of David, that is, may God grant salvation, prosperity, and success to the son of David, may God be present, may he govern his struggles.

Moreover, this whole Psalm must be considered in one’s mind, which itself also describes this kingdom of Christ.

Then, the remaining forms of worship are to cast off garments, that is, in confession to bring one’s fortune and body into danger.

Likewise, to contribute garments, that is, fortunes, to aid the ministry.

Likewise, to offer Christ the palm and the olive, that is, to acknowledge him as leader, not to act against his will, nor to serve the kingdom of the devil.

Fourth.

The picture of the triumphal procession is an image of the Church of all times. These four persons are always to be considered in the Church.

Christ, the Apostles, the hearers, and the adversaries.

Christ is to be acknowledged as King and Savior.

He sits upon a donkey and a colt, that is, the people of the law, and the untamed nations who lived without the law.

True ministers, Prophets, Apostles, and other pious teachers bring the hearers and set Christ upon them.

The pious people sing to Christ, that is, they confess him, they spread their garments, they aid the ministry, they offer palms, that is, they confess him to be the victor and profess that they too will undergo struggles, in the confidence of this victor, and yet they offer palms to him, they acknowledge that they conquer through him and by his help, they offer olives, that is, they seek peace from him, and confess him to be the author of eternal peace with God.

For thus were triumphing kings once received: by palms, the praise of victory was attributed to them; olives signified that the conquered were seeking peace.

Now let us remember that we too are in this assembly.

We spread our garments when we aid the ministry or come into danger on account of confession.

We offer palms when we undergo labors and struggles looking toward the glory of Christ.

Thus the studies of the pious are palms.

We offer olives when we preach the author of peace and ourselves aid, retain, etc., the true peace of the Church.

The chief priests and Pharisees, however, burning with hatred for Christ and indignant, forbid him to be received in this way. Such are always the hypocrites who oppose the Gospel. Wherefore let us not be deterred from the Gospel by the judgments of the chief priests and Pharisees. Let us know that the Church is always engaged in such struggles.

On the other hand, one must also consider the contrary picture of the chief priests, who impose themselves on the back of the people, that is, who prefer impious and idolatrous worship to the commands of God. Likewise, those who trample upon Christ and his members.

But the impious also have those who offer olives and palms, that is, who offer flattery to the impious chief priests, but throw stones at Christ. Let us set these images before our eyes, so that they may warn us of the distinction between the true and the false Church, and may stir up the recognition of Christ and true worship, and confirm us against scandals, that is, against the power and authority of the adversaries. Second Sunday.

Latin:

Dominica prima Adventus.

Evangelium

Matth. 21. Et cum appropinquassent Hierosolymis, et venissent Bethphage ad montem Olivarum, tunc Iesus misit duos discipulos, dicens eis: Ite in castellum, quod contra vos est, et statim invenietis asinam alligatam, et pullum cum ea, solvite et adducite mihi. Et si quis vobis aliquid dixerit, dicite: Dominus his opus habet, et confestim emittet eos. Hoc autem totum factum est, ut adimpleretur, quod dictum est per Prophetam dicentem: Dicite filiae Sion, Ecce rex tuus venit tibi mansuetus, sedens super asinam et pullum filium subiugalis. Euntes autem discipuli, fecerunt sicut praeceperat illis Iesus. Et adduxerunt asinam et pullum, et imposuerunt super eos vestimenta sua, et eum super illam collocaverunt. Plurima autem turba straverunt vestimenta sua in via. Alii vero caedebant ramos de arboribus, et sternebant in via. Porro turbae quae praecedebant et sequebantur clamabant, dicentes: Hosanna filio David, Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini, Hosanna in altissimis.

Quatuor sunt praecipui loci huius Evangelii.

I. Pompa ingressus. II. Quale sit regnum Christi. III. Qui sint veri cultus in eo regno. IV. Pompa triumphalis est pictura Ecclesiae.

Primus. Pompa ingressus est publicum testimonium exhibiti Messiae qui promissus fuerat. Voluit enim Deus esse multiplicia testimonia exhibitae promissionis, ad confirmandos pios, et refutandos impios.

Sicut initio Angeli, Pastores, Elisabeth, Zacharias, Iohannes Baptista, fuerunt testes, et accesserunt miracula ipsius Christi, et sonuit vox Dei de coelo, Hic est Filius meus dilectus: ita habet Evangelium sua testimonia, non est ignotum, tametsi res illae non ita geruntur in conspectu omnium, ut res Alexandri, aut Iulii.

Secundus.

Quale sit regnum Messiae, describitur in dicto Zachariae: Ecce rex tuus venit tibi iustus, salvator, et pauper sedens super asinam etc. Sed tota concio apud Zachariam intuenda est, quae docet regnum Christi non fore politiam mundanam, Non erunt, inquit, deinceps in Israël, equi, quadrigae, arcus belli.

Haec descriptio, sicut constat, significat regnum Christi non fore mundanum imperium, sed spirituale regnum, quod etsi in hac carne incoatur, tamen post resurrectionem magis conspicietur, et perficietur.

Et hae descriptiones ad totum regnum, incoatum et futurum referendae sunt.

Et quidem nominatim de morte Messiae, et modo liberationis concionatur.

In sanguine testamenti tui, educes vinctos de lacu, id est, Messias suo sanguine, quo confirmabit testamentum, et pactum vitae aeternae, educet vinctos de lacu, id est, mortuos liberabit a captivitate mortis et peccati.

Ideo hic ait, Veniet pauper, id est, non ut victor mundanus, sed ut crucem subiturus.

Prodest autem haec testimonia Prophetarum tenere, non solum contra Iudaeos, sed etiam contra nostros hypocritas, qui non recte intelligunt regnum Christi, non norunt praecipuum beneficium esse, quod delevit peccatum sua morte, quod est factus victima pro nobis.

Non norunt hoc apprehendendum esse fide, non norunt hac fide vinci peccatum et mortem, et sic incoari regnum Christi in hac vita, et simul carne subiici cruci et mortificationi.

Interim homines fanatici falso imaginantur regnum Christi, aut esse politiam pontificiam, aut politiam Cynicam, qualis est Anabaptistica.

Tertius.

Quando dicimus, quale sit regnum Christi, et quae sint eius beneficia, addendum est, qui sint proprii cultus in eo regno. Hi quoque proponuntur in hoc triumpho: praecipuus est vera agnitio huius salvatoris, et fides, qua credimus eum factum esse victimam pro nostris peccatis, etc.

Sicut Iohannes inquit: Omnis qui credit in Filium, habet vitam aeternam.

Secundus est, hanc ipsam doctrinam celebrare et confiteri, sicut hic pii addunt faustas precationes ex Psalmis, et fatentur hunc esse Messiam.

Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini: id est, Hic Rex a Deo missus, est benedictus, id est, diligitur, adiuvatur a Deo, magnas res geret, liberabit populum ab aeternis malis.

Hosianna filio David, id est, salutem, prosperitatem, successus impertiat Deus filio David, Deus adsit, gubernet eius certamina.

Est autem hic quoque totus Psalmus animo intuendus, qui et ipse describit hoc regnum Christi.

Deinde, reliqui cultus sunt, exuere vestes, id est, in professione fortunam et corpus in discrimen adducere.

Item, conferre vestes, id est, fortunas, ad invandum ministerium.

Item, offerre Christo palmam et oleam, id est, agnoscere eum ducem, non facere contra voluntatem eius, nec servire regno diaboli.

Quartus.

Pictura pompae triumphalis est imago Ecclesiae omnium temporum. Semper hae quatuor personae in Ecclesia considerandae sunt.

Christus, Apostoli, auditores, et adversarii.

Christus est agnoscendus Rex et Salvator.

Hic insidet asinae et pullo, id est, populo legis, et gentibus indomitis, qui sine lege vixerunt.

Veri ministri, Prophetae, Apostoli, et alii pii doctores adducunt auditores, et imponunt Christum.

Populus pius canit Christo, id est, confitetur eum, substernit vestes, iuvat ministerium, Offert palmas, id est, fatetur esse victorem, et profitetur se quoque subiturum esse certamina, fiducia huius victoris, et tamen huic palmas offert, agnoscit se vincere per istum et huius auxilio, Offert oleas, id est, petit ab eo pacem, et fatetur esse autorem aeternae pacis cum Deo.

Sic enim olim triumphantes reges excipiebantur: per palmas tribuebatur eis laus victoriae, oleae significabant victos pacem petere.

Iam meminerimus nos quoque in hoc coetu esse.

Substernimus vestes, cum iuvamus ministerium, aut venimus in periculum propter confessionem.

Offerimus palmas, cum labores et certamina subimus spectantia ad gloriam Christi.

Sic studia piorum sunt palmae.

Offerimus oleas, cum praedicamus et pacis autorem, et ipsi veram pacem Ecclesiae adiuvamus, retinemus etc.

Pontifices autem et Pharisaei ardentes odio Christi et indignantes, vetant eum sic excipi. Tales sunt semper hypocritae adversantes Evangelio. Quare non deterreamur ab Evangelio, propter iudicia Pontificum et Pharisaeorum. Sciamus Ecclesiam semper in talibus certaminibus versari.

Econtra etiam cogitanda est contraria pictura Pontificum, sese imponentium tergo populi, id est, anteferentium impios et idolatricos cultus mandatis Dei. Item, conculcantium Christum, et membra eius.

Habent autem et impii, qui oleas et palmas, id est, assentatione impiis Pontificibus offerunt, saxa vero iaciunt in Christum. Has imagines oculis proponamus, ut nos de discrimine verae et falsae Ecclesiae admoneant, et agnitionem Christi, et veros cultus exuscitent, et confirment adversus scandala, hoc est, potentiam et auctoritatem adversariorum.

## 21:1 Sermons on Matthew: Argument
Chapter XXI.

Go into the village, which is in your sight.

Here, first, the doctrine concerning the kingdom of the Messiah is to be recited. And at the beginning, the dream of the Jews concerning an earthly kingdom is to be narrated and rejected. Secondly, the true narrative concerning the spiritual and eternal kingdom is to be opposed, that the Messiah was promised from the beginning, when the first parents were received after the fall. And that the Church was thus founded by the voice of the promise, so that in it this promise concerning this Lord might always sound, on account of whom the eternal Father is willing to remit sins, and that He is willing to be worshipped and invoked by this faith, that on account of this Lord sins are remitted to those who believe, and we are heard, and we are made heirs of eternal life, and are saved. The Pharisees lost this doctrine necessary to the Church of God, and it has often been obscured, just as before these times it was obscured by the Monks and by the Pope. But after the true doctrine has now been renewed, by the singular benefit of God, let us be diligent in learning it and keeping it, and exercising it in invocation.

Now let it be spoken of the history and of the signification. Why did Christ then enter Jerusalem publicly with such pomp? I answer: God does not want the Church to be invisible, but He wants it to be truly seen and heard among the human race. Therefore He established a certain place, and a certain people, where Christ would be born, would teach, would be seen, would perform miracles, would suffer, and would rise again. Therefore Christ wanted to be seen, He did not want to be hidden. And because He Himself is the true and chief king of this people, therefore He enters the city as a king, but He does not want to have political dominion, but an eternal kingdom, in which He may reign in all eternity with the elect whom He has liberated. But Christ censures many errors of the woman and the Apostles, and signifies that the Church must be subject to the cross in this life. And see the foolishness of the Apostles; they say they can endure that passion which Christ was about to undergo. These things are recounted so that we may consider what great and many infirmities remain in the saints in this life.

But Jesus called them to himself and said: You know that the princes of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those who are greater exercise power among them. It shall not be so among you, etc.

Afterwards, he distinguishes the empires of the world from the Church. And he clearly says that there are ranks in empires, and that some have power over others. As the first place belongs to kings, princes and other inferiors are compelled to obey kings in political affairs. And God wills that kings and princes be equipped with power and authority, so that they may be able to compel inferiors who, in legitimate causes, do not wish to obey. God gave the same power to kings and princes to establish laws concerning civil matters, but not those that conflict with natural and divine law. But in sum, this whole order in empires, by which civil society is governed, is a thing instituted by God and necessary for the common society.

But it differs from the Ecclesiastical ministry. The ministry of the Gospel, the preaching office, is the ministry of teaching the Gospel and administering the sacraments, and it does not have corporal power and authority to compel men; therefore, they themselves do not have ranks among them, as are the ranks of kings and princes. Nor are they equipped with power and wealth, as kings are, nor do they have the power to establish new laws and institute new forms of worship. The Pope and the Bishops have perverted all these things, who from the Ecclesiastical ministry have made a worldly kingdom, and having oppressed the Gospel, have sought wealth and corporal authority, and have neglected the ministry of the Gospel, and have established new laws and idols.

The Son of man came to give his life as a ransom (λύτρον) for many. This is a remarkable sentence, which must be diligently considered, so that we may think about what a great thing sin is, and on the other hand, how great is the severity of God's justice, and then how great is his mercy.

Therefore, let us first learn this: Let us acknowledge that we are weak and hard-hearted, because we do not greatly tremble at the thought of our sins, nor do we see what a great thing sin and the wrath of God is. For although God has for this reason burdened the human race with such various and such many and great calamities, and with death, and with civil punishments, such as the gallows, the wheel, and other tortures, likewise wars, pestilence, famine, and manifold diseases, so that they may be signs reminding us of the wrath of God: yet these so horrendous punishments move few, unless it be those very ones who are suffering. Others lightly regard these terrible signs.

But let us deplore this hardness of ours, and let us truly tremble, and let us think that God is seriously angry at all the sins of the saints and the impious, because God is just, and let us not think that he remits sins out of levity, as if he were not truly angry. But at the same time, these things are: he is truly angry at sins, and yet he spares his creature, and did not wish it to perish. He is at once just and merciful. And no one can sufficiently express this wonderful mixture of justice and mercy, but we shall learn it in eternal life.

And yet this doctrine must be begun here. For Scripture so often says that the Son was the price and compensation for us. Since such a great price has been paid, it is necessary that the wrath against sin be great. These things must be thought about often and much.

Next, it must be thought about: Why was there a need for a price and such a great sacrifice? To this, it must be answered: God has these two virtues, justice and mercy. And he retains both in a wonderful way.

But it belongs to justice to be angry at sins and to punish them. Since, therefore, God wished to spare the human race, and yet not omit justice, he decreed that he who was the intercessor for us should sustain the punishment for the whole human race. And therefore he wished the Son to assume human nature, because since the human race was guilty, it was necessary for someone in the human race to sustain the punishment, and this one had to be innocent. But in order for such a one, sustaining the punishment, to be a sufficient and equivalent price, and in order to be able to conquer death, it was necessary for this one, sustaining such a burden, to be God, because human nature alone would neither have been an equivalent price, nor could it have sustained the punishment, nor conquered death. Since, therefore, the invocation and studies of such people are pleasing to God, parents should be diligent in accustoming children to prayer and to learning.

Here they should set before themselves the saying of Paul in Ephesians 6: "Bring up your children in the discipline and instruction of the Lord." He commands two things: that children be taught, and indeed about God; secondly, that their morals be governed by honest discipline, and that no license be granted for drinking, gluttonizing, whoring, and committing other sins, just as youth lives most dissolutely now, and is miserably corrupted by wicked associations and examples.

The third doctrine.

The third doctrine is most serious, and proposes an excellent consolation to us old men.

We old men are also children, and very weak. For we do not understand many things, and we have great infirmities in our hearts; we do many things foolishly. But although we do not understand many things, nevertheless God accepts our invocation, and approves our obedience, however beggarly it may be. He receives, cares for, and defends us, just as a mother does children. Indeed, this little verse says more: God accomplishes great things through our invocation, confession, and the ministry of teaching.

Therefore he says: "You have perfected praise." God perfects His own praise, gathers the Church, represses the Devils, and gives us present and eternal goods through this voice sounding in the Church, through weak men: for the saying pertains to us all: "Out of the mouths of infants and nursing babes You have perfected praise."

But why does He say: "nursing babes"? Because it signifies that we all in the Church are nourished by divine milk, that is, by the Word of God and the Holy Spirit. Those salutary works are not done by human virtue.

And let us learn here that God wishes to help us, as is very often said: "Ask and you shall receive." Likewise: "Without me you can do nothing." "He who abides in me will bear much fruit."

"I am the vine, you are the branches." Returning to the city in the morning, He was hungry, and saw a fig tree, etc. This is the day immediately following Palm Sunday, again full of the greatest struggles in the temple, and on that day He spoke those horrible imprecations: "Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees."

And He had many useful sermons about the distinction between the kingdom of the Messiah and the worldly kingdom, about the punishments of the unbelievers, and about the difference between true and false worship. The first story is about the cursing of the fig tree, and about the efficacy of faith.

The story in itself is a miracle, and is a testimony about the teacher and the doctrine, just like many other miracles. Nor does it need another long declaration, nor is there need here for a dispute about how hunger, thirst, bodily fatigue, and then other affections—anger, joy, and sadness—existed in Christ. Although He was without sin, nevertheless the human nature in Him was truly an integral human nature, having all the powers proper to human nature; He truly hungered, truly thirsted, truly was saddened.

But the meaning is proposed in the fig tree. The fig tree signifies the synagogue at any time, that is, then the people of the Jews, and now the Pope and the Monks, that is, those who arrogate to themselves the title of the Church, and have leaves, that is, true doctrine and true worship, just as leaves of the fig tree also signify hypocrisy elsewhere.

As Adam and Eve cover themselves with fig leaves, that is, human nature, after it lost true righteousness, then covers that deformity of its own with some kind of appearance of external righteousness, etc. And yet this does not free one from sin and death. Therefore, just as the fig tree was withered after the curse, so the synagogue has withered, and all the pomp of the Pontiff and Bishops and Canons and Monks will wither, and subsequently, when others also abandon the Word and true worship, then they too will wither.

There follows the doctrine about the efficacy of faith.

A very magnificent promise is proposed here, which both demands faith and affirms that invocation in faith is efficacious. And an oath is added: "Amen I say to you, all things that you ask in your prayer, believing, you shall receive." Observe the particle "all," and learn how it should be rightly and truly understood: all... namely, good things, which do not conflict with the commandments of God.

And first you should know that all things are obtained without any exception which are necessary for the salvation of the soul, such as the remission of sins, and the gift of the Holy Spirit, and eternal life. These goods they are to be sought by name, and you should believe that these very things are certainly given and obtained, just as it is said elsewhere: How much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?

Next, regarding... bodily goods, understand it thus: He also gives all things necessary for the body, but not in kind, nor in the same way.

And yet He gives the goods of the body, in one way or another, because He wants us to be subject to the cross as well. He does not give you the kingdom of France, because such things are not necessary for individuals, but yet He gives you food, health of body, a better state for your sons and daughters, etc.

But here it is objected: Nay, He often allows us to have great poverty, allows us to be sick, as Job, nay, He even allows saints to be miraculously killed, as Jonathan.

To this I answer: It is said regarding bodily things that He does not give them in the same way.

He does indeed give all things necessary, in such a way that He either gives those very goods which we ask for, as He restores David to the kingdom, or at least He mitigates the evil, and gives other goods, as He consoles Jonathan in his heart, and preserves his posterity.

But that He does not give all bodily things in the same way, this happens because He wants us to be subject to the cross, as Job, and sometimes He even punishes us, as David.

But hold this rule most firmly: That an invocation made in faith is never void, even in bodily things, because it always either obtains this very good which it asks for, or a mitigation, as it is often said: Ask and you shall receive.

Likewise: Whatever you ask the Father in my name, He will give to you. But Christ adds in this saying: If you do not doubt.

Likewise: Believing. In these words faith is commanded.

Do not think thus: I will indeed ask, but I do not know if my petition is profitable, perhaps God does not receive my prayers.

Nay, you should conclude most certainly that your prayers are truly heard on account of the Son, and will not be void, and you should retain hope and expectation of help, so that faith and hope may be together, which are now true faith and true hope, when you feel that by this very faith and hope you have a quieter heart, and in some way acquiescing in God.

You shall say to this mountain.

It is a figure, because God does not want miracles to be done out of curiosity, just as the Devil tempts Christ, and commands him to fly.

God wants necessary things to be asked for, and in such necessary things He often helps us above nature.

As when the children of Israel come to the Red Sea, and cannot escape unless the sea yields to them and provides a way, here God helps them with a notable miracle.

And there God says to the mountain, that is, to Pharaoh and his power: You shall be cast into the sea.

For the mountain signifies the power of a great king or prince.

And by this similitude the Lord shows this very thing, that the Church by its prayers and faith is to overcome and repress kings and princes.

Therefore let us be more ardent in asking.

Just as the enemies could not harm Elisha.

Isaiah and Hezekiah conquered Sennacherib by asking for help from God.

Neither princes nor lions could harm Daniel.

Thus God preserves many in the midst of enemies at all times.

Nay, the Church is almost always surrounded on all sides by enemies, and is miraculously preserved amidst the snares of the Devil and the tumults of the world, according to that: The Church is like a rose among thorns.

Likewise: I have given my beloved soul into the midst of its enemies.

He calls the Church his soul, that is, his most dear one; this one, even if it is most dear, yet he says it is surrounded by enemies, and among these it is miraculously protected, because it is most dear to God.

And when he had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him saying: By what authority do you do these things?

It is very necessary to know the difference between sins.

There are three degrees.

One is sins and infirmities, which are born with us, such as doubts, vicious inclinations to anger, to wandering loves, etc.

Likewise many ignorances. The second degree is to violate the commandments of God against conscience, such as adultery, theft, homicide, etc.

Although these two degrees are sins, and God is very angry at them and punishes them, yet they can be forgiven, and are forgiven to those who do penance.

But the third degree is blasphemy: When someone, knowing and convicted by the evidence of the testimonies of scripture or miracles, attacks the acknowledged truth, and yet pertinaciously opposes it, either for the sake of the kingdom or ambition, or hatred, or in any way burning with Diabolical hatred, as now the Papists disapprove of the marriages of priests and defend impious Masses, and the invocation of the dead. Such were the Pharisees then, who although they saw manifest miracles, yet they ask: By what authority do you do these things?

Therefore Christ distinguishes their sin from other degrees. Others arrive at repentance, and are converted. You Pharisees will perish, and you do not wish to be converted. Let us diligently consider these degrees, therefore it is said here: Harlots and publicans will precede you in the kingdom of God.

And so that the stubbornness of the Pharisees might be more conspicuous, Christ makes mention of the preaching of John, as if to say: Already before you showed your impiety and stubbornness, because you wished to hear John, to whom God had given testimonies at his birth, because he was born of a mother who was old and barren. And the Angel had expressly said that he would be a witness of the Messiah. But you stubbornly despised his preaching, now you despise mine. And the Pharisees add impiety to impiety, because they say against their conscience that they do not know whether John was sent by God. Afterwards he proposes an example concerning those who do repentance, and those who do not.

A certain man had two sons. The one said he would not go into the vineyard, and doing repentance, he went. The other said he would go, and did not go. This one, persevering in contumacy, sins more. Such, he says, are the Pharisees. Hear another parable.

A man indeed was a householder, who planted a vineyard, and put a hedge around it, etc.

The householder planted a vineyard, that is, God chose the people of Israel. And he put a hedge around it, that is, the law. And he made a winepress there, that is, the ministry of doctrine. And he built a tower, that is, he gave them a kingdom and a temple. And he let it out to husbandmen, that is, to the seed of Jacob. And he went away, and sent servants, that is, the Prophets at any time, Elijah, Elisha, Isaiah, Zechariah, Jonah, Jeremiah, these the people killed. Finally he sent his son, this one also the people killed. And indeed, so that he might describe the signs of stubbornness and blasphemy, he says by name that they, having shaken off the Lord, wish to establish their own kingdom.

Let us seize, they say, the inheritance, just as afterwards in the passion they say: We do not want this man to reign over us. This blasphemy, and this disease, is the cause of all evils.

The impious wish themselves, by their own judgment, by their own wisdom, by their own will, to establish religions and regimes, and they bend religions to their own convenience, and do not wish to suffer God as governor. Always in their heart they cry: We do not want this man to reign over us. This is a horrendous insanity, to despise God, and to wish to establish religions and kingdoms useful to us, as if God were nothing, just as the kings of Israel, just as Nebuchadnezzar sets up a statue, just as Antiochus and many others wished to institute religions and cults by their own will, as if God were nothing, but their own wisdom were the governess and not God. This evil often rages in the world, and now it also rages.

The Pope and kings also wish to establish a state, such as they themselves wish, having shaken off God, and they cry like the Jews: We do not want this man to reign over us. Let us learn to understand and flee this sin, and let us pray to God, that we may not fall into this blindness, but always with our whole heart let us pray, that the Son of God may be our governor, that he himself may rule, that the inheritance of the kingdom may remain with him.

Here are two opposites.

This is my beloved Son, hear him. And, We do not want this man to reign. Let us obey God who commands that we hear the Son, just as it is also said in the Psalm: Kiss the son. And punishments are added against the despisers of the son: When his wrath shall be kindled. And here concerning the punishment it is said: He will miserably destroy the wicked. God has destroyed such despisers from the beginning, in the flood, in the punishment of the people of Israel, and then with Jerusalem destroyed, so also he will destroy the Canons, and Bishops and Monks.

The saying of the Psalm follows.

The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner. This is the Lord's doing, and it is wonderful in our eyes. You all ought to remember this most sweet verse, and those who can read, let them often read this whole Psalm, which indeed the Jews then sang every Sabbath, and it is a wonder that there was such blindness, that they did not want to understand.

But it clearly predicts that the Messiah would suffer, and yet afterwards he would reign, and would gather an eternal Church. Therefore this short verse teaches us many things, namely:

That the Messiah was to come and to suffer, and that the Synagogue itself would be opposed to the Messiah, and that the Messiah would be a victor, and would gather a Church from the Gentiles and the Jews.

Latin:

Caput XXI.

Ite in castellum, quod est in conspectu vestro.

Hic primum est recitanda doctrina de regno Messiae. Et initio somnium Iudaeorum de regno mundi narrandum et reiiciendum. Secundo opponenda vera narratio de regno spirituali et aeterno, quod Messias ab initio promissus sit, cum primi parentes reciperentur post lapsum. Et quod ita condita sit Ecclesia voce promissionis, ut in ea semper sonaret haec promissio de hoc Domino, propter quem velit Pater aeternus remittere peccata, et quod velit hac fide coli et invocari, quod propter hunc Dominum remittantur peccata credentibus, et exaudiamur, et haeredes vitae aeternae efficiamur, et salvemur. Hanc doctrinam necessariam Ecclesiae Dei amiserunt Pharisaei, et saepe obscurata est, sicut et ante haec tempora a Monachis et a Papa fuit obscurata. Postquam autem iam renovata est vera doctrina, singulari Dei beneficio, simus diligentes in ea discenda et custodienda, et exercenda in invocatione.

Nunc de historia dicatur et de significatione. Quare publice cum tali pompa ingressus est Christus tunc Ierosolymam? Respondeo: Deus vult Ecclesiam non esse invisibilem, sed vult eam vere conspici et exaudiri in genere humano. Ideo locum certum, et gentem certam constituit, ubi nasceretur Christus, doceret, conspiceretur, ederet miracula, pateretur et resurgeret. Ideo voluit Christus conspici, non voluit latere. Et quia ipse est verus et praecipuus rex huius populi, ideo ut rex ingreditur in urbem, sed non vult dominationem politicam habere, sed regnum aeternum, in quo cum electis, quos liberavit, in omni aeternitate regnet. Sed Christus taxat multos errores mulieris et Apostolorum, et significat Ecclesiam oportere in hac vita subiectam esse cruci. Et vide stultitiam Apostolorum, dicunt se posse sustinere illam passionem, quam Christus subiturus erat. Haec recitantur, ut cogitemus, magnas et multas infirmitates in sanctis reliquas esse in hac vita.

Iesus autem vocavit eos ad se, et ait: Scitis quia principes gentium dominantur eorum, et qui maiores sunt, potestatem exercent inter eos. Non ita erit inter vos, etc.

Postea discernit imperia mundi ab Ecclesia. Et clare dicit, in imperiis esse gradus, et alios habere potentiam super alios. Ut primus locus est regum, regibus coguntur obedire in negotiis politicis principes et alii inferiores. Et reges et principes vult Deus instructos esse potentia et praesidiis, ut possint cogere inferiores, qui in causis legitimis nolunt obedire. Idem dedit Deus potestatem regibus et principibus condendi leges de rebus civilibus, sed non pugnantes cum iure naturae et divino. Sed in summa hic totus ordo in imperiis, quo gubernatur civilis societas, est res a Deo instituta, et necessaria communi societati.

Sed differt a ministerio Ecclesiastico. Ministerium Evangelii das Predigampt, est ministerium docendi Evangelium, et sacramenta administrandi, et non habet potentiam corporalem, et praesidia ad cogendos homines, ideo nec ipsi inter se gradus habent, ut sunt regum et principum gradus. Nec sunt instructi potentia et opibus, sicut reges, nec habent potestatem condendi novas leges, et instituendi novos cultus. Haec omnia perverterunt Papa et Episcopi, qui ex ministerio Ecclesiastico fecerunt regnum mundanum, et oppresso Evangelio quaesiverunt opes et praesidia corporalia, et neglexerunt ministerium Evangelii, et condiderunt novas leges, et idola.

Venit Filius hominis dare animam suam λύτρον pro multis. Haec est insignis sententia, quae diligenter consideranda est, ut cogitemus, quanta res sit peccatum, et econtra quanta sit severitas iustitiae Dei, et deinde quanta sit misericordia.

Primum igitur hoc discamus: Agnoscamus nos infirmos et duros esse, quod non valde expavescimus cogitatione peccatorum nostrorum, nec videmus, quanta res sit peccatum et ira Dei. Quanquam enim Deus ideo genus humanum oneravit tam variis et tam multis et magnis calamitatibus, et morte, et poenis civilibus, ut patibulo, rota, et aliis suppliciis, item bellis, pestilentia, fame et morbis multiplicibus, ut sint signa nos commonefacentia de ira Dei: tamen hae tam horrendae poenae paucos movent, nisi tunc illos ipsos, qui patiuntur. Alii leviter curant haec terribilia signa.

Sed hanc nostram duritiem deploremus, et vere expavescamus, et cogitemus, Deum serio irasci peccatis omnibus sanctorum et impiorum, quia Deus est iustus, et non cogitemus eum peccata ex levitate remittere, quasi non vere irascatur. Sed simul illa sunt, vere irascitur peccatis, et tamen parcit suae creaturae, et non voluit eam perire. Simul et iustus et misericors est. Et hanc mirabilem mixturam iustitiae et misericordiae nemo satis eloqui potest, sed in vita aeterna discemus.

Et tamen hic incipienda est haec doctrina. Toties enim scriptura dicit, filium pro nobis fuisse pretium et compensationem. Tantum pretium cum persolutum sit, necesse est iram esse magnam adversus peccatum. Haec saepe et multum cogitanda sunt.

Deinde cogitandum est: Quare opus fuit pretio et tanto sacrificio? Ad hoc respondendum est: Deus habet has duas virtutes, iustitiam et misericordiam. Et utramque retinet mirabili modo.

Iustitiae autem est, irasci peccatis et ea punire. Cum igitur vellet Deus parcere generi humano, et tamen non omittere iustitiam, decrevit, qui erat deprecator pro nobis, sustineret poenam pro toto genere humano. Et ideo voluit filium adsumere naturam humanam, quia cum genus humanum esset reum, oportuit aliquem in genere humano poenam sustinere, et hunc oportuit esse innocentem. Ut autem talis sustinens poenam, esset pretium sufficiens et aequivalens, et ut posset vincere mortem, oportuit hunc sustinentem tantum onus, esse Deum, quia natura humana sola, nec fuisset aequivalens pretium, nec potuisset sustinere poenam, nec vincere mortem. Cum igitur talium invocatio et studia placeant Deo, parentes sint seduli in adsuefaciendis pueris ad precationem et ad discendum.

Hic sibi proponant dictum Pauli Ephes. 6.: Educate pueros in disciplina et doctrina Domini. Duo praecipit, ut pueri doceantur, et quidem de Deo, secundo ut honesta disciplina mores regantur, non concedatur licentia potandi, helluandi, scortandi, et alia delicta faciendi, sic ut nunc dissolutissime vivit adolescentia, et miserabiliter corrumpitur sodalitiis pravis et exemplis.

Tertia doctrina.

Tertia doctrina gravissima est, et nobis senibus consolationem egregiam proponit.

Nos senes etiam sumus pueri, et valde infirmi. Multa enim non intelligimus, et habemus magnas infirmitates in corde, multa stulte facimus. Etsi autem multa non intelligimus, tamen Deus accipit invocationem, approbat obedientiam quanquam mendicam. Recipit et curat et defendit nos, sicut mater pueros. Imo amplius dicit hic versiculus: Deus magnas res efficit per nostram invocationem, confessionem, ministerium docendi.

Ideo inquit: Perfecisti laudem. Deus perficit suam laudem, colligit Ecclesiam, reprimit Diabolos, dat nobis bona praesentia et aeterna, per hanc vocem sonantem in Ecclesia, per homines infirmos: nam ad nos omnes pertinet dictum: Ex ore infantium et lactentium perfecisti laudem.

Quare autem dicit: lactentium? Quia significat nos omnes in Ecclesia ali lacte divino, id est, verbo Dei et Spiritu sancto. Non fiunt illa salutaria opera virtute humana.

Et hic discamus, Deum velle nobis opitulari, sicut saepissime dicitur: Petite et accipietis. Item: Sine me nihil potestis facere. Qui manet in me, fructum copiosum feret.

Ego sum vitis, vos palmites. Mane rediens in urbem, esuriebat, et vidit ficum, etc. Haec est dies proxima post diem palmarum, rursus plena maximorum certaminum in templo, et eo die illas horrendas imprecationes dixit: Vae vobis Scribae et Pharisaei.

Et multas utiles conciones habuit de discrimine regni Messiae et regni mundani, de poenis incredulorum, de differentia verorum et falsorum cultuum. Prima historia est de maledictione ficus, et de efficacia fidei.

Historia per sese est miraculum, et est testimonium de doctore et doctrina, sicut alia multa miracula. Nec indiget alia longa declaratione, nec opus est hic disputatione, quomodo fuerint in Christo, fames, sitis, defatigatio corporis, et deinde alii adfectus, ira, laetitia, et tristitia. Quanquam fuit sine peccato, tamen natura humana in eo fuit vere natura humana integra, habens omnes potentias humanae naturae proprias, vere esuriit, vere sitiit, vere tristatus est.

Significatio autem in ficu proposita est. Ficus significat synagogam quolibet tempore, id est, tunc populum Iudaeorum, et nunc Papam et Monachos, id est, illos, qui sibi titulum arrogant Ecclesiae, et habent folia, id est, veram doctrinam, et veros cultus, sicut etiam alias folia fici significant hypocrisin.

Ut Adam et Heva tegunt se foliis fici, id est, natura humana, postquam amisit veram iustitiam, deinde illam suam deformitatem tegit qualicunque specie iustitiae externae etc. Et haec tamen non liberat a peccato et morte. Sicut igitur ficus arefacta est post maledictionem: sic arefacta est synagoga, et arefient omnes pompae Pontificis et Episcoporum et Canonicorum et Monachorum, et deinceps, cum alii etiam relinquent verbum et veros cultus, tunc etiam arefient.

Sequitur doctrina de efficacia fidei.

Valde magnifica promissio hic proponitur, quae et postulat fidem, et adfirmat invocationem in fide efficacem esse. Et additum est iuramentum: Amen dico vobis, omnia, quae petetis in oratione vestra credentes, accipietis. Observa particulam omnia, et discas, quomodo recte et vere intelligenda sit: omnia,... scilicet bona, quae non pugnant cum mandatis Dei.

Et primum scias, omnia sine ulla exceptione impetrari, quae sunt necessaria ad salutem animae, ut remissionem peccatorum, et donationem Spiritus sancti, et vitam aeternam. Haec bona nominatim petenda sunt, et nominatim haec ipsa certo dari et impetrari omnia credas, sicut et alibi dicitur: Quanto magis Pater vester coelestis dabit Spiritum sanctum petentibus?

Deinde de bonis corporalibus sic intelligas: dat etiam omnia ...necessaria corpori, sed non in specie, nec eodem modo.

Et tamen dat bona corporis, alias aliter, quia vult nos etiam subiectos esse cruci. Non dat tibi regnum Galliae, quia nec singulis talia necessaria sunt, sed tamen dat tibi victum, sanitatem corporis, meliorem statum filiorum et filiarum etc.

Sed hic opponitur: Imo saepe sinit nos paupertatem magnam habere, sinit nos aegrotare, ut Iob, imo sinit etiam sanctos mirabiliter interfici, ut Ionathan.

Ad haec respondeo: Ideo dictum est de corporalibus, quod non det eodem modo.

Dat quidem omnia necessaria, sic, ut vel illa ipsa bona det, quae petimus, ut Davidem reducit in regnum, vel certe mitiget malum, et det alia bona, ut Ionathan consolatur in corde, et servat eius posteritatem.

Quod autem non dat eodem modo omnia corporalia, ideo fit, quia vult nos subiectos esse cruci, ut Iob, aliquando etiam punit nos, ut Davidem.

Sed hanc regulam teneas firmissime: Invocationem factam in fide, nunquam irritam esse etiam in corporalibus, quia semper aut impetrat nominatim hoc bonum, quod petit, aut mitigationem, ut saepe dicitur: Petite et accipietis.

Item: Quicquid petieritis Patrem in nomine meo, dabit vobis. Addit autem Christus in hoc dicto: Si non dubitabitis.

Item: Credentes. In his verbis praecipitur fides.

Non sic cogites: Ego quidem petam, sed nescio an prosit mea petitio, fortassis Deus meas preces non recipit.

Imo sic statuas certissime, vere audiri propter Filium tuas preces, et non fore irritas, et retineas spem et expectationem auxilii, ut sint fides et spes simul, quae nunc sunt vera fides et vera spes, quando sentis te hac ipsa fide et spe habere cor quietius, et aliquomodo acquiescens in Deo.

Dicetis huic monti.

Figura est, quia non vult Deus miracula ex curiositate fieri, sicut Diabolus tentat Christum, et iubet eum volare.

Deus vult res necessarias peti, et in talibus necessariis iuvat nos saepe supra naturam.

Ut cum filii Israël veniunt ad mare rubrum, nec possunt effugere, nisi mare eis cedat, et viam praebeat, hic Deus insigni miraculo eis opitulatur.

Et ibi dicit Deus monti, id est, Pharaoni, et eius potentiae: Abiiciaris in mare.

Significat enim mons potentiam magni regis aut principis.

Et hac similitudine hoc ipsum ostendit Dominus, quod Ecclesia suis precibus et fide sit superatura et repressura reges et principes.

Ideo simus ardentiores in petendo.

Sicut Elisaeo non potuerunt nocere hostes.

Esaias et Ezechias vicerunt Sennacherib, petendo auxilium a Deo.

Danieli nec principes nec leones nocere potuerunt.

Sic Deus inter medios hostes servat omni tempore multos.

Imo Ecclesia fere semper undique circumdata est hostibus, et inter insidias Diaboli et tumultus mundi mirabiliter servatur, iuxta illud: Ecclesia est sicut rosa inter spinas.

Item: Dedi dilectam animam meam in medium inimicorum eius.

Nominat Ecclesiam animam suam, id est, carissimam, hanc, etsi est carissima, tamen ait circumdatam esse hostibus, et inter hos mirabiliter protegitur, quia est carissima Deo.

Et cum venisset in templum, accesserunt ad eum principes Sacerdotum et seniores populi dicentes: Qua potestate haec facis?

Differentiam peccatorum scire valde necessarium est.

Tres gradus sunt.

Unus est peccata et infirmitates, quae nobiscum nascuntur, ut dubitationes, vitiosae inclinationes ad iram, ad amores vagabundos etc.

Item ignorantiae multae. Secundus gradus est contra conscientiam violare mandata Dei, ut adulterium, furtum, homicidium etc.

Hi duo gradus etsi sunt peccata, et Deus valde eis irascitur, et ea punit, tamen possunt remitti, et remittuntur agentibus poenitentiam.

Sed tertius gradus est blasphemia: Cum agnitam veritatem oppugnat aliquis sciens et convictus evidentia testimoniorum scripturae vel miraculorum, et tamen pertinaciter adversatur, vel regni causa vel ambitione, vel odio, vel quocunque modo Diabolico odio ardens, ut nunc Papistae Sacerdotum coniugia improbant et defendunt impias Missas, et invocationem mortuorum. Tales tunc erant Pharisaei, qui quanquam manifesta miracula videbant, tamen interrogant: Qua potestate haec facis?

Ideo Christus eorum peccatum discernit ab aliis gradibus. Alii perveniunt ad poenitentiam, et convertuntur. Vos Pharisaei peribitis, nec vultis converti. Hos gradus diligenter consideremus, propterea hic dicitur: Meretrices et publicani praecedent vos in regno Dei.

Ac ut pertinacia Pharisaeorum sit conspectior, facit mentionem Christus praedicationis Iohannis, quasi dicat: Iam antea ostendistis impietatem et pertinaciam vestram, quia voluistis audire Iohannem, cui Deus testimonia dederat in nativitate, quia natus est ex matre anu et sterili. Et Angelus expresse dixerat, eum fore testem Messiae. Sed huius praedicationem pertinaciter contemsistis, nunc meam contemnitis. Et addunt Pharisaei impietatem impietati, quod dicunt contra conscientiam, se nescire, an Iohannes fuerit a Deo missus. Postea proponit exemplum de agentibus poenitentiam, et non agentibus.

Homo quidam habuit duos filios. Alter dixit se non iturum in vineam, et agens poenitentiam, ivit. Alter dixit se iturum, et non ivit. Hic perseverans in contumacia, plus peccat. Tales inquit esse Pharisaeos. Aliam parabolam audite.

Homo quidem erat paterfamilias, qui plantavit vineam, et sepem circumdedit ei, etc.

Paterfamilias plantavit vineam, id est, Deus elegit populum Israël. Et circumdedit sepem, id est, legem. Et fecit ibi torcular, id est, ministerium doctrinae. Et aedificavit turrim, id est, dedit eis regnum et templum. Et elocavit agricolis, id est, semini Iacob. Et abiit, et misit servos, id est, Prophetas quolibet tempore, Eliam, Elisaeum, Esaiam, Zachariam, Ionam, Ieremiam, hos interfecit populus. Tandem misit filium, hunc quoque interfecit populus. Et quidem ut signa pertinaciae et blasphemiae describeret, nominatim dicit, eos excusso Domino velle proprium regnum constituere.

Occupemus, inquiunt, haereditatem, sicut postea in passione dicunt: Nolumus hunc regnare super nos. Haec blasphemia, et hic morbus est causa omnium malorum.

Impii volunt ipsi suo iudicio, sua sapientia, suo arbitrio constituere religiones, et regimina, et inflectunt religiones ad suam commoditatem, et non volunt pati gubernatorem Deum. Semper in corde clamant: Nolumus hunc regnare super nos. Haec est horrenda insania, contemnere Deum, et velle religiones et regna constituere utilia nobis, quasi nihil sit Deus, sicut reges Israël, sicut Nabogdonosor statuam erigit, sicut Antiochus et alii multi voluerunt religiones et cultus instituere suo arbitrio, quasi nihil sit Deus, sed ipsorum sapientia sit gubernatrix et non Deus. Hoc malum in mundo saepe grassatur, et iam etiam grassatur.

Papa et reges etiam volunt constituere statum, qualem ipsi volunt, excusso Deo, et clament sicut Iudaei: Nolumus hunc regnare super nos. Hoc peccatum discamus intelligere et fugere, et Deum oremus, ut in hanc coecitatem non ruamus, sed semper toto corde oremus, ut filius Dei sit gubernator noster, ut ipse regat, ut haereditas regni penes ipsum maneat.

Hic duo contraria sunt.

Hic est Filius meus dilectus, hunc audite. Et, Nolumus hunc regnare. Obtemperemus Deo praecipienti, ut Filium audiamus, sicut et in Psalmo dicitur: Osculamini filium. Et poenae adduntur contra filii contemptores: Cum exardescet ira eius. Et hic de poena dicitur: Malos male perdet. Perdidit Deus tales contemptores inde usque ab initio, in diluvio, in poena populi Israël, et deinde deleta Ierosolyma, sic etiam perdet Canonicos, et Episcopos et Monachos.

Sequitur dictum Psalmi.

Lapidem quem reprobaverunt aedificantes, hic factus est caput anguli. A Domino factum est hoc, et est mirandum in oculis nostris. Hunc dulcissimum versiculum debetis meminisse omnes, et illi, qui legere possunt, totum hunc Psalmum saepe legant, quem quidem Iudaei tunc singulis Sabbatis cantabant, et mirum est, tantam fuisse coecitatem, ut intelligere noluerint.

Praedicit autem clare Messiam passurum esse, et tamen postea regnaturum esse, et collecturum aeternam Ecclesiam. Multa igitur docet nos hic brevis versiculus, videlicet:

Quod Messias venturus fuerit et passurus, et quod ipsa Synagoga sit adversatura Messiae, et quod Messias sit futurus victor, et collecturus Ecclesiam ex gentibus et Iudaeis.

## 22:1-4 Twentieth Sunday After Trinity
Twentieth Sunday after Trinity. Gospel of Matthew 22.

And Jesus answering, spoke again in parables to them, saying: The kingdom of heaven is like to a king, who made a marriage for his son, and sent his servants, to call those who were invited to nuptials, and they did not want to come. Again he sent other servants, saying: Tell those invited, behold I have prepared my dinner, my oxen and fatlings are killed, and all things are ready, come to the nuptials. But they neglected it, and went away, one indeed to his own field, another however to his business, but the rest held his servants, and having affected them with insults, killed them. But when the king had heard, he was angry, and having sent his armies, he destroyed those murderers, and burned their city. Then he says to his servants: The nuptials indeed are ready, but those who were invited were not worthy. Go therefore to the exits of the ways, and whomever you find, call to the nuptials. And the servants having gone out into the ways, gathered all whom they found, bad and good, and the nuptials were filled with those reclining. But the king entered, that he might look at those reclining, and he saw there a man not clothed with a nuptial garment. And he says to him: Friend, how did you enter here, not having a nuptial garment? But he was silent. Then the king said to the ministers: Bind his feet and hands, and cast him into outer darkness, there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. For many are called, but few are chosen.

The whole parable is an image of the Church of all times, and although here he speaks especially of the rejection and punishment of the Jewish nation, yet this discourse must be accommodated to similar events of all times. God called the Church in the beginning, but most despised the vocation, many even killed those calling, therefore punishments followed, such as the flood, the overthrow of the Sodomites, of Egypt, of the Canaanites, afterwards of the kingdom of Israel, then of the Jews, afterwards of the Romans, and of other kingdoms. Some however who were called came, and there was always some Church. Let us learn therefore here, what and of what kind the Church is, what its species, what the punishments of the enemies of the Church, and of the wicked in the Church.

On the second.

What is the Church?

It is the congregation of all who believe in the Gospel, and are sanctified by the Holy Spirit, to which congregation however many wicked are mixed in, consenting concerning doctrine, and the use of the Sacraments, who also themselves are associates or members of the external society, and of the administration of the Church. But what the species of this assembly is, is signified here, when he says, that the greatest part of men spurn the vocation itself. Others, he says, prefer their own fields, others their own businesses, others kill those calling, that is, outside the Church are all who do not embrace the true doctrine, as Ethnics, Jews, Mahometans, Epicureans, and those who now are enemies of true doctrine, even if they are called Christians. Nor does place or title, but the profession of true doctrine discern the Church from those who are outside the Church.

Now also many who are called Christians, yet because of their fields flee the profession of doctrine, and become either openly Epicureans, or defend customary errors because of their belly, as many Bishops, Canons, and others. Others because of their businesses flee the profession of doctrine.

Here especially are taxed princes and courtiers, who even if they do not exercise cruelty, yet neglect the Gospel and the Churches, and think that the care of these things is unworthy of them, that they have great occupations, necessary for the life of men, namely the constitution and defense of empires. This occupation they consider to be glorious. They care nothing for the Churches.

Thus in another parable it is said, that seed falls among thorns, where especially courtly thorns are understood. The third genus is of tyrants, who attempt to destroy the Gospel. The Church will therefore be a small assembly, because the three superior genera are outside the Church.

Therefore it is said in Zephaniah 3: And I will leave in the midst of thee a poor and needy people, and they shall hope in the name of the Lord. These things must be considered, lest we think the people of God to be the greater multitude, and empires, which flourish more in glory and power, and lest, having cast aside the word of God, we fall away to that multitude, just as human reason is moved by multitude and fortune, and thinks that so many, so flourishing, are not neglected by God.

Against these scandals let us confirm ourselves with the descriptions of the Church, handed down by Christ and the Prophets, as in the parable of the seed, and Paul says 1 Cor. 1: Not many wise according to the flesh, not many powerful, not many noble etc. But diligently observe in the description in Zephaniah, what he adds: And they shall hope in the name of the Lord.

…The Church is bound to true doctrine, not to certain empires of kings and pontiffs, and invocation makes the distinction. Even if Jews and Turks say they invoke one God, the creator of things, they deny that He is the Father of Jesus Christ, they deny that there is need of a mediator, although God has revealed Himself through the Son, and does not wish to be invoked, except by trust in the Son, as it is often said: Through Him we have access to the Father. Likewise: No one knows the Father, except the Son, and he to whom the Son has revealed Him. Therefore, the Turks do not invoke God. Likewise, they… confess that they invoke without the Word, without promises, without a mediator, with perpetual doubt. But the true members of the Church invoke the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ the mediator, the creator of all things, and indeed by trust in this propitiator, revealed in the Gospel, and exhibited, they seek and expect salvation. This invocation distinguishes the Church from other nations. Therefore, let the saying be diligently observed: And they shall hope in the name of the Lord.

Finally, let us consider here that this worship, namely invocation, must be especially performed. For He both demands it and adds promises, because He wishes to hear, etc. If we think of ourselves as members of the Church, let us be of the assembly of those who invoke.

On the third.

Here Christ testifies that punishments hang over all nations and men who are outside the Church of God, as the examples from the beginning of the world show, which God set forth so that He might warn us about the final judgment and eternal punishments, about which Christ preaches when He says: Go, you cursed, into eternal fire, etc.

On the fourth. On the wedding garment.

Above, it was spoken of the punishments of all who are outside the Church. Now follows a sad sermon. Even in the Church of God there are hypocrites, who, being condemned, will be cast into eternal punishments, just like the enemies of the Gospel, just as Saul was condemned just as Goliath was.

What, therefore, is the wedding garment? One names one thing, another another, but it must be that of which Paul says: Desiring to be clothed upon, if indeed we shall be found clothed, and not naked. And by the confession of all, this garment is the spiritual light by which we are reborn, of which he speaks in the second to the Corinthians, chapter three: We are all transformed, with unveiled face beholding the glory of the Lord, from glory to glory, as by the Spirit of the Lord. But what is that spiritual light which makes the distinction between hypocrites and the reborn? It is undoubtedly to tremble at the recognition of the wrath of God against sins, and again to be raised up by faith, and to trust that God receives us, and by this trust to invoke Him, to be subject to Him, to seek and expect from Him guidance and defense, not, while distrusting God, to seek human protections, nor, while neglecting God, to indulge one's own desires. We embrace all these things when we name repentance and faith, or regeneration.

The wedding garment is, therefore, that very regeneration which embraces the movements of repentance and faith, which receives the remission of sins, and in all of life seeks and expects help from God, and begins a new obedience.

However, there are many in the external society of the Church without this wedding garment. First, those who persevere in sins against their conscience. Then also hypocrites, like Ahaz, who although he seems an honest man and of right profession, yet is, without that light, that is, without repentance and without faith, he accumulates acts of worship, thinks himself to be righteous, manages many affairs, but by trust in his own wisdom, and distrusting God, he neither seeks nor expects help from Him, from wherever he seeks human protections, even with the Prophets dissuading him. Conversely, in David and Hezekiah there are terrors and consolations. These tremble at the recognition of their own weakness, and again by faith determine that they have been received by God, and by this trust they invoke, obey, seek from God, and expect help. These examples in the prophetic histories were described for this reason, that we might learn to distinguish hypocrisy from the wedding garment, that is, from regeneration, or repentance and faith.

Augustine was adorned with this garment when, shortly before his death, he was preaching about repentance and faith, and was lamenting the security of his past life, and again was raising himself up by the invocation and faith of the Son of God. Conversely, Ahaz was without true fear and without true faith; he did not acknowledge that he was sinning when he fashioned acts of worship by his own will, when he indulged his hatred against the Prophets, he did not believe that he was received or heard on account of the divine promise; indeed, he doubted whether he would be heard, and therefore, distrusting, he sought other protections.

Thus, there are also those without the wedding garment who are joined to the true profession and living without public disgrace, if, however, they are secure, without repentance, and with a certain negligence and doubt, they do not seek nor expect anything from God, but trust in their own counsels and human protections. Likewise, in adversities they do not acknowledge that they are justly punished, they think the punishments punishments or happen by chance, or by the unjust judgment of God, just as Saul rages against God in calamity.

Much more do they lack the wedding garment who openly defend errors and vicious cults, but of this assembly it has been spoken before, which,... since it is outside the Church, is condemned without any doubt.

Furthermore, weakness remains even in the saints; one has a cleaner garment than another, just as there are many errors of the saints, and sins of ignorance, which are nevertheless forgiven to those who hold the foundation, that is, true invocation and trust in the mercy granted on account of the Son of God, just as Paul says: There is now no condemnation for those who walk in Christ Jesus.

Latin:

Dominica XX. post Trinitatis. Evangelium Matth. 22.

Et respondens Iesus, dixit iterum in parabolis eis, dicens: Simile est regnum coelorum homini regi, qui fecit nuptias filio suo, et misit servos suos, ut vocarent invitatos ad nuptias, et nolebant venire. Iterum misit alios servos, dicens: Dicite invitatis, ecce prandium meum paravi, tauri mei et altilia mactata sunt, et omnia parata, venite ad nuptias. Illi autem neglexerunt, et abierunt, alius quidem in proprium agrum, alius vero ad negotiationem suam, reliqui vero tenuerunt servos eius, et contumeliis affectos, occiderunt. Rex autem cum audisset, iratus est, et missis exercitibus suis, perdidit homicidas illos, et civitatem illorum succendit. Tunc ait servis suis: Nuptiae quidem paratae sunt, sed qui invitati erant, non fuerunt digni. Ite ergo ad exitus viarum, et quoscunque inveneritis, vocate ad nuptias. Et egressi servi in vias, congregaverunt omnes quos invenerunt, malos et bonos, et impletae sunt nuptiae discumbentibus. Intravit autem rex, ut spectaret discumbentes, et vidit illic hominem non vestitum veste nuptiali. Et ait illi: Amice, quomodo huc intrasti, non habens vestem nuptialem? At ille obmutuit. Tunc dixit rex ministris: Ligate ei pedes et manus, et mittite eum in tenebras exteriores, ibi erit ploratus et stridor dentium. Multi enim sunt vocati, pauci autem electi.

Tota parabola est imago Ecclesiae omnium temporum, Et quanquam hic praecipue loquitur de reiectione et poena Iudaicae gentis, tamen ad omnium temporum similes eventus haec concio accommodanda est. Vocavit Deus initio Ecclesiam, sed plerique vocationem contemserunt, multi etiam interfecerunt vocantes, ideo sunt secutae poenae, ut diluvium, eversio Sodomorum, Aegypti, Cananaeorum, postea regni Israël, deinde Iudaeorum, postea Romanorum, et aliorum regnorum. Aliqui tamen vocati convenerunt, et semper aliqua fuit Ecclesia. Discamus ergo hic, quid et qualis sit Ecclesia, quae species, quae poenae hostium Ecclesiae, et malorum in Ecclesia,

De secundo.

Quid est Ecclesia?

Est congregatio omnium qui credunt Evangelio, et sanctificantur Spiritu sancto, cui congregationi tamen multi mali admixti sunt, consentientes de doctrina, et usu Sacramentorum, qui et ipsi sunt socii seu membra externae societatis, et administrationis Ecclesiae. Qualis autem sit species huius coetus, significatur hic, cum ait, maximam partem hominum aspernari ipsam vocationem. Alii, inquit, anteferunt suos agros, alii sua negocia, alii occidunt vocantes, id est, extra Ecclesiam sunt omnes, qui non amplectuntur doctrinam veram, ut Ethnici, Iudaei, Mahometistae, Epicurei, et qui nunc sunt hostes verae doctrinae, etiamsi vocantur Christiani. Nec locus aut titulus, sed doctrinae verae professio discernit Ecclesiam ab iis, qui sunt extra Ecclesiam.

Nunc quoque multi qui vocantur Christiani, tamen propter agros suos fugiunt doctrinae professionem, et fiunt aut palam Epicurei, aut defendunt usitatos errores propter ventrem, ut multi Episcopi, Canonici, et alii. Alii propter sua negocia fugiunt doctrinae professionem.

Hic praecipue taxantur principes et aulici, qui etiamsi non exercent saevitiam, tamen negligunt Evangelium et Ecclesias, et putant harum rerum curam se indignam esse, habere se occupationes magnas, necessarias hominum vitae, videlicet constitutionem et defensionem imperiorum. Hanc occupationem ducunt esse gloriosam. Ecclesias nihil curant.

Sic in alia parabola dicitur, semen inter spinas cadere, ubi praecipue spinae aulicae intelligantur. Tertium genus est tyrannorum, qui delere Evangelium conantur. Erit igitur exiguus coetus Ecclesia, quia superiora tria genera sunt extra Ecclesiam.

Ideo dicitur Sopho. 3.: Et reliquum faciam in medio tui populum pauperem et egenum, et sperabunt in nomine Domini. Haec consideranda sunt, ne cogitemus populum Dei esse maiorem multitudinem, et imperia, quae magis florent gloria et potentia, et ne abiecto verbo Dei, ad illam multitudinem deficiamus, sicut humana ratio movetur multitudine et fortuna, cogitat tam multos, tam florentes, non negligi a Deo.

Adversus haec scandala confirmemus nos descriptionibus Ecclesiae, traditis a Christo et Prophetis, ut in parabola de semine, et Paulus inquit 1. Cor. 1.: Non multi sapientes secundum carnem, non multi potentes, non multi nobiles etc. Diligenter autem observa in descriptione apud Sophoniam, quod addit: Et sperabunt in nomine Domini.

Ecclesia alligata est ad doctrinam veram, non ad certa imperia regum et pontificum, et invocatio discrimen facit. Etsi Iudaei et Turci dicunt se invocare unum Deum, conditorem rerum: tamen negant Deum conditorem rerum esse patrem Iesu Christi, negant opus esse mediatore, cum tamen Deus revelaverit se per Filium, et non velit invocari, nisi fiducia Filii, sicut saepe dicitur: Per hunc habemus accessum ad patrem. Item: Nemo novit patrem, nisi Fi- lius, et cui Filius revelaverit. Non igitur invocant Deum Turci. Item fatentur se invocare sine verbo, sine promissionib., sine mediatore, cum perpetua dubitatione. Sed vera membra Ecclesiae invocant patrem Domini nostri Iesu Christi mediatoris, conditorem omnium rerum, et quidem fiducia hu- ius propiciatoris, revelati in Evangelio, et exhi- biti, petunt et expectant salutem. Haec invocatio discernit Ecclesiam a caeteris gentibus. Ideo di- ligenter observetur dictum: Et sperabunt in no- mine Domini.

Postremo hic cogitemus etiam hunc cultum, scilicet invocationem, praecipue praestandum esse. Ideo enim et flagitat et addit promissiones, quia vult exaudire etc. Si cogitamus nos esse membra Ecclesiae, simus ex coetu invocantium.

De tertio.

Testatur hic Christus poenas impendere omni- bus gentib. atque hominibus, qui sunt extra Ec- clesiam Dei, sicut ostendunt exempla ab initio mundi, quae proposuit Deus, ut nos de ultimo iudicio et de aeternis poenis admoneat, de qui- bus concionatur Christus, cum inquit: Ite male- dicti in ignem aeternum etc.

De quarto. De veste nuptiali.

Supra dictum est de poenis omnium, qui sunt extra Ecclesiam. Nunc sequitur tristis con- cio. Etiam in Ecclesia Dei sunt hypocritae, qui damnati abiicientur in poenas aeternas, sicut ho- stes Evangelii, ut Saul perinde damnatus est, ut Goliath.

Quae est igitur vestis nuptialis? Alius aliud nominat, sed necesse est id esse, de quo Paulus inquit: Cupientes superindui, si tamen vestiti, et non nudi reperiemur. Et confessione omnium haec vestis est lux spiritualis, qua renascimur, de qua dicit secundae Corinthios tertio: Nos trans- formamur omnes retecta facie gloriam Dei spe- culantes, a gloria in gloriam, tanquam a Domini spiritu. Quid est autem illa lux spiritualis, quae discrimen facit inter hypocritas et renatos? Est haud dubie agnitione irae Dei adversus peccata expavescere, et rursus fide erigi, et confidere quod Deus recipiat nos, et hac fiducia eum invo- care, ei subiici, petere et expectare ab eo guber- nationem et defensionem, non diffidentem Deo, quaerere humana praesidia, non neglecto Deo, indulgere propriis cupiditatibus. Haec omnia complectimur, cum nominamus poenitentiam et fidem, seu regenerationem.

Est igitur vestis nuptialis illa ipsa regenera- tio, quae complectitur motus poenitentiae et fidei, quae accipit remissionem peccatorum, et in omni vita petit et expectat a Deo auxilium, et in- coat novam obedientiam.

Sunt autem in externa societate Ecclesiae multi sine hac veste nuptiali. Primum qui per- severant in peccatis contra conscientiam. Deinde et hypocritae, ut Achas, qui etsi videtur vir ho- nestus et rectae professionis, tamen est, sine illa luce, id est, sine poenitentia, et sine fide, cu- mulat cultus, putat se iustum esse, gerit res mul- tas, sed fiducia suae sapientiae, ac diffidens Deo, nec petit, nec expectat ab eo auxilium, undecun- que quaerit praesidia humana, dehortantibus etiam Prophetis. Econtra in Davide, Ezechia sunt pa- vores et consolationes. Hi expavescunt agnitione suae infirmitatis, et rursus fide statuunt se a Deo receptos esse, et hac fiducia invocant, obediunt, petunt a Deo, et expectant auxilium. Haec exem- pla in historiis propheticis ideo descripta sunt, ut discamus hypocrisin a veste nuptiali, id est, a regeneratione, seu poenitentia et fide discerni.

Hac veste ornatus est Augustinus, cum paulo ante mortem de poenitentia et fide concionaretur, ac deploraret vitae actae securitatem, et rursus seipsum erigeret invocatione et fide Filii Dei. Econtra Achas erat sine vero timore, et sine vera fide, non agnoscebat se peccare, cum cultus fin- geret suo arbitrio, cum indulgeret suo odio adver- sus Prophetas, non crederet se recipi, exaudiri propter promissionem divinam, imo dubitabat an exaudiretur, ideoque diffidens quaerebat alia praesidia.

Sic sunt sine veste nuptiali etiam adiuncti verae professioni, et sine publica turpitudine vi- ventes, si tamen sunt securi, sine poenitentia, et quadam negligentia ac dubitatione, non petunt, nec expectant a Deo quicquam, sed confidunt suis consiliis et humanis praesidiis. Item, in adver- sis non agnoscunt se iuste puniri, existimant poe- poenas vel casu accidere, vel iniusto iudicio Dei, sicut Saul fremit adversus Deum in calamitate.

Multo magis carent veste nuptiali, qui palam defendunt errores et viciosos cultus, sed de hoc coetu prius dictum est, qui cum sit extra Ecclesiam..., sine ulla dubitatione damnatus est.

Caeterum etiam in sanctis manet imbecillitas, habet alius alio vestem nitidiorem, ut multa sunt etiam sanctorum errata, et peccata ignorantiae, quae tamen condonantur tenentibus fundamentum, id est, veram invocationem et fiduciam donatae misericordiae propter Filium Dei, sicut Paulus inquit: Nulla nunc condemnatio his qui in Christo Iesu ambulant.

## 22:1 Sermons on Matthew: Argument
Chapter XXII.

The kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain king, which made a marriage for his son, etc.

It is a common similitude to compare the covenant and love of the Son of God towards the Church with a marriage.

Likewise, the preaching of the Gospel with the marriage feast itself.

And if this miserable nature did not have such wandering and impure loves, this similitude would be more illustrious.

And this very similitude is recited in Ephesians 5 and in Psalm 45: My heart is inditing a good matter, where it is said: So shall the king greatly desire thy beauty, for he is thy Lord God, and they shall worship him.

And this love of the Son must often be pondered: Thus he loved us in the first fall, that he might be a mediator for us. Thus he loves us thereafter, that he was made a victim for us, and that he might always care for, hear, help, and save us who call upon him.

And see how the Psalm says: So shall the king greatly desire thy beauty. How wonderful is this description? What is the beauty of the Church? The miserable Church is still diseased, it carries about a vicious flesh, and furthermore it is burdened with the highest calamities, death, and various persecutions.

What is the appearance of Adam and Eve, standing beside the corpse of Abel? What is the appearance of David fleeing, and of all the Martyrs? What is our appearance now? We are most miserable.

But let us oppose these consolations to this appearance, that our king, the Son of God, declares us to be beautiful, and indeed desires us; let us be content that we please our bridegroom.

But conversely, this Psalm teaches how this bridegroom is to be received and loved. He commands that we worship him, and specifically says he is God, as the text says. He therefore wishes to be feared, he wishes to be believed, he wishes to be invoked, and conversely to be loved, as a bridegroom and savior.

Let these things be said briefly concerning this marriage, but it is to be lamented that men do not care for this such great goodness of God, and such great magnitude of love towards us.

This the similitude now narrates; it says that those invited to the feast do not come, nay, they even kill the teachers, Prophets, and Apostles, who call the human race to this feast. And specifically, Christ here predicts the destruction of this people of the Jews. And he says afterwards that the Church is to be gathered from the Gentiles.

In these sermons, one must always think about the punishments for the ingratitude of the world, so that we may rouse ourselves to the fear of God and to repentance.

Likewise, the doctrine must be learned that we are received freely for the sake of the Son of God, not for the sake of the law.

But after he spoke of that new Church gathered from the Gentiles, here he again shows the distinction between those who truly believe and hypocrites, who according to external appearance are in the Church and at the feast, and yet do not truly believe, do not truly worship the bridegroom, and do not have, he says, a wedding garment.

I omit, however, long and manifold disputes about the garment, and I say simply: The wedding garment is true and living faith, which is felt in true repentance, and lifts up hearts, and kindles true invocation, hope, and confession, and other fruits which ought to follow. This true faith, not feigned, is the wedding garment, as it is said in Hosea: I will betroth thee unto me in faith.

And in this very Psalm it is said: Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear. This bridegroom wishes to be heard, he wishes us to incline our ears, that is, to embrace the Gospel with true faith, etc.

Let us therefore learn these three things in this place:

1. That the true forms of worship in the Church are this faith and true repentance, true invocation, hope, and love.

2. That in the Church, in this life, true believers and hypocrites are mixed together, and that we should not take offense that not all in the Church are holy and steadfast, but let us know that the Church is such a body as contains many wicked men. And yet it is certain that the elect Church of God never exists except in this very assembly of the called, in which at the same time many hypocrites are present. Therefore one must not run off into solitude, as the hermits did, nor must other congregations be formed in secret, as the Anabaptists did. But remain in this Church, where you hear the Son of God; incline your ear to him.

3. There follows the punishment of the impious, and he names darkness, which is outside, that is, the darkness is outside the kingdom of heaven, and the gnashing of teeth, that is, horrible terrors and pains, about which let us think, so that, fearing the judgment and wrath of God, we may be converted to God, and seek this bridegroom of ours, the Son of God, who truly loves us with an ardent love.

Latin:

Caput XXII.

Simile est regnum coelorum homini regi, qui fecit nuptias filio suo, etc.

Usitata est similitudo, conferre foedus et amorem filii Dei erga Ecclesiam, cum nuptiis.

Item Evangelii praedicationem cum ipso convivio nuptiali.

Et si haec misera natura non ita vagos et impuros amores haberet, illustrior haec similitudo esset.

Et haec ipsa similitudo ad Ephes. 5. recitatur et in Psalm. 45.: Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum, ubi dicitur: Concupiscet rex decorem tuum, quia ipse est Dominus Deus tuus, et adorabunt eum.

Et hic amor filii saepe cogitandus est: Sic nos amavit in primo lapsu, ut esset pro nobis deprecator. Sic nos amat deinceps, ut sit factus victima pro nobis, et ut semper curet, exaudiat, iuvet, salvet nos ipsum invocantes.

Et videte quomodo Psalmus dicit: Et concupiscet rex decorem tuum. Quam mira est haec descriptio? Qualis est decor Ecclesiae? Misera Ecclesia adhuc est morbosa, circumfert carnem vitiosam, et praeterea est onerata calamitatibus summis, morte, et persecutionibus variis. Qualis species est Adae et Hevae, stantium iuxta cadaver Habel?

Qualis est species David fugientis, et omnium Martyrum? Qualis species nunc est nostra? sumus miserrimi.

Sed huic speciei has consolationes opponamus, quod rex noster, filius Dei, pronuntiat nos pulcros esse, et quidem concupiscit nos, simus contenti, quod nostro sponso placeamus.

Vicissim autem docet hic Psalmus, quomodo hic sponsus excipiendus et amandus sit. Iubet, ut eum adoremus, et nominatim dicit esse Deum, ut textus inquit. Vult igitur eum timeri, vult ei credi, vult eum invocari, et vicissim diligi, ut sponsum et salvatorem.

Haec breviter dicta sint de his nuptiis, sed dolendum est, quod hanc tantam bonitatem Dei, et tantam magnitudinem amoris erga nos non curant homines.

Hoc narrat iam similitudo, dicit vocatos ad convivium non venire, imo etiam occidere doctores, Prophetas et Apostolos, qui vocant genus humanum ad hoc convivium. Et nominatim praedicit hic Christus huic populo Iudaeorum interitum. Et dicit postea, Ecclesiam ex gentibus colligendam esse.

In his concionibus semper de poenis ingratitudinis mundi cogitandum est, ut nos ad timorem Dei et ad poenitentiam exsuscitemus.

Item discenda est doctrina, quod gratis propter filium Dei, non propter legem recipiamur.
