Since there was then such great blindness in that learned and practiced people, let us be vigilant, and pray to God, that he may not allow the light of truth to be extinguished among us. Secondly, just as David confesses this Messiah, of whom he speaks, to be Lord, ruling over him, and by whom he wishes to be ruled and saved: so let us also with firm faith establish that this same Messiah, the Lord of David, is our Lord, and let us believe that he is present with us, gives us eternal goods, righteousness and life, and defends us even in this life. Let us exercise this faith daily in invocation, let us flee to him in all dangers and business, just as he himself said: Come to me all, who are burdened and labor, and I will refresh you. He calls all, and truly wishes to bring help, not only to David, but also to me and to you, and to all of us invoking him, and rightly acknowledging who he is, namely, that he is truly the Son of God, and is constituted Mediator, Redeemer and Savior, so that through him and because of him there may be given to us remission of sins, righteousness, and eternal life, and so that through him and because of him we may also be protected in this life. And let us know that now also he is truly present with us, and guards us just as he himself says: Behold, I am with you even to the consummation of the age, etc. Item: Wherever two or three are gathered in my name, I am in the midst of them, etc. These things are to be thought of in invocation.

Latin:

In illo die accesserunt ad eum Sadducaei.

Hic iterum consideretur, qualis tunc fuerit forma Ecclesiae, et discamus in tanta varietate sectarum quaerere, quae et ubi sit vera Ecclesia, et sciamus nos singulos oportere esse membra verae Ecclesiae, et sit in nobis cura, ut adiungamus nos verae Ecclesiae Dei, sicut scriptum est Psalm. 27.: Unum hoc petii a Domino, hoc requiro, ut inhabitem in domo Domini omnibus diebus vitae meae. Et Psalm. 84.: Beati qui habitant in domo tua Domine. Et Psalm. 92.: Plantati in domo Domini, in atriis domus Dei nostri florebunt.

Haec et similia dicta praecipiunt, ut quaeramus, ubi et quae sit vera Ecclesia, ut curemus, ut nos ipsos etiam ei adiungamus.

Iam videte, qualis tunc fuerit species. Habebant nomen populi Dei, omnes in illa politia, et tamen multi erant hostes verae Ecclesiae, erant sectae duae potentes Pharisaei et Sadducaei. Et Sadducaei adeo impii erant, ut negarent animas esse immortales, et negarent resurrectionem mortuorum, denique prorsus negabant restare aliam vitam, post hanc, sed hominum vitam credebant finiri in morte, sicut pecudum vitam, et nullum restare iudicium post hanc vitam. Cumque negarent hoc praecipuum fundamentum articulorum fidei de vita post hanc vitam, et de iudicio futuro, manifeste erant hostes Dei et Ecclesiae.

Alii erant Pharisaei, qui corrumpebant doctrinam de Messia, et nihil norant de iustitia fidei.

Erant tales, quales nunc sunt Mahometistae. Cum igitur nec Sadducaei nec Pharisaei essent Ecclesia Dei, servavit Deus tamen aliqua vera membra suae Ecclesiae, videlicet, Zachariam, Simeonem, Ioseph, Elisabeth, Annam, Mariam, et alios valde multos, qui fundamentum doctrinae integrae retinebant.

Ita nunc sunt Papistae, Monachi, Canonici, fanatici, partim prorsus sunt Epicurei, partim tollunt aliquos articulos fidei, et manifesta idola stabiliunt, et tamen nominant se Ecclesiam, et summos Episcopos Ecclesiae.

Ubi igitur est Ecclesia? et qui homines sunt Ecclesia? Respondeo: Deus semper servat aliquem coetum in genere humano, qui est vera Ecclesia, custos Evangelii, hic coetus amplectitur puram Evangelii doctrinam et incorruptam, in omnibus articulis fidei, et habet verum usum sacramentorum, et non pertinaciter defendit idola. Imo damnat et fugit omnem idololatriam, quatenus eam agnoscit et intelligit.

Talis coetus sine ulla dubitatione est Ecclesia Dei, in qua homines exaudiuntur et salvantur a Deo, iuxta haec dicta: Ioh. 14. Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit, et Pater meus diliget eum, et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus. Item Ioh. 17.: Pater sanctifica eos in veritate tua, sermo tuus est veritas.

Item Gal. 1.: Si quis aliud Evangelium docet, anathema sit.

Haec dicta utrumque docent, et quod Ecclesia Dei ibi sit, ubi vox Evangelii incorrupta est, et quod illi homines non sint Ecclesia, qui sunt hostes verae doctrinae.

Hanc consolationem teneas, et scias vere esse Ecclesiam Dei, ubicunque Evangelium recte et sine corruptelis docetur, et recte administrantur sacramenta, et non defenduntur idola pertinaciter. Et cum didicisti, quae sit vera Ecclesia, te quoque adiungas illi Ecclesiae in usu sacramentorum, et in confessione tua.

Talis est Dei beneficio Ecclesia in hoc ipso oppido, et in aliis, ubicunque eadem doctrina docetur.

Et scitote vos esse in vera Dei Ecclesia, cum estis adiuncti huic congregationi.

Hanc consolationem non sinatis vobis eripi. Haec admonitio hoc tempore necessaria est, et saepe repetenda, et a vobis saepe cogitanda.

Nunc venio ad argumentum Christi de vita post hanc vitam.

Videte quam tristes tenebrae fuerint in illo populo. Sadducaei palam negaverunt vitam post hanc vitam, et quaesiverunt ridicula argumenta. Ita insaniunt homines, quando discedunt a verbo Dei, et quaerunt ipsi cavillationes pro suis opinionibus. Christus solvit eorum argumentum, et dicit in vita aeterna non futuram commixtionem talem, ut fit in coniugio in hac vita.

Postea opponit egregium argumentum: Deus est Deus viventium, non mortuorum. Deus est Deus Abrahae. Ergo Abraham vivit.

Hoc argumentum continet egregiam consolationem, non solum de futura vita, sed etiam de hac vita, quod scilicet Deus vere curet nos, quia dicere, quod Deus sit Deus viventium, est dicere, quod curet, quod benefaciat, servet eos, quorum se nominat Deum, sicut in primo praecepto dicitur: Ego sum Dominus Deus tuus, id est, te curans, exaudiens, iuvans, servans.

Hoc bene consideres, et in tua invocatione semper excitetur fides, quod invokes non otiosum Deum, sed qui te verissime vult curare, exaudire, iuvare, salvare, si credis in filium.

Caeterum bene refutati sunt Sadducaei, ipsa resuscitatione Christi, et aliorum multorum, qui resuscitati sunt et conspecti a multis.

Pharisaei autem audientes, quod silentium imposuisset Sadducaeis, etc. Interrogavit eum unus ex eis Legislator.

Audivistis pugnam cum Sadducaeis. Nunc sequitur pugna cum Pharisaeis, hos quoque refutat et vincit Christus, et taxat eorum praecipuum errorem, quod ignorabant, quis esset Messias, et quae sint eius vera beneficia, et quale futurum esset regnum. Et sicut doctrinam veram de Messia ignoraverunt, ita doctrinam de iustitia fidei nesciverunt. Has tantas tenebras hic taxabit Christus. Et sunt hic duae disputationes: prior de lege, altera de Evangelio. Hic primum necesse est nos cogitare de discrimine Legis et Evangelii. Hoc discrimen conspici in Ecclesia necesse est.

Lex est doctrina a Deo tradita, praecipiens, quales nos esse oporteat, et quid nos facere aut non facere oporteat, et requirens perfectam obedientiam, et promittens bona pro perfecta obedientia, et vere irascens omnibus, qui non praestant perfectam obedientiam, et puniens omnem inobedientiam, sicut scriptum est: Maledictus qui manet in omnibus, quae sunt scripta in lege. Et in summa, lex est ipsa vox Decalogi, qui damnat omnes homines in hac corruptione naturae, quia nemo est sine multis et magnis peccatis, et Deus vere irascitur peccatis, sicut ibi dicitur: Deus est ignis consumens.

Vel: Lex Dei est aeterna et immota sapientia Dei, et norma iustitiae in voluntate Dei, discernens bona et mala, communicata rationali creaturae in creatione, et patefacta postea suo verbo, ut sciamus, qualis sit Deus, et obligans omnes rationales creaturas, et vult omnes sibi conformes esse, et damnans omnes non congruentes ad illam aeternam et immotam sapientiam Dei, etc.

Sed Evangelium est praedicatio poenitentiae, et promissio remissionis peccatorum, et iustitiae et vitae aeternae, exhibendae propter mediatorem filium Dei, gratis, et accipiendae fide.

His discriminibus constitutis, iam sciendum est, quod homo non accipiat remissionem peccatorum, nec sit iustus propter legem vel sua merita, et multo minus propter Monachatus et similes ceremonias.

Sed lex ideo praedicanda est, ut ostendat et accuset peccatum, et nos territi agnita ira Dei confugiamus ad filium Dei, ut ab ipso sanemur.

Incipiunt ergo disputationem de lege: Pharisaeus interrogat, quod sit magnum mandatum in lege? Respondet Christus sapientissime de summa legis et praecipuis mandatis: Diligas Deum ex toto corde. Et secundum simile huic: Diligas proximum tuum sicut teipsum.

Quare adiecit Christus: Secundum? Hic taxat Pharisaeum, quia Pharisaeus imaginatur, longe maiora mandata esse ceremonialia, quae ipsis erant quaestuosa, quam mandatum de dilectione proximi. Et Prophetae et Christus saepe hunc errorem taxant. Et semper inter homines manent talia somnia. Papistae olim existimabant, maius peccatum esse, in die sexta comedere carnes, quam occidere hominem. Contra haec deliramenta dicit Propheta.

Hoseae 6: Misericordiam volo, non sacrificium, et scientiam Dei plusquam holocaustum. Id est, Volo agnitionem veram Dei, timorem et fidem. Deinde misericordiam, id est, dilectionem proximi, haec ait, sunt anteferendae ceremoniis.

Ita hic Christus ponit vocabulum simile. Quare sic loquitur? Videtur certe hoc secundum, longe inferius esse primo.

Respondeo: Dicit contra illam pharisaicam opinionem, quod putabant posse negligi dilectionem proximi, et ceremonias et oblationes multo potiores esse. Imo multi etiam hoc faciebant: Committebant adulteria, et postea volebant compensare sacrificiis, sicut adhuc est opinio Papistarum de Missa.

Ideo ostendit Christus, hoc praeceptum de dilectione nequaquam negligendum esse, et dicit simile esse primo, scilicet. nes, quam occidere hominem.

Contra haec deliramenta dicit Propheta. Hoseae 6.: Misericordiam volo, non sacrificium, et scientiam Dei plus quam holocaustum. Id est, Volo agnitionem veram Dei, timorem et fidem. Deinde misericordiam, id est, dilectionem proximi, haec ait, sunt anteferenda ceremoniis.

Ita hic Christus ponit vocabulum simile. Quare sic loquitur?

Videtur certe hoc secundum, longe inferius esse primo. Respondeo: Dicit contra illam pharisaicam opinionem, quod putabant posse negligi dilectionem proximi, et ceremonias et oblationes multo potiores esse.

Imo multi etiam hoc faciebant: Committebant adulteria, et postea volebant compensare sacrificiis, sicut adhuc est opinio Papistarum de Missa. Ideo ostendit Christus, hoc praeceptum de dilectione nequaquam negligendum esse, et dicit simile esse primo, scilicet, quia obligatio similis est sub poena aeternae damnationis, et obedientia etiam fit cultus Dei, sicut cultus primi praecepti.

De secunda quaestione.

Postquam respondit Dominus Pharisaeis de lege, vult iam ostendere eorum ignorantiam, de fundamento praecipuo Ecclesiae, scilicet de Messia. Quia in Ecclesia, non satis est nosse legem, nec legis notitia discrimen facit inter Ethnicos et Ecclesiam Dei, sed notitia promissionis Messiae, et fides iuxta eam promissionem.

Hunc Mediatorem agnosci in Ecclesia oportet, iuxta illa dicta: Nemo venit ad Patrem nisi per Filium. Item: Qui non honorat Filium, non honorat Patrem. Item: Haec est vita aeterna, ut agnoscant te solum, verum Deum, et quem misisti, Iesum esse Christum.

Item 1. Corinth. 3.: Fundamentum aliud poni non potest, nisi quod est positum, quod est Christus Iesus. Haec testimonia et similia debent esse notissima omnibus hominibus, ut discant, quae sit Ecclesia vera Dei, et discant seiungere Ecclesiam veram Dei ab Ethnicis.

Sed hanc totam doctrinam de Messia ignorabant Pharisaei. Hanc impiam et damnatam ignorantiam ostendit in eis haec disputatio.

Ac primum recitabimus quaestionem Domini, et postea de officiis Messiae dicemus. Norant Pharisaei, Messiam venturum esse, et quidem ex posteris Davidis, sed imaginabantur tantum regem mundanum fore, et divisurum inter Iudaeos imperium mundi: nihil sciebant de passione Messiae, nihil de remissione peccatorum, nihil de imputatione iustitiae.

In summa horribilis caligo fuit in Pharisaeis. Interrogat igitur Dominus: Cuius filius est Messias?

Hi recte respondent: Davidis, sed non possunt dicere, quomodo hoc congruat cum Psalmo, in quo Messias nominatur Dominus Davidis. Ideo opponit Christus: Quomodo David in Spiritu nominat eum Dominum, si est filius?

Declaratio.

Hic imperitis opus est declaratione.

Quomodo valeat argumentum vel obiectio. Potest enim homo rudis cogitare, non esse inusitatum in sermone, filium rustici factum doctorem vel potentem Canonicum, adpellari Dominum. Sed dicta Scripturae non loquuntur tantum de inani vocabulo, sed Dominum intelligit David, qui revera superior est ipso.

Et est talis Syllogismus: Nullus filius in eodem ordine regni, est Dominus patris, aut avi, ut nunquam Carolus est dignior Maximiliano, nec dominatur Maximiliano. Messias est filius Davidis: Ergo non poterit esse Dominus Davidis, ut vos Pharisaei imaginamini.

Hoc argumentum non posset solvi, si Messias tantum esset homo, et tantum constitueret regnum mundi. Tum vere David esset dignior quam Messias, et esset Dominus Messiae, tanquam Rex prior in eodem regno.

Firmissimum igitur argumentum Christus Pharisaeis proposuit. Sed solutio haec est: Propter duas causas Messias est Dominus Davidis, quanquam est filius.

Prior causa est, quia Messias simul est natura filius Dei, et semper fuit et est Dominus Ecclesiae, et est agnitus semper in Ecclesia, quod ei praesens adesset, custodiret et servaret eam. Ipse fuit apud Abraham, qui etiam nominat eum Dominum, et adorat hunc Dominum.

Ipse fuit cum Mose in deserto. David etiam loquitur cum eo, et nominat eum Palmoni et Michaël. Palmoni, id est: mirabilis, Wundertheter, Wunderbarlich. Michaël, quis sicut Deus? quasi dicat: Iste Dominus est sicut Deus, aequalis Patri, et per hunc et propter hunc Deus nos recipit et servat, et salvos facit. Haec tanta testimonia omnia Pharisaei neglexerunt et corruperunt, et cogitabant nondum esse Messiam in ista Ecclesia Israël, nec fuisse apud Patres.

Hae tenebrae profecto fuerunt magnae.

Secunda solutio, Messias ideo est revera Dominus Davidis, quia regnum aliud instituit aeternum, quod longe superat regnum Davidis, et dat liberationem aeternam, et bona aeterna, non, sicut David, tantum praesentes et mortales hostes repressit. Est igitur Messias Dominus Davidis, quia in illo aeterno regno delet peccatum et mortem, et reddit Davidi et omnibus credentibus iustitiam et vitam aeternam. Imo et in hac ipsa politica gubernatione Davidis, hic Dominus Messias adest, regit in praeliis dextram Davidis, est custos totius huius Ecclesiae, et eam valde diligit, pro ea aeternum Patrem deprecatur, defendit, et salvat eam tunc quoque, cum David et alii reges regnant, qui omnes sunt tantum Ministri et organa illius superioris Domini, qui est filius Dei. Haec nesciebant Pharisaei. Quare cum articulum fidei praecipuum de filio Dei, et de remissione peccatorum ignoraverint, manifestum est, eos non fuisse membra Ecclesiae, sed erant hypocritae similes Turcis et impiis Iudaeis huius temporis. Haec brevis declaratio iam sufficiat.

Sed nos haec duo iam consideremus.

Primum de magna coecitate in populo Dei. Cum fuerit tunc tanta coecitas in illo populo erudito et exercitato, simus nos vigilantes, et Deum oremus, ut non sinat extingui lucem veritatis inter nos. Secundo, sicut David fatetur hunc Messiam, de quo loquitur, esse Dominum, ipsi imperantem, et a quo velit regi et salvari: ita nos quoque firma fide statuamus, hunc eundem Messiam Dominum Davidis, esse nobis Dominum, et credamus eum nobis adesse, nobis dare bona aeterna, iustitiam et vitam, defendere etiam nos in hac vita. Hanc fidem quotidie in invocatione exerceamus, confugiamus ad eum in omnibus periculis et negotiis, sicut ipse dixit: Venite ad me omnes, qui onerati estis et laboratis, et ego reficiam vos. Omnes vocat, et revera vult opem ferre, non tantum Davidi, sed etiam mihi et tibi, et nobis omnibus invocantibus eum, et recte agnoscentibus, quis sit, videlicet, quod sit vere filius Dei, et sit constitutus Mediator, Redemtor et Salvator, ut per eum et propter eum dentur nobis remissio peccatorum, iustitia, et vita aeterna, et ut per eum et propter eum etiam in hac vita protegamur. Et sciamus, quod nunc quoque vere adsit nobis, et custodiat nos sicut ipse dicit: Ecce, ego vobiscum sum usque ad consummationem seculi, etc. Item: Ubicunque duo aut tres congregati sunt in nomine meo, in medio eorum sum, etc. Haec in invocatione cogitanda sunt.

## 22:34-40 Sunday XVIII After Trinity
Sunday XVIII after Trinity.

Gospel of Matthew 22.

But the Pharisees, hearing that He had imposed silence on the Sadducees, gathered together. And one of them, a doctor of the law, asked Him, testing Him, and said: "Master, which is the great commandment in the law?" But Jesus said to him: "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind. This is the first and great commandment. The second, however, is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.

On these two commandments the whole law and the Prophets depend." And when the Pharisees were gathered, Jesus asked them, saying: "What do you think about Christ? Whose son is He?" They say to Him: "David's." He says to them: "How then does David in the Spirit call Him Lord, saying, 'The Lord said to my Lord, sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet'? If then David calls Him Lord, how is He his son?" And no one was able to answer Him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day to ask Him any more questions.

There are four principal points.

I. Concerning the doctrine of the law, which is the chief law.

II. Concerning the dignity of the second table.

III. It is not enough in the Church to propose the law, but it is necessary that the Gospel concerning Christ be set forth.

IIII. Concerning the Psalm: The Lord said to my Lord.

On the first.

Just as the Monks valued the Mass or their own vows more than the entire Decalogue, so the Pharisees amplified sacrifices and traditions.

Christ rebukes this error when He prefers the com- commandment concerning the love of God, which requires an inward and perfect obedience of the human heart toward God, namely, the true knowledge of God according to the word divinely revealed, fear, trust, and love. However, it is certain that ...the human heart is far from this precept, because it is full of darkness and doubt about God, it does not fear the wrath of God, it does not trust in God, and it is certain that a burning love for God is lacking. Therefore, Christ rebukes the Pharisees, who boasted of the righteousness of the law, when they did not even have a shadow of it.

Now it is asked here: If the law does not justify, why was it given? I answer: It was given to show sin and to condemn us, as Paul says: The sting of death is sin, the power of sin is the law, that is, because of sin we feel the wrath of God.

But there would be no obligation if there were no law. Therefore, the law cries out in consciences, shows the wrath of God, and brings eternal terrors.

And it is a foolish imagination to think that the law of God is like a tablet hanging on a wall, which can be taken away or cast aside. Nay, as long as sin and death remain, the law remains, accusing, cursing, showing the wrath of God, and it is not overcome except by the knowledge and trust of the Son of God.

Furthermore, concerning the beginning of the law, it is said elsewhere: when we have been justified by faith, a certain begun obedience follows, as has often been said.

On the second. It is a paradox that Christ says the second table is like the first, and without doubt it gravely offends the Pharisees, just as if one were to say to a monk that the work of a pious executioner is to be preferred to his own vows.

This comparison, therefore, must be diligently observed. For Christ wishes especially to teach them that the duties of the second table are among the chief forms of worship, just as the love of God is the chief worship, as if he were saying that the duties of the second table excel ceremonies, just as he says elsewhere: I desire mercy more than sacrifice.

This doctrine is useful and adorns the duties of civil life, so that we may know that they please God and are worship of God. Therefore, they are to be done with greater care.

On the third.

When Christ had disputed such sublime things about the law, he begins to refute the impiety of the Pharisees, asking about the Messiah, as if he were saying: You blind teachers in Israel, you ask about the law and you do not understand it, because you have false opinions about the Messiah, thinking he will be a king who will give you the wealth and empires of the world.

He asks, therefore, about the person and office of the Messiah, whose son he will be, and what he will do, since David calls him Lord? If he were only a political king, he would certainly not be the lord of David, because an heir is by no means the lord of his superiors.

Likewise, if he were only to give the empires of the world, it would profit David nothing, just as Augustus profits Camillus nothing. Why, therefore, did David call the Messiah Lord?

This was a most grave dispute, and inexplicable to the Pharisees, who were dreaming of an empire of the world and not understanding the prophecies about the Messiah. But the explanation is easy for those who correctly understand the prophecies.

First, it is certain that the prophecies speak of liberation from sin and death, and of a new and eternal life, as is said in this Psalm: You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek. He calls him Lord, therefore, because he knows that he is to receive these benefits from him: liberation from sin and death, and eternal life.

Likewise, he calls him Lord because he knows that he will reign by divine power, as he says: Sit at my right hand. Likewise, he knows that he is the promised liberator, the Son of God, as he said before: Today I have begotten you.

He knows that he is already reigning and warring with the devil, just as Isaiah calls him Immanuel, and in Psalm 71 it is said: And they shall worship before him always, where the whole Psalm speaks of the coming Messiah, because he is nevertheless eternal.

His name shall be eternal, his name exists before the sun, and all nations shall be blessed in him.

Latin:

Dominica XVIII. post Trinitatis.

Evangelium Matth. 22.

Pharisaei autem audientes, quod silentium imposuisset Sadducaeis, convenerunt in unum. Et interrogavit unus ex eis legis doctor, tentans eum, et dixit: Magister, quod est mandatum magnum in lege? Ait autem illi Iesus: Diliges Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, et ex tota anima tua, et ex tota mente tua. Hoc est primum et magnum mandatum. Secundum autem simile huic: Diliges proximum tuum sicut teipsum. In his duobus mandatis tota lex pendet et Prophetae.

Congregatis autem Pharisaeis, interrogavit eos Iesus dicens: Quid vobis videtur de Christo? Cuius filius est? Dicunt ei: David. Ait illis: Quomodo ergo David in spiritu vocat eum Dominum, dicens, Dixit Dominus Domino meo, sede a dextris meis, donec ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum? Si ergo David vocat eum Dominum, quomodo filius eius est? Et nemo poterat ei respondere verbum, neque ausus fuit quisquam ex illa die eum amplius interrogare.

Quatuor sunt praecipui loci.

I. De doctrina legis, quae sit lex praecipua.

II. De dignitate secundae tabulae.

III. Non satis est in Ecclesia proponi legem, sed oportet extare Evangelium de Christo.

IIII. De Psalmo: Dixit Dominus Domino meo.

De primo.

Sicut Monachi pluris fecerunt Missam, aut sua vota, quam universum Decalogum, ita Pharisaei amplificabant sacrificia et traditiones.

Hunc errorem reprehendit Christus cum antefert praeceptum de dilectione Dei, quod requirit interiorem et perfectam obedientiam humani cordis erga Deum, videlicet veram agnitionem Dei iuxta verbum divinitus revelatum, timorem, fiduciam, dilectionem. Constat autem cor humanum procul abesse ab... hoc praecepto, quia plenum est caligine et dubitatione de Deo, non timet iram Dei, non confidit Deo, et constat deesse flagrantem dilectionem Dei. Reprehendit igitur Christus Pharisaeos, qui legis iusticiam iactabant, cum ne umbram quidem haberent.

Iam hic quaeritur: Si non fit lex, quare data est? Respondeo: Data est, ut monstret peccatum, et condemnet nos, sicut inquit Paulus: Aculeus mortis peccatum est, potentia peccati lex, id est, propter peccatum sentimus iram Dei.

Sed nulla esset obligatio, nisi lex esset. Ideo lex clamat in conscientiis, monstrat iram Dei, et affert aeternos terrores.

Ac stulta imaginatio est, cogitare legem Dei esse velut tabulam in pariete pendentem, quae auferri aut abiici possit. Imo donec manent peccatum et mors, manet lex accusans, maledicens, iram Dei ostendens, nec vincitur nisi agnitione et fiducia Filii Dei.

Caeterum de incoatione legis alias dicitur, cum fide iustificati sumus, accedit quaedam incoata obedientia, ut saepe dictum est.

De secundo. Paradoxum est, quod inquit Christus, secundam tabulam similem esse primae, et haud dubie graviter offendit Pharisaeos, ut si quis diceret Monacho, opus pii lictoris anteferendum esse ipsius votis.

Haec igitur collatio diligenter observanda est. Vult enim Christus praecipue eos docere, officia secundae tabulae esse inter praecipuos cultus, sicut dilectio Dei est praecipuus cultus, quasi dicat, officia secundae tabulae antecellere ceremoniis, sicut alibi inquit: Magis volo misericordiam, quam sacrificium.

Haec doctrina est utilis, et ornat officia civilis vitae, ut sciamus ea Deo placere, et esse cultus Dei. Ideo maiore cura facienda sunt.

De tertio.

Cum de lege tam sublimia disputasset Christus, incipit coarguere impietatem Pharisaeorum, interrogans de Messia, quasi dicat, vos coeci doctores in Israël, de lege quaeritis, et eam non intelligitis, quia de Messia habetis falsas opiniones, putatis futurum esse regem, qui vobis opes et imperia mundi daturus sit.

Quaerit igitur de persona et officio Messiae, cuius filius erit, et quid aget, cum David vocet eum Dominum? Si tantum esset rex politicus, profecto non esset dominus Davidis, quia haeres nequaquam est dominus superiorum.

Item, si tantum esset daturus imperia mundi, nihil prodesset Davidi, ut Camillo nihil prodest Augustus. Cur igitur David vocavit Messiam Dominum?

Haec fuit gravissima disputatio, et inexplicabilis Pharisaeis somniantibus imperium mundi, et non intelligentibus prophetias de Messia. Sed facilis est explicatio recte intelligentibus prophetias.

Primum constat prophetias loqui de liberatione a peccato et a morte, et de nova et aeterna vita, ut in hoc Psalmo dicitur: Tu es sacerdos in aeternum, secundum ordinem Melchisedech. Vocat igitur Dominum, quia scit se accipere ab eo haec beneficia, liberationem a peccato et a morte, et vitam aeternam.

Item vocat Dominum, quia scit eum divina potentia regnaturum esse, sicut inquit: Sede a dextris meis. Item, scit illum promissum liberatorem esse Filium Dei, sicut antea inquit: Hodie genui te.

Scit eum iam regnare, et belligerari cum diabolo, sicut Esaias vocat eum Emanuel, et Psal. 71. dicitur: Et adorabunt coram ipso semper, ubi totus Psalmus loquitur de venturo Messia, quia tamen est aeternus.

Erit nomen eius aeternum, ante solem existit nomen eius, et benedicentur in ipso omnes gentes.

## 23:1 Sermons on Matthew: Argument
Chapter XXIII.

Then Jesus spoke to the crowds, and to his disciples, saying: In the chair of Moses sit the Scribes and the Pharisees, etc. Here begins the sermon, which commands the judging of doctrine, and shows what kind of power those teaching in the Church have. And first, it is always necessary in life to discern the doctrine revealed by God concerning the true knowledge of himself and invocation, from human traditions, and it must be known what is to be thought of each kind.

First rule.

Let this, therefore, be the first rule. No doctrine concerning the essence and will of God, and concerning our salvation, is to be received or approved, except this doctrine of the Gospel alone, handed down through Christ and the Prophets and the Apostles. To this doctrine alone God gave testimonies, that it was revealed by him, according to that: The Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared it to us. And this rule is confirmed by the saying of Paul: If an angel from heaven shall preach another Gospel, let him be anathema. Therefore, every doctrine contrary to the Gospel is to be rejected constantly, whether it be named Mahometan, or Papistical, or Jewish, or Monastic, or Manichaean.

Indeed, all opinions and cults outside the Gospel should be rejected, but let us acknowledge and invoke God most firmly only as He has revealed Himself.

Second rule. For the propagating and preserving of this true doctrine, God has always instituted and preserves a public ministry, that is, He wills that certain persons be chosen who shall teach and administer the Sacraments. And He commands that the voice of these be heard, as in Luke 10: "He who hears you, hears me, and he who rejects you, rejects me."

He wills that there be no conventicles in the dark, as were the gatherings of the heathens, where great indecencies were committed.

But God wills that the voice of His Gospel be heard openly; He wills that the Son be known to the whole human race. Therefore, He instituted and preserves the ministry.

Thus it is said in Ephesians 4: The Son sits at the right hand of the Father, giving gifts to men, Prophets, Apostles, Evangelists, Pastors, Teachers. And indeed, He preserves this ministry and is present with it for this reason, that we may not be tossed about by every wind of doctrine. He wills that all ministers sound the one perpetual voice of His Gospel; He wills that the true God be invoked in the acknowledgment of the Son. He does not will that new Gods or new cults be devised.

He says the same thing here concerning the ministry: The Scribes and Pharisees sit on Moses' seat. All things that they say, do, etc.

In these words, He first teaches that the ministry is instituted and is necessary, because the seat of Moses signifies the ministry instituted by God. And such a ministry, which sounds the voice delivered to Moses and the other Prophets, and in that understanding in which the Prophets taught.

Nor does the seat of Moses signify human, Pharisaical, or other traditions devised outside the prophetic voice.

When the Pharisees taught that their sacrifices merited the remission of sins.

Likewise, that the Messiah would come to establish the empires of the world, etc., then they were not sitting in the seat of Moses, but in the seat of pestilence.

Thus the Pope does not sit in the seat of Peter when he teaches falsely concerning the Remission of sins, concerning the Mass, concerning Penance, concerning the invocation of Saints, concerning Marriage, etc.

This distinction must be diligently observed: when teachers sit in the seat of Moses, that is, of the true ministry, and when they do not sit in the seat of Moses, but in the seat of pestilence.

And it is necessary to join the words of Christ: All things that they say, do. He is not speaking of human traditions, because it is most clearly said elsewhere: If anyone teaches another Gospel, let him be anathema. But He is speaking of the true ministry: All things that they say, namely in the seat of Moses, in the true ministry, do, when they sound the word of God delivered to Moses and the Prophets. Do not do other things which they say against the voice of the Prophets. That Christ wills this, He Himself testifies when He soon adds: Do not be called Rabbi.

One is your Master, Christ. That is, do not invent a new doctrine, but hear the one Master, Christ. This is the Son, who brought forth the doctrine from the bosom of the eternal Father; sound this one thing with a concordant voice.

Consider this consideration well, because Papists and Bishops often cite this saying for their own authority: All things that they say, do. Here let us know that it is necessary to join the words of Christ: which they say, namely in the seat of Moses, that is, in the true ministry, sounding the word delivered to the Prophets, and in that understanding in which it was delivered to the Prophets, because the rule remains unmoved: If anyone teaches another Gospel, let him be anathema.

And thus Duke Frederick the Elector solved this objection for Duke George, when Duke George was disputing with Duke Frederick in Grimma concerning the traditions of the Pope and the Bishops.

Let us, however, learn to venerate the true ministry, and let us hear the word of God sounding there, and let us give thanks to God who preserves the ministry, and let us pray that He may preserve it.

Third rule.

Through this ministry, that is, through the voice of the Gospel and the Sacraments, it is most certain that God gathers to Himself an eternal Church, and is efficacious, moving hearts by the Holy Spirit through the voice of the Gospel, as is said in Rom. 1: The Gospel is the power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes.

Behold, this great thing, namely the conversion of men to God, and regeneration unto life and eternal salvation, is not done through any other doctrines, or in any other way, but is done only through the voice of the Gospel and the Sacraments.

Nor is the Church of the elect anywhere else, except among those who hear the voice of the Gospel and use the Sacraments.

This is a great consolation to the pious. It is certain that there is always some elect Church, and this is only among those who hear the voice of the Gospel.

One is your Master. He who is greatest among you, let him be your minister etc.

In the last sermon it was said concerning the ministry of the Gospel, that there must be a single doctrine handed down by God, and that it must not be corrupted by human traditions, and that God is effective through the ministry which He instituted. To know these things in the Church is very necessary, and it is a most sweet consolation.

Now indeed he begins to censure many vices which corrupt and destroy the Church.

The first is idolatry, that is, false doctrine.

He therefore forbids the establishing of traditions and the instituting of new forms of worship. Therefore he says: One is your Master. Concerning this part it has been spoken recently, and it will have to be said often again.

Ambition.

The second sin, of which he speaks here presently, is ambition or domination, which is established in the Church under the pretext of doctrine or under the pretext of ministry.

And here he principally condemns the Pope and all Bishops who have turned the ministry into kingdoms, principalities, and worldly domination.

Here therefore it must first be asked, how political power differs from the ministry. Therefore I will speak first concerning the duties of political power.

Political power is a power ordained by God, that it may be the guardian of discipline and peace, and punish the disobedient with the sword. For God wills that men be ruled by such external government.

First, that there may be discipline in external morals according to all the precepts of the Decalogue, so that men may be able to be taught and instructed concerning God and concerning the Son of God, because where there is no discipline, there men become wild and beastly, indeed diabolical, just as Nero, Caligula, and many similar to Devils lived.

Secondly, God wills that men be ruled by that external government, so that there may be peace, because we could not live together in society if robberies, thefts, and manifold violence were not restrained.

These, therefore, are the three duties of political power.

First, that it set forth the Decalogue to the people, because the Decalogue ought to be the source and norm of all laws. And the magistrate is placed in the human race for this reason, that he may be the voice of God sounding the Decalogue in external government.

The second duty: God has also given this authority to political power, that it may establish its own laws, not indeed conflicting with the Decalogue, but which determine some circumstance of the Decalogue. As the Decalogue only says: You shall not steal. Afterwards, the power adds the kinds of punishments, etc.

The third duty: It is necessary for political power to be an avenger and punisher of all external disobedience through the sword and other corporal punishments. Because a law without punishments is useless. And God has most severely commanded in Deut. 10: You shall not pity him, etc.

But in order that it may be able to exercise corporal punishments and be able to repel robberies, it is necessary to establish courts, and for the power to be armed with soldiers, money, and many instruments. Therefore, it is necessary for political power to have tributes, etc.

Such is an honest political power, when it rightly performs its duty. And yet there are few such.

But most are tyrants, and who are tyrants can be understood from these three duties: If they do not set forth the Decalogue, but confirm idols, persecute the truth, etc. If they kill men unjustly, if they do not punish adulteries, etc. If they bring forth unjust laws, and only plunder the people, and do not exercise judgments, and do not punish robberies.

I have already spoken about political power; let us see what the evangelical Ministry is.

For this ministry is also a certain venerable power, divinely ordained, but unlike the political, without the sword, without soldiers, without arms, without opulence.

What is it, therefore? It is the mandate of teaching the Gospel, administering the Sacraments, remitting sin, and punishing by the word, without corporal force. It differs likewise in many things from worldly power.

First, because it teaches the Gospel and remits sins before God; this power is absolutely not that of a political magistrate.

Secondly, he ought not to establish laws, just as political power can establish laws for a reasonable cause.

Thirdly, the manner of punishment is different. The minister of the Gospel punishes only by word and excommunication, but the magistrate by the sword. Fourthly, they differ in their instruments. The magistrate must be equipped with arms, resources, and power. But the evangelical minister is without arms, without resources, without power, just as John the Baptist wanders alone in the desert and says: I am the voice of one crying out. What is weaker than a voice? Yet, through this voice, God is effective, as was recently said. May you always keep these differences in sight, and now see how the Pope and the Bishops have turned the ministry of the Gospel into kingdoms and tyrannies.

They do not teach the Gospel; rather, they are enemies of the Gospel, they establish laws, and indeed manifestly impious ones, such as the prohibition of marriage. They punish with the sword; indeed, they say that both swords were given to Peter by Christ, and they snatch empires from kings, just as they have often waged great wars against emperors. And the Emperor Frederick Barbarossa lay at the feet of the Pontiff, and the Pontiff struck the head of the Emperor with his foot. And the Emperor asked for forgiveness, as if he had unjustly waged war against the Pope. You see also how great is the power, how great the wealth of the Bishops. Foreseeing all these things, Christ here warns the Apostles: Whoever is greater, let him be a minister among you, that is: I do not want the Church to be like the empires of the world, but understand that you are ministers and messengers of my voice, without arms, without royal power, without royal opulence. Be faithful in the ministry, and serve your calling; do not drag us into the governance of the Kings and Princes of the world. This is the simple meaning in this passage, because here Christ speaks principally about the ministers of the Gospel.

He also threatens a punishment: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled. It is certain that when someone breaks out beyond his calling and takes on governments not pertaining to his calling, then he sins and is punished, just as Absalom sinned and was punished, and many others who wanted to become kings without a legitimate calling. Even many Pontiffs in this life have been horribly punished, as when the son of Pope Alexander wanted to kill certain Cardinals invited to the table with poison, the father, Pope Alexander, drank the poison by mistake and thus died. Many such examples have occurred in Rome: Pope Clement, the one immediately before Paul III, was also killed by poison. But other, much greater eternal punishments will also follow the present ones. And God will finally destroy this power of the Pontiffs and Bishops, even if He has tolerated it for a long time, because at the end of the world this kingdom of the Pope had a certain time, just as the Pharisaic kingdom among the Jews had a certain time. Let it be enough to have said these things in general about this saying: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled. It is, however, a common saying, which teaches not only ministers but also other men universally, so that they may learn to remain within their calling, and not take on governments out of pride, without a calling: human pride is not happy, but is undoubtedly confounded and put to shame.

Therefore, it is said in Luke 16: What is sublime before men is an abomination before God. It is a very harsh condemnation of pride that it says it is an abomination. Because an abomination is something that God greatly detests. Thus He speaks about pride. And it is a just condemnation, because God wants us to acknowledge our sins and His wrath against sins. Those who do this grieve and acknowledge themselves to be miserable, and they are not proud. Those, however, are proud who are secure, despising the wrath of God, elated because of their opinion of their own righteousness and wisdom. Thus pride encompasses many sins, therefore God most justly grows angry at pride. And against pride we should always propose to ourselves the example of Christ, who says: Learn from me, for I am meek and humble of heart.

And see how great humility is: He lies before the eternal Father and is guilty of the wrath of God, as if He had polluted Himself with your sins and mine, and He transfers your and my ignominy onto Himself. And afterwards, for you and for me, He hangs on the cross, despised and mocked. When we see such humility, we ought to be ashamed that we often want to stir up great tumults because of one slight insult. Likewise, see the entire calling of the holy angels.

Their duty is to be guardians of our bodies and our affairs: they themselves drive away the Devils from your house, from your children, from your furnace. The holy angels sit there, simultaneously beholding the face of God and guarding your furnace, your kitchen, your bed. This is great humility and great love toward us miserable and sordid men.

Let us, therefore, be ashamed that we are proud. and let us do penance, and let us learn humility from the Lord Jesus Christ, and from the holy angels. Let this general admonition now suffice.

Latin:

Caput XXIII.

Tunc Iesus locutus est ad turbas, et ad discipulos suos, dicens: In cathedra Mosi sedent Scribae et Pharisaei, etc. Hic incipit concio, quae praecipit diiudicationem doctrinae, et ostendit, qualis sit potestas docentium in Ecclesia. Et primum semper in vita discerni oportet doctrinam a Deo patefactam de vera agnitione ipsius et invocatione, et traditiones humanas, et sciendum est, quid de utroque genere sentiendum sit.

Prima regula.

Sit ergo haec prima regula. Nulla doctrina de Dei essentia et voluntate, et de nostra salute, recipienda est vel adprobanda, nisi sola haec doctrina Evangelii, tradita per Christum et Prophetas et Apostolos. Huic soli doctrinae Deus testimonia dedit, quod ab ipso revelata sit, iuxta illud: Filius, qui est in siou Patris, ipse enarravit nobis. Et hanc regulam confirmat dictum Pauli: Si angelus de coelo aliud Evangelium docebit, anathema sit. Reiicienda est igitur constanter omnis doctrina, contraria Evangelio, sive nominetur Mahometica, sive Papistica, sive Iudaica, sive Monastica, sive Manichaea.

Imo omnes opiniones, et cultus extra Evangelium reiiciantur, sed tantum sic agnoscamus et invocemus Deum firmissime, sicut se patefecit.

Secunda regula. Ad hanc veram doctrinam propagandam et conservandam instituit Deus semper et conservat publicum ministerium, id est, vult esse electas certas personas, quae doceant et administrent Sacramenta. Et praecipit horum vocem audiri, ut Lucae 10.: Qui vos audit, me audit, et qui nos spernit, me spernit.

Vult non esse conventicula in tenebris, sicut erant ethnici conventus, ubi magnae turpitudines fiebant.

Sed vult Deus palam audiri vocem Evangelii sui, vult toti generi humano filium notum esse. Ideo instituit et conservat ministerium.

Sic dicitur ad Ephesios 4.: Sedet ad dextram Patris Filius, dans dona hominibus, Prophetas, Apostolos, Evangelistas, Pastores, Doctores. Et quidem ideo servat hoc ministerium, et ei adest, ut non circumferamur omni vento doctrinae. Vult unam perpetuam vocem sui Evangelii sonare omnes ministros, vult verum Deum invocari in agnitione filii. Non vult novos Deos aut novos cultus excogitari.

Idem de ministerio hic dicit: Sedent super cathedram Mosi Scribae et Pharisaei. Omnia quae dicunt, facite etc.

In his verbis primum docet, quod ministerium sit institutum, et sit necessarium, quia cathedra Mosi significat ministerium a Deo institutum. Et tale ministerium, quod sonat vocem Mosi et aliis Prophetis traditam, et in eo intellectu, sicut Prophetae docuerunt.

Nec significat Mosi cathedra traditiones humanas, pharisaicas, aut alias, excogitatas extra vocem propheticam.

Quando docebant Pharisaei, sua sacrificia mereri remissionem peccatorum.

Item Messiam venturum esse, ut constituat imperia mundi etc., tunc non sedebant in cathedra Mosi, sed in cathedra pestilentiae.

Sic Papa non sedet in cathedra Petri, quando falsa docet de Remissione peccatorum, de Missa, de Poenitentia, de invocatione Sanctorum, de Coniugio, etc.

Haec distinctio diligenter observanda est, quando sedeant doctores in cathedra Mosi, id est, veri ministerii, et quando non sedeant in cathedra Mosi, sed in cathedra pestilentiae.

Et coniungi verba Christi oportet: Omnia quae dicunt, facite. Non loquitur de traditionibus humanis, quia clarissime dicitur alibi: Si quis aliud Evangelium docet, anathema sit. Sed loquitur de vero ministerio: Omnia quae dicunt, scilicet in cathedra Mosi, in vero ministerio, facite, quando sonant verbum Dei traditum Mosi et Prophetis. Non facite alia, quae dicunt contra vocem Prophetarum. Quod hoc velit Christus, ipse testatur, cum mox addit: Non vocemini Rabbi.

Unus est Magister vester, Christus. Id est, non fingite novam doctrinam, sed audite unicum Magistrum Christum. Hic est Filius, qui ex sinu aeterni Patris protulit doctrinam, hanc unam concordi voce sonate.

Hanc considerationem bene considerate, quia Papistae et Episcopi saepe pro sua autoritate citant hoc dictum: Omnia quae dicunt, facite. Hic sciamus oportere coniungi verba Christi, quae dicunt, scilicet in cathedra Mosi, id est, in vero ministerio, sonantes verbum traditum Prophetis, et in eo intellectu, in quo Prophetis traditum est, quia manet regula immota: Si quis aliud Evangelium docet, anathema sit.

Et sic solvit hanc obiectionem Duci Georgio Dux Fridericus Elector, cum Dux Georgius disputaret cum Duce Friderico in Grim de traditionibus Papae et Episcoporum.

Discamus autem verum ministerium venerari, et audiamus verbum Dei ibi sonans, et Deo gratias agamus conservanti ministerium, et oremus, ut conservet.

Tertia regula.

Per hoc ministerium, id est, per vocem Evangelii et Sacramenta certissimum est, Deum sibi colligere aeternam Ecclesiam, et efficacem esse, movere corda Spiritu sancto per vocem Evangelii, ut dicitur Rom. 1.: Evangelium est potentia Dei ad salutem omni credenti.

Ecce haec tanta res, scilicet hominum conversio ad Deum, et regeneratio ad vitam et salutem aeternam, non fit per alias doctrinas ullas, aut alio modo, sed fit tantum per vocem Evangelii et Sacramenta.

Nec alibi est Ecclesia electorum, nisi inter hos, qui audiunt vocem Evangelii, et Sacramenta utuntur.

Haec est magna consolatio piis. Certum est semper aliquam esse electam Ecclesiam, et haec tantum est inter hos, qui audiunt vocem Evan- gelii.

Unus est Magister vester. Qui est maior inter vos, sit minister etc.

In proxima concione dictum est de ministe- rio Evangelii, quod oporteat esse unicam doctri- nam a Deo traditam, et quod non sit corrum- penda per traditiones humanas, et quod Deus sit efficax per ministerium, quod instituit. Haec scire in Ecclesia valde necesse est, et dulcissima consolatio est.

Iam vero incipit multa vitia taxare, quae corrumpunt et perdunt Ecclesiam.

Primum est idololatria, id est, falsa doctrina.

Prohibet igitur condere traditiones, et novos cultus instituere. Ideo dicit: Unus est Magister vester. De hac parte nuper dictum est, et rursus saepe dicendum erit.

Ambitio.

Secundum peccatum, de quo mox hic dicit, est ambitio seu dominatio, quae in Ecclesia con- stituitur praetextu doctrinae, vel praetextu mi- nisterii.

Et hic principaliter damnat Papam et omnes Episcopos, qui verterunt ministerium in regna, principatus, et dominationem mundanam.

Hic igitur primum quaerendum est, quid differat potestas politica a ministerio. Ideo di- cam primum de officiis potestatis politicae.

Potestas politica est potestas ordinata a Deo, ut sit custos disciplinae et pacis, et puniat non obedientes gladio. Vult enim Deus regi homines, tali externa gubernatione.

Primum, ut sit disciplina in externis mori- bus iuxta omnia praecepta Decalogi, ut doceri et institui homines possint de Deo, et de filio Dei, quia ubi non est disciplina, ibi fiunt homines feri et bestiales, imo diabolici, sicut vixerunt Nero, Caligula, et multi similes Diabolis.

Secundo vult Deus regi homines illa externa gubernatione, ut sit pax, quia non possemus si- mul in societate vivere, si non coërcerentur la- trocinia et furta et multiplex violentia.

Sunt igitur haec tria officia potestatis poli- ticae.

Primum, ut proponat populo Decalogum, quia Decalogus debet esse fons et norma omnium legum. Et magistratus est ideo collocatus in genere humano, ut sit vox Dei sonans Decalogum in externa gubernatione.

Secundum officium: Deus etiam politicae potestati dedit hanc autoritatem, ut proprias leges condat, non quidem pugnantes cum Decalogo, sed quae determinent aliquam circumstantiam Decalogi. Ut Decalogus tantum dicit: Non furtum facies. Postea potestas addit genera poenarum etc.

Tertium officium: Oportet potestatem politicam esse vindicem, et punitricem omnis inobedientiae externae per gladium et alias poenas corporales. Quia lex sine poenis est inutilis. Et Deus severissime praecepit Deut. 10.: Non misereberis eius etc.

Ut autem possit corporales poenas exercere, possit depellere latrocinia, oportet constituere iudicia, et potestatem armatam esse militibus, pecunia et instrumentis multis. Ideo oportet potestatem politicam habere tributa etc.

Talis est honesta potestas politica, quando recte facit officium. Et tamen pauci sunt tales.

Plurimi vero sunt tyranni, et qui sint tyranni, ex his tribus officiis intelligi potest, Si non proponunt Decalogum, sed confirmant idola, persequuntur veritatem etc. Si interficiunt homines iniuste, si non puniunt adulteria, etc. Si leges ferunt iniustas, et tantum expilant populum, et non exercent iudicia, et non puniunt latrocinia.

Iam dixi de politica potestate, videamus quid sit Ministerium evangelicum.

Est enim et hoc ministerium quaedam veneranda potestas, divinitus ordinata, sed dissimilis politicae, sine gladio, sine militibus, sine armis, sine opulentia.

Quid est igitur? Est mandatum docendi Evangelii, administrandi Sacramenta, remittendi peccati, et puniendi verbo, sine vi corporali. Differt item in multis rebus a potestate mundana.

Primum, quia docet Evangelium, et remittit peccata coram Deo, haec potestas prorsus non est magistratus politici.

Secundo, non debet condere leges, sicut potestas politica potest leges ex causa rationabili condere.

Tertio, modus poenae est dissimilis. Minister Evangelii tantum punit verbo et excommunicatione, sed magistratus gladio. Quarto differunt instrumentis. Magistratum oportet esse instructum armis, opibus, potentia. Sed minister evangelicus est sine armis, sine opibus, sine potentia, sicut Iohannes Baptista solus in deserto vagatur, et dicit: Ego sum vox clamantis. Quid est infirmius voce? sed tamen per hanc vocem Deus est efficax, ut nuper dictum est. Has differentias semper teneatis in conspectu, et iam videte, quomodo Papa et Episcopi verterint ministerium Evangelii in regna et tyrannides.

Non docent Evangelium, imo sunt hostes Evangelii, condunt leges, et quidem manifeste impias, ut prohibitionem coniugii. Puniunt gladio, imo dicunt Petro datum esse a Christo utrunque gladium, et eripiunt imperia regibus, sicut saepe magna bella gesserunt cum imperatoribus. Et Friedericus Barbarossa Imperator, iacuit ad pedes Pontificis, et Pontifex caput Imperatoris pede percussit. Et Imperator veniam petivit, quasi iniuste gessisset bellum adversus Papam. Videtis item quanta sit potentia, quantae opes Episcoporum. Haec omnia praevidens Christus hic praemonet Apostolos: Qui est maior, sit minister inter vos, id est: Non volo Ecclesiam similem esse imperiis mundi, sed intelligatis vos esse ministros, et nuncios meae vocis, sine armis, sine potestate regia, sine opulentia regia. Sitis fideles in ministerio, et servite vestrae vocationi, non trahite ad nos gubernationem Regum et Principum mundi. Haec est simplex sententia in hoc loco, quia hic principaliter loquitur Christus de ministris Evangelii.

Poenam etiam minitatur: Qui exaltat se, humiliabitur. Certum est, quando aliquis erumpit extra vocationem suam, et suscipit gubernationes non pertinentes ad suam vocationem, tunc peccat et punitur, sicut peccavit et punitus est Absolon et alii multi, qui voluerunt reges fieri, sine legitima vocatione. Etiam multi Pontifices in hac vita horribiliter puniti sunt, ut cum Papae Alexandri filius vellet veneno interficere quosdam Cardinales invitatos ad mensam, pater Papa Alexander errore hausit venenum, et ita mortuus est. Talia exempla Romae multa acciderunt: Papa Clemens, proximus ante Paulum tertium, etiam veneno necatus est. Sed aliae poenae aeternae multo maiores praesentibus etiam sequentur. Et Deus tandem hanc potentiam Pontificum et Episcoporum destruet, etiamsi diu eam toleravit, quia in fine mundi hoc regnum Papae habuit certum tempus, sicut pharisaicum regnum apud Iudaeos habuit certum tempus. Haec in genere dixisse satis sit de hoc dicto: Qui se exaltat, humiliabitur. Est autem commune dictum, quod non solum ministros, sed etiam alios homines universaliter docet, ut discant manere intra vocationem, non suscipiant gubernationes ex superbia, sine vocatione: non est felix humana superbia, sed haud dubie confunditur et pudefit.

Ideo Lucae 16. dicitur: Quod coram hominibus sublime est, abominatio est coram Deo. Valde atrox vituperatio est superbiae, quod dicit, abominatio est. Quia abominatio est aliquid, quod Deus valde detestatur. Sic loquitur de superbia. Et iusta vituperatio est, quia Deus vult nos agnoscere nostra peccata, et suam iram contra peccata. Hoc qui faciunt, dolent, et agnoscunt se esse miseros, et non sunt superbi. Illi vero sunt superbi, qui sunt securi, contemnentes iram Dei, elati propter opinionem iustitiae et sapientiae de se. Ita multa peccata complectitur superbia, ideo Deus iustissime irascitur superbiae. Et contra superbiam semper deberemus nobis proponere exemplum Christi, qui dicit: Discite a me, quia mitis sum, et humilis corde.

Et vide quanta sit humilitas: Ipse iacet coram aeterno Patre, et est reus irae Dei, quasi polluisset se tuis et meis peccatis, et tuam et meam ignominiam in se transfert. Et postea pro te et me pendet in cruce, spretus et derisus. Tantam humilitatem cum videmus, pudere nos oportuit, quod saepe propter unum leve convicium, volumus movere magnos tumultus. Item vide totam angelorum sanctorum vocationem.

Horum officium est, ut sint custodes corporum et rerum nostrarum: ipsi depellunt Diabolos a tua domo, a tuis pueris, a tua fornace. Sedent ibi sancti angeli simul intuentes faciem Dei, et custodientes tuam fornacem, tuam culinam, tuum lectum. Haec est magna humilitas, et magnus amor erga nos miseros et sordidos homines.

Pudeat igitur nos, quod sumus superbi. et agamus poenitentiam, et discamus a Domino Iesu Christo, et a sanctis angelis humilitatem. Haec generalis admonitio iam sufficiat.

## 23:13 Sermons on Matthew
Woe to you Scribes and Pharisees, who shut the kingdom of heaven, etc.

It is customary in scripture to name the sword and the keys. The sword signifies political power, because it restrains members with external and corporal punishments, just as a thief is punished by the sword. The keys signify economic power, just as a mother of a family carries the keys. And because the government of the Church is more similar to an economy, therefore the keys also signify the ministry of the Gospel and the Sacraments. And this is what the Lord means when He says to Peter: To thee I will give the keys of the kingdom of heaven, that is, the ministry of the Gospel and the Sacraments, by which the kingdom of heaven is opened. Let it therefore be the first care of all who are called to the ministry, that they teach rightly, and rightly administer the Sacraments. And just as this command is proper to the office: so Christ here begins the accusation and condemnation from this principle, He condemns them because they do not teach the Gospel, but rather propose a false and impious doctrine. Thus they shut heaven to themselves and to others.

This condemnation is often repeated in the Prophets. Ezekiel 3: If thou shalt not announce his blood, I will require it at thy hand. Isaiah 5: Woe to you that rise up early to drunkenness, and neglect the work of the Lord. Hosea 4: Because thou hast rejected my knowledge, therefore I will reject thee, etc. Micah 3: For this cause, because of you, Sion shall be plowed as a field. And Matthew 5: If the salt shall lose its savor, it shall be cast out and trodden under foot. Let these threats exhort everyone to be more diligent in their office.

But the powerful Bishops and Canons, who dominate in the Church, deride these threats, but God horribly punishes and will punish them. And especially the Pope abuses the keys with great fury. He pretends that there is a power to establish new laws, to invent cults, to seize the empires of the world. How great these grave sins are will be seen at the final judgment, when that False Prophet shall be cast into hell, while the whole Church, resurrected from the dead, looks on.

Woe to you who devour the houses of widows, etc.

He spoke before about those who do not perform their office or who corrupt doctrine. Here He speaks of avarice, He condemns those who seem to perform their office, but serve their own avarice, and because of avarice invent new cults, just as Monks and Mass-priests sold Masses, Vigils, and Monks sold the merits of their own order. Likewise, innumerable frauds have been invented to hunt for money. The cult of saints, false miracles, crowds at certain statues, relics of saints, and other similar things. All these idolatries are condemned here, and it is to be wondered at that the Devil's power is so great that he has raised up, and continues to raise up and stabilize, such manifest idolatries, not only among the Gentiles, but even in the Church.

Therefore let us fear God, and let us be solicitous that we retain the truth, and let us pray that God may govern us, because man cannot escape the snares of the Devil without the help of God, just as the Lord commands us to pray: Lead us not into temptation. And Peter says: The Devil goes about like a roaring lion, whom resist, being strong in the faith. Likewise, this kind of Demon is not cast out, except by fasting and prayer.

Latin:

Vae vobis Scribae et Pharisaei, qui clauditis regnum coelorum, etc.

Usitatum est in scriptura nominare, gladium et claves. Gladius significat potestatem politicam, quia coërcet membra externis et corporalibus poenis, ut latro punitur gladio. Claves significant potestatem oeconomicam, sicut materfamilias gerit claves. Et quia Ecclesiae gubernatio similior est oeconomiae, ideo claves significant etiam ministerium Evangelii et Sacramentorum. Et hoc vult Dominus, cum ait ad Petrum: Tibi dabo claves regni coelorum, id est, ministerium Evangelii et Sacramentorum, quo aperitur regnum coelorum. Sit igitur prima cura omnium, qui sunt vocati ad ministerium, ut recte doceant, et recte administrent Sacramenta. Et sicut hoc mandatum proprium est officii: ita Christus hic accusationem et condemnationem ab hoc principio orditur, damnat eos, quod non doceant Evangelium, imo proponant falsam et impiam doctrinam. Ita claudunt coelum sibi ipsis et aliis.

Haec condemnatio saepe repetita est in Prophetis. Ezechielis 3.: Si non annunciaveris sanguinem eius, de manu tua requiram. Esaiae 5.: Vae qui consurgitis mane ad ebrietatem, et opus Domini negligitis. Oseae 4.: Quia repulisti scientiam meam, ideo repellam te, etc. Micheae 3.: Propter hoc, causa vestri, Sion velut ager arabitur. Et Matthaei 5.: Si sal infatuatum fuerit, eiicietur et conculcabitur. Hae comminationes singulos hortentur, ut sint in officio diligentiores.

Sed potentes Episcopi et Canonici, qui dominantur in Ecclesia, derident has comminationes, sed Deus horribiliter eos punit et puniet. Ac praecipue Papa magno furore abutitur clavibus. Fingit esse potestatem condendi novas leges, fingendi cultus, rapiendi imperia mundi. Haec magna peccata quanta sint in novissimo iudicio conspicietur, quando ille Pseudopropheta abiicietur in infernum, spectante tota Ecclesia resuscitata a mortuis.

Vae qui devoratis domus viduarum, etc.

Prius dixit de non facientibus officium vel corrumpentibus doctrinam. Hic dicit de avaritia, damnat eos, qui videntur facere officium, sed serviunt suae avaritiae, et propter avaritiam excogitant novos cultus, sicut Monachi et Sacrificuli vendiderunt Missas, Vigilias, Monachi vendiderunt sui ordinis merita. Item excogitatae sunt innumerabiles fraudes ad pecuniam venandam. Cultus sanctorum, falsa miracula, concursus ad certas statuas, reliquiae sanctorum, et alia similia. Hae idololatriae omnes hic damnantur, et mirandum est, tantam esse Diaboli potentiam, ut tam manifestas idololatrias, non solum inter Ethnicos, sed etiam in Ecclesia erexerit, et erigat, et stabiliat.

Ideo timeamus Deum, et simus soliciti, ut veritatem retineamus, et oremus, ut Deus nos gubernet, quia non potest homo effugere Diaboli laqueos, sine auxilio Dei, sicut iubet nos Dominus orare: Ne nos inducas in tentationem. Et Petrus dicit: Circumit Diabolus tanquam leo rugiens, cui resistite fortes in fide. Item, hoc genus Daemoniorum non eiicitur, nisi in ieiunio et oratione.

## 23:15 Sermons on Matthew
Woe to you who go about sea and land, to make one proselyte.

Here you may learn that God at all times gathers to Himself a Church, even from the Gentiles. And at the time of the kingdom of Israel and Judah there were three statuses of men who were members of the Church. The first status was the seed of Abraham. This was required to be circumcised, and to observe the ceremonies according to the law of Moses. The second status was that of proselytes, that is, of strangers, who were not born from the seed of Abraham, but nevertheless wished to be part of this people, and wished to be circumcised. Because these wished to be circumcised, they were also required to observe other ceremonies, like Uriah.

The third status was that of those who are called in the Acts, religious men, that is, Gentiles, such as Naaman the Syrian, Nebuchadnezzar, Cyrus, Cornelius, and many others, who learned the promises concerning the coming Messiah, and the doctrine concerning the true God, and concerning good works, according to the Decalogue. And yet they were neither circumcised, nor did they keep the Mosaic ceremonies.

Take note of these differences, and here consider the distinction between the Law and the Gospel. No status, neither the seed of Abraham, nor proselytes, nor religious men deserved the remission of sins by the law, nor were they righteous by the law, but only by believing according to the promise concerning the Messiah, they received remission, and by faith they were righteous, just as we are.

Nor was it necessary for the Gentiles to be circumcised. Therefore, Christ censures this, because the Pharisees taught many errors, persuading the Gentiles that by the law they deserved the remission of sins, and were made righteous by the law, and thus they created in them the opinion that it was necessary to be circumcised, and that they were righteous by the law, and they destroyed the doctrine concerning the promise and the righteousness of faith.

Just as in our time the Monks used to go about, and invited men to Monasticism with false and impious opinions, that Monasticism was a new Baptism, deserved the remission of sins, and was righteousness and a state of perfection. From this example, this member in the text can also be understood.

Latin:

Vae qui circumitis mare et aridam, ut faciatis unum proselytum.

Hic discatis, quod Deus omni tempore sibi colligit Ecclesiam, etiam ex gentibus. Ac tempore regni Israël et Iuda erant tres status hominum, qui erant membra Ecclesiae. Primus status erat, semen Abrahae. Hoc oportuit circumcidi, et servare ceremonias iuxta legem Mosi. Secundus status erat, proselytorum, id est, advenarum, qui non erant nati ex semine Abrahae, sed tamen volebant esse pars huius populi, et volebant circumcidi. Hi quia volebant circumcidi, debebant etiam servare alias ceremonias, ut Urias.

Tertius status erat, qui in actis vocantur, viri religiosi, id est, Ethnici, ut Nahaman Syrus, Nabogdonosor, Cyrus, Cornelius et alii multi, qui discebant promissiones de venturo Messia, et doctrinam de vero Deo, et de bonis operibus, iuxta Decalogum. Et tamen nec circumcisi erant, nec servabant ceremonias Mosaicas.

Has differentias merentote, et hic considerate discrimen Legis et Evangelii. Nullus status, neque semen Abrahae, neque proselyti, nec viri religiosi merebantur remissionem peccatorum lege, nec lege erant iusti, sed tantum credentes iuxta promissionem de Messia, accipiebant remissionem, et fide erant iusti, sicut nos.

Nec necesse fuit Ethnicos circumcidi. Hoc igitur taxat Christus, quod Pharisaei multos errores docebant, persuadebant Ethnicis, quod lege mererentur remissionem peccatorum, et fierent iusti lege, et ita faciebant eis opinionem, quod necesse esset circumcidi, et quod essent lege iusti, et delebant doctrinam de promissione et de iustitia fidei.

Sicut nostro tempore Monachi discurrebant, et invitabant homines ad Monachatum falsis et impiis opinionibus, quod Monachatus esset novus Baptismus, mereretur remissionem peccatorum, esset iustitia et status perfectionis. Ex hoc exemplo intelligi et hoc membrum in textu potest.

## 23:16 Sermons on Matthew
Woe to you who swear by the temple.

Let the true doctrine concerning an oath be explained in order. What an oath is, that it is an invocation of God, so that He may be a witness of the truth, and punish the liar. And God established this order, and so He does.

But the world sins in many ways in swearing.

1. In imprecations, because God is invoked so that He may harm others, contrary to the second commandment. 2. In swearing by other things and not by God, because other things cannot be witnesses, as the dead or stones are ignorant of our actions. 3. In swearing about objects, that is, illicit things, such as celibacy. 4. In deceiving, whether sophistically or openly, and not fulfilling promises made by an oath. Just as he deceived who promised a thirty-day truce, and at night ravaged the fields, because the truce was promised for the days, not the nights.

All these kinds of sins violate the second commandment of the Decalogue, and are great sins, which God punishes in this life, and if men do not repent, He punishes them with eternal punishments after this life.

But just as Christ here censures the traditions of the Pharisees, which cunningly eluded oaths: so now the Papists have similar evasions.

When someone becomes a Bishop in title only, he swears that he wishes to travel to that place, he departs from the city of Rome, and protests about the impossibility, then he asks for absolution, and obtains it.

Many such things happen in the many affairs of Bishops, and no one has played with oaths as the Bishops have.

Latin:

Vae qui iurat per templum.

Exponatur ordine vera doctrina de iuramento. Quid sit iuramentum, quod sit invocatio Dei, ut sit testis veritatis, et puniat mentientem. Et Deus hunc ordinem sanxit, et ita facit.

Sed mundus peccat multipliciter in iurando.

1. In execrationibus, quia invocatur Deus, ut aliis noceat, contra secundum mandatum. 2. In iurando per alias res et non per Deum, quia aliae res non possunt esse testes, ut mortui vel lapides ignorant nostras actiones. 3. In iurando de obiectis, id est, rebus illicitis, ut de coelibatu. 4. In fallendo sive sophistice sive aperte, et non faciendo promissa per iuramentum. Sicut fefellit ille, qui promisit triginta dierum inducias, et noctu populatus est agros, quia dierum induciae promissae erant, non noctium.

Omnia haec genera peccatorum violant secundum praeceptum Decalogi, et sunt magna peccata, quae Deus in hac vita punit, et si non agant homines poenitentiam, punit aeternis poenis post hanc vitam.

Ut autem Christus hic taxat Pharisaeorum traditiones, quae astutae eludebant iuramenta: sic nunc nabent Papistae similes elusiones.

Quando aliquis fit Episcopus titulo tenus, iurat, se velle ad illum locum proficisci, egreditur ex urbe Roma, et protestatur de impossibilitate, deinde petit absolutionem, et impetrat.

Talia multa fiunt in multis negotiis Episcoporum, et nulli sic luserunt iuramentis sicut Episcopi.

## 23:23 Sermons on Matthew
Woe to you Scribes and Pharisees, who tithe mint etc.

This sin also always remains in the world, because men slide down into ceremonies, they contend greatly about these, and omit other greater and simply necessary things. As before this time, it was considered a much greater sin to eat meat on Friday than to commit adultery. And Priests polluted with wandering lusts were much more grieved by the omission of some word in the Canon than because of their own lusts. And now many quarrel about small things, and say not a word about the greatest idolatry of the carrying about of the bread.

Monks and Summists have written many things about sins against human traditions, about the violation of fasting, and similar trifles. Meanwhile, they were blind in other greater matters. They said nothing about faith receiving the remission of sins. They said nothing about the manifold idolatry in the worship of saints, and other idolatries.

Christ therefore condemns the neglect of the foundation. And here it is very useful to learn the degrees of the commandments. Let this distinction therefore be: There is a different doctrine concerning some ceremonies beyond the foundation.

Rules.

The doctrine of the foundation is the doctrine of all the articles of faith, and the doctrine of the Decalogue. Concerning this, Paul says: No other foundation can be laid, besides that which is laid, etc. This doctrine of the foundation must be known by all, and obeyed. If any adult errs in one article of faith, or if he violates the Decalogue against his conscience, he is guilty of eternal death. According to these words: Those who do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God. Gal. 5.: Therefore let us be attentive, and let us rightly learn the doctrine of the foundation, and the necessary doctrine of the Decalogue, and in these let us keep our consciences unharmed. For invocation of God is not rightly done when someone errs in an article of faith, or when he persists in sins against conscience.

Another Rule.

The doctrine concerning ceremonies is twofold.

Some ceremonies are instituted by God, such as Baptism and the Lord's Supper. The use of these things is also necessary, but sometimes in a case of necessity it admits of a dispensation. Others are ceremonies instituted by human authority. The rank of these is to be placed far below divine ceremonies. Indeed, ceremonies instituted by human authority can be omitted entirely without any sin. And sometimes it is a sin to observe them, as when they conflict with the law of God, or when superstition is added: as those sin who observe the law of celibacy or monastic vows, etc.

It is necessary that this distinction be most well-known to all men, and from this the exposition of Christ's saying is to be taken.

"You tithe mint, etc. And you omit the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith." When He names faith, He understands all the articles of faith, and the whole interior worship, and confession according to the first and second commandment.

Afterwards, when He names judgment, He understands all necessary works; He wants all sins against any commandments whatsoever to be reproved, and He wants necessary works to be done, and idolatries, adulteries, thefts, and lies to be avoided. When He names mercy, He commands the works of the second Table, by which one's neighbor is helped, such as alms, the defense of those unjustly oppressed, etc. Thus it is clear that Christ here in these three members embraces the foundation, that is, the articles of faith and the Decalogue.

And of these He says: "These you ought to have done." Let us know that the foundation is so necessary that a man who errs or acts against the foundation is guilty of eternal death. John 3: "The wrath of God remains upon him." But why does He say: "And not to omit the others"? I answer: Christ is speaking of ceremonies which God had instituted, because giving tithes was a command of God for the sustenance of the Levites.

I said, however, that ceremonies handed down by God must be distinguished from those instituted by men. Human ones can be omitted entirely.

Blind guides, straining out a gnat, and swallowing a camel. He depicts hypocrites with this figure, who neglect great things and are anxious about small or worthless matters, as I said before concerning the priests, who made more of the omission of one word in the Canon than of adultery.

And this saying of Christ is well to be considered, because in the whole of life there is great wisdom in discerning necessary and unnecessary things, principal and non-principal things. In courts, the principal thing should have been to exercise judgments diligently and to prohibit injuries.

Princes care less for these than for the equipment of some spectacle. Thus, for the most part, men do secondary things and neglect the necessary and principal ones.

Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who cleanse the outside of the cup. Just as He rebuked superstition above, which neglects the order of good works, omits the greatest things, and harshly demands the lighter ones: so here He also rebukes a similar superstition, which neglects necessary and interior things commanded by God, and curiously observes external rites that are not necessary, which are only human traditions.

Universally, such are hypocrites; they observe some external rites for the sake of appearance and title, but neglect other necessary works, just as Canons and the like abstain from meat on the sixth day, while meanwhile they are adulterers, Epicureans, and full of all crimes. As He says here, they wash the cups on the outside, while meanwhile they themselves are full of rapine and incontinence within. He names two manifest vices, which we see most in Bishops and Canons.

Those goods which Bishops and Canons now possess were given in the beginning for the ministry, for studies, and for hospitals. Now Bishops seize them, and shamefully squander them, and nothing is enough for them, and furthermore they plunder the people. And one Canon usually has three, four, or more Prebends, and these have been snatched away from the offices of Pastors, just as I know very many places where the revenues established for Pastors have been transferred to Canonries.

And the Pope himself is a most shameful thief and robber; he has seized many cities in Italy. Likewise, he has seized money from German, Gallic, and Hispanic Bishoprics.

Likewise, the entire gain from Masses is rapine. Nor is there need for a long declaration about the other, manifest and incontinence, adultery, and many turpitudes. And where these manifest vices are, there the heart within has many other vices, contempt of God, and Epicurean blasphemies, and other sins.

But the law of God commands that hearts within should be upright toward God, just as the first commandment says: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart. So here it says: Cleanse that which is within. You are like whitewashed sepulchers. This similitude says the same thing: That hypocrites show a modest appearance outwardly, and inwardly they are full of deception and disobedience of every kind. Here he used a general name, disobedience, ἀνομίαν, which signifies contempt of the whole law. He added another name, hypocrisy, which is deception, increasing other sins, because it boasts of righteousness and of the name of God, and abuses the name of God for the sake of gain or power, so that robbers in the woods, who snatch money from men by force, sin less than the Pope or Monks who sell Masses, and under the pretext of the divine name snatch money and power.

You are the sons of those who killed the Prophets. And you fill up the measure of your fathers etc. It is a double accusation, that they even now kill the Prophets and Teachers sent by God, and that many hypocrites in all times always persecute the Church.

And he shows how great the magnitude of this sin is. Since the will is similar in all persecutors, and all are incited by the Devil, and they want the same thing, that is, that God be blasphemed: likewise, that the Son of God be blasphemed, and that the truth be oppressed, and by their individual examples they confirm others. Individuals are guilty of many persecutions, therefore all will be horribly punished.

Therefore he says here: All the just blood comes upon you, shed from Abel even to Zacharias. Let us always consider this most sad threat, and let us seek the truth, so that we may not be associates of persecutors, and let us avoid the counsels of those who persecute the truth, just as Jonathan did not want to be an assistant of the persecution against David.

Here the history of Zacharias is recited, and Basil narrates that there was a report handed down from the elders, that Zacharias, the father of John the Baptist, when he testified about the adolescent born of the Virgin Mary, that he was the Messiah, was killed by the Priests. And because this history was recent, therefore Christ, embracing all times, first names Abel, then this one, the nearest, Zacharias. I am content with this history, nor do I wish to seek another interpretation, but let us consider what a great evil it is to be a member of that assembly which persecutes the Church, which accumulates blasphemies, idolatry, homicides in the world, and is ruled by the Devil, who is a liar and a murderer.
