Ubi autem mansura sit Ecclesia, simul indicat cum nominat verbum. Spiritus qui in te est, et verbum in ore tuo. Ibi est Ecclesia, ubi sonat Evangelium, sicut Christus inquit: Si manseritis in me, et verba mea manserint in vobis, quicquid volueritis, petetis, et fiet vobis. Item: Oves meae vocem meam audiunt.

Hac confirmatione tunc maxime opus est, cum dicitur: Ecce hic est Christus, ecce illic. Et removendae sunt imaginationes, quae alligant Ecclesiam ad pontificum et regum dominationem. Nam Ecclesia ad Evangelium alligata est, et in Evangelio gestari eam tanquam foetum in alvo cogitemus, nec gestari eam in imperiis externis, aut dominatione Episcoporum existimemus. Est enim coetus dissimilis aliis politiis.

Magna autem consolatio est, quod testatur Christus mansuram esse Ecclesiam, quicquid sit futurum de regnis mundi, sicut manebat Ecclesia tempore Apostolorum, etiamsi reges et principes patronos non habebat. Interim tamen Deus aliqua hospitia exulanti Ecclesiae curavit.

De tertio.

Usitata phrasis est Ebraeis, idola vocare abominationes. Et recitat Christus locum ex Daniele, ut afferat testimonium suae praedictioni de excidio Hierosolymorum, quasi dicat: Multum vos vestra opinio fallit, si arbitramini me et vos in hoc templo regnaturos esse. An non meministis Danielem, qui praedicit excidium, et addit signum, scilicet fore, ut stet in loco sancto, id est, in templo, idolum denuntians perpetuam vastitatem, id cum videbitis, fugite, significat enim excidium.

Quod autem erat hoc idolum? Etsi omnes cultus hostium Christi sunt idola, tamen hic de re insigni loquitur, quia vult commonefieri Apostolos de excidio. Fuit ergo praecipuum idolum manifestae blasphemiae adversus Christum, deinde accesserunt statuae, ut vexilla Tiberii, statuae Caligulae, qui se mandarat adorari, et multae caedes in templo factae, quibus tunc assidue prophanabatur templum. Haec, inquit, cum fient, scitote instare finem.

Ut autem tunc in templo Iudaico fuit idolum, ita praedicitur futurum, ut post Apostolos ultimo mundi tempore in Ecclesiis colatur idolum. Quod est illud? Non potest haec res sine ingenti dolore cogitari. Delevit Ecclesias Mahometus, et proposuit colendum idolum, videlicet manifestas blasphemias adversus Christum. Hae sunt praecipuus nervus regni ipsius et cultus, imo huius ipsius articuli professione iudicant se esse populum Dei, quod negant Filium Dei, quod negant redemtorem, quod abolent Evangelium, propter hoc opus praedicant se diligi a Deo, et ornari victoriis et imperiis. Sed pii sciant, hoc ipsum opus Mahometicae sectae praecipue damnatum esse voce Dei, sicut clare inquit Daniel de Mahometo alibi: Dicet blasphemias contra Dominum. Ergo haec capita non errant.

Haec ratio num. Sed non de solo Mahometo hic dicitur. Ait enim: Stabit in loco sancto, id est, in eo coetu, in quo adhuc manet nomen Christi et Ecclesiae, et in quo sunt aliqui recte invocantes Deum. Ibi quoque erunt idola vastantia verum cultum. Dixi autem cultus omnes sine agnitione Christi idololatriam esse, quare hi, qui non norunt doctrinam Evangelii, de fide in Christum, et de invocatione in hac fide facienda, omnes sunt ignari veri cultus, et qui veram doctrinam persequuntur, sunt idololatrae. Sed semper homines amisso Evangelio sibi ipsi nova et manifesta idola excogitant, ergo accedunt etiam externa idola, ut statuae, ad quas concurritur, ipsa invocatio mortuorum, prophanatio coenae Domini, in qua fit falsa oblatio et falsa adoratio. hometo alibi: Dicet blasphemias contra Domino. Sed non de solo Mahometo hic dicitur. Ait enim: Stabit in loco sancto, id est, in eo coetu, in quo adhuc manet nomen Christi et Ecclesiae, et in quo sunt aliqui recte invocantes Deum. Ibi quoque erunt idola vastantia verum cultum. Dixi autem cultus omnes sine agnitione Christi idololatriam esse, quare hi, qui non norunt doctrinam Evangelii, de fide in Christum, et de invocatione in hac fide facienda, omnes sunt ignari veri cultus, et qui veram doctrinam persequuntur, sunt idololatrae. Sed semper homines amisso Evangelio sibiipsi nova et manifesta idola excogitant, ergo accedunt etiam externa idola, ut statuae, ad quas concurritur, ipsa invocatio mortuorum, prophanatio coenae Domini, in qua fit falsa oblatio et falsa adoratio.

Item, fiducia humanarum traditionum, ut Monachatus. Haec quatuor nihil differunt ab ethnicis idolatriis, nec ulla humana vox dicere potest, quam tetra sint haec idola, et quantam iram Dei provocent, sed poenae utcunque significant. Nequaquam essent tanti successus Turcorum, nisi magna esset idolomania in Ecclesia, et quia haec non satis dici possunt, vero timore Dei cogitemus apud nos vocem Spiritus sancti: Fugite idololatriam, et discamus veros cultus, et fugiamus defensionem idolorum, ne cum impiis pereamus.

De quarto. An Ecclesia possit errare?

Proprie ad tempora post Apostolos pertinet descriptio quae hic additur. Dicent vobis: Ecce hic est Christus, ecce illic est, id est, magna erunt dissidia dogmatum, Ecclesia lacerabitur, et quaelibet pars gloriabitur se habere Christum. Quid tali tempore faciendum erit? quis poterit iudicare, quae pars sit populus Dei? nam errare aliquas partes necesse est. Hic mundus sequitur politicum argumentum. Ut ibi iudicamus esse rempub. ubi sunt principes et magistratus ordinarii, caeteros iudicamus esse seditiosos: ita cum sunt dissidia Ecclesiae, accurrunt plurimi ad hos, qui titulum habent ordinariae potestatis, et his attribuunt praerogativam, quod non possint errare, quia dicunt, Ecclesiae factam esse promissionem.

Ecclesia autem non est truncatum corpus, sine capite, sine ministerio. Ergo haec capita non errant. Haec ratio plausibilis est, et plurimes in toto orbe ita tenet fascinatos, ut contradici non sinant.

Sed nos sciamus Ecclesiam dissimilem esse caeteris politiis, nec tamen loquendum esse de invisibili Ecclesia. Deus ideo condidit genus humanum, ideo redemit, ut ipse invocetur et celebretur, et Christus innotescat: necesse est igitur conspici Ecclesiam, necesse est confessionem et invocationem notam fieri. Quanquam autem Ecclesia est visibilis coetus, tamen dispersa est, nee est politia similis regno, alligata loco, successioni, et certis legibus humanis. Sed alligata est purae doctrinae Evangelii. Haec consociat Ecclesiam ubicunque est, iuxta illud: Oves meae vocem meam audiunt.

Sopho. 3.: Reliqui mihi populum pauperem et egenum, et sperabunt in nomine Domini. Talis semper est aliqua vera Ecclesia, ut sub Achab, Eliae tempore, erant Elias, Elisaeus, et alii multi, sicut dicit textus: Reliqui mihi septem millia etc. Sic sub Hanna et Caipha erant, Simeon, Zacharias, Elisabeth, Maria, Ioseph, et alii multi, etiamsi reges et pontifices erant palam idololatrae et Epicurei.

Est autem ille coetus verae Ecclesiae Dei, qui amplectitur verbum Dei, per Prophetas, Christum et Apostolos traditum, et non defendit pertinaciter idola, et errores pugnantes cum verbo Dei. Suntque in hoc coetu partim renati, vero timore Dei, et vera fide Deum invocantes, partim mali, et sine vero timore Dei, sed tamen in professione doctrinae consentientes, qui si admittant publica delicta, eiciendi sunt, et puniendi.

Hic coetus de cultu Dei consulit, et sequitur purum Evangelium, non opiniones traditas autoritate humana. Sicut Simeon, Zacharias, Maria sequebantur doctrinam Prophetarum relictis deliriis Sadducaeorum et Pharisaeorum.

De eo coetu, amplectente purum Evangelium, recte dicitur, Ecclesiam non errare in articulis fidei, seu in necessariis ad salutem, sed interim fieri potest, ut ingens multitudo omnium ordinum, Episcoporum, Sacerdotum, Monachorum, Regum, Principum et populi sit contaminata idolis, et multis erroribus perniciosiis, qui pugnant cum articulis fidei, sicut Pharisaei et Sadducaei defendebant errores pugnantes cum articulis fidei, quia haec multitudo errans anteponit

Evangelio opiniones traditas humana autoritate, et quia potentia et numero antecellit, pertinaciter defendit errores.

Sciamus autem nos a Christo propter gravissimam causam praemonitos esse, ne errores approbemus, et severe mandatum est: Fugite idololatriam. Cum igitur disputamus, an Ecclesia possit errare, primum quaeramus, ubi et quae sit Ecclesia, nec alligemus eam ad imperia, multitudinem, Episcopos. Fieri enim potest, ut plurimi eorum non sint membra Ecclesiae, sicut nunc magna pars eorum palam est Epicurea, nec curat, quid in alterutram partem doceatur, tantum in hoc sunt attenti, ne quid mutetur, ne labefiat eorum potentia. Sed quaeramus Ecclesiam ibi, ubicunque sonat pura vox Evangelii.

Porro et in hoc coetu pio et amplectente Evangelium, tamen alias plus, alias minus est lucis, et aliquid contagii manet, ut multi discipuli Apostolorum imaginabantur ceremonias Mosaicas retinendas esse. Et Paulus inquit, Hunc coetum partim aurum, partim stipulas supra fundamentum extruere. Sed tamen fundamentum retinet articulos fidei de Christo, et veram invocationem, et non defendit errores pertinaciter, sed audit Evangelium, cupit doceri et proficit.

Haec admonitio de Ecclesia utilis est, et hortetur nos, ut iudicio et voluntate coniungamus nos cum Ecclesia, et cum ea Deum recte invocemus, et retineamus Evangelii puritatem, nec anteferamus opiniones humana autoritate confictas, sed meminerimus illud: Lucerna pedibus meis verbum tuum.

De quinto.

Consolatio et doctrina traditur, quomodo praemuniendi sint animi in his periculis. Consolationes hae quatuor sunt praecipue.

I. Quod sit mansura Ecclesia vera, etiam in hoc mundo, ante resurrectionem mortuorum, iuxta illud Esaiae 56.: Spiritus meus, qui est in te, et verba mea, quae sunt in ore tuo, non recedent ab ore tuo, nec ab ore seminis tui etc.

II. Quod ubicunque erunt amplectentes purum Evangelium, hi sunt membra Ecclesiae, iuxta illud: Si manseritis in me, et verba mea manserint in vobis, quicquid volueritis, petite, et fiet vobis.

III. Quod in his periculis Filius Dei aderit propugnator, sicut Daniel inquit: Stat Michaël dux pro populo Dei.

IIII. Quod Christus rursus se ostensurus sit mundo, et glorificaturus Ecclesiam, ac impios abiecturus in aeternos cruciatus. Ideo hic dicitur: Sic erit adventus Filii hominis. Nec diu duraturum esse hunc mundum post Apostolos ipsi testati sunt, cum vocant novissimam horam. Et notum est dictum Eliae: Sex millia mundus, et postea erit destructio, Duo millia inane, Duo millia lex, Duo millia Messias, et si quid deerit, deerit propter peccata nostra.

Doctrina vero est, quod monet, ut Evangelium retineamus, nec assentiamur impostoribus. Item, iubet precari, ac significat Deum calamitates mitigaturum esse precantibus. Orate, ut possitis evadere ex futuris malis, et stare coram filio hominis.

ENARRATIONES EVANGELIORUM, QUAE LEGUNTUR DE FESTIS CHRISTI, ET HISTORIIS SANCTORUM.

## 25:1 Sermons on Matthew: Argument
Chapter XXV.

The kingdom of heaven is like unto ten Virgins, etc.

The similitude of the Virgins is an image of the Church at any time, but especially in the last time, and it contains doctrine, rebuke, and consolation.

This is the doctrine: always in the Church in this life, there are, have been, and will be good and evil, wise and foolish Virgins. And they are called Virgins, even the hypocrites, because in appearance and title they are similar to those who truly call upon [God]. And it is necessary to remember this doctrine, so that because of the multitude of the wicked in the Church, we do not think that the whole human race is rejected by God, and that there is no Church, just as the saints are often vexed by this sorrow, looking around at such a great multitude of the wicked and those who think wrongly everywhere.

Against this temptation, the Lord often fortifies us, as in the parable of the sower. Likewise, Paul says in Romans 3: "Did their unbelief nullify the faithfulness of God?" as if to say: Even if many fail, yet God remains truthful, and preserves some Church, and gives to the Church good promises, the remission of sins, the Holy Spirit, eternal life, and other good things. And in the Creed, when we recite the article: "I believe in the holy catholic Church." Let us be consoled by this thought: Behold, God commands that we believe that the Church is always preserved, and that the good promises are given to it. We are, therefore, also members of the Church, and we ask for and receive these good things.

Second topic. Concerning rebuke.

But here He predicts that there will be many foolish Virgins. How do wise virgins differ from foolish ones? Both are called Virgins. The title is the same, and the appearance of the hypocrites and those who call upon [God] rightly is the same.

But they differ much in reality itself. What are wise Virgins? We wish to define it briefly and clearly. Wise Virgins are those who retain the foundation, and in true repentance and true faith call upon God.

Now, the foundation signifies the doctrine necessary in all articles of faith, among which it is also necessary to include the true understanding of the righteousness of faith. And such people avoid idolatry, even if they have some sins of ignorance, as before these times Saint Bernard and other true believers did, yet they mixed in some errors concerning Monasticism and the invocation of the dead, but they did not approve of such gross abuses as others did. Let us give thanks to God that we have been liberated from many errors. And these wise Virgins not only retain the foundation, but also resist security; they are in the exercises of true repentance, they have consolation through true faith and true invocation, and in true faith and hope they always await the Lord. Therefore, the lamp is in the vessel, that faith in Christ shining according to true doctrine in true repentance and invocation. But the foolish Virgins are those who either do not retain the foundation, or retain the foundation hypocritically without repentance and without faith in Christ.

Those not retaining the foundation, like many who are gravely erring and seduced, Heretics, Idolaters, Papists, Monks, who are ignorant of the righteousness of faith, who trust that they are righteous by their own righteousness: likewise, those who invoke the dead, run to statues, etc. Others retain the foundation as far as the knowledge of doctrine is concerned, but they are hypocrites, they are without repentance, without true faith in Christ, without true invocation, they are secure, they despise judgment, or they trust in their profession, thinking they please God because they do not wish to be called Papists, even if they are adulterers, fornicators, and without repentance, without true faith in Christ, and without true invocation, just as the hypocrites among the Jews thought they pleased God, merely because of the title, because they were called Jews, and they were adulterers and usurers, and without any repentance, without the fear of God.

And neither have oil or a lamp, that is, true faith in Christ shining according to true doctrine in repentance and invocation. Therefore, the Lord rebukes both, and warns us that we should take care that we be wise virgins, and not foolish, just as the Lord often cries out: "Watch, pray, that you do not perish." Let us know, therefore, that this carnal security, which is without a lamp, that is, without true faith, displeases God, and let us rouse ourselves to repentance, to faith, and to true invocation, and in true faith and hope let us await the bridegroom.

But see what the foolish Virgins do? Foolish Virgins ask for oil from the wise, that is, they wish to be saved by the righteousness of other men, not by their own faith. This imagination is vain, because it is written: The just shall live by his faith. His, that is, his own, he says. You yourself must be converted to God and believe, because the oath remains valid in all eternity: I live, says the Lord, I do not desire the death of the sinner, but that he be converted and live. He swears that conversion must take place, and that to the converted he will give the remission of sins. Here you see the errors of those who wanted to be saved by the Masses of Priests, likewise, by the good works of Monks. All such things are idolatrous. Likewise, they err similarly who run to the Saints and want the merits of the Saints to be applied to themselves. Against this error, this similitude of the foolish Virgins must also be applied, and Hilary applied it thus.

But hear the history concerning this matter. Three hundred years ago there was Frederick, Landgrave of Thuringia, from whom these Dukes of Saxony, who still live, are descended: he was an honest and magnanimous man, and he waged great wars, and was fortunate. When, however, he was already an old man, in Eisenach a play was performed before him, in which this reading of the Gospel concerning the foolish Virgins was applied against the invocation of Saints. For there was some learned man who, by this spectacle, wished to censure the invocation of the dead. After that spectacle, the Prince, recognizing the error concerning the invocation of the dead, and complaining much about this great abuse, began to fall ill from grief over the public error, and afterwards died in the true invocation of the Son of God. Also, Emperor Charles V ordered the Monks to be removed from his dying wife, and ordered his son's tutor to propose to his wife the consolations concerning Christ.

Third point. Concerning consolation.

Consolation is that he calls himself the bridegroom. And thus he testifies that there is a great and ardent love with which he embraces the Church, nay, that he, as a bridegroom, never wishes to desert us. And this is also a great consolation, that he predicts that there will always be some true Church and wise Virgins, who with true faith and hope await him. Let us consider all these things in this beautiful similitude, about which much more could be said, but no one can fully exhaust the wisdom of God. Let us take care that we perform penance, and progress, so that we may be prepared, that we may have oil in our vessels etc., that is, in our hearts, etc.

Another similitude. As a man going abroad called his servants and gave them his substance. This parable of the talents distinguishes the faithful and diligent from the unfaithful and negligent or secure. And it is to be understood in both ways, concerning public ministry, and privately concerning the use of gifts.

But again it must be known that here both doctrine and rebuke, and consolation are proposed, just as in the previous parable. This is the first doctrine: That there always are and will be in the Church some faithful and diligent, and some unfaithful and negligent, just as we said recently, that there have always been, are, and will be in this life such in the Church who are like the foolish Virgins, and others like the wise Virgins. And this must be known, so that we do not fall away from God because of this scandal, when we see a great multitude of the impious.

Another doctrine is near the end: To him who has, it shall be given, and from him who has not, even what he has shall be taken away. Here the Lord clearly teaches us that he wants us to exercise his gifts, and not to be negligent once the gifts are received. He says gifts are increased for those who labor to use them. Just as he increases gifts for Joseph or Daniel, because they labor in learning, teaching, and praying, and they govern their morals with temperance, chastity, and sobriety, and other necessary exercises. For it must in no way be thought that God wishes to increase gifts to those who willingly squander them.

Thus he speaks the doctrine concerning the negligent: Because you have rejected knowledge, I will reject you, that you may not serve me as a Priest. Hosea 4. Item: He who stands, let him see that he does not fall, 1 Cor. 10. Item: The Devil finds the house empty etc., Matt. 12. These and similar sayings command that we should not be negligent, but use the gifts, as Paul says in 2 Corinthians 6: See that you have not received the grace in vain.

And a man already gifted with the Holy Spirit can and ought to ask more and more to be helped by the Holy Spirit, as Christ says in Matthew 7: Ask, and you shall receive. How much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him, Luke 11. And thus, asking for the Holy Spirit, one can resist evil temptations, one can retain the gifts of God, as Paul says: I bring my body into subjection, 1 Corinthians 9.

By no means was it necessary for David to seize another man's wife, but he could have, at that time when he possessed the Holy Spirit, resisted the temptation of adultery.

Thus also in this place it is said: To him who has, it shall be given.

If David were to use the gifts, the gifts would grow in him. And conversely: From him who does not have, that which he has shall be taken away.

David, not using the gifts, falls, and loses even the many present gifts; after the seizure of another's wife, he loses good counsel, he orders the man to be killed, because the door was already open to the Devil, and he is driven from one crime into another. Afterwards, he loses divine protection; God allows him to be cast out of the kingdom, and allows many most sorrowful punishments to occur.

In this example it is discerned what it means: From him who does not have, that which he has shall be taken away.

Take another example. Saul is adorned with a kingdom and the Holy Spirit, with glorious victories. Afterwards, he begins to become a tyrant and proud. There he loses even what he had: the kingdom, the Holy Spirit, life, glory.

These most sorrowful examples show how men fall after they have been adorned with the gifts of God and did not wish to add care to using them.

And the excuse of those who say that they cannot abstain from sins against conscience is utterly false and diabolical.

Indeed, the text most clearly says in 1 John 3: He who is born of God does not commit sin, because the seed of God is in him.

God gave you the Holy Spirit so that you might be able to resist evil temptations: and God commands that you use such a great gift of His. Indeed, it is an insult against God to think that He gave you the Holy Spirit so that you might live only negligently and loosen the rein on evil desires.

Concerning rebuke.

The rebuke in these sayings is that the negligent one, who did not wish to use the talent, is punished and loses even that which he has.

Such are the rebukes often repeated in Scripture. As Peter says in 2 Peter 2: That these negligent ones are like those who return to their vomit.

But someone might say: Who is sufficiently diligent?

All are weak, and sometimes they fall. I answer: Here the common doctrine must be held, which we often repeat: In all saints there are weaknesses and sins and falls, as it is written: There is no just man on earth who, when he does good, does not also sin.

But nevertheless, in each individual there ought to be a purpose of doing good, and we must avoid, and we can avoid, falls against conscience. And if anyone has fallen, he ought to return immediately to repentance, just as David returned, just as Aaron returned.

Cain Saul Judas } did not return to repentance.

Consolation.

Consolation is that some remain in the Church who use the gifts well. And to these, greater gifts are later bestowed, as you have notable examples.

Joseph rightly used the gift, he did not wish to become an adulterer, and he patiently bore the prison; therefore God exalted him and made him a chief and salutary Prince in Egypt. Another beautiful example: The poor widow in Zarephath used the gift. She fed Elijah, and gave him food before herself; therefore God blessed her house.

For it was a hospice for the Church, it was not destroyed by famine, the son was raised from the dead.

And it is most certain that small good works are often adorned with the greatest public and private rewards, so that we are compelled to say, as Jacob says in Genesis 32: I am less than all your mercies.

And conversely, when men do not wish to perform repentance, then afterwards horrible punishments follow. God waits sometimes, and grants a space for repentance. But when repentance is not begun, and greater obstinacy occurs, then the final punishments come, the devastations of nations, and eternal punishments, as is said about the fig tree in the parable.

XII. ANNOTATIONS AND SERMONS ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW.

MATTHEW.

Luke 13: Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this tree, and find none, cut it down therefore.

This is that simple and true explanation of this parable; now see, each of you, that you may rouse yourselves to exercise the gifts of God, and fix these very words in your heart: To him who has, it shall be given, and from him who has not, even what he has shall be taken away; that is, from him who loses the Gospel and the Holy Spirit, many other gifts are taken away, counsel, and all good things, eternal and temporal. And in the use of gifts, the chief use is invocation and prayer, as it is written in Luke 11: Pray always.

And you see now the necessity in dangers because of the gathering, because of storms, because of wars, because of fires, and finally because of many calamities. God warns us in many ways, and yet we are negligent, but truly the time demands that we wake up, lest we perish, just as that fig tree, just as Sodom, just as Jerusalem, just as all Asia, Greece, and other regions perished under the Turks, indeed just as all regions in Germany and elsewhere perished, oppressed by the armies of the Emperor, where churches are disturbed, and many other evils happen.

Ah God, avert such calamities from us.

When the Son of Man shall come. Concerning the final judgment.

This is an express prediction concerning the final judgment, such as none is recorded in the Old Testament.

There are indeed many sayings that predict the resurrection of the dead, and say that the impious will be in punishments, and those who call upon God will have eternal salvation, as it is written in the last chapter of Isaiah, yet there is no prediction so express as this sermon of the Son of God, who wished to declare this article in clear words. Therefore, let these words of the Lord be most known to all, and be constantly pondered.

And this sermon needs no explanation; the words are clear in themselves, but let us bring faith and the fear of God, and let us constantly contemplate this judgment, let us fear the wrath, and let us console ourselves, because we know that the true Church is to be delivered from all evils in that judgment. This is the chief admonition necessary in this text.

But yet we shall add some other admonitions.

First admonition. Let all men diligently learn that this human life is ordered by God, and that men do not live like beasts, without the law of God, and without any order, and die like beasts, without any judgment after this life, but God created the human race in such a way that He added doctrine, how He wishes to make men saved, and without any doubt He punishes all who despise His doctrine.

And punishments are twofold. Corporal in this life, and others afterwards eternal after this life.

Second admonition. It is most certain that God in this life punishes with corporal punishments all who commit sins against their conscience, and when they are great, the punishments are also great.

Concerning such sins it is expressly said: He who takes the sword, shall perish by the sword. Here it is said that all murderers are without any doubt punished in turn by the sword, as examples show.

It is most certain that no murderer can escape punishments in this life. And men greatly err who think they can hide.

Just as you heard the recent example of the murderer of his brother in the valley of Joachim. The true voice remains: He who takes the sword, shall perish by the sword.

So the true voice remains: Honor your father and mother, that you may be long-lived upon the earth. It is most certain that those who treat their parents badly are punished in this life.

There was at Frankfurt a certain gunner, an industrious man, who was loved because of his art. When he wished to put gunpowder into a new cannon again, the powder ignited from the cannon suddenly erupts, and lifts the master of the cannon himself into the air, and ignites him, and afterwards kills him, afflicted, on the ground.

Most people who knew him said the cause was that he had treated his mother badly. I could recite more such stories.

Likewise, concerning the perjured, it is certain that they are punished in this life. Likewise, concerning fornicators and adulterers, the text says: God will judge fornicators and adulterers.

Hence there are so many diseases, such as the French disease and others. Likewise, sins committed in the seed are punished in the seed.

Therefore David, having snatched the wife of another, is afterwards punished thus: his sons are killed. The son stirs up sedition, and, what is horrible, he afterwards defiled his father's wives.

And it is manifest that punishments wander through the families of Princes and Kings, because they were adulterers, just as we see examples everywhere. Let all men learn this doctrine, that it is most certain that offenses against conscience are punished in this life, and greater offenses are punished with greater punishments. Although many neglect and mock this rule, yet know that it is most true, and this rule must often be recited to all men. And God declares it to the people with terrible examples, the gallows, and many punishments of murderers, and other modes of punishment. These things must be thought upon in all of life, and it must be known that such punishments do not happen without the counsel of God.

But here you should also know: What are the causes why God punishes in this life, since He wishes to punish afterwards? I answer: The causes of punishments are five.

The first is the justice of God: because God wishes justice to be seen and acknowledged in the human race even in this life. Therefore He horribly punishes manifest offenses, so that He may show Himself to be just, and to be angry at injustice.

The second cause is public peace: because God wishes the delinquents themselves to be restrained. If thieves were not hanged, they would not cease to steal, and there would be no peace.

The third cause is example: because God deters others with such punishments, and some are moved, even if not all are moved, Deut. 17 and 19.

The fourth cause is because God signifies by these corporal punishments that a future judgment most certainly remains, because these brief punishments in the impious are not equal to the sins of the impious who do not convert. But the sins of such are infinite, therefore the order of justice imposes eternal punishments upon them; these things must be well considered.

The sin in the godless who are not converted is so great that no temporal punishment is equal to it, but it is immeasurable, and therefore eternal and immeasurable punishment is due, not only temporal punishment, which comes to an end. May God protect us from such cruel misery.

The fifth cause is because God wishes these punishments to be signs drawing us back to repentance. When a thief is led to the gallows, let him know that he is not being damned for that reason, provided he performs repentance, on account of political peace, and at the same time, so that he may be an admonition drawing [others] back to repentance. It is useful to often recite and think upon these causes as well.

Third admonition.

Now where neither the doctrine of God nor corporal punishments bend men to repentance, punishments follow after this life, of which he speaks here.

And the text does not need any declaration, and they are horrendous punishments, the magnitude of which cannot be told in words. They are eternal fire, dread and pain greater than any pains of bodies, and the damned would wish to be reduced to nothing, if it could be done.

Fourth admonition.

But someone might ask: Who are to be saved? Who can say that he has satisfied these words? I was hungry, and you gave me food, etc.

I answer: Here it is necessary for you to know both, the doctrine of faith, and of good works. It is most certain that eternal life is given to believers on account of our Lord Jesus Christ, just as the text said: This is the will of the Father, that everyone who believes in the Son may have eternal life. We must know this consolation; this is the proper voice of the Gospel.

Thus he says here: Come, you blessed of my Father, etc. But they are blessed through the seed of Abraham, etc.

Then, however, it must be known that good works must also follow, and that these please God through faith on account of Christ, even if they are insufficient. But nevertheless, we must be such that we do not persevere in an evil purpose against conscience.

Conversely, the impious are without faith, and have an evil purpose; they do not feed the Church, but kill the Saints. They do not give drink to the Church, but try to torture it with every kind of cruelty, etc.

And both can easily be seen in confession and persecution. Believers confess the faith and do many good works. But the impious burn with hatreds and seek occasions for exercising cruelty. Thus both can be discerned.

The History of the Passion of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Latin:

Caput XXV.

Simile est regnum coelorum decem Virginibus, etc.

Similitudo de Virginibus imago est Ecclesiae quocunque tempore, sed maxime postremo tem- pore, et continet doctrinam, obiurgationem, et consolationem.

Doctrina haec est, semper in Ecclesia in hac vita, sunt, fuerunt et erunt boni et mali, Virgines prudentes et fatuae. Et nominantur Virgines etiam hypocritae, quia specie et titulo sunt similes vere invocantibus. Et hanc doctrinam oportet meminisse, ne propter multitudinem malorum in Ecclesia cogitemus, totum genus humanum abiectum esse a Deo, et nullam esse Ecclesiam, sicut sancti saepe hoc dolore vexantur, circumspicientes tam magnam multitudinem malorum et male sentientium ubique.

Contra hanc tentationem saepe munit nos Dominus, ut in parabola de seminante. Item Paulus dicit Rom. 3.: Num incredulitas eorum fidem Dei evacuavit? quasi dicat: Etiam si multi deficiunt, tamen Deus manet verax, et servat aliquam Ecclesiam, et dat Ecclesiae bona promissa, remissionem peccatorum, Spiritum sanctum, vitam aeternam, et alia bona. Et in Symbolo cum recitamus articulum: Credo Ecclesiam sanctam catholicam. Nos consolemur hac cogitatione: Ecce Deus praecipit, ut credamus semper servari Ecclesiam, et dari ei bona promissa. Sumus igitur et nos membra Ecclesiae, et petimus et accipimus haec bona.

Secundus locus. De obiurgatione.

Praedicit autem hic fore multas Virgines fatuas. Quid differunt virgines prudentes a fatuis? Utraeque dicuntur Virgines. Titulus idem est, et species eadem est hypocritarum et recte invocantium.

Sed multum differunt re ipsa. Quae sunt Virgines prudentes? Volumus breviter et clare definire. Virgines prudentes sunt, quae retinent fundamentum, et in vera poenitentia et vera fide Deum invocant.

Fundamentum autem significat doctrinam necessariam in omnibus articulis fidei, inter quos etiam necesse est complecti verum intellectum iustitiae fidei. Et tales vitant idololatriam, etiamsi aliqua peccata ignorantiae habent, ut ante haec tempora sanctus Bernhardus et alii vere credentes, tamen miscuerunt aliquos errores de Monachatu, et de invocatione mortuorum, sed tamen tam crassos abusus non probaverunt, ut alii. Nos Deo gratias agamus, quod a multis erroribus liberati sumus. Et hae prudentes Virgines non solum retinent fundamentum, sed etiam repugnant securitati, sunt in exercitiis verae poenitentiae, habent consolationem vera fide et veram invocationem, et in vera fide et spe semper exspectant Dominum. Est ergo lychnus in vase, illa fides in Christum lucens iuxta veram doctrinam in vera poenitentia et invocatione. Sed fatuae Virgines sunt, aut non retinentes fundamentum, aut retinentes fundamentum hypocritice sine poenitentia et sine fide in Christum.

Non retinentes fundamentum, ut multi graviter errantes et seducti, Haeretici, Idololatrae, Papistae, Monachi, qui ignorant iustitiam fidei, qui confidunt se esse iustos sua iustitia: item, qui invocant mortuos, currunt ad statuas etc. Alii retinent fundamentum, quo ad cognitionem doctrinae, sed sunt hypocritae, sunt sine poenitentia, sine vera fide in Christum, sine vera invocatione, sunt securi, contemnunt iudicium, aut confidunt professione, cogitant se placere Deo, quia non velint nominari Papistae, etiamsi sunt adulteri, scortatores, et sine poenitentia, sine vera fide in Christum, et sine vera invocatione, sicut hypocritae inter Iudaeos putabant se placere Deo, tantum propter titulum, quia dicerentur Iudaei, et erant adulteri et foeneratores, et sine ulla poenitentia, sine timore Dei.

Ac neutri habent oleum aut lychnum, id est, veram fidem in Christum lucentem iuxta veram doctrinam in poenitentia et invocatione. Taxat igitur utrosque Dominus, et praemonet nos, ut curemus, ut simus virgines prudentes, et non fatuae, sicut saepe clamat Dominus: Vigilate, orate, ut non pereatis. Sciamus igitur hanc securitatem carnalem, quae est sine lychno, id est, sine vera fide displicere Deo, et exsusciemus nos ad poenitentiam, ad fidem, et veram invocationem, et in vera fide et spe exspectemus sponsum.

Sed videte quid faciant stultae Virgines? Fatuae Virgines petunt oleum a sapientibus, id est, volunt salvari aliorum hominum iustitia, non propria fide. Haec imaginatio inanis est, quia scriptum est: Iustus fide sua vivet. Sua, id est, propria inquit. Teipsum oportet converti ad Deum et credere, quia iuramentum manet ratum in omni aeternitate: Vivo ego, dicit Dominus, nolo mortem peccatoris, sed ut convertatur, et vivat. Iurat oportere fieri conversionem, et conversis se daturum esse remissionem peccatorum. Hic videtis errores illorum, qui voluerunt salvari per Missas Sacerdotum, item, per bona opera Monachorum. Talia omnia sunt idololatrica. Item errant similiter, qui currunt ad Sanctos, et volunt sibi applicari merita Sanctorum. Contra hunc errorem etiam accommodanda est haec similitudo de fatuis Virginibus, et sic accommodavit Hilarius.

Audite autem historiam de hac re. Ante annos trecentos fuit Landgravius Turingiae Fridericus, a quo orti sunt hi Duces Saxoniae, qui adhuc vivunt: ille fuit vir honestus et magnanimus, et magna bella gessit, et fuit fortunatus. Cum autem iam esset senex, in Isenach coram eo exhibita est comoedia, in qua haec lectio Evangelii de fatuis Virginibus accommodata est contra invocationem Sanctorum. Quia fuit doctus aliquis, qui hoc spectaculo voluit taxare invocationem mortuorum. Post spectaculum illud Princeps agnoscens errorem de invocatione mortuorum, et multa de hoc tanto abusu conquerens, coepit aegrotare ex dolore de publico errore, et postea in vera invocatione filii Dei est mortuus. Etiam Imperator Carolus V. iussit amoveri Monachos a coniuge moritura, et iussit praeceptorem filii sui proponere coniugi consolationes de Christo.

Tertius locus. De consolatione.

Consolatio est, quod se nominat sponsum. Et sic testatur magnam et ardentem dilectionem esse, qua Ecclesiam complectitur, imo se, ut sponsum, nunquam velle nos deserere. Est et haec magna consolatio, quod praedicit, semper fore aliquam veram Ecclesiam et Virgines prudentes, quae vera fide et spe ipsum expectant. Haec omnia consideremus in hac pulcra similitudine, de quam multo plura dicenda essent, sed nemo potest sapientiam Dei penitus exhaurire. Curemus, ut agamus poenitentiam, et proficiamus, ut simus parati, habeamus oleum in nostris vasis etc., id est, in nostris cordibus, etc.

Alia similitudo. Sicut homo peregre abiens, vocavit servos suos, et dedit eis substantiam suam. Haec parabola de talentis discernit fideles et diligentes, ab infidelibus et negligentibus sive securis. Et intelligenda est utroque modo, de publico ministerio, et privatim de usu donorum.

Rursus autem sciendum est, hic et doctrinam et obiurgationem, et consolationem proponi, sicut in priore parabola. Doctrina est prima haec: Quod semper sunt et erunt in Ecclesia aliqui fideles et diligentes, et aliqui infideles et negligentes, sicut nuper diximus, semper in Ecclesia fuisse, esse, et futuros esse in hac vita tales, qui sint similes fatuis Virginibus, et alios similes sapientibus Virginibus. Et hoc sciendum est, ne a Deo deficiamus propter hoc scandalum, cum videmus magnam multitudinem impiorum.

Alia doctrina est circa finem: Habenti dabitur, et a non habente etiam quod habet, auferetur. Hic manifeste docet nos Dominus, quod velit nos sua dona exercere, et acceptis donis non esse negligentes. Dicit dona augeri his, qui laborant, ut eis utantur. Sicut auget dona Ioseph aut Danieli, quia laborant in discendo, docendo et orando, et regunt suos mores temperantia, castitate et sobrietate, et aliis necessariis exercitiis. Quia nullo modo cogitandum est, Deum velle augere dona iis, qui volentes effundunt.

Sic dicit de negligentibus doctrinam: Quia repulisti scientiam, repellam te, ne Sacerdotio fungaris mihi. Oseae 4. Item: Qui stat, videat ne cadat, 1. Corinth. 10. Item: Invenit Diabolus domum vacuam etc., Matth. 12. Haec et talia dicta praecipiunt, ut non simus negligentes, sed donis utamur, sicut Paulus dicit 2. Corinth. 6.: Videte ne frustra gratiam receperitis.

Et homo iam donatus Spiritu sancto, potest et debet magis magisque petere se iuvari Spiritu sancto, sicut Christus inquit Matth. 7.: Petite, et accipietis. Quanto magis Pater vester coelestis dabit Spiritum sanctum petentibus, Lucae 11. Et sic petens Spiritum sanctum potest resistere malis tentationibus, potest retinere dona Dei, sicut Paulus inquit: Ego corpus meum redigo in servitutem, 1. Corinth. 9.

Nequaquam oportuit Davidem rapere alterius coniugem, sed poterat tunc cum haberet Spiritum sanctum, resistere tentationi adulterii.

Sic et hoc loco dicitur: Habenti dabitur.

Si David uteretur donis, crescerent in eo dona. Et contra: A non habente auferetur id quod habet.

David non utens donis, labitur, et amittit etiam praesentia dona plurima, post raptum alienae coniugis, amittit consilium bonum, iubet interfici virum, quia Diabolo iam aperta erat ianua, et impellitur ex alio scelere in aliud. Postea amittit custodiam divinam, Deus sinit eum eiici ex regno, et sinit multas tristissimas poenas accidere.

In hoc exemplo cernitur, quid sit: A non habente auferetur, quod habet.

Sumatis aliud exemplum. Saul est ornatus regno et Spiritu sancto, gloriosis victoriis. Postea incipit fieri tyrannus et superbus. Ibi amittit etiam quod habuerat, regnum, Spiritum sanctum, vitam, gloriam.

Haec exempla tristissima ostendunt, quomodo homines labantur, postquam fuerunt ornati donis Dei, et non voluerunt addere curam eis utendi.

Et prorsus falsa et diabolica est excusatio eorum, qui dicunt, se non posse abstinere a peccatis contra conscientiam.

Imo textus clarissime 1. Iohan. 3. dicit: Qui natus est ex Deo, peccatum non facit, quia semen Dei in eo est.

Dedit tibi Deus Spiritum sanctum, ut possis resistere malis tentationibus: et Deus praecipit, ut tanto suo dono utaris. Imo contumelia est adversus Deum, cogitare, quod dederit tibi Spiritum sanctum, ut tantum negligenter vivas, et laxes frenum malis cupiditatibus.

De obiurgatione.

Obiurgatio est in his dictis, quod ille negligens, qui noluit uti talento, punitur, et amittit etiam hoc quod habet.

Tales sunt obiurgationes saepe repetitae in scriptura. Ut Petrus inquit 2. Petri 2.: Hos negligentes similes esse iis, qui redeunt ad vomitum.

Sed dicat aliquis: Quis est satis diligens?

Omnes sunt infirmi, et aliquando labuntur. Respondeo: Hic tenenda est communis doctrina, quam saepe repetimus: In omnibus sanctis sunt infirmitates et peccata et lapsus, sicut scriptum est: Non est iustus in terra, qui cum bene faciat, non etiam peccet.

Sed tamen in singulis debet esse propositum benefaciendi, et debemus vitare, et possumus vitare lapsus contra conscientiam. Et si quis est lapsus, debet mox redire ad poenitentiam, sicut rediit David, sicut rediit Aaron.

Cain Saul Iudas } non redierunt ad poenitentiam.

Consolatio.

Consolatio est, quod aliqui maneant in Ecclesia, qui donis bene utuntur. Et his postea maiora dona tribuuntur, ut habetis insignia exempla.

Ioseph est recte usus dono, non voluit fieri moechus, et patienter tulit carcerem, ideo Deus eum exaltavit, et fecit eum praecipuum et salutarem Principem in Aegypto. Aliud pulchrum exemplum: Paupercula vidua in Sarepta est usa dono. Pavit Eliam, et prius ei cibum dedit quam sibi, ideo Deus benedixit eius domui.

Fuit enim hospitium Ecclesiae, non est exstincta fame, filius a morte resuscitatus est.

Et certissimum est, quod parva opera bona maximis praemiis publicis et privatis saepe ornantur, ut cogamur dicere, sicut Iacob inquit Genes. 32.: Minor sum cunctis miserationibus tuis.

Et contra, quando homines non volunt agere poenitentiam, tunc postea horribiles poenaes sequuntur. Exspectat Deus aliquando, et concedit spatium poenitentiae. Sed quando non inchoatur poenitentia, et fit contumacia maior, tunc veniunt ultimae poenae, vastationes gentium, et poenae aeternae, sicut de arbore ficu dicitur in parabola.

XII. ANNOTATIONES ET CONCIONES IN EVANG.

MATTHAEI.

Luc. 13.: Eccé anni tres sunt, ex quo venio quaerens fructus in hac arbore, et non invenio, succide ergo illam.

Haec est illa simplex et vera declaratio huius parabolae, nunc singuli videte, ut vos ad dona Dei exercenda exsuscitetis, et haec ipsa dicta cordi infigite: Habenti dabitur, et a non habente etiam quod habet auferetur, id est, ab amittente Evangelium et Spiritum sanctum, auferuntur multa alia dona, consilium, et omnia bona, aeterna et temporalia. Et in usu donorum praecipuus est usus, invocatio et precatio, sicut scriptum est Lucae 11.: Semper orate.

Et videtis iam necessitatem in periculis propter conventum, propter tempestates, propter bella, propter incendia, denique propter multas calamitates. Deus multis modis nos commonefacit, et tamen sumus negligentes, sed profecto tempus postulat, ut expergiscamur, ne pereamus, sicut illa ficus, sicut Sodoma, sicut Ierosolyma, sicut tota Asia, Graecia, et aliae regiones sub Turcis perierunt, imo sicut etiam perierunt omnes regiones in Germania et alibi, oppressae a Caesaris exercitibus, ubi Ecclesiae turbantur, et alia multa mala accidunt.

Ah Deus averte a nobis tales calamitates.

Quando veniet Filius hominis. De extremo iudicio.

Haec est expressa praedictio de iudicio extremo, qualis nulla est in veteri Testamento recitata.

Sunt quidem multa dicta, quae praedicunt resurrectionem mortuorum, et dicunt impios fore in poenis, et invocantes Deum habituros salutem aeternam, ut Esaiae ultimo scriptum est, tamen adeo expressa praedictio nulla est, ut haec concio filii Dei, qui hunc articulum claris verbis voluit declarare. Igitur haec verba Domini sint notissima omnibus, et adsidue cogitentur.

Et non indiget haec concio ulla declaratione, verba per se se perspicua sunt, sed fidem et timorem Dei adferamus, et hoc iudicium adsidue intueamur, metuamus iram, et consolemur nos, quod scimus Ecclesiam veram liberandam esse ab omnibus malis in eo iudicio. Haec est praecipua admonitio necessaria in hoc textu.

Sed tamen addemus et alias quasdam admonitiones.

Prima admonitio. Omnes homines diligenter discant, hane vitam humanam ordinatam esse a Deo, et non vivere homines sicut pecudes, sine lege Dei, et sine ullo ordine, ac mori sicut pecudes, sine ullo iudicio post hanc vitam, sed Deus condidit genus humanum ita, ut addiderit doctrinam, quomodo velit homines salvos facere, et sine ulla dubitatione punit omnes contemtores suae doctrinae.

Et sunt poenae duplices. Corporales in hac vita, et aliae postea aeternae post hanc vitam.

Secunda admonitio. Certissimum est, Deum in hac vita corporabilus poenis punire omnes, qui delicta committunt contra conscientiam, et quando sunt magna, sunt etiam poenae magnae.

De talibus delictis expresse dictum est: Qui gladium acceperit, gladio peribit. Hic dicitur, omnes homicidas sine ulla dubitatione rursus puniri gladio, sicut exempla ostendunt.

Certissimum est nullam homicidam posse effugere poenas in hac vita. Et valde errant homines, qui putant se posse latere.

Sicut recens exemplum audivistis, de interfectore fratris in valle Ioachimi. Manet vera vox: Qui gladium acceperit, gladio peribit.

Sic manet vera vox: Honora patrem et matrem, ut sis longaevus super terram. Certissimum est, qui male tractant parentes, puniri in hac vita.

Erat Francofordiae quidam bombardarius, industrius homo, qui diligebatur propter artem. Is cum vellet in novam bombardam rursus immittere pulverem bombardarium, pulvis accensus ex bombarda mox erumpit, et arreptum ipsum magistrum bombardae levat in altum, et accendit, et postea afflictum terrae interficit.

Causam homines plurimi, qui eum norant, dicebant esse, quia matrem male tractaverat. Tales historias possem recitare plures.

Item de periuris certum est, quod in hac vita puniantur. Item de scortatoribus et adulteris dicit textus: Scortatores et adulteros iudicabit Deus.

Hinc sunt tot morbi, ut morbus Gallicus et alii. Item peccata facta in semine, puniuntur in semine.

Ideo David rapta alterius coniuge, postea sic punitur, interficiuntur ei filii. Filius movet seditionem, et quod horrendum, patris coniuges postea contaminavit.

Et manifestum est vagari poenas per familias Principum et Regum, quia fuerunt adulteri, sicut ubique videmus exempla. Hanc doctrinam discant omnes homines, quod certissimum sit, puniri in hac vita delicta contra conscientiam, et maiora delicta maioribus poenis puniri. Quanquam autem multi hanc regulam negligunt et derident, tamen scitote verissimam esse, et saepe haec regula omnibus hominibus recitanda est. Et Deus eam populo declarat terribilibus exemplis, patibulo, et multis suppliciis homicidarum, et aliis modis poenarum. Haec cogitanda sunt in omni vita, et sciendum, quod tales poenae non accidunt sine consilio Dei.

Hic autem etiam sciatis: Quae sunt causae, quare Deus in hac vita punit, cum velit postea punire? Respondeo: Causae poenarum sunt quinque.

Prima est iustitia Dei: quia Deus vult conspici et agnosci iustitiam in genere humano etiam in hac vita. Ideo horribiliter punit manifesta delicta, ut ostendat se esse iustum, et irasci iniustitiae.

Secunda causa est pax publica: quia vult coërceri Deus ipsos delinquentes. Si fures non suspenderentur, non desinerent furari, et nulla pax esset.

Tertia causa est exemplum: quia Deus talibus poenis alios deterret, et aliqui moventur, etiamsi non moventur omnes, Deut. 17. et 19.

Quarta causa est, quia Deus significat his poenis corporalibus, certissime restare futurum iudicium, quia hae breves poenae in impiis non sunt aequales peccatis impiorum, qui non convertuntur. Sed peccata talium sunt infinita, ideo ordo iustitiae imponit eis poenas aeternas, haec bene consideranda sunt.

Die Sünd in den Gottlosen die nicht bekeret werden, ist so groß, das ir keine zeitliche straffe gleich ist, sonder sie ist vnermeslich, vnd gebürt dagegen ewige vnd vnermesliche straffe, nicht allein zeitliche straffe, die ein ende nimet. Gott behüt vns für solchem grausamen jamer.

Quinta causa est, quia Deus vult has poenas esse signa retrahentia nos ad poenitentiam. Quando fur ducitur ad patibulum, sciat se non propterea damnari, si modo agit poenitentiam, propter pacem politicam, et simul, ut sit admoniti retrahens ad poenitentiam. Has quoque causas saepe recitare et cogitare utile est.

Tertia admonitio.

Iam ubi nec doctrina Dei, nec poenae corporales flectunt homines ad poenitentiam, sequuntur poenae post hanc vitam, de quibus hic dicit.

Et textus non indiget ulla declaratione, Et sunt poenae horrendae, quae quantae sint, verbis dici non potest. Sunt ignis aeternus, pavor et dolor maior quam ulli dolores corporum, et vellent damnati redigi in nihilum, si fieri posset.

Quarta admonitio.

Sed quaerat aliquis: Qui sunt salvandi? Quis potest dicere, quod satisfecerit his verbis? Esurivi, et dedistis mihi cibum, etc.

Respondeo: Hic oportet vos utrunque scire, doctrinam de fide, et de bonis operibus. Certissimum est, quod vita aeterna datur propter Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum credentibus, sicut dixit textus: Haec est voluntas Patris, ut omnis, qui credit in Filium, habeat vitam aeternam. Hanc consolationem oportet nos scire, haec est vox propria Evangelii.

Ita hic dicit: Venite benedicti Patris mei, etc. Sunt autem benedicti per semen Abrahae etc.

Deinde vero oportet sciri, quod etiam sequi bona opera oporteat, et quod haec placeant Deo per fidem propter Christum, etiamsi sunt insufficientia. Sed tamen oportet nos tales esse, ne perseveremus in malo proposito contra conscientiam.

Econtra impii sunt sine fide, et habent malum propositum, non cibant Ecclesiam, sed interficiunt Sanctos. Non potant Ecclesiam, sed omni genere crudelitatis eam excruciare conantur etc.

Et facile conspici possunt utrique in confessione et persecutione. Credentes confitentur fidem, et faciunt multa bona opera. Sed impii ardent odiis, et quaerunt occasiones exercendae crudelitatis. Ita utrique discerni possunt.

Historia Passionis Domini nostri Iesu Christi.

## 26:1 Sermons on Matthew: Argument
Chapter XXVI. Ye know that after two days the Passover will come to pass.

There follows the history of the fourth day in the week of Palms, namely, Wednesday, because it says: After two days the Passover will come to pass, namely after Wednesday and after Thursday, because the day of the Passover was begun on the evening preceding the sixth day, Friday, and on this day the deliberation was held about capturing and killing the Lord.

Here let the horrendous furies be considered. They saw manifest miracles and testimonies of God, in these very days, the resurrection of Lazarus, and many other things. And yet such was the fury, that they dared to think about killing such a man, to whom God had attributed such great testimonies. And I do not add here a long narration, because there is no obscurity in this part of the text. I only exhort you all, that you may tremble thinking of such fury, and more ardently pray to God, that He may not allow us to fall in such a way. Ah God, for the sake of Thy glory, and for the sake of Thy Son, have mercy on us, and rule Thou us by Thy Holy Spirit, and do not allow us to be polluted by blasphemies and such sins, which are irremissible, as are the sins of Judas, Caiaphas, and their like.

Concerning the feast in Bethany.

In John there is also a description of the feast in Bethany, which took place on the Sabbath before Palms. This feast which Matthew recounts, took place on the fourth day, Wednesday, after Palm Sunday. And it is not absurd to say that there were two feasts, because I think the Lord ate in Bethany on these days, as often as He ate.

However, this history contains two examples.

The one is a work of confession, which the Lord praises. The other is the hypocritical judgment of Judas, or even of others, who blame the good work of the woman.

From this let us learn, that in the Church itself this often happens, that hypocrites judge and condemn the Saints, even when they are doing right. And let us learn to patiently tolerate such hypocritical judgments, and not become more negligent on account of them.

Thus the wife of David, the daughter of Saul, used to rebuke David singing with the harp before the ark of the Lord. And now there is great audacity in judging and condemning others. And yet those judges ought to consider the saying of Christ: Why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye? It is written: Judge not, that ye be not judged, that is, do not condemn, do not wound the consciences of the brethren, when they do works useful to the Church, which in themselves are not sins.

And see the present example, what a beautiful pretext it is. Judas saw an opportunity to steal being offered to him, if that ointment were sold; he covers this greed of his with this pretext: It would be better if the ointment were sold, and the poor were helped by that money.

Such is human cunning, it seeks honest pretexts for its own vices and greeds, and in the schools it is called a fallacy, according to a non-cause, a 'sham-cause' for a 'true cause'. But God judges the hearts, and will condemn and punish the hypocrites, and will raise up those who do right and faithfully serve the Church.

So it happens here: God rebukes those judging the woman, and affirms that the woman did a good work, because whatever this work was, and whatever the will of the woman was, yet this was the principal intention, that she wanted to show by this work that she confessed this man to be a teacher sent by God, and the Messiah, and that she was not in the number of his enemies. And she wanted to refresh him, exhausted by the labors of those days, because this nation was medicinal, and had many excellent things, such as balsam and others. This intention and such a significance of this intention is a work of confession, which is a good work, just as on Palm Sunday the signs of confession, to cry Hosanna to the son of David, and to spread garments, were good works, and works of confession.

So also the work of David preceding the ark with the cithara was a confession. Such works are pleasing to God, according to this saying: Whosoever shall confess me before men, him will I also confess before my Father which is in heaven. Our whole life ought to be a confession, as the Lord says: Let your light so shine before men, that your heavenly Father may be glorified.

Here let us think on the contrary, how great the sins are, when life is not a confession, but rather scandalous, and is the cause that the Gospel is ill-heard, and the Saints are grieved, and many are deterred from the doctrine; therefore let us be more diligent, and let us take care that our life may be a confession.

Afterwards, the Lord makes a comparison of works: "The poor you have always with you, but me you have not always," as if he were saying: It is good to help the poor who are truly needy, and you always have the opportunity. But it is better to show confession, and I will not always be with you in visible presence. Thus, let this saying be understood only simply, and it does not conflict with the other saying: "I am with you even unto the consummation of the world, all the days." He is with us and is truly present, ruling, defending, guarding, and saving us by his divine power.

It is one thing to speak of visible conversation, such as it was then, and it signifies that he was soon to die; and then they would be not only in sorrow, but also in great doubt. "Me you will not have," that is: Even if I will be with you, lying in the sepulcher, yet you will not have me, that is, you will not believe that I am about to rise again, you will not then believe that I am the savior, restoring life to the dead. And consider, he does not say: I will not be with you, but "you will not have me." The Lord is present then at the very feast visibly.

And yet not all had him, that is, not all recognized him to be the Messiah, not all believed.

Afterwards, the Lord praises the work for a singular circumstance, which the woman perhaps had not thought of, but the Holy Spirit in the woman, moving her, wished to signify this mystery. It was the custom to drench the dead bodies of the Jews with balsam, so that they might last a long time. The Lord therefore adapts this anointing to the burial, and to the preservation of the body in the sepulcher.

"She has anointed me," he says, "because I shall be buried," and she herself wishes my body not to be corrupted, but awaits the resurrection. See, how much wisdom he says is in this small work?

Perhaps the woman had not thought so much, but the Holy Spirit in the woman was thinking these things, and the Lord adorns the work of confession with such great praise, and shows that the Holy Spirit in the Saints considers many things in all good works. Always in one good work, many good works are contained.

And conversely, in one crime, many sins are contained at once; these things are to be well considered. Afterwards he says: "Wherever this Gospel shall be preached in the whole world, this work shall be praised." This is an excellent consolation.

True confession cannot be suppressed, even if many oppose it, and in some places extinguish it, yet God always preserves some Church, in which the light of confession remains. Let this be a brief narration of the example.

And remember, that this work of the woman is a work of confession. Monks wish to excuse their own chosen works without mandate by this example.

But their works are not examples of confession, and they themselves act as if they were prices and satisfactions for sins, etc. Lastly, from this example of the woman, let us learn that the ministers of the Gospel are also to be treated with honor.

Therefore this work is praised, because this was the intention, to refresh this weary preacher. Then went Judas, etc.

In the whole history of the Passion of Christ, just as in other histories, these six things must be considered: Persons.

Causes, why the persons fight among themselves. Acts. Associates of the persons. Punishments of the wicked. Liberations of the just. Thus, in this history, first let the persons be considered.

And the principal person is the Son of God, who came so that in this way he might become a victim for the human race, and he teaches the Gospel, reproves impiety and all sins. And he teaches the will of God concerning punishments, and concerning justice, and concerning the liberation of the just. This person is accompanied by a few, who are members of the Church of God, and they hear him, they grieve when he grieves, they rejoice when he is resurrected.

The principal contrary persons are the Devils, the impious High Priests, and the impious Princes, and their impious ministers, and the rest of the impious multitude, because the human race is distracted into two parts: into the true Church of God, which invokes and rightly worships the true God, and into the multitude that despises God.

And just as in all affairs which are carried out by many, the persons are various, so in the history of the Passion, on the side inimical to Christ, the persons are many: the Devil is the instigator, the High Priests are the principal visible enemies, who govern the highest councils, afterwards they have armed men, they have also traitors; thus it happens in wars. And that is notable here, that the traitor is found in the very number of the Apostles. David was betrayed by Doeg, who was an Edomite. This brought him not only pain, but as much pain as there was when his son and chief counselors defected from him. Likewise, how great was the pain of Joseph, when his brothers wanted to kill him, and afterwards sold him? Let us consider, therefore, in the very assembly which is called the Church, that there are many such who are like Judas, and let us grieve greatly, and pray to God that He may not allow us to be conquered by the Devil and impelled to evil counsels, just as it is written in John: Satan entered into his heart. And the Lord Himself says: Satan has demanded to have you, that he might sift you, but I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail. May these words warn us, that we may not be secure, thinking nothing of the snares of the Devil, but let us pray to God assiduously, that He may rule us, that we may not fall into the snares of the Devil. Let these things now be said enough about the persons, and remember this division, because often afterwards it must be said again about the works of the various persons.

2. Concerning the cause.

In the Son of God, the cause why He wills to suffer is good, namely, because He knows this obedience to be the price by which the justice of God is satisfied, and wrath is appeased, and God receives the human race, just as it is written in the Psalm: In the head of the book it is written of me, that I should do your will, O my God, I desire it, and your law is in the midst of my heart, etc. The whole scripture speaks of this wondrous counsel of God, that God in this way willed to save the human race, and often this wondrous deliberation must be pondered: the Son is the intercessor for Adam and Eve, and a decree is made that the punishment should be derived onto Him, because the order of justice was that the human race would not be received unless compensation was made, and the redeemer paid a penalty equivalent to it. This wondrous counsel must be pondered daily, and thanks must be given to God for the given Son. But the cause of the passion in the enemies of Christ was the hatred of God in the Devil, and the hatred of Christ in the Pharisees, who did not want their errors and sins to be accused, and in the same way hypocrites always hate the true Church.

3. We shall recite the acts in order, how they attempt to destroy Christ simultaneously with lies and manifest violence. 4. The associates of the persons, as I said. The associates of Christ are a few listeners, the Apostles, Mary, and a few others, who grieve with Him as He suffers, and rejoice with Him as He rises. But the associates of the impious Pontiffs and Pharisees are tyrants, who assist the persecution with arms. Likewise the traitor Judas, and the remaining blasphemers and impious ones, who persevere in impiety. To all these it will be said: Depart, you cursed, into eternal fire.

5. The punishments of the impious begin even in this life, as the punishment of Judas, and undoubtedly many others, Pilate, Herod, and the Pontiffs had punishments even in this life, but afterwards follow eternal punishments much greater. 6. On the contrary, the liberation of the just begins in the resurrection; there the Apostles manifestly see what the liberation of the whole Church will be in the resurrection. Let this be enough to have said about Judas, and let us pray to God ardently that He may rule us by His Holy Spirit, that the Devil may not entangle us in his snares, so that we may defect from Christ; let us also pray to Christ Himself, that He may rule us, and intercede for us, just as He interceded for Peter, and confirmed him.

The First of Unleavened Bread.

The history follows concerning the Paschal lamb, and concerning the institution of the Lord's Supper. We do not wish, however, to speak now of the old rite of the Paschal lamb. But we wish to speak of our Sacraments, and of the causes why there have always been Sacraments in the Church, and what their use is. This doctrine must be repeated often, and this is the first cause of the institution of the Sacraments for all times. Since God, in His immense mercy, wills to gather an eternal Church from the human race, He brought forth from the beginning His promise concerning reconciliation, and added external visible signs, because He wills that that promise should resound in the human race, and so that the promise might become more notable, external visible signs were also proposed to the eyes. Likewise, since He wills the Church to be a certain assembly distinct from other nations, He wills there to be distinguishing signs, just as circumcision distinguished the Israelites from all other nations, Baptism distinguishes us from those nations. He also wills some signs to be bonds of public assemblies, because it is most certain that God to will that public, honest assemblies be held, and He Himself preserves them in the human race, and dissipations, such as the Anabaptists or others make, who run into hiding and cause divisions without necessary cause, do not please Him.

God wills that the Church be distinct from other nations, and He wills that it be seen and heard in the whole human race. Therefore, He wills that there be honest assemblies, and He preserves them, and He added signs, so that the Church might be discerned and seen. Consider this reason well, so that afterwards you may better understand those things which are said about the Lord's Supper. For it is instituted in such a way that it is that public ceremony connecting the public assembly.

After this reason, which speaks of the public assembly or distinction, there is also this reason to be recognized for the conscience of each person: Sacraments are also testimonies of the will toward you, and they are applications of the promises through faith. When you take the body and blood of the Lord, think and believe that the promise of grace pertains to you also. Otherwise, men think: "Behold, the promise is a general statement, perhaps it pertains nothing to you." But know that in this very rite God testifies that the promise pertains to you. The Lord gives you His body and blood, He makes you a member of His body, He therefore wills to truly bestow the promises upon you.

Consider this reason diligently, and at the same time learn here of the great and horrible abuse which has always wandered in the world, concerning the merit of the work, or the use of the Sacraments without faith. Just as the Pharisees taught that sins were remitted on account of their sacrifices and slaughterings, and said absolutely nothing about faith: so the people in the Papacy run to the Lord's Supper, and thought that by this work and this obedience they merited the remission of sins. This insanity is a great idolatry. But you must know that this your taking or obedience is by no means a merit for the remission of sins, but that the Son of God by His death merited remission for us all, and that this must be received by faith in true repentance. Afterwards, indeed, this taking is a testimony to you that the promise also pertains to you, and your mind may look upon the Son of God sitting at the right hand of the eternal Father, who already makes you a member of His body, and long before merited remission for you, and wills that you console yourself with His promise. Here the true use must be distinguished from the papistic and heathen abuse, which performed ceremonies as if they were merits for the remission of sins.

After I have spoken about the causes and the use of the Sacraments, generally, we shall speak next also about the text and about the Mass.

Latin:

Caput XXVI. Scitis quod post biduum Pascha fiet.

Sequitur historia diei quarti in septimana Palmarum, scilicet, des Mitwochens, quia dicit: Post biduum Pascha fiet, scilicet post Mitwoch et post Donnerstag, quia dies Paschatos fuit inchoatus vespere praecedente feriam sextam den Freitag, et isto die deliberatio fuit de capiendo et interficiendo Domino.

Hic cogitentur horrendi furores. Viderunt manifesta miracula et testimonia Dei, his ipsis diebus, resuscitationem Lazari, et alia multa. Et tamen tantus furor fuit, ut auderent cogitare de interficiendo tali viro, cui Deus tanta testimonia tribuerat. Et non addo hic longam enarrationem, quia nihil obscuritatis est in hac parte textus. Tantum vos omnes adhortor, ut expavescatis cogitantes tantum furorem, et ardentiùs oretis Deum, ne sinat nos ita ruere. Ah Deus propter tuam gloriam, et propter Filium tuum, miserere nostri, et rege tu nos Spiritu sancto tuo, et non sinito nos pollui blasphemiis et talibus peccatis, quae sunt irremissibilia, ut sunt peccata Iudae, Caiphae et similium.

De convivio in Bethania.

In Iohanne est etiam descriptio convivii in Bethania, quod factum est Sabbato ante Palmarum. Hoc convivium quod recitat Matthaeus, factum est feria quarta am Mitwochen, post diem Palmarum. Et non est absurdum, dicere, quod sint duo convivia, quia existimo Dominum his diebus comedisse in Bethania, quoties comedit.

Historia autem haec continet exempla duo.

Alterum est opus confessionis, quod laudat Dominus. Alterum est hypocriticum iudicium Iudae, vel etiam aliorum, qui reprehendunt bonum opus mulieris.

Hinc discamus, in ipsa Ecclesia saepe hoc accidere, ut hypocritae iudicent et condemnent Sanctos, etiam recte facientes. Et talia hypocritica iudicia discamus patienter tolerare, et non propterea fiamus negligentiores.

Sic uxor Davidis, filia Saul, reprehendebat Davidem canentem fidibus ante arcam Domini. Et nunc magna audacia est iudicandi et damnandi alios. Et tamen considerare illi iudices deberent dictum Christi: Quare vides festucam in oculo fratris tui, et non consideras trabem in tuo oculo? Scriptum est: Nolite iudicare, ne iudicemini, id est, non damnate, non sauciate fratrum conscientias, quando faciunt opera utilia Ecclesiae, quae per se non sunt peccata.

Et videte praesens exemplum, quam pulcer praetextus est. Iudas videbat occasionem furandi sibi offerri, si venderetur illud unguentum, hanc suam cupiditatem tegit isto praetextu: Melius esset vendi unguentum, et pecunia illa iuvari pauperes.

Talis est astutia humana, suis vitiis et cupiditatibus, quaerit praetextus honestos, et in scholis nominatur fallacia, secundum non causam, Scheinursach für wahrhafftige Ursach. Sed Deus iudicat corda, et damnabit et puniet hypocritas, et exsuscitabit recte facientes et fideliter servientes Ecclesiae.

Ita fit hic: Deus obiurgat iudicantes mulierem, et adfirmat mulierem fecisse opus bonum, quia qualecunque fuit hoc opus, et quaecunque fuit voluntas mulieris, tamen haec fuit principalis intentio, quod voluit ostendere hoc opere se fateri hunc virum esse doctorem a Deo missum, et Messiam, et se non esse in numero hostium ipsius. Et voluit eum defatigatum laboribus illorum dierum recreare, quia haec natio fuit medica, et habuit multas res optimas, ut balsamum et alia. Haec intentio et talis significatio huius intentionis est opus confessionis, quod est opus bonum, sicut in die Palmarum signa confessionis, clamare Osanna filio David, et prosternere vestes, fuerunt opera bona, et opera confessionis.

Sic etiam opus Davidis praecedentis arcam cum cithara, fuit confessio. Talia opera sunt Deo placentia, iuxta hoc dictum: Qui confessus fuerit me coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram Patre meo coelesti. Tota nostra vita debet esse confessio, sicut dicit Dominus: Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus, ut glorificetur Pater vester coelestis.

Hic cogitemus contra, Quanta peccata sint, quando vita non est confessio, sed potius scandalosa, et est causa, ut male audiat Evangelium, et doleant Sancti, et multi deterreantur a doctrina, ideo simus diligentiores, et curemus, ut vita sit confessio.

Postea facit Dominus collationem operum: Pauperes semper habetis vobiscum, me autem non semper, quasi dicat: Bonum est iuvare pauperes vere egentes, et semper habetis occasionem. Sed melius est, ostendere confessionem, et non semper ego visibili praesentia vobiscum ero. Sic tantum simpliciter intelligatur hoc dictum, et non pugnat cum alio dicto: Ego vobiscum sum usque ad consummationem seculi omnibus diebus.

Est nobiscum et vere praesens est, sua divina potentia nos regens, defendens, custodiens, salvans. Aliud est loqui de visibili conversatione, qualis tunc erat, et significat cito se moriturum esse; et tunc ipsos futuros non solum in moerore, sed etiam in magna dubitatione. Me non habebitis, id est: Etiam si ero vobiscum, iacens in sepulcro, tamen me non habebitis, id est, non credetis me esse resurrecturum, non tunc credetis me esse salvatorem, reddentem vitam mortuis.

Et consideres, non dicit: Non ero vobiscum, sed non habebitis me.

Adest Dominus tunc in ipso convivio visibiliter. Et tamen non omnes habebant eum, id est, non omnes agnoscebant eum esse Messiam, non omnes credebant. Postea Dominus laudat opus a singulari circumstantia, quam mulier fortassis non cogitaverat, sed Spiritus sanctus in muliere, movens eam, significare hoc arcanum voluit.

Mos erat corpora Iudaeorum mortua perfundere balsamo, ut diu durarent. Accommodat igitur Dominus hanc unctionem ad sepulturam, et ad conservationem corporis in sepulcro, Unxit me, inquit, quia sepeliar, et ipsa vult meum corpus non corrumpi, sed exspectat resurrectionem.

Videte, quantam sapientiam ait esse in hoc exiguo opere? Tantum fortassis non cogitaverat mulier, sed tantum Spiritus sanctus in muliere haec cogitabat, et Dominus hac tanta laude ornat opus confessionis, et ostendit, Spiritum sanctum in Sanctis multa considerare in omnibus bonis operibus.

Semper in uno bono opere multa bona opera insunt. Et contra, in uno delicto multa peccata simul insunt, haec bene consideranda sunt.

Postea inquit: Ubicunque praedicabitur hoc Evangelium in toto mundo, laudabitur hoc opus. Haec est egregia consolatio.

Confessio vera non poterit opprimi, etiamsi multi adversantur, et in aliquibus locis exstinguunt, tamen semper servat Deus aliquam Ecclesiam, in qua manet lux confessionis. Haec sit brevis enarratio exempli.

Et mementote, hoc opus mulieris esse opus confessionis, Monachi sua opera electa sine mandato volunt per hoc exemplum excusare. Sed ipsorum opera non sunt exempla confessionis, et ipsi faciunt tanquam pretia et satisfactiones pro peccatis, etc.

Postremo ex hoc exemplo mulieris discamus etiam honore afficiendos esse ministros Evangelii. Ideo hoc opus laudatur, quia haec fuit intentio, hunc defessum concionatorem recreare.

Tunc abiit Iudas, etc.

In tota historia Passionis Christi, sicut in aliis historiis, oportet haec sex considerari. Personas. Causas, cur inter se personae pugnent. Acta. Personarum socios. Poenas malorum. Liberationes iustorum. Sic in hac historia primum considerentur personae.

Et principalis persona est Filius Dei, qui venit, ut hoc modo fiat victima pro genere humano, et docet Evangelium, arguit impietatem et omnia peccata. Et docet voluntatem Dei de poenis, et de iustitia, et de liberatione iustorum. Hanc personam comitantur pauci, qui sunt membra Ecclesiae Dei, et audiunt eum, dolent ipso dolente, laetantur ipso resuscitato.

Contrariae personae principales sunt, Diaboli, impii Pontifices, et impii Principes, et horum ministri impii, et reliqua multitudo impia, quia genus humanum in duas partes est distractum, in Ecclesiam Dei veram, quae verum Deum invocat et recte colit, et in multitudinem contemtricem Dei.

Et sicut in omnibus negotiis, quae per multos aguntur, personae variae sunt, ita in historia Passionis, in parte inimica Christo, personae multae sunt, Diabolus est excitator, Pontifices sunt praecipui hostes visibiles, qui summa consilia gubernant, postea habent armatos, habent et proditores, sic fit in bellis. Et illud est hic insigne, quod invenitur proditor in ipso numero Apostolorum. David proditus fuit a Doëg, qui fuit Idumaeus. Hoc non tantum ei dolorem attulit, quantus dolor fuit, cum filius et praecipui consiliarii ab eo deficerent. Item, quantus fuit dolor Ioseph, cum fratres eum voluerunt interficere, et postea vendiderunt? Consideremus igitur in ipso coetu, qui nominatur Ecclesia, tales multos esse, qui sunt similes Iudae, et valde doleamus, et Deum oremus, ne sinat nos per Diabolum vinci et impelli ad mala consilia, sicut in Iohanne scriptum est: Satanas intravit in cor eius. Et Dominus ipse dicit: Satanas expetivit vos, ut cribraret vos, Ego autem pro te oravi, ut non deficiat fides tua. Haec dicta moneant nos, ne simus securi nihil cogitantes de insidiis Diaboli, sed Deum oremus assidue, ut nos regat, ne incidamus in laqueos Diaboli. Haec iam satis dicta sint de personis, et mementote hanc divisionem, quia saepe postea rursus dicendum est de diversarum personarum operibus.

2. De causa.
