It is certain that the Gospel primarily delivers the promise concerning eternal things, namely, that the Son of God is a victim for the human race, and that to him who does penance and believes, God certainly gives for his sake the remission of sins, the Holy Spirit, and eternal life: on the contrary, he certainly casts those who despise the Gospel into eternal punishments.

Let us know that this revelation of the divine will, brought forth from the bosom of the eternal Father concerning eternal things, is the principal voice of the Gospel, just as Christ says in John 6: This is the will of the Father, that everyone who believes in the Son may have eternal life. Let us first embrace this doctrine concerning eternal things, afterwards let us know that promises have also been added to the Gospel concerning present things, as in Matthew 6: Seek first the kingdom of God, and the rest shall be added unto you. 1 Timothy 4: Godliness is profitable for all things, having promises of the present life and of the future. Mark 10: Whoever has left house for my sake and for the sake of the Gospel, shall receive a hundredfold in this time, with tribulation, and in the future eternal life. To this, many promises from the Psalms are added. Psalm 36: In the days of famine they shall be satisfied. Item: I have not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed seeking bread. 32: That he may feed them in famine. 33: There is no want to those who fear him. 54: Cast your care upon the Lord, and he himself will nourish you. 111: Blessed is the man who fears the Lord, wealth and riches are in his house. It is profitable to have such sentences in view, so that they may instruct and console us, as I shall say later. Therefore, let us first remember that there are these two kinds of promises.

On the second. But someone may say: The outcomes do not seem to correspond to these generous promises; great empires, great wealth are for the most part with the ungodly.

The Apostles wander about as vagabonds, beggars, and for the most part pious teachers go hungry, are in hatred, are slaughtered, and the common saying is: Probity is praised and freezes. Item: Let him leave the court who wishes to be pious. Indeed, it is manifest that the Church is subject to the cross and is without human protections. And truly it happens to us, what Christ said of himself and of his whole flock: The Son of man has nowhere to lay his head. To all these things I answer: Although the whole human race is subject to death and many huge calamities, yet by the certain counsel of God the Church is more pressed, namely, so that we may recognize the wrath of God against sins, and know that the Church is preserved divinely. And yet God wills that there be some Church of his in this life, he does not will the whole human race to perish, but that there be some flower, some assembly, by which he may be acknowledged, invoked, and celebrated, as Amos 3: As if a shepherd should rescue from the mouth of the lion two legs, so shall the children of Israel be rescued. He commanded therefore that the article be believed: I believe the catholic Church, that is, I believe that there is some people of God, embracing the word delivered through the Prophets and Apostles, to which the catholic Church bears witness, and I believe that such some a community that will always remain, as He said: I will be with you even unto the consummation of the age, etc.

It is therefore always necessary that these two be joined: the doctrine of the cross and that of consolation. It is true that the Church is subject to the cross, as Christ says: Whoever wishes to follow me, let him take up his cross. And Jeremiah 12: I have given my beloved soul into the hands of her enemies. And yet, since God wishes the Church to remain, which is nevertheless without human protections, He Himself proposes the most ample and sweetest consolations regarding defense, sustenance, peace, and success in our functions—ecclesiastical, political, and economic.

And let us understand the promises as they sound, and not attach corruptions and inept interpretations to them, as many inept people do in the customary prayer, "our daily bread," forbidding it to be understood as bodily bread; indeed, He speaks of bodily bread, of the defense of this life, and of governance, and God does indeed provide these goods and bestows them according to His promises.

Why, then, do the outcomes not correspond? Indeed, they do correspond. And first, let the promises be understood regarding the whole body of the Church. As in the Red Sea, so amidst the tyrannies of the world and the furies of the devil, God assiduously preserves the Church in this life. It is therefore clear that the promises are valid for the whole body of the Church. For the Church is always preserved, and in our prayers, let us first ask for the whole body, and let us firmly establish that this prayer is not in vain.

Regarding the third point.

Why bodily promises have been given.

The first cause is this: The human mind, without the light of faith, thinks that men grow rich either by chance, as Pythius did from metallic veins, or by industry, whether just or unjust, and it does not firmly establish that our resources are offered, defended, and increased by any work of God. For it sees many growing through embezzlement and various frauds, like Crassus.

And although God allows thieves and robbers to run rampant publicly and privately for a time, yet in the end He shakes them out of their fortunes, to testify that He does not neglect the administration or acquisition of resources; therefore it is said: Woe to you who plunder, for you will be plundered in turn. And from experience that saying has arisen: Ill-gotten, ill-spent. And they say that that rich man Pythius died of hunger, and how miserable the end of Crassus was, one may read in his history.

Again, God also gave promises to the just, so that they might truly establish that these goods do not come by chance, nor are they prepared solely by human industry. For although God wishes everyone to labor, as his calling commands each one, and wishes things to be prepared and retained by honest labor, and not dissipated by profusion, as is said in Solomon, "Do not give your substance to the cruel": yet in the meantime He wishes us to know that this diligence alone does not bring resources. Just as the farmer's labor alone does not produce crops, but they come forth because God makes the earth fertile, and just as an army's labor does not only produce victory, but it is necessary for divine aid to be added, as it is said: The horse is deceptive for salvation. Thus, because God favors the one who serves Him faithfully in his calling, He advances resources by His goodness.

To this sentiment Solomon says: The blessing of the Lord makes one rich.

And David, 1 Kings 17: Let the whole Church know this, that the Lord does not save by the sword, for the battle is His.

Therefore, He also sometimes proposes examples where He increases things without secondary causes, as He fed the widow of Zarephath, fed the people in the desert, and gave Isaac a hundredfold, when in other fields so much would not have been produced. And there are daily examples in pious families, who experience that additions are offered to them divinely, or at least that their affairs are defended, even if some detriments, losses, and hardships intervene.

For as it has been said: The Church is at the same time subject to the cross.

These things must be impressed upon the mind, so that we may learn the article of Creation, and believe that our resources are benefits of God, so that we may truly be able to ask God for daily bread. For those who do not believe these to be gifts of God recite these words idly, and insult God. Now let us consider how few recite these words piously: Give us this day our daily bread. For one man imagines that these things are of no concern to God, another thinks himself unworthy, that surely these gifts are not given to him by God; in short, there are great darknesses in souls, which must be removed through the Word of God.

The second cause is why these promises have been handed down. Since God wishes there to always be some Church of His in this life, it is necessary for the body to have sustenance, lodging, defense, political order, and some peace, so that offspring can be raised and studies cultivated. Therefore He also added these promises, and God bestows these benefits, but miraculously.

The devil rages against the Church, and there are constant tumults in the world, by which the persistent sins of the human race are horribly punished; amidst these tumults, God preserves His Church, just as He preserved it standing in the Red Sea. And the body remains, even if some members are slaughtered, just as David's army remains, even if some soldiers fighting are killed, because, as has been said so often, the Church is still subject to the cross.

These promises therefore offer us great consolation. We are distressed by such great tumults of empires, by the seat of the Church, by our studies: and although other times are for others more tranquil and happier, yet let us know that the seat of the Church and of our studies will be a care to God, wherever it may be, as it is said in Isaiah: In my womb you are carried. I will carry the aging Church. Item: Even if a mother should forget her children, I will not forget you, I will embrace you in the hollow of my hand. Let us often set these consolations before ourselves, so that we may propagate doctrine with good hope, and by faith ask for these good things from God.

Therefore, the third reason why these promises have been given is that they may be exercises of faith and invocation: God wants to be acknowledged through invocation. Therefore, He has proposed many things that might admonish us about invocation. He has given promises of grace, and of bodily benefits, and of eternal life; He wants us to flee to Him, even when we seem deserted and cast out by the whole nature of things. Just as David says: Father and mother have forsaken me, but the Lord has taken me up.

Concerning the fourth. In what order they are to be sought.

The order is clearly proposed in the saying of Christ: Seek first the kingdom of God, and the rest will be added to you.

Let the first care be that we obey God, and celebrate Him by learning and teaching the truth.

Indeed, let us also first ask that He may kindle in us the true light by His Holy Spirit for Christ's sake, just as it is commanded: Ask, and you shall receive. If men can give good things to men, how much more will the heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask?

So also David prays: Deal with your servant according to your mercy, and teach me your justifications.

So also Solomon is praised because he first asked for wisdom, and it is added: Therefore I will also give you riches. And in Proverbs 30, the order is shown: Two things I have asked of you, remove vanity and lies far from me.

Do not give me deceit and riches, and he recites the reasons why he desires mediocrity. Because the wealthy more easily indulge in depraved desires, and amidst pleasures they forget God, and gradually fall further. Just as it is said in Ezekiel 16: This was the iniquity of Sodom, pride, fullness of bread, abundance, idleness, and they did not reach out their hand to the needy. Therefore they were lifted up, and committed abominations.

And the verses are known: Souls generally luxuriate in prosperous things, Nor is it easy to bear favorable circumstances with an equal mind. Item: While hearts rejoice, and are not distracted by pain, They lie open, then Venus enters with seductive

art. Therefore Solomon does not ask for opulence, but yet he asks for things necessary for sustenance, as the text speaks, so that I may not commit theft or perjury. For as opulence feeds pleasures, so on the contrary, poverty drives many to evil arts.

Let honest minds foresee these dangers on both sides, so that they may ask God for what is necessary, but in order, as has been said. Let them also know that with this petition for resources, honest labor is requested, according to one's vocation, as is often commanded, 1 Thess. 4: We exhort you, that you may excel in this matter, and do this ambitiously, namely to retain tranquility, and to do your own duty, and to labor with your hands. This brief sentence is full of political wisdom, and is to be diligently considered. For restless and meddlesome (πολυπραγμονικὰ) natures are most dangerous to all cities. There are many who, because they have restless natures, attempt to govern many things, and enact many ordinances, then neither remain within the limits of their own duty, but touch upon the affairs of others. Thus Alcibiades and Demosthenes overthrew Athens. For they stirred up unnecessary tumults for this very reason, because they had restless natures. Therefore Paul commands that we be quiet, not turbulent, that is, that we stir up nothing except what is necessary, attempting nothing outside our vocation. Seneca records a saying from Cato: Buy not what is useful, but what is necessary. The same should be observed in affairs. Let us consider not only what is beneficial or useful, but what it is necessary to undertake. And in Thucydides it is said that one ought to be a lover of tranquility, and when it is necessary to accomplish something, to be keen, not turbulent in stirring things up, nor sluggish in acting.

XII. ANNOTATIONS ON THE GOSPELS. These things must be thought of at the same time as labor, whenever we ask for bodily things, because sloth is a sin. And what a monster is a man who is such a useless weight upon the earth, who contributes nothing of his works to the propagation of the knowledge of God, or to the protection and adornment of other good things in life. Indeed, it is commanded specifically to Titus that we should learn things useful for life.

Meanwhile, however, let us know that God blesses labor in this way, when we add invocation, as is said in Luke 5: At thy word I will let down the net. And Psalm 33: This poor man cried unto the Lord, and the Lord heard him. Item: Ask, and ye shall receive.

Concerning the fifth.

How faith is to be exercised in the petition for bodily things.

This is the principal place in this doctrine concerning promises.

But first it must be known that faith must always shine before the petition for bodily things, by which we believe that we are received and heard on account of Christ. Indeed, in order that this faith may be kindled and grow in us, so many various external occasions, actions, dangers, and afflictions have been set before us. Let us know, therefore, that the first and highest promise concerning the mediator and reconciliation must always be embraced at the same time. Therefore, when sayings about faith are cited, even if the external objects vary, yet they all embrace at the same time this faith concerning reconciliation.

Abraham, Jacob, and David therefore ask for and expect defense from God, because they believe that they have been received and are heard by God on account of the promised Lord. Daily, therefore, when you recite these words at the table, Give us this day our daily bread, because our infirmity soon clamors, God does not hear you as unworthy, He does not want you defended or fed. Here the promise concerning Christ must be looked upon, and faith must be embraced, that on account of the mediator we are received and heard. Therefore it follows immediately: And forgive us our debts. Therefore, let this sentence always be in sight: Through Christ we have access to the Father, therefore it is necessary that this faith concerning the remission of sins on account of Christ always shine before us.

Afterwards, let that faith think of the three things which I recounted above, that God wills that the goods of the body be asked of Him. First, That we may yield that they are given divinely, and not think they are thrown at us by chance. Second, Because He wills that the Church be preserved in this life, He gives sustenance, defense, and shelter miraculously, etc. Third, God wills to be acknowledged and worshipped by this invocation, therefore He has proposed many things which He wills to be asked for, and He wills that faith be confirmed by the petition for bodily things.

For who does not dare to ask for bodily things, and already doubts the presence of God, when we are deserted by all creatures? Isaiah 57: Dwelling with the contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and the heart of the contrite. Faith is also confirmed when experience shows that prayer has not been in vain, as is said in the Psalm: This poor man cried unto the Lord, and the Lord heard him.

Finally, God also wills to be worshipped by thanksgiving on account of deliverances, as is most sweetly said in 2 Cor. 1, where Paul commands many to ask on his behalf, so that many may give thanks, etc. This order and all these causes must be thought of when we ask for bodily things.

And the dangers are great enough, public and private, which warn us to think of these things. When the Church stood at the Red Sea, certainly it had to be thought of first by Moses, whether it pleased God, and why it pleased Him, namely on account of the promised Lord. Then he saw in reality the salvation of bodies given by God, he thought that God wills to preserve the Church in this life, he thought also that God wills that knowledge in invocation should grow in us, amidst such dangers and miracles. But the Church is always involved in huge dangers, almost as if standing at the Red Sea: now Turkish arms are raging against it, and many other domestic difficulties exercise individuals.

There is no certain seat for anyone, the life of many pious people is in danger: warned therefore by public and our own dangers, let us ask for help and defense, in that order, as has been said, and let us think of those causes, so that faith may be exercised. But then also, having obtained benefits, let us give thanks, and with greater zeal in every duty let us declare our gratitude.

But here human weakness objects, What does it matter to ask, when we know that we must be afflicted? just as it is written, But the body is subject to death on account of sin. Item, it is manifest that very often the saints are not delivered from present calamities, such as Jonathan, the Maccabee, and others. And Christ says: Nevertheless not my will, but thine. Since therefore we ought to offer obedience, what does petition profit, and indeed with doubt? I answer.

The rule must be held most firmly, that God has commanded and demands invocation, and that the invocation of the pious is never empty or in vain, even if deliverance is deferred, or events do not respond as we imagine, and not It is not for us to prescribe to God a method of helping, but we are bound to obedience, just as Christ says: Thy will be done, etc.

But the greatest part of men, because they do not see the results of prayer immediately, dream that invocation is an empty murmur. This impious imagination must be resisted most sharply, and these shadows must be dispelled by gathering promises: Call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver you. Likewise: Ask, and you shall receive, etc.

Next, let us know that two objects must always be included in the petition for bodily things: the universal Church, and private necessity.

The petition of the pious always obtains for the universal Church, and thus let faith establish that this petition is ratified, and let it not doubt that the petition is received by God for the universal Church. Thus David, praying for the army, asks first not for himself privately, but for the assembly, because we know that God gives bodily goods so that the Church may be preserved in this life. But we ought to ask privately for ourselves with this condition, that we offer ourselves to obedience, just as Christ offers himself.

Thus David both asks and is prepared for obedience. Because he knows that in such dangers God wills some to obey, and yet because the army is preserved, it is necessary that many members be preserved, and the evil is mitigated for the others. Thus the prayer of Jeremiah profited the people first, even if he did not know whom and how God was going to save; then it also profited him, and yet he himself was prepared for obedience, and he knew that God preserves his ministers until they complete their course, and gives others a different course.

Elijah taught for about twenty years. Elisha for about seventy. Isaiah for about eighty. Jeremiah for forty years until the destruction of Jerusalem, and afterwards he presided for some time in Egypt over the remnants of his people, until he was killed by the tyrant Apries. Daniel taught for more than seventy years. John the Baptist for two years. Christ for three years. Paul for thirty-five years. John the Apostle for sixty-eight years, James the brother of John for three years after the ascension of Christ. James the Less for thirty years, killed some time before the siege of Jerusalem. Timothy is said to have been killed under Nero. Titus's old age is recounted, the time of his preaching is not certainly known, but they say he died in the ninety-fourth year of his age. Polycarp was killed in the eighty-sixth year of his age, who as a young man had been a hearer of John the Evangelist. Irenaeus, a hearer of Polycarp, was killed under Maximian at Sirmium; he therefore lived in the meantime for about eighty years. This dissimilarity must be observed, so that we may know that God has prescribed different struggles and different spans to different people, and yet we should consider that for some, life was prolonged so that they might be pious witnesses and propagators of doctrine who survived.

David, seeking defense, uses a most sweet figure: Hide me in your tabernacle, that is, in your Church.

Here he simultaneously embraces a petition for others and the cause: Defend me with your Church, and for the sake of the Church. For bodily goods are promised only for this reason, that they may serve the Church; defense is asked for this reason, that we may be able to serve the Church and our children. And because God wills that we ask for the whole body, let us know that this petition is always ratified, and obtains some good for the whole body. And although we individuals must be prepared for obedience, yet liberation is often obtained for individuals as well, and when some assembly is preserved, it is necessary that many be preserved. Let us therefore rouse ourselves to ask for bodily goods by gathering the reasons: because God commands them to be asked for us and for others, he wills that public and private calamities be understood as punishments for the sins of the world: therefore he wills that we ask for pardon, and be affected by concern for our own and the common salvation; he wills that faith, fear, and love grow through these exercises.

On the sixth. Application of the history of Mark 8.

That Christ feeds his hearers is shown by the example of the promise: Seek first the kingdom of God, and the rest shall be added unto you.

With this faith let us follow Christ, let us be faithful in the study and propagation of the Gospel, and let us expect help, sustenance, and defense from the Son of God.

But that he orders the Apostles to propose and gather the fragments, they warn the governors of the Church that they should take care that alms are given, and know that resources are not diminished, but increased by alms.

He signifies doctrine covertly; let the teachers propose this, and gather the fragments, let them take care that true expositions are propagated, lest the light of doctrine be extinguished for posterity, and by this study the teachers themselves become more learned.

The baskets, however, signify letters and schools, in which it is necessary that doctrine be guarded.

Latin:

Dominica VII. post Trinitatis.

Evangelium Marci 8.

In diebus illis, cum turba admodum multa esset, nec haberent quod manducarent, vocatis ad se Iesus discipulis suis, ait illis: Misereor super turbam, quia ecce iam triduo manent apud me, et non habent quod manducent, et si dimisero eos ieiunos in domum suam, deficient in via. Quidam enim ex eis de longe venerunt. Et responderunt ei discipuli sui: Unde istos quis poterit hic satiare panibus in solitudine? Et interrogavit eos: Quot panes habetis? Illi autem dixerunt: Septem. Et praecepit turbae discumbere super terram. Et accipiens septem panes, gratias agens, fregit, deditque discipulis suis ut apponerent, et apposuerunt turbae. Et habebant pisciculos paucos, et benedixit, ac iussit apponi et hos, manducaverunt autem et saturati sunt, et sustulerunt quod supererat de fragmentis, septem sportas. Erant autem, qui manducaverant, quasi quatuor millia, et dimisit eos.

Sex sunt praecipui loci.

I. Differentia promissionum de rebus aeternis, et de rebus praesentibus. II. Quod semper promissioni corporali addenda sit doctrina de cruce. III. Cur sint traditae promissiones de rebus praesentibus. IIII. Quo ordine sint petendae. V. Quomodo fides exercenda sit, in petitione corporalium bonorum. VI. Applicatio huius historiae.

De primo.

Certum est, Evangelium principaliter tradere promissionem de rebus aeternis, videlicet, quod Filius Dei sit victima pro genere humano, et quod agenti poenitentiam, et credenti propter ipsum certo det Deus remissionem peccatorum, Spiritum sanctum, et vitam aeternam: econtra contemnentes Evangelium certo abiiciat in aeternas poenas.

Hanc revelationem voluntatis divinae depromtam ex sinu aeterni patris de rebus aeternis, sciamus praecipuam Evangelii vocem esse, sicut Christus inquit Iohan. 6.: Haec est voluntas patris, ut omnis qui credit in Filium, habeat vitam aeternam. Hanc doctrinam de rebus aeternis primum amplectamur, postea sciamus etiam promissiones additas esse Evangelio, de rebus praesentibus, ut Matth. 6.: Primum quaerite regnum Dei, et caetera adiicientur vobis. 1. Tim. 4.: Pietas ad omnia utilis est, promissiones habens praesentis vitae et futurae. Marci 10.: Qui reliquerit domum propter me et propter Evangelium, recipiet centuplum in tempore hoc, cum tribulatione, et in futuro vitam aeternam. Huc addantur multae promissiones ex Psalmis. Psal. 36.: In diebus famis saturabuntur. Item: Non vidi iustum derelictum, nec semen eius quaerens panem. 32.: Ut alat eos in fame. 33.: Non est inopia timentibus eum. 54.: Iacta super Dominum curam tuam, et ipse te enutriet. 111.: Beatus vir qui timet Dominum, opes et divitiae in domo eius. Tales sententias multas prodest in conspectu habere, ut nos erudiant et consolentur, ut postea dicam. Primum ergo meminerimus esse haec duo genera promissionum.

De secundo. Sed dicat aliquis: His largis promissionibus non videntur eventus respondere, magna imperia, magnae opes plerumque sunt apud impios.

Apostoli vagantur ut errones, mendici, et plerumque pii doctores esuriunt, sunt in odio, trucidantur, et vulgare dictum est: Probitas laudatur et alget. Item: Exeat aula, qui vult esse pius. Imo manifestum est, Ecclesiam subiectam esse cruci et sine praesidiis humanis esse. Ac vere nobis accidit, quod de se ac de universo grege suo dixit Christus: Filius hominis non habet ubi reclinet caput. Ad haec omnia respondeo: Etsi totum genus humanum obnoxium est morti et multis ingentibus calamitatibus, tamen certo consilio Dei magis premitur Ecclesia, videlicet, ut agnoscamus iram Dei adversus peccata, et sciamus servari Ecclesiam divinitus. Et tamen vult Deus in hac vita esse aliquam suam Ecclesiam, non vult totum genus humanum perire, sed aliquem esse florem, aliquem coetum, a quo agnoscatur, invocetur et celebretur, ut Amos 3.: Quomodo si eruat pastor de ore leonis duo crura, sic eruentur filii Israël. Mandavit igitur credi articulum: Credo Ecclesiam catholicam, id est, credo aliquem esse populum Dei, amplectentem verbum traditum per Prophetas et Apostolos, cui catholica Ecclesia testimonium perhibet, et credo talem aliquem coetum semper mansurum esse, sicut dixit: Ero vobiscum usque ad consummationem seculi etc.

Semper igitur haec duo coniungi necesse est, doctrinam de cruce, et de consolatione. Verum est Ecclesiam subiectam esse cruci, ut Christus inquit: Qui vult me sequi, tollat crucem suam. Et Ieremiae 12.: Dedi dilectam animam meam in manus inimicorum eius. Et tamen cum velit Deus manere Ecclesiam, quae tamen sine praesidiis humanis est, ipse proponit consolationes amplissimas et dulcissimas, de defensione, de victu, de pace, de successibus in nostris functionibus, ecclesiasticis, politicis, oeconomicis.

Et intelligamus promissiones, ut sonant, nec affingamus corruptelas et ineptas interpretationes, ut multi inepti in precatione usitata, panem nostrum quotidianum, vetant intelligi panem corporalem, imo de corporali pane, de defensione huius vitae, et de gubernatione loquitur, et quidem suppeditat haec bona Deus, et largitur iuxta suas promissiones.

Cur igitur non respondent eventus? Imo respondent, Ac primum de toto corpore Ecclesiae intelligantur promissiones, Ut in mari rubro, sic inter mundi tyrannides, et furores diaboli, assidue Deus Ecclesiam servat in hac vita. Perspicuum est igitur de toto corpore Ecclesiae ratas esse promissiones. Semper enim servatur Ecclesia, et nos in precationibus nostris, primum pro toto corpore petamus, et certo statuamus eam precationem non esse irritam.

De tertio.

Cur promissiones corporales, traditae sint.

Prima causa haec est: Mens humana sine luce fidei cogitat, aut casu ditescere homines, ut Pythium ex venis metallicis, aut industria, seu iusta seu iniusta, nec firmiter statuit aliquo Dei opere nobis offerri, defendi et augeri facultates. Videt enim multos crescere peculatu, et variis fraudibus, ut Crassum.

Etsi autem sinit Deus grassari fures et praedones publice et privatim aliquandiu, tamen tandem excutit eos ex fortunis, ut testetur se non negligere facultatum administrationes, aut acquisitiones, ideo dictum est: Vae qui praedaris, quia vicissim spoliaberis. Et ab experientia dictum illud ortum est: Male partum, male disperit. Et Pythium illum divitem fame periisse dicunt, et quam miserabilis fuerit exitus Crassi, legatur in eius historia,

Rursus etiam tradidit Deus promissiones iustis, ut vere statuant haec bona non obiici casu, nec parari tantum humana industria. Quanquam enim Deus vult laborare omnes, ut quemque iubet vocatio, et vult labore honesto res parari et retineri, non vult profusionibus dissipari, sicut dicitur in Salomone, Substantiam tuam ne des crudeli: tamen interim vult nos scire, hanc diligentiam solam non adferre facultates. Sicut agricolae labor solus non gignit fruges, sed quia Deus foecundat terram, proveniunt, et sicuti exercitus labor non solum parit victoriam, sed necesse est accedere auxilium divinum, sicuti dicitur: Fallax equus ad salutem est. Ita quia Deus fideliter servienti in vocatione favet, facultates sua bonitate provehit.

In hanc sententiam dicit Salomon: Benedictio Domini divites facit.

Et David 1. Reg. 17. Sciat universa Ecclesia haec, quod non in gladio salvat Dominus, ipsius est enim bellum.

Ideo et interdum exempla proponit, ubi sine causis secundis auget res, ut pavit viduam Sareptanam, pavit populum in deserto, dedit Isaac centuplum, cum in aliis agris non proveniret tantum. Et sunt quotidiana exempla in familiis piis, quae experiuntur sibi divinitus offerri accessiones, aut certe defendi suas res, etiamsi aliqua detrimenta, iacturae et aerumnae interveniunt.

Nam ut dictum est: Ecclesia simul subiecta est cruci.

Haec infigenda sunt animo, ut discamus articulum de Creatione, credamus facultates Dei beneficia esse, ut vere possimus a Deo petere panem quotidianum. Nam qui non credunt Dei munera haec esse, ociose haec verba recitant, et Deum contumelia adficiunt. Iam cogitemus quam pauci pie recitant haec verba: Panem quotidianum da nobis hodie. Nam alius fingit, Deo haec non esse curae, alius cogitat se indignum ease, sibi certe non dari haec munera a Deo, denique magnae sunt tenebrae in animis, quas per verbum Dei tolli oportet.

Altera causa est, cur hae promissiones traditae sint. Cum Deus velit in hac vita semper aliquam esse suam Ecclesiam, opus est corpori victu, hospitio, defensione, politiis, pace aliqua, ut educari soboles, et coli studia possint. Ideo et addidit has promissiones, et haec beneficia praestat Deus, sed mirabiliter.

grassatur diabolus adversus Ecclesiam, et sunt assidui tumultus in mundo, quibus humani generis peccata assidua horribiliter puniuntur, inter hos tumultus servat Deus Ecclesiam suam, ut stantem in mari rubro servabat. Et manet corpus, etiamsi aliqua membra trucidantur, ut manet Davidis exercitus, etiamsi aliqui milites praeliantes interficiuntur, quia ut toties dictum est, adhuc subiecta est cruci Ecclesia.

Magnam igitur consolationem proponunt nobis hae promissiones. Angimur in tantis tumultibus imperiorum, de sede Ecclesiae, de studiis: etsi autem alia tempora aliis sunt tranquilliora et feliciora, tamen sciamus, sedem Ecclesiae et studiorum Deo curae futurum esse, ubicunque erit, ut in Esaia dicitur: In utero meo portamini. Senescentem Ecclesiam portabo. Item: Etiamsi mater obliviscerentur filii sui, ego non obliviscar tui, pugillo manus meae complectar te. Has consolationes saepe nobis proponamus, ut bona cum spe propagemus doctrinam, et fide petamus haec bona a Deo.

Tertia igitur causa est, cur hae promissiones traditae sint, ut sint exercitia fidei et invocationis: vult Deus se agnosci per invocationem. Ideo multa proposuit, quae nos de invocatione admoneant. Tradidit promissiones gratiae, et beneficiorum corporalium, et vitae aeternae, vult nos ad se confugere, etiam cum a tota rerum natura deserti et proiecti videmur. Sicut David inquit: Pater et mater dereliquit me, Dominus autem suscepit me.

De quarto. Quo ordine sint petendae.

Ordo in dicto Christi clare propositus est: Primum quaerite regnum Dei, et caetera adiicientur vobis.

Prima sit cura, ut Deo obediamus, celebremus eum vera discendo et docendo.

Imo etiam primum petamus, ut accendat in nobis veram lucem Spiritu sancto suo propter Christum, sicut praecipitur: Petite, et accipietis. Si homines possunt bona dare hominibus, quanto magis pater coelestis dabit Spiritum sanctum petentibus?

Sic et David precatur: Fac cum servo tuo secundum misericordiam tuam, et iustificationes tuas doce me.

Sic et Salomon laudatur, quod primum petivit sapientiam, et additur: Ideo etiam divitias dabo. Et Proverb. 30. ostenditur ordo: Duo rogavi te, vanitatem et mendacium longe depelle a me. Mendacitatern et divitias ne dederis mihi, Et causas recitat, cur mediocritatem optat.

Quia opulenti facilius indulgent pravis cupiditatibus, et inter voluptates obliviscuntur Dei, et paulatim langius ruunt. Sicut Ezech. 16. dicitur: Haec fuit iniquitas Sodomae, superbia, saturitas panis, abundantia, ocium, et manum egenti non porrigebant. Ideo elevati sunt, et fecerunt abominationes.

Et noti sunt versiculi: Luxuriant animi rebus plerumque secundis, Nec facile est aequa commoda mente pati. Item: Pectora dum gaudent, nec sunt abstracta dolore Ipsa patent, blanda tunc subit arte Venus.

Ideo Salomon non petit opulentiam, sed tamen petit necessaria victui, ut textus loquitur, ne furta aut periuria committam. Nam ut opulentia alit voluptates, sic econtra, egestas multos impellit ad malas artes.

Haec pericula prospiciant honestae mentes in utraque parte, ut petant a Deo necessaria, sed ordine, ut dictum est. Sciant item, cum hac petitione facultatum postulari laborem honestum, iuxta vocationem, sicut saepe praecipitur, 1. Thes. 4.: Adhortamur vos, ut in hac re excellatis, et ambitiose hoc agatis, videlicet retinere tranquillitatem, et facere proprium officium, et laborare manibus vestris. Haec brevis sententia plena est politicae sapientiae, et diligenter consideranda. Nam omnibus civitatibus maxime periculosa sunt ingenia inquieta et πολυπραγμονικὰ. Ut multi sunt, qui quia habent ingenia inquieta, multa regere conantur, et condunt multas ordinationes, deinde nec manent intra metas sui officii, et attingunt aliena. Sic Alcibiades et Demosthenes everterunt Athenas. Tantum enim ideo moverunt non necessarios tumultus, quia habebant naturas inquietas. Ideo praecipit Paulus, ut simus quieti, non turbulenti, id est, nihil nisi necessaria moveamus, nihil extra vocationem tentemus. Seneca recitat ex Catone dictum: Emas non quod opus est, sed quod necesse est. Idem in negotiis servetur. Non solum quid prosit aut opus sit spectemus, sed quid necesse sit moveri. Et apud Thucydiden dicitur, oportere esse amantem tranquillitatis, et tunc cum necesse est aliquid gerere acrem, non turbulentum in movendo, et in agendo segnem.

XII. ANNOTATIONES IN EVANGELIA. Haec de labore simul cogitanda sunt, quoties petimus corporalia, quia ignavia peccatum est. Et quale monstrum est homo, qui tantum inutile pondus est terrae, nihil confert operarum ad Dei notitiam propagandam, aut caeteras bonas res in vita tuendas et ornandas. Imo ad Titum nominatim praecipitur, ut discamus utilia vitae.

Interim vero sciamus, Deum ita benedicere labori, cum addimus invocationem, sicut Lucae 5. dicitur: In verbo tuo laxabo rete. Et Psal. 33.: Iste pauper clamavit ad Dominum, et Dominus exaudivit eum. Item: Petite, et accipietis.

De quinto.

Quomodo sit exercenda fides in petitione corporalium.

Hic praecipuus locus est in hac doctrina de promissionibus.

Primum autem sciendum est, semper petitioni corporalium oportet praelucere fidem, qua credimus nos propter Christum recipi et exaudiri. Imo ut haec fides in nobis accendatur et crescat, ideo tam variae externae occasiones, actiones, pericula, afflictiones propositae sunt. Sciamus ergo primam et summam promissionem de mediatore, et de reconciliatione, semper simul complectendam esse. Ideo cum citantur dicta de fide, etiamsi externa obiecta variant, tamen omnia simul complectuntur hanc fidem de reconciliatione.

Abraham, Iacob, David ideo petunt et expectant a Deo defensionem, quia credunt se receptos esse, et exaudiri a Deo propter promissum Dominum. Quotidie igitur cum ad mensam recitas haec verba, Panem nostrum quotidianum da nobis hodie, quia mox obstrepit infirmitas nostra, Deus te indignum non exaudit, te non vult defensum aut alitum. Hic intuenda est promissio de Christo, et complectenda fides, quod propter mediatorem recipiamur et exaudiamur. Ideo mox sequitur: Et remitte nobis debita nostra. Semper igitur in conspectu sit haec sententia: Per Christum habemus accessum ad patrem, ideo necesse est semper praelucere hanc fidem de remissione peccatorum propter Christum.

Postea fides illa tria cogitet, quae supra recensui, Deum vella a se peti bona corporis. Primum, Ut cedamus ea dari divinitus, non putemus obiici casu. Secundo, Quia vult servari Ecclesiam in hac vita, dat victum, defensionem, hospitia mirabiliter etc. Tertio, Vult agnosci ac coli Deus hac invocatione, ideo multas res proposuit, quas peti vult, vult et confirmari fidem, petitione corporalium.

Nam qui non audet petere corporalia, et iam dubitat de praesentia Dei, cum deserimur ab omnibus creaturis? Esaiae 57.: Habitans cum contrito et humili spiritu, ut vivificet spiritum humilium, et cor contritorum. Confirmatur etiam fides, cum experientia ostendit non fuisse irritam precationem, ut in Psalmo dicitur: Iste pauper clamavit ad Dominum, et Dominus exaudivit eum.

Postremo vult etiam Deus gratiarum actione coli propter liberationes, ut dulcissime dicitur 2. Cor. 1., ubi Paulus iubet multos pro se petere, ut multi agant gratias etc. Hic ordo et hae causae omnes cogitandae sunt, cum petimus corporalia.

Et satis magna pericula sunt, publica et privata, quae admonent nos ut haec cogitemus. Cum Ecclesia staret in mari rubro, certe cogitandum fuit primum Moisi, an Deo placeret, et cur placeret, scilicet propter promissum Dominum. Deinde vidit reipsa salutem corporum a Deo dari, cogitavit Deum in hac vita velle servare Ecclesiam, cogitavit item Deum velle in nobis crescere agnitionem in invocatione, inter talia pericula et miracula. Semper autem Ecclesia versatur in periculis ingentibus, pene ut stans in mari rubro: iam Turcica arma in eam grassantur, et aliae multae difficultates domesticae singulos exercent.

Nulli certa sedes est, vita multorum piorum periclitatur: admoniti ergo publicis et nostris periculis, petamus auxilium et defensionem, illo ordine, ut dictum est, et causas illas cogitemus, ut fides exerceatur. Deinde vero etiam consecuti beneficia, gratias agamus, et maiori studio in omni officio declaremus gratitudinem.

Sed hic obiicit humana imbecillitas, Quid attinet petere, cum sciamus oportere nos adfligi? sicut scriptum est, Corpus autem subiectum est morti propter peccatum. Item, manifestum est saepissime non liberari ex praesentibus calamitatibus sanctos, ut Ionathan, Maccabaeum, et alios. Et Christus dicit: Veruntamen non mea voluntas, sed tua. Cum igitur debeamus offerre obedientiam, quid prodest petitio, et quidem cum dubitatione? Respondeo.

Tenenda est regula firmissime, quod Deus mandaverit et postulet invocationem, et quod nunquam sit inanis aut irrita invocatio piorum, etiamsi liberatio differtur, aut non ita respondent eventus, ut nos imaginamur, et non est nostrum praescribere Deo modum opitulandi, sed nos ad obedientiam obligati sumus, sicut Christus inquit: Tua voluntas fiat etc.

Sed maxima pars hominum, quia non videt subito eventus precationis, somniat invocationem inane murmur esse. Huic impiae imaginationi acerrime repugnandum est, et pellendae sunt hae tenebrae collectis promissionibus: Invoca me in die tribulationis, et eripiam te. Item: Petite, et accipietis etc.

Deinde sciamus semper duo obiecta includenda esse in petitionem corporalium, universam Ecclesiam, et privatam necessitatem.

Petitio pii semper impetrat universae Ecclesiae, et ita fides statuat ratam esse hanc petitionem, et non dubitet recipi petitionem a Deo pro universa Ecclesia. Ita David orans pro exercitu, primum petit non pro se privatim, sed pro coetu, quia scimus Deum dare bona corporalia, ut in hac vita Ecclesia servetur. Privatim vero pro nobis petere debemus, cum hac conditione, ut nos ad obedientiam offeramus, sicut se offert Christus.

Ita David et petit, et paratus est ad obedientiam. Quia scit in talibus periculis Deum velle aliquos obedire, et tamen quia servatur exercitus, multa membra servari necesse est, et caeteris mitigatur malum. Sic Ieremiae precatio proderat primum populo, etsi non sciebat quos et quomodo servaturus esset Deus, deinde et ipsi proderat, et tamen ipse ad obedientiam paratus erat, et sciebat Deum servare suos ministros, donec curriculum absolvant, et dare aliis aliud curriculum.

Elias circiter viginti annos docuit. Elisaeus circiter septuaginta. Esaias circiter octaginta. Ieremias quadraginta annis usque ad excidium Ierosolymae, et postea aliquandiu in Aegypto reliquiis suorum praefuit, donec ab Aprye tyranno interfectus est. Daniel docuit amplius septuaginta annis. Iohannes Baptista biennio. Christus triennio. Paulus triginta quinque annis. Iohannes Apostolus sexaginta octo annis, Iacobus frater Iohannis triennio post ascensionem Christi. Iacobus minor annis triginta, interfectus aliquanto ante obsidionem Ierosolymae. Timotheus sub Nerone interfectus dicitur. Titi senectus recitatur, tempus praedicationis non certo scitur, sed dicunt mortuum esse anno aetatis suae nonagesimo quarto. Polycarpus interfectus est anno aetatis suae octuagesimo sexto, qui adolescens fuerat auditor Iohannis Evangelistae. Auditor Polycarpi Irenaeus sub Maximiano interfectus est Syrmii, vixit igitur annos interim circiter octoginta. Haec dissimilitudo observanda est, ut sciamus Deum alia certamina, et alia spacia aliis praescripsisse, et tamen consideremus aliquibus prorogatam esse vitam, ut pii testes et propagatores doctrinae superstites essent.

David petens defensionem dulcissima figura utitur: Absconde me in tabernaculo tuo, id est, in Ecclesia tua.

Hic simul complectitur petitionem pro aliis, et causam, Defende me cum Ecclesia tua, et propter Ecclesiam. Nam ideo tantum corporalia bona promissa sunt, ut serviant Ecclesiae, ideo defensio petitur, ut servire Ecclesiae et nostris liberis possumus. Et quia Deus pro toto corpore vult peti, sciamus semper hanc petitionem ratam esse, et toti corpori aliquid boni impetrare. Etsi autem singuli ad obedientiam parati esse debemus, tamen et singulis saepe impetratur liberatio, et cum coetus aliquis servatur, multos servari necesse est. Excitemus ergo nos ad petenda bona corporalia collectis causis, quia Deus praecipit ea peti pro nobis et pro aliis, vult intelligi publicas et privatas calamitates poenas esse peccatorum mundi: ideo vult nos veniam petere, et affici cura nostrae et communis salutis, vult crescere his exercitiis, fidem, timorem, et dilectionem.

De sexto. Applicatio historiae Marci 8.

Quod Christus pascit auditores suos, ostenditur exemplum promissionis: Primum quaerite regnum Dei, et caetera adiicientur vobis.

Hac fide sequamur Christum, simus fideles in studio et propagatione Evangelii, et expectemus a Filio Dei auxilium, victum, et defensionem.

Quod vero iubet Apostolos proponere, et colligere reliquias, monent gubernatores Ecclesiae, ut curent eleemosynas dari, et sciant non minui, sed augeri facultates eleemosynis.

Tecte et doctrinam significat, hanc proponant doctores, et colligant reliquias, curent propagari veras enarrationes, ne doctrinae lux extinguatur ad posteros, et hoc studio ipsi doctores fiunt eruditiores.

Sportae vero significant literas et scholas, in quibus doctrinam custodiri necesse est.

# Luke

## 1:26-38 On the Day of the Annunciation of Mary. Concerning the Conceived Christ
On the day of the Annunciation of Mary. Concerning the conceived Christ. Gospel of Luke 1.

In the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God into a city of Galilee, whose name was Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David, and the name of the virgin was Mary. And the angel having entered to her, said: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you, blessed are you among women. But she, when she had seen him, was troubled at his speech, and was thinking what manner of salutation this might be. And the angel said to her: Fear not, Mary, for you have found grace with God. Behold, you shall conceive in your womb, and shall bring forth a son, and shall call his name Jesus. He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Most High. And the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of David his father, and he shall reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there shall be no end. But Mary said to the angel: How shall this be, since I know not a man? And the angel answering, said to her: The Holy Spirit shall come upon you, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow you. And therefore also that which shall be born holy, shall be called the Son of God. And behold, Elisabeth your kinswoman, she also has conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her, who is called barren, because no word shall be impossible with God. But Mary said: Behold the handmaid of the Lord, be it done to me according to your word. And the angel departed from her.

There are five principal points.

I. Concerning the state of the Jewish kingdom at that time, and the form of the Church.

II. Mary's consternation.

III. The angel's narrative concerning the eternal kingdom.

IIII. The testimony that Christ was conceived without male seed.

V. Concerning these words: The Holy Spirit shall overshadow you.

On the first.

…It is of the greatest importance that the form of the Church be considered at all times, lest on account of the multitude, the empires, and the power of the wicked, we stray from the true Church. Herod had now held the royal name among this people for 36 years, but because he was a foreigner, the princes and chief priests refused to obey him, because they knew that the kingdom had been promised to the lineage of Judah. And since they interpreted the promises wrongly, they hoped that God would be present to them as they expelled Herod. With this hope, they stirred up constant riots, and they stirred them up unsuccessfully; nor did Herod only conquer by slaughtering many thousands, but he also utterly destroyed the principal college or council, which they called the Sanhedrin, which was the highest in that people, instituted for the preservation of doctrine and religion. These things happened in this way because it had been predicted that Christ would come when the lineage of Judah was oppressed by servitude.

And let us remember that this servitude and these miseries were punishments. For first the brothers, the sons of Hyrcanus, then the grandsons, had contended for the kingdom with acts of parricide. The Sadducees and Pharisees were also in honor, who had oppressed the true doctrine. Therefore these punishments followed, just as now the world is oppressed by most sad servitude under the Turks and others, because of idols, lusts, and other crimes.

Consider, however, that then, amidst such great dissipations of the kingdom and doctrine, the remnants of the true Church were nevertheless preserved: Zechariah, Elizabeth, Joseph, Mary, Simeon, Anna, and many others, who still retained the pure doctrine of the Prophets, and in these miseries, while they sought consolation from the reading of the Prophets, they learned much, and daily prayer taught them much.

But so that Mary might believe the angel, a miracle concerning the pregnant old woman is added; therefore mention is made of the number of months since Elizabeth's conception: this time was expected so that it might now be certain that that old woman was pregnant. The angel therefore alleges this testimony: Believe, he says, my voice, because God proposes to you the testimony of my mission, that this old woman has been made pregnant.

On the second.

All the works of God in men happen in such a way that at the beginning their minds are terrified, according to that: Where will the Lord dwell? In a contrite and humbled spirit, and one that trembles at my words, because God wants us first to acknowledge our infirmity, He wants us to be terrified, so that He may afterwards console us, just as it is written: He leads to the underworld, and afterwards leads back. Likewise: He gives grace to the humble. Furthermore, the nature of man without divine confirmation cannot even sustain God, whether He is speaking by Himself, or through angels, or through men; whenever the heart is struck by the word of God, it is terrified, just as the people cry out at Mount Sinai: Let not the Lord speak to us, lest we die. But in these very terrors, those who believe are raised up again by the voice of the Gospel, just as here Mary hears this voice: Do not fear, for you have found grace with God.

Examples are everywhere obvious in the scriptures, which show that this is the order, as often as God speaks, that terrors precede, and consolation follows: this order is also seen in conversion. David, Paul, are rebuked, and they are terrified; afterwards they are raised up. And in the sermons of this feast, Bernard discusses this matter, and hands down a memorable sentence about faith: Do not only believe this, that sins are remitted, but that they are remitted freely, and believe that they are remitted to you on account of Christ. By this faith the Apostle says that a man is justified.

On the third.

The angel affirms that Mary will be pregnant, and will give birth to the son promised through the fathers and Prophets, and in a long narration he recites the very words of the promises. Think, however, how much consolation this great matter brought to a pious mind, especially when looking at the most miserable dissipation of the Church of that time, which was greatly attenuated. The angel recites the words of the promise, and clearly says that this child born will reign without end. Such cannot be an empire in this mortal nature. Nor is there any doubt that these things were explained to many, just as immediately afterwards the angel says to Joseph: He will save the people from their sins. What is this? He will not only remit them in this life, but will truly abolish them, having given a new life in the resurrection.

And to this point must be referred the sentences of the Prophets, which speak about the abolishing of sin and the abolishing of death, and about the granting of a new and perpetual life and righteousness. As: O death, I will be your death. Likewise: I will strike a new covenant, I will give my law into their hearts. There will therefore be such a kingdom, in which Christ, living an eternal life, will reign among those gifted with eternal life.

On the fourth.

…This passage is a testimony of the article that Christ was conceived by the efficacy of the Holy Spirit, without male seed, as it is clearly said in Matthew 1: That which is born in her is from the Holy Spirit. That testimony let it be transferred to this passage of Luke. But Mary is confirmed by an example; the old woman Elizabeth is already pregnant, and since that example is above nature, you should also believe my voice, promising a thing above the order of nature. The testimony of Isaiah pertains to this: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and his name shall be called Immanuel. For because an unclean nature is propagated by the commingling of seeds, and is infected by the disease of origin, therefore God willed that Christ be born without any commingling, and yet that he might be the seed of Abraham and David, a mass was taken, sanctified by the Holy Spirit from the virgin, as it is said to the Galatians, born of a woman. This example also warns that divine promises are exhibited miraculously, and far otherwise than human reason expects. These things must be meditated upon piously, and at the same time the causes of this admirable counsel must always be embraced, why the Son of God had to be sent, why God willed such wondrous things to happen. Because all these things are outside the view of human reason, profane men mock them, but let us know that God truly exists, and that it was revealed in the word which He gave to the fathers from the beginning, by which He testifies that wrath against sin is not a light matter, and that it had to be appeased by the Son as mediator.

Concerning the fifth.

The figure is taken from history, which narrates that the people in the desert were covered by a cloud, which provided shade by day, but light by night. And as that was a wondrous consolation then, and a testimony of the presence of God. So let the pious always know that they are thus ruled by night, that is, in darkness, dangers, and death, and that light, counsel, consolation, and life are ministered to them. Again, in the heat, shade, that is, in punishment, sustenance, lest the weak nature be consumed by divine terrors, just as it says in Psalm 89 concerning the judgment and wrath of God: You have set our iniquities before you. In your wrath we have failed. Likewise, Deut. 4: Your God is a consuming fire. Finally, no man can sustain the judgment or the work of God, unless an overshadowing occurs, that is, unless the mercy of God cherishes and vivifies man.

Therefore, mention is made here of overshadowing. And just as it is said here of Mary, so let us know universally that the Church is cherished by overshadowing, just as it is said in Isaiah 4: And the Lord will create over every place of Mount Zion, and where He is invoked, a cloud by day, and a flaming light by night, and against the brightness a covering, and a shade from the heat by day. If this promise is compared to the external appearance of the Church, nothing similar will be seen. For it has no human protections, it is pressed by huge hardships, and is most cruelly torn by tyrants. But let us know that the promise is truly understood as the overshadowing in the judgment of God, by which we know that we are truly received through mercy, and become heirs of eternal life, and are cherished, lest we be consumed by eternal wrath.

Afterwards, let us know concerning bodily defense, that some assembly is preserved, even if the members are torn and exercised by afflictions, as it is said in Amos: Behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon the sinful kingdom, that I may destroy it from the face of the earth. But I will not destroy Jacob, but I will shake it as wheat in a sieve, and not a grain shall fall upon the earth.

Latin:

Die annunciationis Mariae. De concepto Christo. Evangelium Lucae 1.

In mense sexto missus est angelus Gabriel a Deo in civitatem Galilae, cui nomen Nazareth, ad virginem desponsatam viro, cui nomen erat Ioseph, de domo David, et nomen virginis Maria. Et ingressus angelus ad eam, dixit: Ave gratiosa, Dominus tecum, benedicta tu in mulieribus. Illa vero cum vidisset, turbata est in sermone eius, et cogitabat, qualis esset ista salutatio. Et ait angelus ei: Ne timeas Maria, invenisti enim gratiam apud Deum, Ecce concipies in utero, et paries filium, et vocabis nomen eius Iesum, Hic erit magnus, et filius altissimi vocabitur. Et dabit illi Dominus Deus, sedem David patris sui, et regnabit super domum Iacob in aeternum, et regni eius non erit finis. Dixit autem Maria ad angelum: Quomodo fiet istud, quoniam virum non cognosco? Et respondens angelus, dixit ei: Spiritus sanctus superveniet in te, et virtus altissimi obumbrabit te. Ideoque et quod nascetur sanctum, vocabitur Filius Dei. Et ecce Elisabeth cognata tua, et ipsa concepit filium in senectute sua, et hic mensis est sextus illi, quae vocatur sterilis, quia non erit impossibile apud Deum omne verbum. Dixit autem Maria: Ecce ancilla Domini, fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum. Et discessit ab illa angelus.

Quinque sunt loci praecipui.

I. De statu regni Iudaici eo tempore, et de forma Ecclesiae.

II. Mariae consternatio.

III. Angeli narratio de regno aeterno.

IIII. Testimonium, quod Christus sine virili semine conceptus sit.

V. De his verbis: Obumbrabit te Spiritus sanctus.

De primo.

Plurimum conducit formam Ecclesiae omnibus temporibus considerari, ne propter multitudinem, imperia, potentiam impiorum, a vera Ecclesia aberremus. Herodes iam annos 36 tenuerat nomen regium in hoc populo, sed quia peregrinus erat, principes et pontifices ei parere recusabant, quia sciebant stirpi Iuda regnum pro- missum esse. Et cum male accommodarent pro- missiones, sperabant Deum adfuturum esse ipsis expellentibus Herodem. Hac spe assiduos tumul- tus movebant, et movebant infeliciter, nec vin- cebat tantum Herodes trucidatis multis millibus, sed etiam praecipuum collegium seu concilium, quod vocabant Sanhedrin, funditus delevit, quod fuit summum in isto populo, ad doctrinae et re- ligionis conservationem institutum. Haec ita fie- bant, quia praedictum erat, tunc venturum esse Christum, cum stirps Iuda esset oppressa ser- vitute.

Et meminerimus hanc servitutem, et has miserias fuisse poenas. Nam prius fratres filii Hircani, deinde nepotes de regno certaverant par- ricidiis. Erant et in honore Zaducaei et Phari- saei, qui oppresserant veram doctrinam. Ideo hae poenae secutae sunt, sicut nunc mundus tristissima servitute sub Turcis et aliis premitur, propter idola, libidines, et alia flagitia.

Consideres autem tunc inter tantas dissipa- tiones regni et doctrinae, tamen servatas esse re- liquias verae Ecclesiae, Zachariam, Elisabeth, Ioseph, Mariam, Simeonem, Annam, et alios multos, qui adhuc puram doctrinam Propheta- rum retinuerunt, et in his miseriis, dum pete- rent ex lectione Prophetarum consolationem, mul- ta didicerunt et multa eos quotidiana precatio docuit.

Ut autem Maria credat angelo, additur mi- raculum de gravida anu, ideo fit mentio numeri mensium a conceptu Elisabeth: hoc tempus ex- pectatum est, ut iam certo constaret anum illam esse gravidam. Allegat igitur angelus hoc testi- monium: Credas, inquit, voci meae, quia Deus proponit tibi testimonium meae legationis, quod haec anus sit gravida facta.

De secundo.

Omnia opera Dei in hominibus ita fiunt, ut initio expavescant animi, iuxta illud: Ubi habi- tabit Dominus? in spiritu contrito et humiliato, et tremente sermones meos, quia Deus vult pri- mum agnoscere nos nostram infirmitatem, vult nos perterrefieri, ut postea consoletur, sicut scri- ptum est: Deducit ad inferos, et postea reducit. Item: Humilibus dat gratiam. Praeterea natura hominis sine confirmatione divina ne potest qui- dem sustinere Deum, sive per se loquentem, sive per angelos, sive per homines, quandocunque cor feritur verbo Dei, expavescit, sicut clamat populus ad montem Sina: Non loquatur nobis Dominus, ne moriamur. Sed in his ipsis terro- ribus illi, qui credunt, rursus eriguntur voce Evangelii, sicut hic Maria audit hanc vocem: Ne timeas, invenisti enim gratiam apud Deum.

Exempla sunt passim obvia in scripturis, quae ostendunt hunc esse ordinem, quoties Deus loquitur, ut praecedant terrores, sequatur con- solatio: hic ordo etiam in conversione cernitur. David, Paulus, arguuntur, et expavescunt, post- ea eriguntur. Et in concionibus huius festi Ber- nardus de hac re disserit, et memorabilem sen- tentiam tradit de fide: Non solum hoc credas, remitti peccata, sed gratis remitti, et tibi remitti credas propter Christum. Hac fide Apostolus ait, Iustificari hominem.

De tertio.

Angelus adfirmat Mariam gravidam fore, et parituram filium promissum per patres et Pro- phetas, et longa narratione recitat ipsa verba pro- missionum. Cogita autem, quantam consolatio- nem piae menti haec tanta res attulerit, praeser- tim intuenti miserrimam dissipationem Ecclesiae eius temporis, quae admodum erat attenuata. Recitat autem angelus verba promissionis, et cla- re inquit, hunc natum regnaturum esse sine fine. Tale non potest esse imperium in hac mortali na- tura. Nec dubium est, haec pluribus explicata esse, sicut statim post angelus ad Ioseph inquit: Liberabit populum a peccatis. Quid hoc est? non solum remittet in hac vita, sed vere abolebit, data nova vita in resurrectione.

Et huc referendae sunt sententiae Propheta- rum, quae de abolendo peccato et de abolenda morte, de donanda nova et perpetua vita et iu- sticia loquuntur. Ut: O mors, ero mors tua. Item: Feriam novum pactum, dabo legem meam in corda eorum. Erit igitur tale regnum, in quo Christus vivens vita aeterna regnabit inter dona- tos vita aeterna.

De quarto.

Hic locus testimonium est articuli, quod Christus conceptus sit efficacia Spiritus sancti, sine virili semine, ut Matth. 1. clare dicitur: Quod in ea natum est, est a Spiritu sancto. Id testimo- nium transferatur ad hunc locum Lucae. Confirmatur autem Maria exemplo, iam est gravida anus Elisabeth, id exemplum cum sit supra naturam, credas etiam meae voci, rem supra naturae ordinem promittenti. Pertinet huc testimonium Esaiae: Ecce virgo erit gravida, et pariet filium, et vocabitur nomen eius Emanuel. Quia enim commixtione seminum propagatur immunda natura, et infecta morbo originis, ideo Deus voluit nasci Christum sine ulla commixtione, et tamen ut esset semen Abrahae et Davidis, sumta est massa sanctificata per Spiritum sanctum ex virgine, ut ad Galat. dicitur, natum ex muliere. Monet et hoc exemplum mirabiliter exhiberi promissiones divinas, ac longe aliter, quam expectat humana ratio. Haec pie meditanda sunt, et semper simul causae huius admirandi consilii complectendae sunt, cur Filius Dei fuerit mittendus, cur tam miras res fieri Deus voluerit. Haec omnia quia sunt extra conspectum humanae rationis, prophani homines derident, sed nos sciamus vere esse Deum, et patefactum esse in verbo, quod ab initio dedit patribus, quo testatur iram adversus peccatum non esse rem levem, et ita fuisse placandam Filio mediatore.

De quinto.

Figura sumta est ex historia, quae narrat, populum in deserto nube tectum fuisse, quae interdiu umbram praebuerit, nocte vero lucem. Et ut tunc fuit miranda consolatio, et testimonium praesentiae Dei. Ita semper pii sciant sic se regi nocte, id est, in tenebris, periculis et morte, ministrari lucem, consilium, consolationem et vitam. Rursus in aestu umbram, id est, in poena sustentationem, ne imbecillis natura terroribus divinis consumatur, sicut de indicio et ira Dei Psalm. 89. inquit: Posuisti iniquitates nostras in conspectu tuo. In ira tua defecimus. Item, Deut. 4.: Deus tuus ignis consumens est. Denique nemo hominum sustinere iudicium vel opus Dei potest, nisi fiat obumbratio, id est, nisi misericordia Dei foveat et vivificet hominem.

Ideo et hic fit mentio obumbrationis. Et sicut hic de Maria dicitur, ita universaliter sciamus obumbratione foveri Ecclesiam, sicut et Esa. 4. dicitur: Et creabit Dominus super omnem locum montis Zion, et ubi invocatur, nubem per diem, et flammam lucentem in nocte, et adversus fulgorem tegmentum, et obumbraculum diei ab aestu. Si haec promissio conferatur ad externam speciem Ecclesiae, nihil simile videbitur. Nulla enim habet humana praesidia, premitur ingentibus aerumnis, et crudelissime laceratur a tyrannis. Sciamus autem promissionem revera intelligi de obumbratione in iudicio Dei, qua scimus nos per misericordiam vere recipi, et fieri haeredes vitae aeternae, et foveri, ne ira aeterna consumamur.

Postea sciamus de corporali defensione, servari coetum aliquem, etiam si membra lacerantur et exercentur afflictionibus, sicut in Amos dicitur: Ecce oculi Domini super regnum peccans, ut conterat illud a facie terrae. Iacob autem non conteram, sed concutiam ut triticum in cribro, et non cadet granum super terram.

## 1:39-41 Day of the Visitation of Mary
Gospel for the day of the Visitation of Mary.

Luke 1.

In those days, Mary rising went into the hill country with haste into the city of Judah, and entered into the house of Zacharias, and saluted Elisabeth. And it came to pass, that when Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the infant leaped in her womb, And Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit. And she cried out with a loud voice, and she said: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. And whence is this to me, that the mother of the Lord should come to me? For behold, as the voice of thy salutation sounded in my ears, the infant in my womb leaped for joy, And blessed is she that believed, because those things shall be accomplished, which were spoken to her by the Lord.

And Mary said: My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour, Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. Because he that is mighty hath done great things to me; and holy is his name. And his mercy is from generation unto generations, to them that fear him. He hath shewed might in his arm: he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart. He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away. He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy. As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever. And Mary abode with her about three months, and returned to her own house.

This is a most beautiful history, and full of spiritual and Christian doctrine. It has, however, three principal points.

I. The testimony concerning the Messiah. II. The image of the Church and of a true synod. III. The Canticle of Mary.

Concerning the first.

There is a great difference between the Church and the empires of the world. The Church is a small assembly of those who retain the pure doctrine of the Gospel and believe in Christ, scattered, despised, and rejected in the world, which admires the power, glory, victories, and triumphs of great empires. And yet this small assembly of the Church truly performs the greatest things. Although, therefore, the actions of Christ are not seen in the world like the deeds of Alexander or Caesar, yet He is not entirely unknown, and He has His testimonies: because there must be some Church in which God wills that He and His Son be known, and wills that some assembly be saved, in which He Himself is celebrated in eternal life; therefore He exhibited many testimonies to confirm our faith regarding all the articles, that this is the Christ exhibited according to the promises.

Thus, here, immediately upon Christ being conceived, testimonies are recited. The witnesses come together: Mary, Elisabeth, an old woman pregnant by a singular miracle of God, the infant leaping in the womb, Zacharias, to whom, though hitherto mute, speech is suddenly restored, and others in this family. For Mary sets out to her kinswoman, not for the sake of private friendship, but for the sake of this illustrious testimony, and for the confirmation of her own faith and that of other saints.

Concerning the second. One must consider the image of the Church and seek consolation from this passage, so that we do not fall away from the truth, deceived by the appearance and title of the Church.

The Pontiffs, Bishops, Kings, and those addicted to them call themselves the Church; just as once Caiphas, Annas, the Pharisees, and the Sadducees did, but they are not the Church. Meanwhile, there is another small, true Church, as Paul says: Not all who are of Israel are Israel. Therefore, just as then Zacharias, Elisabeth, Mary, and a few others were the Church, so now there is a small number of those who believe in Christ and rightly worship God, and this assembly is persecuted by the pontiffs and bishops, just as then Caiphas and his like were the enemies of the saints. For it is said that Zacharias was also killed because he affirmed that the Messiah had come, as Epiphanius writes.

And this meeting of Mary, Elisabeth, and Zacharias is an image of a true, pious, and Christian synod: for this was the first council of the new Church. The maiden Mary came for 20 miles, for that was about the distance from Nazareth to Jerusalem; there she tells her kinswoman Elisabeth and the family about her conception and the testimony of the angel; Elisabeth in turn bears testimony to her, and Zacharias the elder, whose piety is publicly known, and who, from being mute, suddenly speaks, confirms these testimonies with his own voice. Thus, in this assembly, it is concluded concerning the highest and most serious article, the conceived and exhibited Messiah, and it is a true and ratified definition of a most holy synod, even if the decree or approval of the Pontiffs and Pharisees is not added.

To these testimonies are added the Canticles, or thanksgiving, so that a confession may exist even for posterity, and this great benefit of God may be preached, that having had mercy on His people, He sent His Son. Mary wills that this be acknowledged and celebrated openly. She does not will that the truth be hidden or suppressed, but that the knowledge of true doctrine exist, so that God may be acknowledged and glorified, so that He may be rightly worshipped and invoked.

so that God may be acknowledged and glorified, that He may be rightly worshipped and invoked. God approves of such councils that seek the truth and bear witness to Christ according to the word of God, not those that overwhelm the truth with the deceits of sophisms and specious articles.

Concerning the third. Concerning the Canticle of Mary.

In this canticle, Mary bears the person of the whole Church. For it is a confession concerning the Messiah and an act of thanksgiving, and a description of the victory of the Church against the world, tyrants, and all the members of the devil. Wherefore let us also know that it is required of us that we truly sing together and follow this precentor, who, as the leader in the choir, begins this song and brings forth the confession with a great spirit. It therefore comprehends three things.

I. An act of thanksgiving. My soul doth magnify the Lord. That is, with my whole soul, with all my soul, with my whole heart I glorify God. I do not hesitate to offer my life in jeopardy for the sake of the confession.

Thus we also ought to be affected, that we prefer the confession to all things, to life, to possessions, to children. He who is so affected truly sings this hymn, My soul doth magnify the Lord. When John the Baptist, Paul, and the like were being dragged to death, then they truly said: My soul doth magnify the Lord. Thus are Christians most valiant soldiers; they think, My soul doth magnify the King for whom I fight; I cast my life and all things into jeopardy, that I may fight for the King, that He may be great and victorious.

The second part of the Canticle.

He hath regarded the humility of his handmaid. He that is mighty hath done to me great things, etc. This is a narrative of the benefits which God effects in the Church. Though the Church be despised, humble, small, yet God gives it victories, preserves it against tyrants and the wisdom of the world. This is the sum of this part. Mary speaks of herself, but not only of herself alone, but of the whole body of the Church.

God hath regarded the humility, that is, the misery of His handmaid. Although we are abject, although we are weak, without protection, without human defense, yet God regards us, hears us, helps us against the tyrants and the wise of the world. Here let us learn that in the Church alone God is thus acknowledged, that He is a God who forgives sins and hears miserable believers. Human reason and all religions, except the evangelical, think otherwise of God. They have such an opinion that God does not care, does not regard the afflicted. And it is a singular and secret wisdom, and of those alone who believe in Christ, to raise themselves by faith, and to believe in the remission of sins, and to seek and expect help, etc.

Then these things come to pass: He hath shewed strength with his arm, etc., He preserves the Church amidst dangers, just as He preserved the elect when they were being led into the Babylonian captivity. He scatters the proud who are confident in their own wisdom, just as He confounded the magicians of Pharaoh; so now He confounds the Papists and others who are confident in their own wisdom. O great sin, that the wise do not understand: that they wish to rule and change the Church by their own counsels. Of these it is said: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise. He puts down the mighty from their seat, just as He destroyed the Romans who were persecuting Christ. He exalts the humble. He fills the hungry with good things, He consoles, He preserves the Church.

The third part, Confession concerning the Messiah.

The third part is the confession proper to that council, that the Messiah having been given, God was mindful of His promises. This is the sum of the Canticle. So let us also give thanks, and when we recite this Canticle, let us look with our mind upon the whole Church, let us consider what kind of struggles there are in the Church on account of the confession, which God defends by His wonderful works. Let us consider that a confession is required of us, let us consider this to be the highest worship, which this maiden, that is, the whole true Church, performs: to preach God because He gave the Messiah, because He chose the Church to live forever, because He defends and preserves it, not by human strength or counsels. These things are to be learned in the reading of this history, what the true Church is, and what are the true forms of worship, and they are to be repeated in the mind, the testimonies concerning Christ, that we may confirm our faith and stir ourselves up to invocation.

There remains the example of the infant John, who in the womb felt the presence of the Lord and Messiah. Although this is peculiar to John, yet it is a testimony that the Holy Spirit is effective even in little children, and that they have certain motions, although unknown to us, yet pleasing to God. Therefore, when you hear, Of such is the kingdom of heaven, you should think of the Spirit in infants holy, to effect certain motions, such as those of the saints, who are members of the kingdom of heaven, that is, of the true Church. And these pious motions are excited by the word, as it is said here: After your voice sounded, etc.

Latin:

Evangelium die visitationis Mariae.

Lucae 1.

In diebus illis, exurgens Maria abiit in montana cum festinatione in civitatem Iuda, et intravit in domum Zachariae, et salutavit Elisabeth. Et factum est, ut audivit salutationem Mariae Elisabeth, saliit infans in utero eius, Et repleta est Spiritu sancto Elisabeth. Et exclamavit voce magna, et dixit: Benedicta tu inter mulieres, et benedictus fructus ventris tui. Et unde hoc mihi, ut veniat mater Domini ad me? Ecce enim, ut facta est vox salutationis tuae in auribus meis, saliit prae exultatione infans in utero meo, Et beata quae credidit, quoniam perficientur ea, quae dicta sunt ei a Domino.

Et ait Maria: Magnificat anima mea Dominum. Et exultavit spiritus meus in deo salvatore meo, Quia respexit ad humilitatem ancillae suae, ecce enim ex hoc beatam me dicent omnes generationes. Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen eius. Et misericordia eius in progeniem et progeniem, timentibus eum, Fecit potentiam in brachio suo, dispersit superbos mente cordis sui. Deposuit potentes de sedibus, et exaltavit humiles. Esurientes implevit bonis, et divites dimisit inanes, Suscepit Israël puerum suum, recordatus misericordiae suae. Sicut locutus est ad patres nostros, Abraham et semini eius in secula. Mansit autem Maria cum illa quasi mensibus tribus, et reversa est in domum suam.

Pulcerrima est historia, et plena spiritualis, et Christianae doctrinae. Habet autem tres praecipuos locos.

I. Testimonium de Messia. II. Imago Ecclesiae et verae synodi. III. Canticum Mariae.

De primo.

Magnum discrimen est inter Ecclesiam, et inter imperia mundi. Ecclesia est exiguus coetus eorum, qui retinent puram doctrinam Evangelii, et credunt in Christum, dissipatus, contemtus et spretus in mundo, qui miratur potentiam, gloriam, victorias et triumphos magnorum imperiorum. Et tamen hic parvus coetus Ecclesiae vere gerit res maximas. Etsi igitur Christi actiones non sic conspiciuntur in mundo, ut Alexandri aut Caesaris res gestae, tamen non est prorsus ignotus, et habet sua testimonia: quia oportet esse aliquam Ecclesiam, in qua Deus vult se et Filium suum cognosci, et vult aliquem coetum salvum fieri, in quo ipse celebretur in vita aeterna, ideo exhibuit multa testimonia, quae fidem nostram confirment, de omnibus articulis, quod hic sit Christus exhibitus iuxta promissiones.

Ita hic statim a concepto Christo recitantur testimonia. Conveniunt testes, Maria, Elisabeth anus gravida singulari miraculo Dei, infans exultans in utero, Zacharias cui hactenus muto subito redditur loquela, et alii in hac familia. Nam Maria proficiscitur ad cognatam, non propter privatam amicitiam, sed propter hoc illustre testimonium, et propter confirmationem suae fidei et aliorum sanctorum.

De secundo. Consideranda est imago Ecclesiae, et petenda consolatio ex hoc loco, ut non deficiamus a veritate, decepti specie et titulo Ecclesiae.

Vocant se Ecclesiam Pontifices, Episcopi, Reges, et his addicti; sicut olim Caiphas, Annas, Pharisaei, Sadducaei, sed non sunt Ecclesia. Interim est alia parva Ecclesia vera, sicut Paulus inquit: Non omnes qui sunt ex Israël, sunt Israël. Ut igitur tunc erant Ecclesia, Zacharias, Elisabeth, Maria, et pauci alii, ita nunc est exiguus numerus credentium in Christum, et recte colentium Deum, et hunc coetum persequuntur pontifices et episcopi, sicut tunc erant hostes sanctorum, Caiphas et similes. Dicitur enim, et Zacharias interfectus esse, propterea quod adfirmavit Messiam venisse, sicut scribit Epiphanius.
