Quintus, cum nihil dicant de fide, imo iubeant dubitare, non possunt recte docere iustificationem, et tantum tradunt ethnicam invocationem, cum clamitet Christus: Quicquid petieritis patrem in nomine meo, dabit vobis, id est, non fiducia vestrae dignitatis, sed fiducia Christi mediatoris.

## 3:16-21 Monday of Pentecost
Monday of Pentecost.

Acts 2.

And when the days of Pentecost were accomplished, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind. And it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them.

And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.

And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven. Now when this was noised abroad, the multitude came together, and were confounded, because that every man heard them speak in his own language. And they were all amazed and marvelled, saying one to another, Behold, are not all these which speak Galilaeans? And how hear we every man in our own tongue, wherein we were born? Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia, and in Judaea, and Cappadocia, in Pontus, and Asia, Phrygia, and Pamphylia, in Egypt, and in the parts of Libya about Cyrene, and strangers of Rome, Jews and proselytes, Cretes and Arabians, we do hear them speak in our tongues the wonderful works of God. And they were all amazed, and were in doubt, saying one to another: What for what does he want this to be? But others mocking said that they were full of new wine.

But Peter stood with the eleven, and lifted up his voice, and spoke to them: You men of Judea, and all you who inhabit Jerusalem. Let this be known to you, and receive my words with your ears. For they are not as you suppose, drunk, for it is the third hour of the day. But this is what was said by the Prophet Joel: And it shall be in the last days, says God, I will pour out of my spirit, upon all flesh, And your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams. And indeed upon my servants, and upon my handmaids, in those days I will pour out of my spirit, and they shall prophesy, and I will give wonders in heaven above, and signs on the earth below, blood and fire, and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the Moon into blood, before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes. And everyone who shall call upon the name of the Lord, shall be saved.

Since this is a description of the beginning of the kingdom of Christ, the sum of the doctrine, the example of conversion, the form and image of this kingdom are immediately proposed. But first, let the appearance of the Church be considered here attentively, and let the magnificent promises given to this people be repeated in the mind, and let it be thought how magnificent the expectation of a worldly kingdom was. To this expectation, how does this form correspond? Although the gift is much more glorious, namely, the beginning of eternal life, made through the Holy Spirit, and the fellowship of the divine nature, yet a small part of the people obtains this benefit, and they themselves are weak, without wealth, without the power of the world, even if they excel in the knowledge of God and the testimonies of the Holy Spirit. This appearance teaches much.

Peter's Sermon.

First, he refutes the tacit persuasion of the people concerning a worldly kingdom, and teaches that the kingdom of Christ will be the gift of the Holy Spirit, and of eternal life. For this he cites the Prophet, and it is a notable sentence: I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh. This saying testifies that the Holy Spirit is God by nature, because he says, of my spirit. But the particle 'of my spirit' must be diligently observed. What a testimony of love it is, that God imparts himself to us, that by the Holy Spirit being given, he makes us partakers of his nature, and implants power against sin and other evils. But the Prophet joins the first and second advent, because the gift of the Holy Spirit is the beginning of eternal life.

And the new sermon of that time is described: Everyone who shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved, as if he were saying, then the Gospel concerning the remission of sins will be proposed, and the Lord will be acknowledged, who is the author of this kingdom, who will teach invocation. By this invocation all shall be saved, not by the law. And it must be diligently considered that this saying concerning invocation is opposed to the opinions of the law, because the law deters from invocation, since it accuses. But now a mediator and high priest will be proposed to us, through whom we shall be commanded to call upon, through whom the remission of sins and eternal life are given freely. Here let us also learn, in passing, that the true and primary worship of the new Testament is invocation.

Having refuted the error of the Jews concerning a bodily kingdom, and having recited the testimony concerning the Holy Spirit, he now begins to preach about the author of the kingdom, namely that because of the Son of God, crucified and resurrected, the Holy Spirit and eternal life are given, that the Son of God resurrected is effective, is about to save, is about to judge the living and the dead. Here he adds a testimony from the Psalm. Then in the conclusion he argues their sin, that they crucified this Son of God, the author of the new kingdom, and commands them to acknowledge the sin, and to receive the remission of sins. Thus he embraces the sum of the Gospel.

But now see what kind of sin is objected to them, that they crucified the Son of God. He proposes the greatest sin, so that he may show that grace abounds above sin, lest the magnitude of sins drive anyone to despair. But let us remember that this voice pertains to all, at all times. The sins of individuals were the cause why it was necessary for the Son of God to suffer, because otherwise sin could not be blotted out. Likewise, how many have consented to some false dogmas, to the punishments of some, or certainly have not declared their confession, do not defend the saints? Thus individuals in some way crucified the Son of God. Let this particle therefore be considered diligently, both so that we may acknowledge our sins, and so that we may learn that grace abounds above sin.

Latin:

Feria II. Pentecostes.

Actorum 2.

Et cum complerentur dies Pentecostes, erant omnes unanimiter simul. Et factus est repente de coelo sonus tanquam advenientis flatus vehementis. Et replevit totam domum ubi erant sedentes. Et conspectae sunt illis dispertitae linguae, tanquam ignis, seditque supra singulos eorum.

Et repleti sunt omnes Spiritu sancto, et coeperunt loqui aliis linguis, prout spiritus dabat eis eloqui.

Erant autem in Ierusalem habitantes Iudaei, viri religiosi ex omni natione quae sub coelo est. Facta autem hac voce, convenit multitudo, et confusa est, quoniam audiebat unusquisque lingua sua illos loquentes. Stupebant autem omnes, et mirabantur dicentes inter sese: Nonne ecce omnes isti qui loquuntur, Galilaei sunt? Et quomodo nos audimus unusquisque propriam linguam nostram, in qua nati sumus? Parthi, et Medi, et Elamitae, et qui habitant Mesopotamiam, et Iudaeam et Cappadociam, Pontum et Asiam, et Phrygiam, et Pamphyliam, Aegyptum et partes Libyae, quae est circa Cyrenen, et peregrini Romani, Iudaei et proselyti, Cretes et Arabes, audimus eos loquentes nostris linguis magnifica Dei. Stupebant autem omnes, et consternabantur ad invicem dicentes: Quid nam vult hoc esse? Alii autem irridentes dicebant, quod musto pleni essent.

Stetit autem Petrus cum undecim, et elevavit vocem suam, et locutus est eis: Viri Iudaei, et qui habitatis Ierusalem universi. Hoc vobis notum sit, et percipite auribus verba mea. Non enim sicut vos existimatis, hi ebrii sunt, est enim hora diei tertia. Sed hoc est quod dictum est per Prophetam Ioël: Et erit in novissimis diebus, dicit Deus, Effundam de spiritu meo, super omnem carnem, Et prophetabunt filii vestri et filiae vestrae, et adolescentuli vestri visiones videbunt, et seniores vestri somnia somniabunt. Et quidem super servos meos, et super ancillas meas, in diebus illis effundam de spiritu meo, et prophetabunt, ei dabo prodigia in coelo sursum, et signa in terra deorsum sanguinem et ignem, et vaporem fumi. Sol convertetur in tenebras, et Luna in sanguinem, antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et manifestus. Et omnis qui invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit.

Cum haec sit descriptio initii regni Christi, statim proponitur summa doctrinae, exemplum conversionis, forma et imago huius regni. Primum autem hic attente consideretur species Ecclesiae, et repetantur animo magnificae promissiones datae huic populo, et cogitetur quam magnifica fuerit expectatio mundani regni. Ad hanc expectationem quomodo convenit haec forma? Etsi donum est multo gloriosius, videlicet, incoatio vitae aeternae, per Spiritum sanctum facta, et societas divinae naturae, tamen exigua pars populi consequitur hoc beneficium, et illi ipsi sunt imbecilles, sine opibus, sine potentia mundi, etsi excellunt agnitione Dei et testimoniis Spiritus sancti. Haec species multa monet.

Concio Petri.

Primum refutat tacitam persuasionem populi de regno mundano, et docet regnum Christi fore donationem Spiritus sancti, et vitae aeternae. Ad hoc citat Prophetam, et est insignis sententia: Effundam de Spiritu meo super omnem carnem. Hoc dictum testatur Spiritum sanctum esse natura Deum, quia dicit, de spiritu Meo. Diligenter autem observanda est particula de spiritu Meo. Quale testimonium est dilectionis, quod seipsum Deus impertit nobis, quod dato Spiritu sancto, efficit nos participes suae naturae, indit potentiam adversus peccatum et alia mala. Coniungit autem Propheta primum et secundum adventum, quia donatio Spiritus sancti est incoatio vitae aeternae.

Et describitur nova concio eius temporis: Omnis qui invocaverit nomen Domini salvus erit, quasi dicat, tunc proponetur Evangelium de remissione peccatorum, et agnoscetur Dominus, qui est autor huius regni, qui docebit invocationem. Hac invocatione omnes salvabuntur, non lege. Ac diligenter considerandum est, hoc dictum de invocatione oppositum esse opinionibus legis, quia lex deterret ab invocatione, cum accuset. Iam autem proponetur nobis mediator et pontifex, per quem iubebimur invocare, per quem donantur gratis remissio peccatorum et vita aeterna. Hic obiter etiam discamus, verum et praecipuum cultum esse novi Testamenti invocationem.

Refutato errore Iudaeorum de regno corporali, et recitato testimonio de Spiritu sancto, iam incipit concionari de autore regni, scilicet quod propter Filium Dei, crucifixum et resuscitatum, dentur Spiritus sanctus et vita aeterna, quod Filius Dei resuscitatus sit efficax, sit salvaturus, sit iudicaturus vivos et mortuos. Hic addit testimonium ex Psalmo. Deinde in conclusione arguit peccatum eorum, quod hunc Filium Dei, autorem novi regni crucifixerint, et iubet eos agnoscere peccatum, et accipere remissionem peccatorum. Ita complectitur summam Evangelii.

Iam autem vide, quale peccatum eis obiiciatur, quod crucifixerint Filium Dei. Maximum peccatum proponit, ut ostendat gratiam exuberare supra peccatum, ne quem magnitudo peccatorum adigat ad desperationem. Meminerimus autem hanc vocem pertinere ad omnes, omnibus temporibus. Singulorum peccata fuerunt causa quare oportuit Filium Dei pati, quia aliter deleri peccatum non potuit. Item, quam multi consenserunt in aliqua falsa dogmata, in supplicia aliquorum, aut certe non declararunt suam confessionem, non defendunt sanctos? Ita singuli aliquo modo crucifixerunt Filium Dei. Diligenter igitur haec particula consideretur, et ut nostra peccata agnoscamus, et ut discamus, gratiam exuberare supra peccatum.

## 4:46-54 Twenty-first Sunday After Trinity
Twenty-first Sunday after Trinity. Gospel of John

4. And there was a certain official whose son was ill at Capernaum. When he heard that Jesus was coming from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and asked him to come down and heal his son, for he was beginning to die. Jesus therefore said to him: Unless you see signs and wonders, you will not believe. The official said to him: Lord, come down before my son dies. Jesus said to him: Go, your son lives. The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he went. But while he was still descending, his servants met him and announced, saying that his son was alive. He therefore asked them the hour in which he had fared better. And they said to him: Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him. The father therefore knew that it was that hour in which Jesus said to him: Your son lives. And he himself believed, and his whole house. This second sign Jesus did again when he had come from Judea into Galilee.

There are three main points.

I. The rebuke of human infirmity, which values signs more than the word of God, looks around, and seeks miracles, while omitting the word of God. II. The example of faith, which depicts and shows the nature of faith. III. The fruit of faith, confession and preaching.

On the first.

When the word of God is first issued, certain testimonies are added. As when the law was given, great signs were added, so that it might be certain that the doctrine is divine, just as the Fathers and Prophets also had testimonies concerning the promises.

Afterward, when it is established that the word has been delivered by God, we ought to prefer the word itself to miracles, to such an extent that one should not believe even miracles against a certain word. Thus in Israel they knew the promises concerning the Messiah, and they ought to have believed these, more than miracles. But the human mind listens negligently to the word of God, and is moved more by signs.

Christ rebukes these shadows, which are so great that, although all things are full of miracles, we nevertheless demand other unusual ones besides these. This is the order of things: because God makes the fields fruitful every year, and feeds us, because He gave His Son for us, who rose from death and reigns, so that He may defend us in continuous dangers against the devil, we think, "If God were as familiar to me as He was to Abraham, or Moses, if He confirmed me also with similar testimonies, then indeed I would dare to believe Him."

Christ properly rebukes this very error here, and elsewhere, when He says: An adulterous generation seeks a sign. For we have the certain word of God; in this He wants us to look, according to that: Your word is a lamp to my feet. Rom. 15: That through the consolation of the scriptures we might have hope. This doctrine is very useful, so that we may learn the true exercises of faith, and not seek concerning the will of God outside the word. Likewise, let us truly know that God wills to grant us these things which He promises in the word, just as He granted to Abraham, Moses, and others. Why do you look around for wonders? Do you seek unusual examples? Although many of these also occur to almost everyone, nevertheless fix your eyes on the word, and expect those things which have been sent in the word. In these exercises it is learned what faith is. And indeed this faith obtains miracles, just as here, although human infirmity is rebuked, yet Christ afterward adds the miracle, to show that He heals our infirmity.

On the second point. Here let us learn that faith ought to rely upon the word of God, and that it is not to be cast aside on account of our unworthiness, just as the example of the Syrophoenician woman also shows. Regarding this matter, there is even now a controversy with the monks, and pharisaical imaginations in this article always stray from God. For the monks and all who are fascinated by the opinions of the law think thus: God is truthful and keeps His promises, but He bestows them upon the worthy; I would believe that I am regarded and heard, if I were worthy. The Gospel censures this error, and commands all who are doing penance to believe the voice of God, even if they acknowledge themselves to be unworthy and unclean.

This faith is to be exercised and learned in daily invocation. And one must diligently observe the distinction between true faith, relying on gratuitous mercy, and pharisaical imaginations, by which men pretend that they would believe and would invoke [God] if they were worthy, and by this error they omit true worship and the works of the first commandment; they do not believe, they do not invoke God, they do not expect good things from God. But so that we may perform the works of the first commandment, the doctrine concerning this faith must be held—a faith that asks for and expects good things from God, and relies on the promised mercy for the sake of the mediator Christ, even if we are not worthy.

To this pertain innumerable sentences: Ask, and you shall receive. Call upon me in the day of tribulation. The Lord is near to all who call upon Him. And Psalm 36: Be subject to God, and pray to Him. Therefore, just as the nobleman departs, expecting the promised benefit, and is not deterred by his own unworthiness, so let us believe the voice of God, and by this faith let us ask for and expect benefits.

On the third point.

After we have acknowledged God, a new obedience ought to follow, and especially this worship is to be performed, that we invite others by our testimony to the acknowledgment of God. Just as this nobleman invites his household to faith. This worship is the chief one, according to that saying: What shall I render to the Lord for all that He has rendered to me? I will sacrifice to Thee a sacrifice of praise. Likewise Peter: You are called to this light, that you may declare the glory of God. Therefore, those who have acknowledged the true doctrine should remember that they ought to confess it and impart it to others.

Latin:

Dominica XXI. post Trinitatis. Evangelium Iohan.

4. Et erat quidam regulus, cuius filius infirmabatur Capernaum. Hic cum audisset, quod Iesus adveniret a Iudaea in Galilaeam, abiit ad eum, et rogabat eum, ut descenderet, et sanaret filium eius, incipiebat enim mori. Dixit ergo Iesus ad eum: Nisi signa et prodigia videritis, non creditis. Dixit ad eum regulus: Domine, descende priusquam moriatur filius meus. Dixit ei Iesus: Vade, filius tuus vivit. Credidit homo sermoni, quem dixit ei Iesus, et ibat. Iam autem eo descendente, servi occurrerunt ei, et nunciaverunt, dicentes, quod filius eius viveret. Interrogabat ergo horam ab eis, in qua melius habuerat. Et dixerunt ei: Heri hora septima reliquit eum febris. Cognovit ergo pater, quod illa hora erat, in qua dixit ei Iesus: Filius tuus vivit. Et credidit ipse, et domus eius tota. Hoc iterum secundum signum fecit Iesus cum venisset e Iudaea in Galilaeam.

Tres sunt praecipui loci.

I. Reprehensio humanae infirmitatis, quae pluris facit signa, quam verbum Dei, circumspectat, quaerit miracula, omisso verbo Dei. II. Exemplum fidei, quod pingit et ostendit naturam fidei. III. Fructus fidei, confessio et praedicatio.

De primo.

Quando primum editur verbum Dei, adduntur certa testimonia. Ut cum daretur lex, sunt addita ingentia signa, ut certo constet, doctrinam esse divinam, sicut et Patres et Prophetae testimonia habebant de promissionibus.

Postea cum constat verbum a Deo traditum esse, debemus ipsum verbum anteferre miraculis, adeo ut nec miraculis contra certum verbum credendum sit. Ita in Israël norant promissiones de Messia, et his debebant credere, plus quam miraculis. Sed humana mens negligenter audit verbum Dei, et magis movetur signis.

Has tenebras reprehendit Christus, quae tantae sunt, ut cum omnia plena sint miraculis, tamen praeter haec flagitemus alia inusitata. Hic ordo rerum, quod Deus quotannis foecundat agros, et pascit nos, quod dedit Filium suum pro nobis, qui revixit ex morte, et regnat, ut nos defendat in continuis periculis adversus diabolum, cogitamus, Si Deus mihi adeo familiaris esset, ut fuit Abrahae, aut Mosi, si similibus testimoniis me quoque confirmaret, tunc vero ei credere auderem.

Hunc ipsum errorem proprie hic reprehendit Christus, et alibi, cum inquit: Generatio adultera signum quaerit. Habemus enim certum verbum Dei, in hoc vult nos intueri, iuxta illud: Lucerna pedibus meis verbum tuum. Rom. 15.: Ut per consolationem scripturarum spem habeamus. Haec doctrina admodum utilis est, ut discamus vera exercitia fidei, nec quaeramus de voluntate Dei extra verbum. Item, vere sciamus Deum velle nobis haec praestare, quae in verbo promittit, perinde, ut praestitit Abrahae, Mosi, et aliis. Quid circumspectas prodigia? quaeris inusitata exempla? Quanquam haec quoque occurrunt multa fere singulis, tamen defigito oculos in verbum, et expectes ea, quae in verbo missa sunt. In his exercitiis discitur, quid sit fides. Et quidem haec fides impetrat miracula, sicut hic, etsi reprehenditur humana infirmitas, tamen Christus postea addit miraculum, ut ostendat se mederi nostrae infirmitati.

De secundo. Hic discamus fidem debere niti verbo Dei, nec abiiciendam esse propter nostram indignitatem, sicut et exemplum Syrophoenissae ostendit. De hac re et nunc controversia est cum monachis, et semper pharisaicae imaginationes in hoc articulo aberrant a Deo. Nam monachi et omnes fascinati legis opinionibus sic cogitant: Deus est verax et servans promissionum, sed tribuit eas dignis, Crederem me respici et exaudiri, si dignus essem. Hunc errorem taxat Evangelium, ac iubet omnes agentes poenitentiam credere voci Dei, etiamsi agnoscunt se indignos et immundos esse.

Haec fides in quotidiana invocatione exercenda et discenda est. Et diligenter observandum est discrimen inter veram fidem, nitentem gratuita misericordia, et inter imaginationes pharisaicas, quibus fingunt homines se credituros esse, et invocaturos, si essent digni, et hoc errore omittunt veros cultus, et opera primi praecepti, non credunt, non invocant Deum, non expectant bona a Deo. Sed ut praestemus opera primi praecepti, tenenda est doctrina de hac fide, petente et expectante bona a Deo, ac nitente promissa misericordia propter mediatorem Christum, etiamsi nos non sumus digni.

Huc pertinent innumerabiles sententiae: Petite, et accipietis. Invoca me in die tribulationis. Prope est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum. Et Psal. 36.: Subditus esto Deo, et ora eum. Ergo sicut discedit regulus, expectans beneficium promissum, nec deterretur sua indignitate, ita nos credamus voci Dei, et hac fide petamus et expectemus beneficia.

De tertio.

Postquam agnovimus Deum, sequi debet nova obedientia, et praecipue praestandus est hic cultus, ut alios nostro testimonio invitemus ad agnitionem Dei. Sicut hic regius suam familiam invitat ad fidem. Hic cultus praecipuus est, iuxta illud: Quid retribuam domino pro omnibus quae retribuit mihi? Tibi sacrificabo hostiam laudis. Item Petrus: Estis vocati ad hanc lucem, ut enarretis gloriam Dei. Ergo qui agnoverunt veram doctrinam, meminerint se debere eam confiteri, et aliis impertire.

## 6:1-15 Dominica Laetare
Dominica Laetare. The Gospel of John 6.

After these things Jesus went across the sea of Galilee, which is of Tiberias, and a great crowd was following him, because they saw his signs, which he was doing upon those who were infirm. But Jesus went up into a mountain, and there he was sitting with his disciples. And it was near the Passover, the feast day of the Jews. When Jesus therefore had lifted up his eyes, and had seen that a great crowd was coming to him, he says to Philip: Whence shall we buy bread, that these may eat? But he was saying this, testing him. For he himself knew what he was about to do. Philip answered him: Two hundred denarii worth of bread is not enough for them, that each one of them may receive a little something. One of his disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, says: There is a boy here, who has five barley loaves and two fish. But what are these among so many? But Jesus said: Make the men sit down. Now there was much grass in that place. The men therefore sat down, in number about five thousand. But Jesus took the loaves, and when he had given thanks, he distributed them to the disciples, and the disciples to those who were sitting down. Likewise also from the fish as much as they wanted. But when they were filled, he says to his disciples: Gather the fragments that are left over, that nothing may perish. They gathered therefore and filled twelve baskets of fragments from the five barley loaves, which were left over to those who had eaten. Those men therefore, when they had seen that JESUS had done a sign, were saying: Because this is truly that Prophet, who is to come into the world. JESUS therefore, when he had known that they were about to come, and to seize him, that they might make him king, withdrew again into the mountain by himself alone.

I. The Topic, Consolation against the care of sustenance and defense. II. Example concerning the rewards of liberality. III. Precept concerning thrift: Gather the remnants, that they may not perish.

IIII. Allegory, When teachers feed the Church by teaching, by agitation the doctrine becomes more illustrious: and the remnants are to be preserved diligently and with selection.

On the first.

John the Baptist was killed in the second year of Christ's preaching, and after his death, when Herod was also lying in wait for Christ, Christ withdrew for a while. In this withdrawal, when the Apostles undoubtedly saw their own life to be in danger, and feared either punishments, or exiles, and hunger: here Christ shows some consolation to the sorrowful, as often happens in the Church, and proposes an example of this rule: Seek first the kingdom of God, and the rest shall be added unto you. Likewise: Godliness has promises of the present life and of the future. Likewise, the Psalms say: There is no want to those who fear him. Likewise: They shall be satisfied in the day of famine. God wants us to seek the kingdom of God first, that is, the heavenly doctrine, and to obey it, and in to be faithful in their vocation. Afterwards, although He wills the Church to be subject to the cross, yet He does not allow it to be utterly destroyed, but preserves the body, gives sustenance, gives some shelter, gives economies, gives polities, defends and delivers the Church in miraculous ways, even when destitute of human aids: as the examples of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph show.

The history of this text teaches the same, which warns us about the promise, and consoles us in similar dangers, so that now, even if the devil in the Turks and other tyrants and princes threatens that he will utterly destroy the Church, yet let us obey Christ, and let us expect defense from Christ, who by some miraculous event will save the remnants of the Church, just as He said: I will be with you even unto the consummation of the age. And indeed Christ wills us to exercise faith and invocation in these bodily dangers.

On the second. After the distribution, a great heap of remnants remains. Here it is signified that alms are compensated with great rewards, and that resources are not diminished, but defended and increased divinely, as scripture often teaches: Give, and it shall be given to you. Item: He who gives a drink of cold water shall not lose his reward, etc. And God wills us to exercise faith and expectation of help in this duty of liberality: as He shows in the example of the widow of Zarephath.

It is also notable that the distribution is commanded to the Apostles, so that governors especially may be admonished about the care of the poor. Item, food grows in the hands of the Apostles, because the handling and society of the pious is happy, as is said of Abraham: Because of you God has blessed us.

On the third. As before concerning liberality, which is a pious and not ambitious communication, so afterwards He commands concerning parsimony, that vain profusions may not occur, and let us learn here that prodigality is truly a sin, which clearly makes useless expenses.

First, because God wills us to use His gifts reverently, that is, to acknowledge that they are divinely given, and to apply them modestly to those uses for which they were created. To apply things to other uses, by way of mockery, is to offer insult to the gifts of God. Therefore Paul says: Every creature of God is good, and to be received with thanksgiving.

Item, 1 Corinthians 7: Those who use the world, as not abusing it. Item, Romans 13: Make not provision for the flesh, to fulfill the lusts thereof, that is, use things for necessity, not for lust.

God wills us to share things for our own and others' necessities, and He detests luxury and profusions. Just as on the contrary He commands temperance and modesty: Take heed, lest your hearts be burdened with surfeiting and drunkenness. Diligently, therefore, in this place the precept concerning parsimony must be observed: Gather up the remnants, that nothing may perish.

And there are two neighboring virtues, Liberality and Parsimony.

On the fourth. The allegory is most sweet: for it signifies the distribution of doctrine.

This grows by being agitated, just as Paul says elsewhere: The husbandman must be the first to partake of the fruits: so the teacher first receives rewards from God, and is himself illuminated with greater light. Then the remnants of true doctrine must be preserved diligently and with selection. Wherefore let us also preserve the monuments of the ancients, but with selection.

And would that there had been greater care for this matter, and that the monuments handed down through the disciples of the Apostles had been preserved. Baskets signify letters and erudition, by which monuments ought to be preserved.

Latin:

Dominica Laetare. Evangelium Iohannis 6.

Post haec abiit Iesus trans mare Galilaeae, quod est Tyberiadis, et sequebatur eum turba multa, quia videbant eius signa, quae faciebat super his, qui infirmabantur. Subiit autem in montem Iesus, et ibi sedebat cum discipulis suis. Erat autem proximum Pascha, dies festus Iudaeorum. Cum sublevasset ergo oculos Iesus, et vidisset quod turba multa veniret ad se, dicit ad Philippum: Unde ememus panes, ut manducent hi? Hoc autem dicebat, tentans eum. Ipse enim sciebat, quid esset facturus. Respondit ei Philippus: Ducentorum denariorum panes non sufficiunt eis, ut unusquisque eorum modicum quid accipiat. Dicit unus ex discipulis eius Andreas frater Simonis Petri: Est puer unus hic, qui habet quinque panes hordeaceos et duos pisces. Sed haec quid sunt inter tot? Dixit autem Iesus: Facite homines discumbere. Erat autem foenum multum in eo loco. Discubuerunt ergo viri, numero quasi quinque millia. Accepit autem Iesus panes, et cum gratias egisset, distribuit discipulis, discipuli vero discumbentibus. Similiter et ex piscibus quantum volebant. Ut autem impleti sunt, dicit discipulis suis: Colligite quae superfuerunt fragmenta, ut ne quid pereat. Collegerunt ergo et impleverunt duodecim cophinos fragmentorum ex quinque panibus hordeaceis, quae superfuerant his qui manducaverant. Illi ergo homines, cum vidissent, quod IESUS fecerat signum, dicebant: Quia hic est vere ille Propheta, qui venturus est in mundum. IESUS ergo cum cognovisset, quod venturi essent, et rapturi ipsum, ut facerent eum regem, secessit iterum in montem ipse solus.

I. Locus, Consolatio contra curam victus et defensionis. II. Exemplum de praemiis liberalitatis. III. Praeceptum de parsimonia: Colligite reliquias, ne pereant. IIII.

Allegoria, Cum doctores pascunt Ecclesiam docendo, agitatione fit illustrior doctrina: et reliquiae diligenter et cum delectu asservandae sunt.

De primo.

Iohannes Baptista interfectus est secundo anno praedicationis Christi, et post necem eius, cum Herodes etiam insidiaretur Christo, secessit aliquantisper Christus. In hoc secessu, cum haud dubie Apostoli viderent suam vitam in periculo esse, ac metuerent vel supplicia, vel exilia, et famem: hic Christus moestis ostendit aliquam consolationem, ut saepe fit in Ecclesia, et exemplum proponit huius regulae: Primum quaerite regnum Dei, et caetera adiicientur vobis. Item: Pietas habet promissiones praesentis vitae et futurae. Item, Psalmi dicunt: Non est inopia timentibus eum. Item: Saturabuntur in die famis. Vult nos Deus primum quaerere regnum Dei, id est, doctrinam coelestem, et huic obedire, et in vocatione fideles esse. Postea, etsi vult Ecclesiam subiectam esse cruci, tamen non sinit eam penitus deleri, sed conservat corpus, dat victum, dat aliquem nidum, dat oeconomias, dat politias, defendit et liberat Ecclesiam mirabilibus modis, etiam destitutam humanis praesidiis: sicut exempla Abrahae, Isaac, Iacob, Ioseph ostendunt.

Idem docet historia huius textus, quae nos de promissione admonet, et consolatur in similibus periculis, ut iam, etsi diabolus in Turcis et aliis tyrannis et principibus minitatur se funditus deleturum esse Ecclesiam, tamen obediamus Christo, et expectemus defensionem a Christo, qui mirando aliquo eventu servabit reliquias Ecclesiae, sicut dixit: Ero vobiscum usque ad consummationem seculi. Et quidem vult Christus nos exercere fidem et invocationem in his corporalibus periculis.

De secundo. Post distributionem superest magnus cumulus reliquiarum. Hic significatum est compensari eleemosynas magnis praemiis, et non minui facultates, sed defendi et augeri divinitus, ut saepe docet scriptura: Date, et dabitur vobis. Item: Qui dat potum aquae frigidae, non perdet mercedem suam etc. Et vult nos Deus exercere fidem et expectationem auxilii in hoc officio liberalitatis: sicut ostendit in exemplo viduae Sareptanae.

Est et hoc insigne, quod Apostolis mandatur distributio, ut gubernatores praecipue admoneantur de cura pauperum. Item, crescunt cibi in manibus Apostolorum, quia piorum contrectatio et societas est felix, sicut dicitur de Abraham: Propter te benedixit nobis Deus.

De tertio. Ut antea de liberalitate, quae est pia et non ambitiosa communicatio, ita postea de parsimonia praecipit, ne fiant inanes profusiones, Ac discamus hic vere peccatum esse prodigalitatem, quae videlicet facit inutiles sumtus.

Primum, quia Deus vult nos suis donis reverenter uti, hoc est, agnoscere, quod sint divinitus data, et modeste conferre ad eos usus, ad quos condita sunt. Conferre res ad alios usus, per ludibrium, est contumelia afficere dona Dei. Ideo Paulus inquit: Omnis creatura Dei bona, et cum gratiarum actione percipienda.

Item, 1. Corinth. 7.: Utentes mundo sic, ut non abutamini. Item, Rom. 13.: Carnem ne curetis ad concupiscentiam, sed ad necessitatem, id est, utamini rebus pro necessitate, non pro libidine.

Vult Deus comparci res ad nostras, et aliorum necessitates, et detestatur luxum ac profusiones. Sicut econtra praecipit temperantiam et modestiam: Attendite, ne corda vestra graventur crapula et ebrietate. Diligenter igitur hoc loco praeceptum de parsimonia observandum est: Colligite reliquias, ne quid pereat.

Suntque duae vicinae virtutes, Liberalitas et Parsimonia.

De quarto. Allegoria est dulcissima: significat enim distributionem doctrinae.

Haec crescit agitando, sicut alibi dicit Paulus: Colonum oportet primum de fructibus percipere: ita docens primum accipit praemia a Deo, illustratur ipse maiori luce. Deinde reliquiae verae doctrinae diligenter et cum delectu servandae sunt. Quare et nos veterum monumenta, sed cum delectu servemus.

Ac utinam eius rei maior cura fuisset, et monumenta tradita per Apostolorum discipulos conservata essent. Cophini significant literas et eruditionem, quibus conservari monumenta debent.

## 8:1 Dominica Iudica
Dominica Iudica.

Gospel of John 8.

Which of you convicts me of sin?

But if I speak the truth, why do you not believe me? He who is of God hears the words of God; therefore you do not hear, because you are not of God.

Then the Jews answered, and said to Him: Do we not say well that you are a Samaritan, and have a demon? Jesus answered: I do not have a demon, but I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.

But I do not seek my own glory; there is One who seeks and judges. Amen, amen I say to you, if anyone keeps my word, he shall not see death forever.

Then the Jews said: Now we know that you have a demon; Abraham is dead, and the Prophets, and you say, If anyone keeps my word, he shall not taste death forever. Is it greater than our father Abraham, who is dead, and the Prophets are dead. Whom do you make yourself? Jesus answered: If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, whom you say is your God, and you have not known him. But I know him, and if I said that I did not know him, I would be a liar like you, but I know him, and I keep his word. Abraham your father rejoiced to see my day, and he saw it, and was glad. The Jews therefore said to him: You are not yet fifty years old, and have you seen Abraham? Jesus said to them: Amen, amen I say to you, before Abraham was, I am. They took up stones therefore, that they might cast them at him. But Jesus hid himself, and went out of the temple.

I. The passage, the assertion that he teaches rightly, and is sent by God. II. Concerning the cause of the obstinacy or hardening of the impious. III. Refutation of the reproach, which pertains properly to doctrine. IV. The proper doctrine of Christ, that he was sent to abolish death. V. Mutual altercation, whether Christ excels the Fathers and Prophets? and how the Fathers and Prophets were saved. VI. Testimony concerning the divinity of the Son.

Concerning the first.

All who teach in the Church ought to have this certainty, that they teach rightly: therefore Christ says that sin cannot be objected to him, namely that he is a false prophet, that he is an impostor. He speaks especially of this kind. For although he was otherwise without sin, yet the chief question is concerning the ministry, and the rule is common and pertains to all. Let all be certain that they teach the truth, as Peter says: He who speaks, let him speak the words of God. Furthermore, let them also beware lest they deform doctrine with scandals.

Concerning the second. The cause of the obstinacy and hardening of the impious is their own perverse will, deserted by God, because it has opposed itself to doctrine against conscience, and then is confirmed by the devil, who impels them to exaggerate human persuasions to themselves, and to seek pretexts for their hatred, as the Jews argued: that the Law of Moses, delivered by God, could not be changed; that a kingdom had been promised to this people; that the polity divinely constituted was not to be dissolved. These were specious and plausible things, by which Timonic [bitter] hatreds were gradually fed and confirmed. Paul speaks of such things in Rom. 11 and Psalm 69: Let their back be always bowed down. So now the wise dispute that the authority of the Church is great, that the state of the ecclesiastical order is not to be shaken, etc. Fascinated by these imaginations, they gradually conceive greater flames of hatred against the Gospel. Therefore let us be intent, lest the devil pour into us persuasions that beget hatred or contempt for the Gospel, lest afterwards this horrendous punishment follows, the blinding or hardening of Pharaoh, or of Judas, of whom it is said: And Satan entered into him. So he says here: Those who are not of God do not hear, that is, they are deserted by God. But they are deserted because of their blasphemies.

Concerning the third.

Christ passes over one reproach, and refutes another: You have a demon. For this properly pertained to doctrine. To refute such reproaches is a necessary part of confession.

Concerning the fourth.

If anyone keeps my word, he shall not see death forever. This seemed to be a wondrous voice, and far above man, because it promises eternal life. Furthermore, this offended the Jews, because he did not say: If anyone keeps the word of Moses. Likewise, because there is a distinction between the word of Moses and of the Messiah. The Pharisees did not think that the Messiah would bring any other doctrine besides the Mosaic one. But here he testifies that he brings another word, namely the Gospel, that is, he says he is sent to be a victim for sin, and that men are to be reconciled to God, not through the law of Moses, but by faith in the Messiah, and that by this faith God is to be invoked, and that the Messiah is to reign in heaven, and to govern his Church by the Holy Spirit and the word, not to be a lord of the world who holds political empires, that the Church is to be on the cross, and not to have the empires of the world. This discourse differs far from the opinions of the Pharisees which they held concerning the law.

Concerning the fifth.

This very article is the proper one of the Gospel, that the Messiah excels the fathers and the Prophets, as John says: From his fullness we have all received. Therefore, all saints from the beginning unto the end are saved in one and the same way, namely by faith, by which they believe that God forgives them their sins through mercy, on account of the promised deliverer. By this faith Adam, Abraham, Moses, David, and all the saints comforted themselves: by this faith they were pleasing to God, with this confidence they called upon God.

Therefore it is said here: Abraham saw my day, and was glad, that is, he recognized in the promise my advent, my benefits: And was glad, that is, he received the remission of sins, a new light, and the beginning of eternal life, which is joy, peace, etc.

But the Pharisees had far different opinions about the Messiah; they were oppressed by imaginations of the righteousness of the law, they knew nothing of faith in the Messiah, or of a victim for sin, they only expected an earthly kingdom. Therefore they furiously detest these discourses of Christ.

Concerning the sixth.

A clear testimony stands here, that the Son of God was even before the assumption of flesh. As he clearly says: Before Abraham was born, I am, but this must be explained from the first chapter: In the beginning was the word, etc.

Latin:

Dominica Iudica.

Evangelium Iohannis 8.

Quis ex vobis arguet me de peccato?

Si autem veritatem dico, quare vos non creditis mihi? Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit, propterea vos non auditis, quia ex Deo non estis.

Responderunt ergo Iudaei, et dixerunt ei: Nonne bene dicimus nos, quia Samaritanus es tu, et daemonium habes? Respondi Iesus: Ego daemonium non habeo, sed honoro Patrem meum, et vos inhonorastis me.

Ego autem non quaero gloriam meam, Est qui quaerit et iudicat. Amen amen dico vobis, si quis sermonem meum servaverit, mortem non videbit in aeternum.

Dixerunt ergo Iudaei: Nunc cognovimus quod daemonium habes, Abraham mortuus est, et Prophetae, et tu dicis, Si quis sermonem meum servaverit, non gustabit mortem in aeternum. Nunquid maior es patre nostro Abraham, qui mortuus est, et Prophetae mortui sunt. Quem teipsum tu facis? Respondit Iesus: Si ego glorifico meipsum, gloria mea nihil est, Est pater meus, qui glorificat me, quem vos dicitis, quia Deus vester est, et non cognovistis eum, Ego autem novi eum, et si dixero quod non noverim eum, ero similis vobis mendax, sed novi eum, et verbum eius servo. Abraham pater vester exultavit ut videret diem meum, et vidit, et gavisus est. Dixerunt ergo Iudaei ad eum: Quinquaginta annos nondum habes, et Abraham vidisti? Dixit eis Iesus: Amen amen dico vobis, antequam Abraham esset, ego sum. Tulerunt ergo lapides, ut iacerent in eum. Iesus autem abscondit se, et exivit de templo.

I. Locus, Asseveratio, quod recte doceat, et sit missus a Deo. II. De causa pertinaciae, seu indurationis impiorum. III. Refutatio convicii, quod ad doctrinam proprie pertinet. IIII. Doctrina propria Christi, quod sit missus, ut aboleat mortem. V. Altercatio mutua, an Christus antecellat Patribus et Prophetis? et quomodo Patres et Prophetae salvati sint. VI. Testimonium de divinitate Filii.

De primo.

Omnes docentes in Ecclesia oportet habere hanc certitudinem, quod recte doceant: ideo Christus inquit, sibi non posse obiici peccatum, scilicet quod sit pseudopropheta, quod sit impostor. De hac specie praecipue loquitur. Etsi enim et alioqui sine peccato fuit, tamen praecipua quaestio est de ministerio, et regula communis ad omnes pertinet. Omnes sint certi, se vera docere sicut inquit Petrus: Qui loquitur, loquatur sermones Dei. Deinde etiam caveant, ne doctrinam scandalis deforment.

De secundo. Causa pertinaciae et indurationis impiorum est ipsorum perversa voluntas, deserta a Deo, quia contra conscientiam adversata est doctrinae, et deinde confirmata a diabolo, qui impellit, ut humanae persuasiones ipsi sibi exaggerent, quaerant praetextus sui odii, ut Iudaei argumentabantur, Legem Moisi a Deo traditam, non posse mutari, promissum esse huic populo regnum, politiam divinitus constitutam, non esse dissolvendam. Haec erant speciosa et plausibilia, quibus paulatim et alebantur et confirmabantur Timonica odia. De talibus loquitur Paulus Rom. 11. et Psal. 69.: Dorsum eorum semper incurva. Ita nunc disputant sapientes, magnam esse auctoritatem Ecclesiae, non labefactandum esse statum ordinis ecclesiastici etc. His fascinati imaginationibus, maiores paulatim flammas odii adversus Evangelium concipiunt. Ideo simus intenti, ne diabolus offundat nobis persuasiones, quae odium aut contemptum Evangelii pariant, ne postea sequatur haec horrenda poena, excaecatio vel induratio Pharaonis, seu Iudae, de quo dicitur: Et ingressus est in eum satanas. Ita hic dicit: Qui non sunt ex Deo, non audiunt, id est, deserti a Deo. Deseruntur autem propter blasphemias.

De tertio.

Christus alterum convicium praeterit, alterum refutat: Daemonium habes. Hoc enim proprie pertinebat ad doctrinam. Talia convicia refutare pars est necessaria confessionis.

De quarto.

Si quis sermonem meum servabit, mortem non videbit in aeternum. Haec videbatur esse mira vox, et longe supra hominem, quia pollicetur vitam aeternam. Deinde hoc offendit Iudaeos, quod non inquit: Si quis sermonem Moisi servabit. Item, quod discrimen est inter sermonem Moisi et Messiae. Non existimabant Pharisaei Messiam allaturum esse aliam doctrinam, praeter Mosaicam. Sed hic testatur, se alium sermonem afferre, scilicet Evangelium, hoc est, dicit se mitti, ut sit victima pro peccato, et homines reconciliari Deo, non per legem Moisi, sed fiducia Messiae, et hac fiducia Deum invocandum esse, et regnaturum esse Messiam in coelo, ac gubernaturum suam Ecclesiam Spiritu sancto et verbo, non futurum mundi dominum, qui politica imperia teneat, Ecclesiam futuram in cruce, non habituram imperia mundi. Hic sermo longe differt a Pharisaeorum opinionibus, quas de lege ipsi habebant.

De quinto.

Hic ipse articulus est proprius Evangelii, quod Messias antecellat patribus et Prophetis, sicut Iohannes inquit: Ex plenitudine eius omnes accepimus. Ideo omnes sancti ab initio usque ad finem uno et eodem modo salvantur, scilicet fide, qua credunt Deum ipsis remittere peccata per misericordiam, propter liberatorem promissum. Hac fide se Adam, Abraham, Moises, David, et omnes sancti consolabantur: hac fide placebant Deo, hac fiducia Deum invocabant.

Ideo hic dicitur: Abraham vidit diem meum, et laetatus est, id est, agnovit in promissione meum adventum, mea beneficia: Et laetatus est, id est, accepit remissionem peccatorum, novam lucem, et incoationem vitae aeternae, quae est laetitia, pax etc.

Sed Pharisaei longe alias opiniones de Messia habebant, erant oppressi imaginationibus iusticiae legis, nihil norant de fide in Messiam, aut de victima pro peccato, tantum expectabant regnum mundanum. Ideo has conciones Christi furenter detestantur.

De sexto.

Testimonium hic clarum extat, quod Filius Dei fuerit etiam ante assumtam carnem. Sicut clare dicit: Antequam Abraham natus esset, ego sum, sed hoc declarandum est ex primo capite: In principio erat verbum etc.

## 10:1-11 Tuesday of Pentecost
Tuesday of Pentecost.

Acts 15.

But some of the sect of the Pharisees who had believed rose up, saying that it is necessary to circumcise them and to command them to keep the law of Moses.

And the Apostles and elders gathered to see about this matter.

And when a great debate was taking place, Peter rising up, said to them: Men, brethren, you know that from ancient days God chose among us that by my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the Gospel, and believe.

And God, who knows the hearts, bore witness to them, giving them the Holy Spirit, just as also to us, and made no distinction between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.

Now therefore why do you test God, to put a yoke upon the necks of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?

But we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, just as they are.

Question.

Since the Apostles instituted ceremonies, it seems that both follow: that God wishes to be worshipped with such rites, and that the Church can, by imitation of the Apostles, institute acts of worship.

I answer in three ways: First, the Apostles did not institute these, but retained what was used before, for probable causes, and so as not to alienate the less experienced.

Because it was the custom, when cities were captured that received the worship of the true God, to impose these [ceremonies] without Mosaic ceremonies, yet [they did so] for very grave reasons.

Now if the Apostles had abolished this custom, some would have said that it was becoming pure paganism.

And concerning these, there is no doubt that the prohibition of idolatry, of things sacrificed to idols, and of fornication is necessary.

The other two, concerning blood and things strangled, seem to be among the adiaphora (indifferent things).

But this observance was magnified because it was handed down to Noah, and is much older than Moses and circumcision.

And to this precept was added the prohibition of homicide.

Wherefore it was at the same time a political symbol.

Thus, men abhorred the eating of blood almost as they did murder.

Wherefore it is credible that the fathers imposed these on the Gentiles so that, although they were not burdened by the law of Moses, they might nevertheless have some ceremonies useful for the sake of discipline, which would admonish them concerning the true worship of God and divine precepts, and would distinguish the new citizens of the Church of God from other nations that still served idols.

The Apostles therefore retained the customary practice handed down by the fathers, and it contained not ceremonies devised by human authority, but divinely handed down, of which there was some utility.

And in this matter they avoided the offenses and scandals of those who would have been alienated from the Gospel if they had not retained this custom, which was older than the law.

For that they had a reason for scandal in this case is apparent from the fact that they did not abstain from blood everywhere.

Second response concerning acts of worship.

When necessary things are done with true faith and trust in the Son of God, they are acts of worship; that is, they are works that God approves, and are consecrated by His word, and by which He judges Himself to be honored when we do them in faith, and so that we may obey Him and celebrate Him—such as fleeing idols, not being polluted by wandering lusts—they are true acts of worship if they are done as has been said.

But yet, a rule must be held concerning necessary things, which is handed down here: that because of these, the remission of sins is not given, but because of the Son of God, as is said here, "purifying their hearts by faith." Thus also, in the past, Mosaic ceremonies were acts of worship when they were still consecrated and commanded by the word of God, if, however, they were done in faith—that is, trust in the coming Messiah—and for the sake of confession.

By these rites, the Israelites testified that this was the true God who had handed down this word.

But after the Gospel of eternal justice and life shone forth, and the Mosaic rites were about to cease along with the Mosaic polity, most of the rites were now adiaphora.

Some of these could be retained for the sake of discipline or for the sake of confession.

The Apostles therefore retained the rite concerning blood for the sake of discipline and for the sake of confession, because it was a symbol or sacrament of the most severe prohibition concerning murder, and that prohibition was joined to the law concerning blood.

Wherefore the Jews abhorred the eating of blood almost as they did murder itself.

Since, therefore, so many things concurred—discipline, scandal, and confession—it seemed to the Apostles that this rite should be retained, especially in those places where those causes were valid.

They retained it, however, not as an act of worship, and much less did they intend it to be a merit for the remission of sins or righteousness.

The third response. Nor is the consequence valid: The Apostles retained these things, therefore it is permitted for the Church to institute new things as acts of worship.

The consequence must be denied, because the Apostles did not institute, but retained this rite, for the reasons I have stated. Furthermore, even if they had instituted something new, it does not follow that imitation is permitted. This imitation has always harmed the Church: First, the fathers instituted certain rites and sacrifices by divine command; later, imitation, out of a false persuasion, devised various sacrifices, even the slaughter of humans.

And the consequence is not valid at all.

The Apostles retained them for the sake of discipline, or to avoid scandal, therefore it is permitted to imitate them, or to invent new acts of worship. Nor is this consequence valid: The Apostles handed down certain rites, therefore it is permitted for other Bishops to institute new rites.

Because the apostolic calling far surpasses the episcopal. To the Apostles, He first handed down a new ministry, and through them He instituted something new; the Bishop, however, is a listener, and receives the word and the rites from the Apostles, with a specific mandate that he should hand these down to the Church unchanged.

Latin:

Feria III.

Pentecostes.

Actorum 15. Surrexerunt autem quidam de haeresi Pharisaeorum, qui crediderant, dicentes, quod oportet circumcidere eos, et praecipere servare legem Mosi.

Conveneruntque Apostoli et seniores videre de hoc verbo.

Cum autem magna disceptatio fieret, surgens Petrus, dixit ad eos: Viri fratres, vos scitis, quod ab antiquis diebus Deus inter nos elegit per os meum audire gentes verbum Evangelii, et credere.

Et Deus qui novit corda testimonium perhibuit eis, dans eis Spiritum sanctum, sicut et nobis, et nihil discrevit inter nos et illos, fide purificans corda eorum.

Nunc ergo quid tentatis Deum, ut imponatur iugum super cervices discipulorum, quod neque patres nostri, neque nos portare potuimus?

Sed per gratiam Domini Iesu Christi credimus salvari, quemadmodum et illi.

Quaestio.

Cum Apostoli instituerint ceremonias, videtur utrunque sequi, quod et velit Deus coli talibus ritibus, et Ecclesia possit imitatione Apostolorum instituere cultus.

Respondeo tripliciter: Primum Apostoli haec non instituerunt, sed usitata antea retinuerunt, propter probabiles causas, et ne alienarent imperitiores.

Quia mos erat captis urbibus, quae recipiebant veri Dei cultum, sine ceremoniis Mosaicis, tamen haec imponere propter gravissimas causas.

Iam si Apostoli et hunc morem sustulissent, dixissent aliqui, prorsus ethnicismum fieri.

Ac de his non dubium est, necessariam esse prohibitionem idololatriae, idolothytorum et scortationis.

Caetera duo, de sanguine et suffocato videntur esse ex ἀδιαφόροις.

Ideo autem haec observatio magnificabatur, quia tradita est Nohae, et multo vetustior est Moise, et circumcisione.

Fuitque huic praecepto addita prohibitio homicidii.

Quare simul fuit symbolum politicum.

Sic ab esu sanguinis, pene ut a caede abhorrebant homines.

Quare credibile est patres haec imposuisse gentibus, ut quamvis lege Moisi non onerarentur, tamen haberent aliquas ceremonias utiles disciplinae causa, quae admonerent de vero cultu Dei et de praeceptis divinis, et discernerent novos cives Ecclesiae Dei ab aliis gentibus, quae adhuc serviebant idolis.

Retinuerunt ergo Apostoli usitatum morem traditum a patribus, et continentem non ceremonias excogitatas humana autoritate, sed divinitus traditas, quarum aliqua erat utilitas.

Et in hac re vitaverunt offensiones et scandala eorum, qui fuissent alienati ab Evangelio, sine hunc quidem morem vetustiorem lege retinuissent.

Nam quod habuerint scandali rationem in hoc casu, inde apparet, quod non ubique abstinebant a sanguine.

Secunda responsio de cultibus.

Necessaria cum fiunt vera fide, et fiducia Filii Dei, sunt cultus, id est, sunt opera quae Deus approbat, et consecrata ipsius verbo, et quibus iudicat se honore affici, cum ea facimus in fide, ac ut ei obediamus, et eum celebremus, ut fugere idola, non pollui vagis libidinibus, sunt veri cultus, si fiant ut dictum est, sed tamen et de necessariis regula tenenda est, quae hic traditur, quod propter haec non detur remissio peccatorum, sed propter Filium Dei, sicut hic dicitur, Fide purificans corda.

Sic et olim ceremoniae Mosaicae erant cultus, cum adhuc verbo Dei consecratae et praeceptae essent, si tamen fiebant in fide, id est, fiducia venturi Messiae, et propter confessionem.

His ritibus testabantur Israëlitae, hunc esse verum Deum, qui hoc verbum tradiderat.

Postquam autem illuxit Evangelium de aeterna iusticia et vita, et ritus Mosaici desituri erant una cum politia Mosaica, ritus plerique iam erant ἀδιαφόροις.

Horum aliqui retineri poterant disciplinae causa, vel propter confessionem.

Retinuerunt igitur Apostoli ritum de sanguine, disciplinae causa, et propter confessionem, quia ille erat symbolum, seu sacramentum severissimae prohibitionis de caede, et prohibitio illa adiuncta erat legi de sanguine.

Quare propemodum sanguinis esum sic ahominabantur Iudaei, ut caedem ipsam.

Cum igitur tot concurrerent, disciplina, scandalum et confessio, visum est Apostolis hunc ritum retinendum esse, praesertim in iis locis ubi causae illae valebant.

Retinuerunt autem non ut cultum, ac multo minus voluerunt esse meritum remissionis peccatorum, aut iusticiam.

Tertia responsio. Nec valet consequentia, Apostoli haec retinuerunt, ergo licet Ecclesiae nova instituere tanquam cultus.

Neganda est consequentia, quia Apostoli non instituerunt, sed retinuerunt hunc ritum, propter causas quas dixi. Deinde etiamsi quid novi instituissent, non sequitur imitationem concessam esse. Semper haec imitatio nocuit Ecclesiae: Primum, patres mandato divino instituerunt certos ritus et sacrificia, postea imitatio ex falsa persuasione, excogitavit varia sacrificia, etiam hominum mactationes.

Ac minime valet consequentia.

Apostoli retinuerunt propter disciplinam, aut scandalum, ergo licet imitari, aut fingere novos cultus. Neque haec consequentia valet, Apostoli quosdam ritus tradiderunt, ergo licet caeteris Episcopis novos ritus instituere.

Quia apostolica vocatio longe superat episcopalem. Apostolis primum tradidit novum ministerium, et per eos instituit aliquid novi, Episcopus vero est auditor, et accipit verbum, et ritus ab Apostolis, cum certo mandato ut haec non mutata, tradat Ecclesiae.

## 14:1-11 Day of Philip and James
Gospel on the day of Philip and James, John 14.

And Jesus said to his disciples: Let not your heart be troubled. You believe in God, believe also in me. In my father's house there are many mansions. If it were not so, I would have told you, I go to prepare a place for you. And when I have gone, to prepare a place for you, I will come again, and will take you to myself, that where I am, you also may be. And where I go, you know, and you know the way. Thomas says to him: Lord, we do not know where you are going, and how can we know the way? Jesus says to him: I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the father, except through me. If you had known me, you would have known my father also. And from now on you know him, and have seen him. Philip says to him: Lord, show us the father, and it is enough for us. Jesus says to him: Have I been with you so long, and you have not known me? Philip, he who sees me, sees the father, and how do you say, Show us the father?

Do you not believe that I am in the father, and the father is in me? The words that I speak to you, I do not speak from myself: but the father who abides in me, he does the works. Believe me, that I am in the father, and the father is in me: but if not, believe me for the works themselves.

Amen, amen I say to you, he who believes in me, the works that I do, he also will do, and greater than these he will do, because I go to my father. And whatever you ask in my name, this I will do, that the father may be glorified in the son. If you ask anything in my name, I will do it.

There are three principal points.

I. How God is to be acknowledged and worshipped.

II. Concerning the Son as mediator and the Holy Spirit.

III. Concerning the efficacy of invocation.

Concerning the first.

The chief and greatest of all man's works is the acknowledgment and celebration of God, for which we were created. And some light concerning God was implanted in the human mind, but this has been greatly obscured, wherefore many most sorrowful doubts have followed. For although the human mind in all sane persons determines that there is a God, the cause and maker of good in nature, yet it doubts universally whether He is willing to hear, help, and save us who are unworthy. Therefore, God from the very beginning has revealed Himself through a certain word and testimony, through which He willed to be acknowledged, and willed His will toward us to be known, and He affirms that He is rightly worshipped there, where He is thus acknowledged and invoked, according to His word, by faith.

But the human mind easily casts aside the word, either because of the cross or because of the snares of the devil. Afterward, wandering in darkness, it either becomes entirely Epicurean, as is now the custom, or it fashions for itself gods and cults, just as the Gentiles did, and Mahomet.

And all these cults, devised by human counsel, are vain. Because the doubt remains, where the Gospel is ignored, whether God hears. Therefore, let us learn this doctrine, which is handed down in this Gospel: that it is necessary to acknowledge and invoke the living and eternal God just as He has revealed Himself by His word and His testimonies, namely, as the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom He is appeased, and has promised that He will be propitious, and will sanctify through the Holy Spirit.

Then also, by the mention of the mediator, it corrects doubt and affirms that we are heard by God. Thus Christ binds Philip, who is questioning, to the sight of the mediator, as if he were saying: I know that the human mind wanders and seeks God in various ways: but you omit human thoughts, and define that He is truly God who sent this Christ to be crucified and to be raised again, and revealed Himself to the world through Him, and through Him promised salvation, and that He wills to be invoked and worshipped by the trust of this mediator, according to the word handed down to him.

Thus He had bound the fathers in the beginning to the promise: In your seed shall all nations be blessed. But it is difficult for the mind to acquiesce in the word of God, and we require sensible knowledge.

Therefore Philip says: Lord, show us the father, and it is enough for us, as if he were saying: The word does not satisfy our minds; a sight would satisfy, in which we might discern the beginnings and the ends, the causes and the events, about which we are anxious. He thinks wisely and in the human manner.

Indeed, even Moses, incited by a wonderful desire, seeks a more illustrious knowledge, Exod. 33, saying: Show me your face, to whom when God responds, He signifies how He wills to be acknowledged in the Church, even until the resurrection of the dead.

You cannot, He says, see my face, but you shall stand in the cleft of the rock, that is, insisting on Christ, or the Gospel in the Church, and I will pass by, that is, in the whole time of the world I will gather for myself, as if passing by in the world, some Church, and I will protect this with my right hand, and you will see the posterior parts, that is, you will know my presence from the events and deliverances, but after this passing, another glory remains.

Furthermore, just as Moses is placed there in the rock, so Christ here clearly teaches us that we should look upon Him, and determine that this is the eternal God, who revealed Himself in this son Christ, and wills to be invoked by the trust of this mediator: He who sees me, sees my father, that is, if you wish to seek the father, you will acknowledge Him only thus, if you fix your mind on me, the revealed Son, and determine that this one is the eternal father, the creator of things, who sent me, and that this is His will alone, which I announce, concerning the remission of sins, concerning eternal life.

Those who seek God otherwise, without me and without my word, wander, just as He says elsewhere: He who does not honor the Son, does not honor the father.

Concerning the second. This very discourse explains the doctrine concerning the three persons of the divinity, concerning the eternal father, the Son as mediator, and the Holy Spirit.

He distinguishes the Father and Himself, and yet He makes them of equal power. I am in the Father, and the Father is in me. He does the works, that is, we work together, Father and Son, just as it is said in John 5: My Father works until now, and I work. And John 1: All things were made through Him. It is added here also concerning the Holy Spirit: I will ask the Father, and He will give you another paraclete, that He may remain with you forever, the spirit of truth.

Three persons, therefore, are named here, who are simultaneously effective with equal power: the eternal Father, who begat the Son, and the begotten Son, who is the image of the Father, and the Holy Spirit, who is the agitator and vivifier in the hearts of the pious. Let this, therefore, be the form of invocation.

Almighty eternal God, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, creator and preserver of all things, with Thy Son and the Holy Spirit, wise, good, merciful, judge and strong, have mercy on me, for the sake of Jesus Christ Thy Son, whom Thou didst will to be a victim for us, by a wondrous and ineffable counsel, sanctify and rule my heart by Thy Holy Spirit, according to the promise: And He will give you another paraclete, the spirit of truth. This invocation distinguishes the Church from Turks, Heathens, and Jews.

Concerning the third.

Concerning the efficacy of invocation, He says: Whatever you ask in my name, I will do, and below in chapter 16: Whatever you ask the Father in my name, He will give you.

It is necessary, however, to observe that He commands us to ask in His name, namely, for two reasons: that prayer may be directed to the true God; and then that we may hold the certainty that we are heard, and why we are heard.

For it must be known that the Church is heard for the sake of the Son, the mediator. Therefore, we are commanded to ask with confidence in the Son, not with confidence in our own dignity, or with doubt, as the nations, the Jews, and all who are ignorant of the Gospel ask with doubt.

And the meaning is: In my name, that is, for the sake of me the mediator, or with confidence in the mediator. As often, therefore, as you begin your prayer, think of this promise: Whatever you ask the Father in my name, He will give you. Elsewhere He says: I will do it, so that He may show that He Himself hears, and at the same time works with the Father. Let us learn, however, that in the Church, true invocation is the peculiar and proper work of the Church of God alone: therefore, it must be known how it should be done, so that it may be rightly directed to God and be effective. For this, it is necessary to bring faith into the invocation, which truly establishes that we are received for the sake of Christ, and that the invocation is not in vain, but that we receive grace without any doubt, because this is promised by name. In corporal matters, however, [we ask for] mitigation or liberation, according to God's counsel, because we owe obedience in the cross, and God wills these liberations in this life to be different.

But why does He say: He will do greater things than these?

I answer: Daily, secret great works and great liberations happen in the Church, which do not fall into our eyes, but will be seen when the Church is glorified. For unless the Son of God were miraculously restraining the raging devil, he would utterly devastate the Church.

The Son of God, therefore, conquers in those who truly invoke God. But the devil conquers again in the impious, or in those who cast away faith.

Latin:

Evangelium in die Philippi et Iacobi, Iohannis 14.

Et dixit Iesus discipulis suis: Non turbetur cor vestrum. Creditis in Deum, et in me credite. In domo patris mei multae mansiones sunt. Sin autem minus, dixissem vobis, Vado ad parandum vobis locum. Et cum abiero, parare vobis locum, iterum veniam, et accipiam vos ad meipsum, ut ubi sum ego, et vos sitis. Et quo ego vado, scitis, et viam scitis. Dicit ei Thomas: Domine, nescimus quo vadis, et quomodo possumus viam scire? Dicit ei Iesus: Ego sum via, et veritas, et vita. Nemo venit ad patrem, nisi per me. Si cognovissetis me, et patrem meum utique cognovissetis. Et modo cognoscitis eum, et eum vidistis. Dicit ei Philippus: Domine, ostende nobis patrem, et sufficit nobis. Dicit ei Iesus: Tanto tempore vobiscum sum, et non cognovisti me? Philippe, qui videt me, videt patrem, et quomodo tu dicis, Ostende nobis patrem? Non credis, quod ego in patre, et pater in me est?

Verba quae ego loquor vobis, a me ipso non loquor: pater autem in me manens ipse facit opera. Credite mihi, quod ego in patre, et pater in me est: si autem non propter opera ipsa credite mihi.

Amen amen dico vobis, qui credit in me, opera quae ego facio, et ipse faciet, et maiora his faciet, quia ego ad patrem meum vado, Et quodcunque petieritis in nomine meo, hoc faciam, ut glorificetur pater in filio, Si quid petieritis in nomine meo, ego faciam.

Tres sunt praecipui loci.

I. Quomodo agnoscendus sit et adorandus Deus.

II. De Filio mediatore et Spiritu sancto.

III. De efficacia invocationis

De primo.

Praecipuum et omnium operum hominis maximum est agnitio et celebratio Dei, ad quam conditi sumus. Et indita fuit humanae menti lux aliqua de Deo, sed haec valde obscurata est, quare multae tristissimae dubitationes secutae sunt. Etsi enim mens humana in omnibus sanis statuit esse Deum, causam et opificem boni in natura, tamen dubitat universaliter, an velit nos indignos exaudire, iuvare, salvare. Ideo Deus inde usque ab initio per certum verbum et testimonium se patefecit, per quod agnosci se, et voluntatem suam erga nos voluit, et ibi recte se coli affirmat, ubi sic agnoscitur et invocatur, iuxta suum verbum, fide.

Sed mens humana facile abiicit verbum, vel propter crucem, vel propter insidias diaboli, Postea vero errans in tenebris, aut prorsus fit Epicurea, sicut nunc usitatum est, aut fingit sibi ipsa deos et cultus, sicut Ethnici fecerunt, et Mahometus. Et hi cultus omnes conficti humano consilio sunt inanes. Quia manet dubitatio, ubi ignoratur Evangelium, an Deus exaudiat.

Ideo discamus hanc doctrinam, quae in hoc Evangelio traditur: quod oporteat vivum et aeternum Deum sic agnoscere et invocare, sicut se ipse patefecit suo verbo et suis testimoniis, videlicet patrem Domini nostri Iesu Christi, per quem placatus est, et promisit se propicium fore, et sanctificaturum Spiritu sancto. Haec invocatio dupliciter prodest: Discernit invocationem veram ab ethnica, Iudaica et Mahometica, et dirigitur vere ad Deum, non aberrat a Deo.

Deinde et mediatoris mentione corrigit dubitationem, adfirmat nos exaudiri a Deo. Sic alligat Christus interrogantem Philippum ad conspectum mediatoris, quasi dicat: Scio vagari humanam mentem, et varie quaerere Deum: sed tu omitte humanas cogitationes, et definias vere esse Deum, qui hunc Christum crucifigendum, et resuscitandum misit, et se per eum patefecit mundo, et per eum promisit salutem, et velle se invocari, et coli fiducia huius mediatoris, iuxta verbum ipsi traditum.

Sic alligaverat initio patres ad promissionem: In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes. Sed difficile est menti acquiescere in verbo Dei, et requirimus sensibilem noticiam.

Ideo inquit Philippus: Domine ostende nobis patrem, et sufficit nobis, quasi dicat: Verbum non satisfacit mentibus nostris, conspectus satisfaceret, in quo cerneremus initia et exitus, causas et eventus, de quibus angimur. Sapienter et humano more cogitat.

Imo et Moises incitatus mirabili desiderio, petit illustriorem cognitionem, Exod. 33. inquiens: Ostende mihi faciem tuam, cui cum respondet Deus, significat, quomodo velit agnosci in Ecclesia, usque ad resuscitationem mortuorum.

Non poteris, inquit, videre faciem meam, sed stabis in foramine petrae, id est, insistens Christo, seu Evangelio in Ecclesia, et transibo, id est, toto tempore mundi colligam mihi quasi transiens in mundo aliquam Ecclesiam, et hanc protegam dextra mea, et videbis posteriora, id est, meam praesentiam ex eventibus et liberationibus cognoscetis, sed post hunc transitum alia gloria restat.

Porro ut illic Moses collocatur in saxum, ita Christus hic clare nos docet, ut sese intueamur, et statuamus hunc esse Deum aeternum, qui se in hoc filio Christo patefecit, et vult invocari fiducia huius mediatoris: Qui videt me, videt patrem meum, id est, si vis quaerere patrem, sic tantum agnosces, si defiges mentem in me Filium revelatum, et statues hunc solum esse aeternum patrem, conditorem rerum, qui me misit, et hanc esse voluntatem eius solam, quam ego annuncio, de remissione peccatorum, de vita aeterna.

Qui aliter quaerunt Deum, sine me, et sine verbo meo, aberrant, sicut alias inquit: Qui non honorificat Filium, non honorificat patrem.

De secundo. Haec ipsa concio exponit doctrinam de tribus personis divinitatis, de aeterno patre, Filio mediatore, et Spiritu sancto.

Discernit patrem et sese, et tamen facit aequalem potentiam. Ego sum in patre, et patre in me est. Ipse facit opera, id est, simul operamur, Pater et Filius, sicut Iohan. 5. dicitur: Pater meus usque modo operatur, et ego operor. Et Iohan. 1.: Omnia per ipsum facta sunt. Additur et hic de Spiritu sancto: Ego rogabo patrem, et alium paracletum dabit vobis, ut maneat vobiscum perpetuo, spiritum veritatis.

Tres igitur personae hic nominantur, quae simul sunt efficaces aequali potentia, pater aeternus, qui genuit Filium, et Filius genitus, qui est imago patris, et Spiritus sanctus, qui est agitator et vivificator in cordibus piorum. Sit igitur haec forma invocationis.

Omnipotens aeterne Deus, pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, conditor omnium rerum et conservator, cum Filio tuo et S.S., sapiens, bone, misericors, iudex et fortis, miserere mei, propter Iesum Christum Filium tuum, quem voluisti pro nobis esse victimam, mirando et inenarrabili consilio, sanctifica et rege cor meum Spiritus sancto tuo, iuxta promissionem: Et dabit vobis alium paracletum, spiritum veritatis. Haec invocatio discernit Ecclesiam a Turcis, Ethnicis et Iudaeis.

De tertio.

De efficacia invocationis dicit: Quicquid petieritis in nomine meo, ego faciam, et infra cap. 16.: Quicquid petieritis patrem in nomine meo, dabit vobis. Necesse est autem observare, quod iubet petere suo nomine, videlicet, propter duo, ut dirigatur oratio ad verum Deum: deinde ut teneatur certitudo quod exaudiamur, et cur exaudiamur.

Sciendum est enim, exaudiri Ecclesiam propter Filium mediatorem. Ergo fiducia Filii iubemur petere, non fiducia nostrae dignitatis, aut cum dubitatione, ut gentes, Iudaei, et omnes ignorantes Evangelium petunt cum dubitatione.

Estque sententia: In nomine meo, id est, propter me mediatorem, vel fiducia mediatoris. Quoties ergo incoabis tuam precationem, cogita hanc promissionem: Quicquid petieritis patrem in nomine meo, dabit vobis. Alibi inquit: Ego faciam, ut ostendat seipsum exaudire, et simul operari cum patre.

Discamus autem in Ecclesia veram invocationem peculiare et proprium opus esse solius Ecclesiae Dei: ideo sciendum est, quomodo facienda sit, ut recte ad Deum dirigatur, et sit efficax. Ad hoc necesse est afferre in invocatione fidem, quae vere statuat, nos recipi propter Christum, et invocationem non esse irritam, sed sine ulla dubitatione accipere gratiam, quia nominatim haec promissa est. In corporalibus vero, mitigationem aut liberationem, iuxta Dei consilium, quia debemus obedientiam in cruce, et Deus has liberationes in hac vita vult esse dissimiles.

Cur autem dicit: Maiora his faciet?

Respondeo: Quotidie arcana opera magna, magnae liberationes fiunt in Ecclesia, quae non incurrunt in oculos nostros, sed cernuntur cum Ecclesia glorificabitur. Nisi enim grassantem diabolum Filius Dei mirabiliter reprimeret, Ecclesiam funditus vastaret.

Vincit igitur Filius Dei in his, qui vere Deum invocant. Rursus autem vincit diabolus in impiis, aut abiicientibus fidem.

## 14:16-17 On Pentecost
On Pentecost, from the Gospel of John 14.

"If you love me, keep my commandments. And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Paraclete, that He may remain with you forever, the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it does not see Him, nor know Him. But you know Him, because He will remain with you, and will be in you.

I will not leave you orphans, I will come to you." Our negligence is to be deplored, for we do not sufficiently consider the immense and ineffable benefit of God, who on account of the Son gives the Holy Spirit, through whom sin and death are conquered, nor do we value it as much as it is, nay, we do not even stir ourselves to believe that such a great gift is given, and to ask for it. the gift. Let us first acknowledge, accuse, and deplore this infirmity of ours, just as in Luke 11 Christ rebukes this sloth, where mention is made of the widow, who by her persistence causes the judge at last to do his duty.

Where Christ adds: Ask, and you shall receive. If men can give good things to men, how much more will the heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask? Let us diligently propose to ourselves this rebuke of our sloth, and this exhortation of Christ, and let us stir ourselves up with these great promises, and learn to magnify the gift.

But so it is, the world does not know the Holy Spirit, as is said here in the text, because it does not know Christ.

O sad word, The world does not know the Holy Spirit, because it does not know Christ. Indeed, the world either mocks or persecutes the Holy Spirit.

Many seek wealth, pleasures, and do not experience the aids of the Holy Spirit. Papists want to defend their authority, idolatrous worship, and the pomp of works. They do not understand true justice and true invocation; indeed, they persecute them: therefore they know neither the Spirit nor Christ.

But the text adds: But you know the Holy Spirit. Here let us make an effort, that we too may be of this number of those who know.

Let us therefore consider the words of the text: I will ask the Father, and he will give you another paraclete etc.
