Let us not be long-winded, because no one can say enough about these things, but pious people, having heard or read some such part of the Gospel, ought to meditate on it all day and carry it about in their minds. This is to celebrate a feast day, and by this meditation pious hearers make progress. But lest we be long-winded, these two things must be observed. First,

the promise itself, that Christ promises that he will give the Holy Spirit.

Second, what the Holy Spirit does, which is added here, because he calls him παράκλητον (paraclete). This is the sweetest appellation of the Holy Spirit; he is called παράκλητος, which signifies an advocate in a trial. But this appellation embraces many duties: for an advocate is one who undertakes a defense in a trial, especially for him whose cause is in danger, and who is otherwise destitute of defense; he advises him, guides him with counsel, exhorts and confirms him, speaks for him, and as much as he can, protects him so that he may be freed from danger.

Thus when Christ attributes this sweetest appellation to the Holy Spirit, he testifies that his duties are similar, namely, he is sent by the eternal Father and the Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, so that he may be present with us miserable ones, guilty of eternal wrath and divine judgment; he is the patron of these, he undertakes the defense, suggests to us what is salutary, shows the counsel of how we may be freed, because he also kindles light in our hearts, so that they may understand the Gospel concerning the remission of sins, flee to Christ, and believe that they are forgiven for his sake: then he is an exhorter, and moves hearts so that they may assent, and he confirms that assent, raises up the terrified, bids them trust in salvation, and even speaks for us, namely by moving and impelling our hearts, so that they may dare to invoke and certainly expect help, as is said in Rom. 8: You have received the spirit of adoption of sons, by which we cry Abba Father etc. Item: The Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings that cannot be uttered. Finally, even in confession, he is openly our orator; he helps and confirms those who speak, as it is said: I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries will not be able to resist.

What can be said that is sweeter? O happy ones, to whom it is promised, and to whom such a benefit is given.

This briefly concerning the appellation, but let us also consider these two things, both that the Holy Spirit is promised to all who embrace the Gospel, and what his office is.

Concerning the first.

Concerning the first, let us diligently inculcate the promise to ourselves, and let each one know that it pertains to himself.

Many think thus: I see that there were certain great men, such as Moses, Elijah, etc., who did miracles; these I believe were endowed with the Holy Spirit. But we, being weak, are only guided by human reason; we do not dare to ask for or expect the Holy Spirit.

This is an impious and execrable imagination; therefore, the promises must be opposed to it, which testify that all are called: Come to me, all. Christ wishes to impart this benefit to all. And although we are not equal to Moses or Elijah, because God wishes the members of the Church to be unlike, yet to all who invoke Christ by faith, the Holy Spirit is given, as Paul says, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith. And know that the Holy Spirit is thus received, through the hearing of the Gospel and faith, not as the Anabaptists think, or the Monks, who are all Enthusiasts. the Anabaptists withdraw into corners, they invent speculations for themselves, they do not want to live in this civil life. By these means they think they receive the Holy Spirit, just as the Monks, and the idolatrous Papists boast that they obtain the Holy Spirit through their ludicrous ceremonies, Masses, and works of tradition.

But let us learn that the Holy Spirit is given through the word of God, whenever we comfort ourselves with the thought of it, hearing, or reading, or meditating on the word of God, and we call upon God, and believe that our sins are forgiven for Christ's sake, and that we are helped. These things happen in true repentance, and in the daily invocation of all who practice repentance, and do not persevere in sins against their conscience. I have spoken of the first part, namely, of the promise.

Now I will speak of the second, what the Holy Spirit does. Here Christ makes an antithesis.

I will not leave you orphans. This is a brief statement, but it is a true image of the Church before the world, and as we ourselves generally judge, when we feel the burden of our miseries.

See if we are not orphans? The world persecutes us, we are a small group, scattered, poorly connected. We have no human prince, king, or pontiff. It is ridiculous to the Pope and to kings when we call ourselves the Church. Furthermore, let each one consider his own miseries. Are we not orphans, without a defender, without certain aids? And especially then we would understand that we are orphans, if we could in any way perceive the power of the devil. Therefore, against such great enemies, Christ promises the Holy Spirit, saying: I will not leave you orphans, but I am your pontiff, I will ask the Father.

Believe, the Son does not pray in vain, he obtains help for us from the Father. What? The Spirit the Comforter, who shines in us, gives counsel, raises up the spirit, begins eternal life in us, just as it is said here: That he may remain with you forever. But so that we may be able to think about these benefits, and stir ourselves up, let us propose to ourselves the sweetest saying from Zechariah, where it is written: I will pour out upon the house of David the Spirit of grace and of supplications.

This voice embraces everything, and teaches what are good works, what are the highest and true worships of the Church. All nations, even the barbarian ones, have external worships of God, honest works. But these are not yet the worships by which God is properly worshipped and apprehended; only the Church has true worships, which it performs when it receives the spirit of grace and of supplications. What do these words mean?

The Spirit of grace signifies that we are helped by the Holy Spirit, so that we may conclude that we are in the grace of God, that we certainly please God, that our sins are forgiven for Christ's sake. This faith in every affliction recognizes that God is present as a helper, that he is propitious, that he will not leave orphans. By this faith the Holy Spirit is the Paraclete, the comforter and vivifier. There follows the other particle, the Spirit of supplications.

Since we are orphans in the world, we have need of God as a defender and helper. Therefore hearts are stirred by the Holy Spirit, so that they may call upon God, just as Paul also says: The Spirit helps us, so that we may cry Abba Father. Therefore the Church is burdened with huge dangers and miseries, so that we may exercise this invocation, that we may cry to God in faith, that we may expect help. And do not think that these are only magnificent words.

Pious believers truly experience that God is present as a helper and assistant, and great things and great miracles are thus done in the world. Thus your family is saved against the devil. Thus kingdoms are saved, as Hezekiah and Isaiah drove away the Assyrians with prayers. Other miracles, like those of Moses, are perceived more by the eyes, because God wants certain illustrious testimonies to exist. But yet the Church always has its miracles, which happen in invocation, just as Moses, just as Elijah were governed by the Holy Spirit in their invocation, and performed great and illustrious things. So let us ask to be governed by the Holy Spirit, and let us know that Christ's voice is true: He will give you the Spirit the Comforter. Let us know that the Holy Spirit is given to us, that our prayers are heard, that we are helped in all public and private dangers, that great things are accomplished against the devil, even if the world does not see it: because the war between Christ and the devil is waged in a wonderful way, through weak vessels in the Church, which Christ nevertheless makes effective by divine power through the Holy Spirit.

Remember therefore this voice: I will pour out the spirit of grace and of supplications. Stir yourself up by faith, so that you may believe that you are in grace for Christ's sake, ask for the Holy Spirit as a helper, call upon God in all business, so that you may experience this helper being present. Now let us also pray for the Church, that we may retain the Spirit of truth, because the devil most cunningly builds snares for the truth. It attempts to overwhelm the Gospel with new sophistry, and the world is delighted by these lies and deceptions, because it knows neither the Holy Spirit nor Christ. But the pious, who know Christ and seek the spirit of truth, oppose such impostures with all their heart. God, however, will preserve the Church and will repel the Turks, for the sake of the Church, not for the sake of the impious and idolaters. These things must be briefly noted this day, so that the pious may receive these warnings of Christ, and together we may invoke God for the sake of the Son, and ask for the Holy Spirit, just as He promised: My heavenly Father will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him.

Peter's Sermon, Acts 2.

But Peter, standing with the eleven, raised his voice and spoke to them: You men of Judea, and all who dwell in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and receive my words with your ears. For these are not drunk as you suppose, since it is the third hour of the day. But this is what was spoken by the Prophet Joel: And it shall be in the last days, says the Lord, I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh. And your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams. And indeed upon my servants and my handmaids in those days I will pour out of my Spirit, and they shall prophesy, and I will give wonders in heaven above, and signs on the earth below, blood and fire, and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the Moon into blood, before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes. And it shall be: Everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. You men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus the Nazarene, a man approved by God among you, by miracles, and wonders, and signs, which God did through Him in your midst, as you know, this man, delivered by the definite counsel and foreknowledge of God, you have crucified and killed by the hands of wicked men. Whom God raised up, having loosed the pains of hell, according to what was impossible for Him to be held by it. For David says of Him: I foresaw the Lord always before my face, because He is at my right hand, that I should not be moved. Therefore my heart was glad, and my tongue exulted, moreover my flesh also shall rest in hope. Because You will not leave my soul in hell, nor will You give Your holy one to see corruption. You have made known to me the ways of life, You will fill me with gladness with Your face. Men and brethren, let it be permitted to speak boldly to you concerning the patriarch David, because he both died and was buried, and his sepulcher is with us to this very day. Therefore, being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn to him with an oath, that of the fruit of his loins one should sit upon his throne, foreseeing he spoke of the resurrection of Christ, that He was neither left in hell, nor did His flesh see corruption. This Jesus God raised up, of which we all are witnesses. Therefore, being exalted by the right hand of God, and having received the promise of the Holy Spirit from the Father, He poured out this gift, which you see and hear.

Peter's sermon contains three main parts in total. The first is the saying of Joel, containing the promise of the Holy Spirit and of eternal salvation, proper to the New Testament. First, therefore, the benefits of the New Testament are described. The second part is the sermon concerning the death and resurrection of the Messiah, who is the cause of the benefits of the New Testament. And this passage is a testimony that this Jesus is the Messiah, because He rose from the dead. The third part is concerning the application, how we obtain these benefits of the New Testament, acquired through the Messiah, namely: Repent, and let every one of you be baptized in the name of Christ, for the remission of sins, and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

It is a long and very rich sermon, which cannot be fully recounted in a few words. However, it is profitable to meditate often on such passages to nourish the knowledge of the benefits of Christ, and to confirm faith, and to excite thanksgiving and love toward God.

Therefore, let us first speak briefly about the first part of Peter's sermon, namely, concerning the grace of the New Testament and the donation of the Holy Spirit.

It has three principal parts. to be holy, to perform certain motions, such as those of the saints, who are members of the kingdom of heaven, that is, of the true Church.

And these pious motions are excited by the Word, as it is said here: After your voice sounded, etc.

Latin:

In Pentecoste de Evangelio, Iohannis 14.

Si diligitis me, mandata mea servate. Et ego rogabo patrem, et alium paracletum dabit vobis, ut maneat vobiscum in aeternum, spiritum veritatis, quem mundus non potest accipere, quia non videt eum, nec scit eum. Vos autem cognoscitis eum, quia apud vos manebit, et in vobis erit.

Non relinquam vos orphanos, veniam ad vos. Deploranda est negligentia nostra, qui immensum et inenarrabile beneficium Dei, quod propter Filium dat Spiritum sanctum, per quem vincitur peccatum et mors, non satis consideramus, nec tanti facimus, quantum est, imo nec excitamus nos, ut credamus dari, ac petamus tantum munus. tum munus. Hanc nostram infirmitatem primum agnoscamus, accusemus et deploremus, sicut Lucae 11. castigat Christus hanc segniciem, ubi fit mentio de vidua, quae assiduitate perficit, ut iudex tandem faciat officium.

Ubi addit Christus: Petite, et accipietis. Si homines possunt dare bona hominibus, quanto magis pater coelestis dabit Spiritum sanctum petentibus? Hanc castigationem ignaviae nostrae, et adhortationem Christi, diligenter nobis proponamus, et nos excitemus his ingentibus promissionibus, et discamus magnificare munus.

Sed ita est, mundus non novit Spiritum sanctum, sicut hic in textu dicitur, quia non novit Christum.

O tristem vocem, Mundus non novit Spiritum sanctum, quia non novit Christum. Imo mundus aut deridet, aut persequitur Spiritum sanctum.

Plurimi quaerunt opes, voluptates, nec experiuntur Spiritus sancti auxilia. Papistae volunt tueri suam autoritatem, idololatricos cultus, pompas operum. Non intelligunt veram iusticiam, et veram invocationem, imo persequuntur: ideo nec Spiritum, nec Christum norunt.

Sed textus addit: Vos autem agnoscitis Spiritum sanctum. Hic demus operam, ut et nos simus ex hoc numero agnoscentium.

Consideremus igitur verba textus: Ego rogabo patrem, et alium paracletum dabit vobis etc.

Ne simus prolixi, quia nemo de his rebus satis dicere potest, sed pii audita vel lecta aliqua tali parte Evangelii, toto die meditari et circumferre animo debent. Hoc est celebrare festum diem, et hac meditatione proficiunt pii auditores. Sed ne simus prolixi, duo haec observanda sunt.

Primum ipsa promissio, quod Christus promittit se daturum Spiritum sanctum.

Secundo, quid agat Spiritus sanctus, quod hic additur, quia vocat παράκλητον. Haec est dulcissima appellatio Spiritus sancti, vocatur παράκλητος, quod significat advocatum in iudicio. Sed haec appellatio multa officia complectitur: nam advocatus est, qui patrocinium in iudicio suscipit, praesertim eius, cuius causa periclitatur, et alioqui destitutus est defensione, hunc monet, regit consilio, hortatur et confirmat, dicit pro eo, et quantum potest, tuetur ut liberet periculo.

Ita cum Christus hanc suavissimam appellationem tribuit Spiritus sancto, testatur similia eius esse officia, videlicet, ideo mittitur ab aeterno patre, et Filio, Domino nostro Iesu Christo, ut ad sit nobis miseris, reis aeternae irae, et iudicii divini, horum est patronus, suscipit defensionem, suggerit nobis salutaria, monstrat consilium, quomodo liberemur, quia et accendit lucem in cordibus, ut intelligant Evangelium de remissione peccatorum, confugiant ad Christum, et credant sibi propter eum ignosci: deinde est hortator, et movet corda, ut assentiantur, et confirmat assensionem, erigit perterrefactos, iubet confidere de salute, loquitur etiam pro nobis, scilicet movens et impellens corda, ut ausint invocare et certo expectare opem, sicut dicitur Rom. 8.: Accepistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum, quo clamamus Abba pater etc. Item: Ipse spiritus interpellat pro nobis gemitibus inenarrabilibus. Denique etiam in confessione palam est noster orator, adiuvat et confirmat dicentes, sicut dicitur: Dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere omnes adversarii vestri.

Quid potest dici dulcius? o felices, quibus promissum est, et datur tantum beneficium.

Haec breviter de appellatione, sed consideremus etiam haec duo, et quod promissum sit Spiritus sanctus omnibus amplectentibus Evangelium, et quod sit eius officium.

De primo.

De primo, diligenter inculcemus nobis promissionem, et sciant singuli eam ad seipsos pertinere.

Multi sic cogitant, Video quosdam fuisse magnos viros, ut Moisen, Eliam etc. qui mirabilia fecerunt, Hos credo fuisse donatos Spiritu sancto. Sed nos imbecilles tantum regimur humana ratione, non audemus petere aut expectare Spiritum sanctum.

Haec est impia et execranda imaginatio, sunt igitur opponendae promissiones, quae testantur omnes vocari: Venite ad me omnes. Omnibus vult Christus impertire hoc beneficium. Et quanquam non sumus pares Moisi aut Eliae, quia Deus vult esse membra Ecclesiae dissimilia, tamen omnibus invocantibus Christum fide, datur Spiritus sanctus, sicut Paulus inquit, ut promissionem spiritus accipiamus per fidem. Et scito sic accipi Spiritum sanctum, per auditum Evangelii et fidem, non sicut Anabaptistae cogitant, aut Monachi, qui omnes sunt Enthusiastae. baptistae secedunt in angulos, fingunt sibi speculationes, nolunt hac vita civili vivere, His modis putant se accipere Spiritum sanctum, sicut et Monachi, et idololatrae Papistae iactitant se consequi Spiritum sanctum per suas ludicras ceremonias, Missas et opera traditionum.

Sed nos discamus dari Spiritum sanctum per verbum Dei, quandocunque nos eius cogitatione consolamur, audientes, vel legentes, vel cogitantes verbum Dei, et invocamus Deum, ac credimus nobis ignosci propter Christum, et nos iuvari. Haec fiunt in vera poenitentia, et quotidiana invocatione omnium qui agunt poenitentiam, et non perseverant in delictis contra conscientiam. Dixi de prima parte, scilicet, de promissione.

Nunc dicam de secunda, quid agat Spiritus sanctus. Hic Christus facit antithesin.

Non relinquam vos orphanos. Brevis est oratio, sed est vera imago Ecclesiae coram mundo, et sicut nos ipsi plerumque iudicamus, quando sentimus onus aerumnarum nostrarum.

Vide an non sumus orphani? Mundus nos persequitur, sumus coetus exiguus, dissipatus, male cohaerens. Non habemus humanum principem, regem, pontificem. Ridiculum est Papae et regibus, quando nos vocamus Ecclesiam. Deinde singuli suas miserias considerent. Nonne sumus orphani, sine defensore, sine certis auxiliis? Et praesertim tunc intelligeremus nos esse orphanos, si potentiam diaboli aliquo modo cerneremus. Ergo adversus tantos hostes promittit Christus Spiritum sanctum, ait: Non relinquam vos orphanos, sed ego sum pontifex vester, Rogabo patrem.

Crede, non frustra orat Filius, impetrat nobis a patre auxilium. Quod? Spiritum paracletum, qui in nobis lucet, dat consilium, erigit animum, incoat vitam aeternam in nobis, sicut hic dicitur: Ut maneat vobiscum semper. Ut autem de his beneficiis cogitare possimus, et nos ipsos excitare, proponamus nobis dulcissimum dictum ex Zacharia, ubi scriptum est: Effundam super domum David Spiritum gratiae et precum.

Haec vox omnia complectitur, et docet quae sint bona opera, qui sint summi et veri cultus Ecclesiae. Omnes gentes, etiam barbarae, habent cultus Dei externos, honesta opera. Sed hi nondum sunt cultus, quibus proprie colitur et apprehenditur Deus, sola Ecclesia habet veros cultus, quos praestat, cum accipit spiritum gratiae et precum. Quid significant haec verba?

Spiritus gratiae significat Spiritu sancto nos iuvari, ut statuamus nos esse in gratia Dei, certo placere Deo, nobis peccata esse remissa propter Christum. Haec fides in omni afflictione agnoscit Deum adesse opitulatorem, esse propicium, non esse deserturum orphanos. Hac fide Spiritus sanctus est παράκλητος, consolator et vivificator. Sequitur altera particula, Spiritum precum.

Cum simus orphani in mundo, opus est nobis defensore et auxiliatore Deo. Ideo excitantur corda Spiritu sancto, ut invocent Deum, sicut et Paulus inquit: Spiritus adiuvat nos, ut clamemus Abba pater. Ideo Ecclesia est onerata ingentibus periculis et aerumnis, ut hanc invocationem exerceamus, fide clamemus ad Deum, expectemus auxilium. Nec putes haec tantum magnifica verba esse.

Pii credentes experiuntur vere adesse Deum opitulatorem et auxiliatorem, et res magnae et magna miracula sic fiunt in mundo. Sic servatur tua familia contra diabolum. Sic servantur regna, ut Ezechias et Esaias precibus pellebant Assyrios. Alia miracula, ut Moisi, magis cernuntur oculis, quia Deus vult extare illustria quaedam testimonia. Sed tamen Ecclesia semper habet sua miracula, quae fiunt in invocatione, ut Moises, ut Elias in sua invocatione gubernabantur Spiritu sancto, et res magnas et illustres gerebant. Ita petamus nos gubernari Spiritu sancto, et sciamus veram esse Christi vocem: Dabit vobis Spiritum paracletum. Sciamus dari nobis Spiritum sanctum, exaudiri nostras preces, iuvari nos in omnibus periculis publicis et privatis, res magnas effici contra diabolum, etiamsi mundus non cernit: quia bellum inter Christum et diabolum mirabili modo geritur, per vasa infirma in Ecclesia, quae Christus tamen efficit potentia divina per Spiritum sanctum.

Memento ergo hanc vocem: Effundam spiritum gratiae et precum. Excites te fide, ut credas te propter Christum esse in gratia, Petito Spiritum sanctum auxiliatorem, invoca Deum in omnibus negotiis, ut experiaris adesse hunc opitulatorem. Nunc etiam oremus pro Ecclesia, ut retineamus Spiritum veritatis, quia diabolus callidissime struit insidias veritati. Conatur nova sophistica obruere Evangelium, et mundus delectatur his mendaciis et praestigiis, quia nec Spiritum sanctum novit, neque Christum. Sed pii, qui norunt Christum, et petunt spiritum veritatis, toto pectore adversentur talibus imposturis. Deus tamen servabit Ecclesiam, depellet Turcas, propter Ecclesiam, non propter impios et idololatras. Haec breviter hoc die monenda sunt, ut haec monita Christi accipiant pii, et una invocemus Deum propter Filium, et petamus Spiritum sanctum, sicut promisit: Pater meus coelestis dabit Spiritum sanctum petentibus.

Concio Petri, Actorum 2.

Stans autem Petrus cum undecim, elevavit vocem suam, et locutus est eis: Viri Iudaei, et qui habitatis Hierusalem universi, hoc vobis notum sit, et auribus percipite verba mea. Non enim sicut vos existimatis hi ebrii sunt, cum sit hora diei tertia. Sed hoc est, quod dictum est per Prophetam Ioël: Et erit in novissimis diebus, dicit Dominus, Effundam de spiritu meo super omnem carnem. Et prophetabunt filii vestri et filiae vestrae, et iuvenes vestri visiones videbunt, et seniores vestri somnia somniabunt. Et quidem super servos meos et ancillas meas in diebus illis effundam de spiritu meo, et prophetabunt, et dabo prodigia in coelo sursum, et signa in terra deorsum, sanguinem et ignem, et vaporem fumi. Sol convertetur in tenebras, et Luna in sanguinem, antequum veniat dies Domini magnus et manifestus. Et erit: Omnis quicunque invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit. Viri Israëlitae, audite verba haec, Iesum Nazarenum virum approbatum a Deo in vobis, virtutibus, et prodigiis et signis, quae fecit Deus per illum in medio vestri, sicut scitis, hunc definitio consilio, et praesentia Dei traditum per manus iniquorum affigentes interemistis. Quem Deus suscitavit, solutis doloribus inferni, iuxta quod impossibile erat, teneri illum ab eo. David enim dicit in eum: Providebam Dominum in conspectu meo semper, quoniam a dextris est mihi, ne commovear. Propter hoc laetatum est cor meum, et exultavit lingua mea, insuper et caro mea requiescet in spe. Quoniam non derelinques animam meam in inferno, nec dabis sanctum tuum videre corruptionem. Notus fecisti mihi vias vitae, replebis me iucunditate cum facie tua. Viri fratres, liceat audenter dicere ad vos de patriarcha David, quoniam et defunctus est, et sepultus est, et sepulcrum eius est apud nos usque in hodiernum diem. Propheta igitur cum esset, et sciret, quia iureiurando iurasset illi Deus, de fructu lumborum eius sedere super sedem eius, praevidens locutus est de resurrectione Christi, quod neque derelictus est in inferno, neque caro eius vidit corruptionem. Hunc Iesum resuscitavit Deus, cuius omnes testes sumus. Dextera igitur Dei exaltatus, et promissione Spiritus sancti accepta a patre, effudit hoc donum, quod vos videtis et auditis.

Concio Petri tota continet tres praecipuas partes. Prima est dictum Ioëlis, continens promissionem Spiritus sancti, et salutis aeternae propriam novi Testamenti. Primum igitur describuntur beneficia novi Testamenti. Secunda pars est, Concio de morte et resurrectione Messiae, qui est causa beneficiorum novi Testamenti. Estque hic locus testimonium, quod hic Iesus sit Messias, quia resurrexit a mortuis. Tertia pars, de applicatione, quomodo haec beneficia novi Testamenti, parta per Messiam consequamur, videlicet: Agite poenitentiam, et baptizetur unusquisque in nomine Christi, ad remissionem peccatorum, et accipite donum Spiritus sancti.

Longa concio est, et locupletissima, quae non potest paucis tota enarrari. Prodest autem tales locos saepe meditari ad alendam cognitionem beneficiorum Christi, et confirmandam fidem, et ad excitandam gratiarum actionem, et dilectionem erga Deum.

Ideo primum breviter de prima parte concionis Petri dicamus, videlicet, de gratia novi Testamenti, et de donatione Spiritus sancti.

Tres habet praecipuos locos. sanctum, certos motus efficere, quales sunt sanctorum, qui sunt membra regni coelorum, id est, Ecclesiae verae.

Et hi motus pii excitantur verbo, ut hic dicitur: Postquam sonuit vox tua etc.

## 14:23-25 On the Day of Pentecost
On the Day of Pentecost. The Gospel of John 14.

"If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him, and make our home with him. He who does not love me does not keep my words, and the word which you hear is not mine, but the Father's who sent me. These things I have spoken to you while remaining with you.

But the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, He will teach you all things, and will bring to your remembrance all things that I have said to you. Peace I leave with you, my peace I give to you; not as the world gives, do I give to you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid. You have heard that I said to you, I am going away and coming back to you. If you loved me, you would rejoice, because I said, I am going to the Father, for my Father is greater than I."

And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it has happened, you may believe. I will not speak much more with you, for the prince of this world is coming, and he has nothing in me. But so that the world may know that I love the Father, and just as the Father gave me a commandment, so I do. Arise, let us go from here.

On Pentecost.

Two topics.

I. A comparison of the Pentecost of the Old Testament with the Pentecost of the New Testament.

II. On the Holy Spirit, what it is, for what purpose it is given, and to whom.

On the first.

By a singular counsel, God willed that the times of the promulgated law and the given Holy Spirit should coincide, so that the comparison might admonish the pious concerning the end of both actions. On the fiftieth day after the exodus from Egypt, namely after the Passover of the people of Israel, the law was promulgated with a terrible voice from heaven, because God willed that a public testimony of His judgment against the sins of men should exist. And when the people had heard the law, they were terrified and asked that the commandments of God be brought to the multitude through Moses. For they felt that they could not sustain the voice of the law. This history signifies the same things that happen in individuals when we hear the voice of the law, that is, when we feel God judging. For the guilty nature of men cannot sustain the wrath of God who judges and terrifies the conscience with the law, as Hezekiah says: As a lion, he crushed all my bones. Therefore, with the law promulgated, sin and the wrath of God are recognized.

Since He wills to remove these evils by the benefit of the New Testament, just as Passover corresponds to Passover—the true victim to the shadow—so to the promulgation of the law, which shows sin and wrath, there corresponds in this Pentecost the manifest testimony of the donation of the Holy Spirit, through whom a new kingdom is begun, in which the voice of the Gospel sounds concerning the remission of sins and the donation of the Holy Spirit, beginning righteousness and eternal life. This second Pentecost is much more glorious than the former. In the former, sin and the wrath of God are shown; in the second, they are removed.

On the second. What the Holy Spirit is.

As often as we think about the Trinity, let us look at the admirable revelation divinely made in the baptism of Christ, where the three persons are most clearly discerned. And the Holy Spirit is a person proceeding from the Father and the Son, stirring hearts and exciting new and divine motions, consistent with the law of God. And indeed, the very saying of Joel testifies that the Holy Spirit is of the divine substance, because he says: I will pour out of my spirit, My, I say, which is of my substance.

For what purpose is it given? This is taught copiously, but I will take one saying of Zechariah 12: I will pour out upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, a spirit of grace and of prayers. This most sweet sentence embraces all the benefits of the Holy Spirit, and the true worship of God. It testifies that the Holy Spirit is given, and that this is the spirit of grace, that is, testifying in our hearts, first, that we are in the grace of God, or inclining hearts so that they may assent to the promise of grace. For this is the first effect of the Holy Spirit, to incline hearts so that they may recognize the Son of God, and resolve that they are received into grace, just as Christ says: He will glorify me, that is, he will be a witness through the preaching of the Gospel, and he will incline hearts so that they may assent to the Gospel, and he will suffuse them with a new light, so that they may understand the Gospel, and discern it from the wisdom of the world.

But when we know the mercy of God and receive remission, we dare now to approach God, to invoke him, because unless faith is present, establishing the remission of sins, hearts flee from God, they do not invoke him; but by faith through Christ we have access to God, as is said in Romans 5. Likewise, Romans 8: You have received the spirit of adoption of sons, by which we cry Abba Father, that is, when hearts are raised by the voice of the Gospel and faith, they are clothed with the Holy Spirit, they recognize the mercy of God, they truly invoke God with the confidence of the Son, they recognize that he is the Father, etc.

Therefore Zechariah says, a spirit of grace and of prayers, embracing the two first and principal effects of the Holy Spirit, namely, to testify that we are in grace, and to impel us to invocation. Furthermore, invocation embraces the remaining pious motions, love, and new obedience.

These things are amplified by many sermons of Christ and the Apostles, which are promises to be fixed in the mind: I will not leave you orphans. It is certain that the Church in the world, though it wishes to be an orphan without human protections, subject to the cross, is attacked by the devil, who contrives sects, disputes, scandals, slaughters, persecution, and by the instruments of the devil, tyrants and others. But Christ says that he will add a paraclete for us, who may rule with counsel, and confirm minds, who may retain minds in the true sentiment, and enlighten them so that they may rightly understand the Gospel, and discern it from the wisdom of the world, just as Christ says: I will give you the spirit of truth, that is, who makes [men] truthful in doctrine and in invocation.

To whom it is given.

The public exhibition of the Holy Spirit was a testimony that the Holy Spirit is truly given to the whole Church. Therefore, in this testimony, let us contemplate the universal promise. Just as the remission of sins is offered to all, and it is commanded to all that they believe, so the Holy Spirit is promised to all, and is given to all who perform repentance and sustain themselves by faith, as Paul testifies manifestly in Galatians 3: That we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith. And Christ says that he is given to those who ask. Luke 11: How much more will the heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask. But the particle "to those who ask" must be diligently observed, by which Christ requires and demands the petition of this gift. Which indeed he promises liberally in those words.

Therefore let us perform repentance, and exercise faith in invocation, and let us ask for the Holy Spirit, that he may begin a new light and a new obedience in us, as it is said in 2 Corinthians 3: We all, with unveiled face beholding the glory of the Lord, are transformed into the same image, from glory to glory, as by the Spirit of the Lord, that is, we, having heard the Gospel and received the remission of sins, behold the glory of God, that is, we dare to approach God, and we see his glory, that is, the brightness of judgment, and in that judgment, by the voice of the Gospel, we have consolation, and we are clothed with the light of faith, so that we may recognize more and more the wrath of God and his mercy, and be adorned with a new light, which is the image of God, that is, the knowledge of God, trust in the presence of God, love, and other virtues, and he adds, "as by the Spirit of the Lord," so that we may know this renewal to be the work of the Holy Spirit in us.

Let us also know that the Holy Spirit is shaken off by falls against conscience, as it is said in Galatians 5: Walk in the Spirit, and you shall not fulfill the lust of the flesh, and then: The works of the flesh are manifest, adultery, fornication, hatreds, of which I have told you, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God. And of these John says: He who commits sin is of the devil, and Hebrews 10: Trampling under foot the Son of God, and polluting the blood of the testament, and doing despite to the spirit of grace. This doctrine is necessary for Christians, so that they may know that the Holy Spirit is promised to all, and is received by all through faith in true repentance, and is retained while we remain in the exercises of true repentance and invocation.

Latin:

In Die Pentecostes. Evangelium Iohannis 14.

Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit, et pater meus diliget eum, et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus. Qui non diligit me, sermones meos non servat, Et sermonem quem audistis, non est meus, sed eius qui misit me patris. Haec locutus sum vobis, apud vos manens.

Paracletus autem Spiritus sanctus, quem mittit pater in nomine meo, ille vos docebit omnia, et suggeret vobis omnia, quaecunque dixi vobis. Pacem relinquo vobis, pacem meam do vobis, Non quomodo mundus dat, ego do vobis. Non turbetur cor vestrum, neque formidet. Audistis quod ego dixi vobis, Vado et venio ad vos. Si diligeretis me, gauderetis utique, quia dixi, Vado ad patrem, quia pater maior me est.

Et nunc dixi vobis, priusquam fiat, ut cum factum fuerit, credatis. Non iam multa loquar vobiscum, venit enim princeps mundi huius, et in me non habet quicquam. Sed ut cognoscat mundus, quia diligo patrem, et sicut mandatum dedit mihi pater, sic facio. Surgite, eamus hinc.

De Pentecoste.

Loci duo.

I. Collatio Pentecostes veteris Testamenti ad Pentecosten novi Testamenti.

II. De Spiritu sancto, quid sit, ad quid detur, et quibus.

De primo.

Singulari consilio voluit Deus convenire tempora promulgatae legis, et dati Spiritus sancti, ut collatio admoneat pios de utriusque actionis fine. Die quinquagesimo post exitum ex Aegypto, videlicet post Pascha populi Israël, promulgata est lex terribili voce de coelo, quia Deus voluit extare publicum testimonium sui iudicii adversus peccata hominum. Et cum populus audivisset legem, expavit, ac petivit, ut per Moisen deferrentur mandata Dei ad multitudinem. Senserunt enim, se non posse sustinere vocem legis. Haec historia significat eadem quae geruntur in singulis, cum audimus vocem legis, id est, cum sentimus Deum iudicantem. Non enim potest natura hominum rea, sustinere iram Dei iudicantis, et lege terrentis conscientiam, sicut inquit Ezechias: Sicut leo contrivit omnia ossa mea. Ergo promulgata lege agnoscuntur peccatum et ira Dei.

Haec mala cum tollere velit beneficio novi Testamenti, ut Paschati respondet Pascha, umbrae vera victima, sic promulgationi legis monstrantis peccatum et iram, respondet in hac Pentecoste manifestum testimonium donationis Spiritus sancti, per quem incoatur novum regnum, in quo sonat vox Evangelii de remissione peccatorum, et de donatione Spiritus sancti, incoantis iusticiam et vitam aeternam. Haec secunda Pentecoste multo gloriosior est priore. In priore monstrantur peccatum et ira Dei, in secunda tolluntur.

De secunda. Quid sit Spiritus sanctus.

Quoties de Trinitate cogitamus, intuearum admirandam revelationem divinitus factam in baptismo Christi, ubi tres personae clarissime discernuntur. Estque Spiritus sanctus persona procedens a Patre et Filio, agitans corda, et exuscitans novos et divinos motus, convenientes legi Dei. Et quidem ipsum dictum Ioëlis testatur, Spiritum sanctum esse substantiae divinae, quia inquit: Effundam de spiritu meo, Meo, inquam, qui est meae substantiae.

Ad quid datur? Hoc copiose traditur, sed sumam unum dictum Zachariae 12.: Effundam super domum David, et super habitatores Ierusalem, spiritum gratiae et precum. Haec dulcissima sententia complectitur omnia beneficia Spiritus sancti, et veros cultus Dei. Testatur donari Spiritum sanctum, et hunc esse spiritum gratiae, id est, in cordibus nostris testificantem, primum quod simus in gratia Dei, seu inclinantem corda, ut adsentiantur promissioni gratiae. Nam hic primus effectus est Spiritus sancti, inclinare corda ut agnoscant Filium Dei, et statuant se recipi in gratiam, sicut Christus inquit: Ipse me glorificabit, id est, erit testis per Evangelii praedicationem, et inclinabit corda ut adsentiantur Evangelio, et nova luce perfundet, ut intelligant Evangelium, et discernant a sapientia mundi.

Cum autem cognoscimus misericordiam Dei, et accipimus remissionem, audemus iam accedere ad Deum, invocare eum, quia nisi adsit fides, statuens de remissione peccatorum, fugiunt corda Deum, non invocant, sed fide per Christum habemus accessum ad Deum, ut Rom. 5. dicitur. Item, Rom. 8.: Accepistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum, quo clamamus Abba pater, id est, cum corda eriguntur voce Evangelii et fide, induuntur Spiritu sancto, agnoscunt misericordiam Dei, vere Deum invocant fiducia Filii, agnoscunt patrem esse etc.

Ideo Zacharias dicit, Spiritum gratiae et precum, duos primos et praecipuos effectus Spiritus sancti complectens, scilicet testificari quod simus in gratia, et impellere ad invocationem. Porro invocatio complectitur reliquos pios motus, dilectionem, et novam obedientiam.

Haec multis concionibus Christi et Apostolorum amplificantur, quae sunt promissiones infigendae animis: Non relinquam vos orphanos. Constat Ecclesiam in mundo, velit orphanam esse sine praesidiis humanis, subiectam cruci, oppugnari a diabolo, moliente sectas, disputationes, scandala, caedes, persecutionem, et ab organis diaboli, tyrannis et aliis. Sed Christus inquit, additurum se nobis paracletum, qui consilio regat, et confirmet mentes, qui retineat mentes in vera sententia, et illustret ut Evangelium recte intelligant, et discernant a sapientia mundi, sicut Christus inquit: Dabo vobis spiritum veritatis, id est, qui efficit veraces in doctrina et in invocatione.

Quibus detur.

Publica exhibitio Spiritus sancti fuit testimonium, quod vere detur Spiritus sanctus toti Ecclesiae. Ideo in hoc testimonio contemplemur universalem promissionem. Ut omnibus offertur remissio peccatorum, et omnibus praecipitur ut credant, ita Spiritus sanctus promissus est omnibus, et datur omnibus agentibus poenitentiam, et fide sustentantibus, sicut manifeste testatur Paulus Galat. 3. Ut promissionem spiritus accipiamus per fidem. Et Christus inquit, dari eum petentibus. Lucae 11.: Quanto magis pater coelestis dabit Spiritum sanctum petentibus. At diligenter observanda est particula petentibus, qua Christus requirit, et postulat petitionem huius muneris. Quod quidem in verbis illis liberaliter promittit.

Quare agamus poenitentiam, et exerceamus fidem in invocatione, et petamus Spiritum sanctum, ut novam lucem et novam obedientiam in nobis incoët, sicut 2. Corinth. 3. dicitur: Nos omnes revelata facie gloriam Domini speculantes, in eandem imaginem transformamur, a gloria in gloriam, tanquam a Domini spiritu, id est, nos audito Evangelio, et accepta remissione peccatorum, gloriam Dei speculamur, id est, audemus accedere ad Deum, et videmus eius gloriam, id est, fulgorem iudicii, ac in illo iudicio, voce Evangelii, consolationem habemus, ac induimur luce fidei, ut magis magisque iram Dei et misericordiam agnoscamus, et nova luce, quae est imago Dei, ornemur, id est, noticia Dei, fiducia praesentiae Dei, dilectione, et caeteris virtutibus, et addit, tanquam a Domini spiritu, ut sciamus hanc renovationem esse, opus Spiritus sancti in nobis.

Illud etiam sciamus, excuti Spiritum sanctum lapsibus, contra conscientiam, ut Gal. 5. dicitur: Spiritu ambulate, et concupiscentiam carnis non perficietis, et deinde: Manifesta sunt opera carnis, adulterium, scortatio, odia, de quibus dixi, talia facientes, regnum Dei non consecuturos esse. Et de his Iohannes inquit: Qui facit peccatum, ex diabolo est, et Ebrae. 10. Filium Dei conculcans, et sanguinem testamenti polluens, et spiritum gratiae contumelia afficiens. Haec doctrina necessaria est Christianis, ut sciant omnibus promissiam esse Spiritum sanctum, et accipi ab omnibus fide in vera poenitentia, et retineri, dum manemus in exercitiis verae poenitentiae et invocationis.

## 15:26-27 Dominica Exaudi
Dominica Exaudi.

Gospel of John 15. But when the Paraclete shall come, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, He shall bear witness of me. And you also shall be witnesses, because you have been with me from the beginning.

These things I have spoken to you, that you may not be offended in anything. They will make you outcasts from the synagogues, but the hour comes that everyone who kills you will think that he is offering worship to God. And these things they will do to you, because they have not known the Father, nor me. But these things I have spoken to you, that when that time comes, you may remember them, that I have told you. These things, however, I did not tell you from the beginning, because I was with you.

Four Topics.

I. The doctrine concerning God, who He is, and how He is to be acknowledged and invoked.

II. Who the Holy Spirit is, and what His proper office is.

III. A twofold testimony, one through the ministry, the other in the hearts.

IV. The doctrine of the cross.

On the first.

Men must often be admonished concerning invocation. Many say prayers by a certain custom, so that the mind neither thinks about whom it is invoking as God, nor does it itself seek within itself whether God hears, nor does it separate its own invocation from the Turkish [invocation], and minds in the recognition of true doctrine, and may it kindle true fear, true love, and prevent the audacity of inventing opinions without the word of God, etc. As David prays, 'Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right [that is, firm] spirit within me.' On the third. Often the statement from Christ has been repeated: 'The Holy Spirit shall testify of me.' This statement describes the offices already mentioned, but a twofold testimony should always be joined: the exterior through the ministry, and the interior in the heart. Both are the work of the Holy Spirit, and of both it is said: 'He will reprove the world of sin.' He reproves, however, in the ministry publicly, and privately in the hearts of individuals. Likewise, concerning the ministry it is said: 'He ascended, he gave gifts unto men, Prophets, Apostles, Pastors, Teachers.' Furthermore, many fanatical opinions are refuted here. The Anabaptists utterly reject the ministry of the Gospel, the voice, and the doctrine; they invent spiritual motions without and outside the Gospel. The defenders of vicious monastic cults, of the invocation of saints, and of the abuse of the Lord's Supper, invent cults without the word of God, and allege the Holy Spirit, who they claim has approved or shown these things. Against all these errors this statement must be opposed. The Holy Spirit will testify of Christ, that is, He will sound the voice delivered by Christ, just as Christ says: 'He shall bring to your remembrance whatsoever I have said.' Likewise: 'The Holy Spirit shall glorify me.' Therefore, where the ministry or the Gospel is removed, there the Holy Spirit does not testify of Christ. It is necessary to know this first concerning the ministry. Afterwards, the pious understand what interior testimony is, when, with the word of God heard or pondered, there arise senses of the wrath of God, and terrors and sorrows for sin, and again consolations from the recognition of Christ, and faith, and invocation not hindered by an evil conscience. This is the interior testimony, which Paul describes in this statement: 'Ye have received the spirit of adoption of sons, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.' For as I said above concerning Cato, as long as the mind doubts whether God is willing to receive and hear you, it flees from God; but when you recognize the promise concerning the mediator, and believe that you are received, at the same time the Holy Spirit is efficacious, He stirs up invocation, love, and other virtues. And Galatians 3: 'That we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.' This statement must always be kept in view. For it warns both how the Holy Spirit is given, and what is the chief action by which He testifies in us. He is given through the Gospel, just as Paul says elsewhere: 'The Gospel is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth,' that is, the Gospel is truly efficacious, and God indeed imparts good things to one who ponders the Gospel and acquiesces in it, or assents to it, when we acquiesce and believe that we are received and heard, because God has revealed this His will in His Gospel, and He wills that we believe these things, and He sent His Son, that He might be the price, and the witness, and the pledge of this will. In this consolation the Holy Spirit is truly given, and the consolation itself and the invocation in the heart testify of God. The Holy Spirit now kindles this light, so that we may more firmly conclude that we are in God's care, that we are received for the sake of the Son, and He kindles also the invocation. These things are known to the pious, who feel terrors and think: 'Which God should I invoke? Do I think I am heard? And why does God hear?' The greatest part of men recite prayers merely as an empty murmur, and most do not even think about whom they are invoking, or whether God cares for human cries, but they obey custom. This impiety must be corrected, and in every prayer one must think of the word of God, so that faith may be kindled, and who God is, and how He is to be invoked, may be recognized—namely, He who has revealed Himself by His own voice and through His Son Christ. Here again our unworthiness clamors. 'Why would God hear you more than Saul and his like? What virtues do you have? In what do you excel other men? Why do you think God cares for this murmur of yours?' These thoughts harshly torment souls, and are often the darts of the devil, sent to shake faith, so as to drive souls into perpetual despair and Epicurean blasphemies. And many are overturned in this way. Therefore, let us be intent here above all, and let us know that this is the proper office of the Holy Spirit, to testify of God in the heart. Therefore He is given so that hearts may be confirmed by the true recognition of God. But the precepts and promises of God must be gathered, which testify that He demands this cult, namely invocation, and that He truly wills to grant good things to those who ask, just as Christ says: 'Ask, and ye shall receive,' and indeed He hears not because of our dignity, but because of the Son, yet let not a purpose of sinning be brought forward. 'As I live,' He says, 'I have no pleasure in the death of the sinner, but that he should turn and live.' Thus God commands us to acquiesce. in his promise, and not without struggle and labor, the heart is conquered by these testimonies, so that it may acquiesce.

In this struggle, the Holy Spirit is truly effective, and He bends hearts so that they may acquiesce. Thus, let us know that we are helped by the Holy Spirit in invocation, as it says in Zechariah: "I will pour upon them the spirit of grace and of supplications." And as in invocation, so in all our dangers and actions, let us seek and expect this help. As Christ says: "I will give you the Comforter, the Spirit, providing counsel and help," just as He sustains David in exile, so that he does not despair, and bends him toward better counsels, and helps him in those very affairs.

These things are better understood when, in dangers, we seek this governor through true invocation: let us consider, however, that God has not shown such great promises in vain; He wants them to be sought. He did not send the Son in vain, but wants Him to be acknowledged; He does not promise this huge gift to us all in vain, namely, the fellowship of His nature, by pouring His divine Spirit into our hearts, as it is said: "I will pour out of my Spirit," etc. He wants this gift only to be sought, and He gives it to those who ask, as Christ says: "How much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him." And to whom He gives it, I have already said: to all who turn to God and ask.

He does not give it to those who are unwilling to ask, who spurn such a gift, who are unwilling to turn to God. Let us, therefore, rouse ourselves to repentance and to asking for the Holy Spirit.

On the fourth point.

The final part of this lesson preaches about the cross.

For this warning opposes the common imagination of the Jews, who pretended that in the kingdom of the Messiah, He would occupy empires and they would have the sweetest tranquility: He censures this error and warns what the kingdom of the Messiah will be like before the resurrection. "I will scatter my Gospel through you into the whole world, so that I may gather a Church that believes in me and confesses me, which I will rule by the Holy Spirit, so that in them new justice and eternal life may begin.

I do not send you to occupy empires, but often empires will exercise cruelty against you and the Church; indeed, this very people of Israel, who boast in the title of the people of God, will oppose you: they will cast you out of their Church as enemies of God." But now I warn you, so that you may know that the true Church is there where my Gospel will be, and the invocation of God through my name, just as He had said a little before: "If you remain in me, and my words remain in you, whatever you wish, you shall ask, and it shall be done for you." Likewise: "In this my heavenly Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit, and become my disciples." Nothing is sadder than to be cast out of the Church, which is truly called so. Therefore, let us learn what the true Church is: then let us also repeat the general doctrine about the cross, why God wants the Church to be subject to the cross before the resurrection, namely, because sin remains in this weak nature, which He wants to be acknowledged, restrained by calamities, and abolished by death, as Paul says: "The body is destined for death, because of sin," namely, that which clings to the flesh.

He wants afflictions to be constant exercises of repentance and invocation; He also wants them to be testimonies of the doctrine, since when Prophets and Apostles prefer to die rather than cast away the doctrine, they show that they truly feel what they teach. He also wants them to be testimonies that another judgment remains. Because here they seem neglected in death—Isaiah, Jeremiah, Paul—whom God showed beforehand were His concern. It is necessary, therefore, that another judgment remains, in which the tyrants who raged against them will be punished, where God will show the distinction between His Church and the impious.

Latin:

Dominica Exaudi.

Evangelium Iohannis 15. Cum venerit autem Paracletus, quem ego mittam vobis a patre, spiritum veritatis, qui a patre procedit, ille testimonium perhibebit de me. Quin et vos testes estis, quia ab initio mecum estis.

Haec locutus sum vobis, ut ne quid offendamini, Alienos a synagogis facient vos, sed venit hora, ut omnis qui occiderit vos, videatur cultum praestare Deo. Et haec facient vobis, quia non noverunt patrem, neque me. Sed haec locutus sum vobis, ut cum venerit tempus illud, reminiscamini eorum, quod ego dixerim vobis. Haec autem vobis ab initio non dixi, quia vobiscum eram.

Loci quatuor.

I. Doctrina de Deo, quis sit, et quomodo sit agnoscendus et invocandus.

II. Quis sit Spiritus sanctus, et quod sit proprium eius officium.

III. Testificatio duplex, altera per ministerium, altera in cordibus.

IV. Doctrina de cruce.

De primo.

Saepe monendi sunt homines de invocatione. Multi precationes dicunt quadam consuetudine, ita ut mens neque cogitet, quem Deum invocet, neque secum ipsa quaerat, exaudiat Deus, neque seiungat suam invocationem a Turcica, et mentes in agnitione verae doctrinae, et accendat verum timorem, veram dilectionem, prohibeat audaciam fingendi opiniones sine verbo Dei etc. Sicut David orat, spiritum rectum, id est, firmum, innova in visceribus meis. De tertio. Aliquoties repetita est sententia a Christo: Spiritus sanctus testificabitur de me. Hoc dictum describit officia iam recitata, semper autem coniungatur duplex testificatio, exterior per ministerium, et interior in corde. Utraque est opus Spiritus sancti, et de utraque dicitur: Arguet mundum de peccato. Arguit autem in ministerio publice, et privatim in singulorum cordibus. Item de ministerio dicitur: Ascendit, dedit dona hominibus, Prophetas, Apostolos, Pastores, Doctores. Porro hic multae fanaticae opiniones refutantur. Anabaptistae ministerium Evangelii, vocem et doctrinam prorsus abiiciunt, fingunt motus spirituales, sine et extra Evangelium. Defensores vitiosorum cultuum monasticorum, invocationis sanctorum, abusus coenae Domini; fingunt cultus sine verbo Dei, et allegant Spiritum sanctum, qui haec approbaverit aut monstraverit. His erroribus omnibus opponendum est hoc dictum. Spiritus sanctus de Christo testabitur, id est, sonabit vocem a Christo traditam, sicut Christus inquit: Ille rediget vobis in memoriam ea quae dixi. Item: Spiritus sanctus glorificabit me. Quare ubi removetur ministerium, vel Evangelium, ibi Spiritus sanctus non testatur de Christo. Haec primum de ministerio scire necesse est. Postea quid sit interior testificatio, intelligunt pii, cum verbo Dei audito aut cogitato, existunt sensus irae Dei, ac pavores et dolores de peccato, et rursus consolationes ex agnitione Christi, et fide, et invocatione non impedita mala conscientia. Haec est interior testificatio, quam describit Paulus in hoc dicto: Accepistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum, quo clamamus Abba pater. Nam ut supra dixi de Catone, donec mens dubitat, an Deus velit te recipere et exaudire, fugit Deum, sed cum agnoscis promissionem de mediatore, et credis te recipi, simul Spiritus sanctus est efficax, exuscitat invocationem, dilectionem, et alias virtutes. Et Gal. 3.: Ut promissionem spiritus accipiamus per fidem. Hoc dictum semper in conspectu habendum est. Monet enim, et quomodo detur Spiritus sanctus, et quae sit actio praecipua, qua testificatur in nobis. Datur per Evangelium, sicut alias inquit Paulus: Evangelium est potentia Dei ad salutem omni credenti, id est, Evangelium vere est efficax, Deus vero impertit bona cogitanti Evangelium, et acquiescenti in eo, seu assentienti, cum acquiescimus, et credimus nos recipi et exaudiri, Quia Deus hanc suam voluntatem in Evangelio suo patefecit, et vult nos haec credere, ac misit Filium, ut sit precium, et testis, ac pignus huius voluntatis, In hac consolatione vere datur Spiritus sanctus, et ipsa consolatio et invocatio in corde testificantur de Deo. Accendit iam hanc lucem Spiritus sanctus, ut firmius statuamus nos Deo curae esse, nos recipi, propter Filium, accendit et invocationem. Haec piis nota sunt, qui sentiunt terrores, et cogitant, quem Deum invocent, an exaudiri se existiment, et cur exaudiat Deus. Maxima pars hominum recitat preces, tantum ut inane murmur, ac plurimi ne cogitant quidem quid invocent, curetne humanos clamores Deus, sed consuetudini obtemperant. Haec impietas corrigenda est, et in omni precatione cogitandum de verbo Dei, ut fides accendatur, et quis Deus, et quomodo invocandus sit, agnoscatur, videlicet, qui se sua voce, et per Filium Christum patefecit. Hic iterum obstrepit indignitas nostra. Qui magis exaudiet te Deus, quam Saulem et similes, quas habes virtutes? qua in re antecellis caeteris hominibus? Quid putas Deum curare hoc tuum murmur? Hae cogitationes duriter excruciant animos, et saepe sunt tela diaboli, missa ad excutiendam fidem, ut impellant animos in perpetuam desperationem et Epicureas blasphemias. Et multi sic evertuntur. Quare hic inprimis simus intenti, et sciamos hoc proprium esse munus Spiritus sancti, testificari de Deo in corde. Ideo datur ut corda confirmentur agnitione vera Dei. Sed colligenda sunt praecepta et promissiones Dei, quae testantur eum postulare hunc cultum, scilicet invocationem, et vere eum velle praestare bona petentibus, sicut inquit Christus: Petite et accipietis, et quidem exaudit non propter nostram dignitatem, sed propter Filium, sed tamen non adferatur propositum peccandi. Vivo ego, inquit, nolo mortem peccatoris, sed ut convertatur et vivat. Sic iubet nos Deus acquiescere. in sua promissione, et non sine certamine, ac labore, cor his testimoniis vincitur, ut acquiescat.

In hoc certamine vere est efficax Spiritus sanctus, et corda flectit ut acquiescant. Ita sciamus nos iuvari a Spiritu sancto, in invocatione, sicut dicit in Zacharia: Effundam super eos spiritum gratiae et precum. Et ut in invocatione, sic in omnibus nostris periculis et actionibus, hoc auxilium petamus et expectemus. Sicut Christus inquit: Dabo vobis spiritum paracletum, suppeditantem consilium et auxilium, ut Davidem exulantem sustentat, ne desperet, et flectit ad consilia meliora, et adiuvat in ipsis negotiis.

Haec melius intelliguntur, cum in periculis hunc gubernatorem, vera invocatione quaerimus: cogitemus autem Deum non frustra tantas promissiones exhibuisse, vult eas peti. Non frustra misit Filium, sed vult eum agnosci, non frustra promittit nobis omnibus hoc ingens munus, scilicet, societatem suae naturae, effuso in corda nostra, suo divino spiritu, sicut dicitur: Effundam de meo spiritu etc. Vult hoc tantum donum peti, et dat petentibus, ut Christus inquit: Quanto magis pater vester coelestis dabit Spiritum sanctum petentibus. Et quibus det, iam dixi, omnibus qui convertuntur ad Deum, et petunt.

Non dat nolentibus petere, aspernantibus tantum donum, nolentibus converti ad Deum. Excitemus igitur nos ad poenitentiam, et petendum Spiritum sanctum.

De quarto.

Postrema pars huius lectionis de cruce concionatur.

Opponitur enim praemonitio vulgari Iudaeorum imaginationi, qui simulabant in regno Messiae, se imperia occupaturus esse, et habituros dulcissimam tranquillitatem: hunc errorem taxat, et praemonet, quale sit regnum Messiae futurum ante resurrectionem. Spargam per vos Evangelium meum, in totum mundum, ut colligam Ecclesiam credentem mihi, et confitentem me, quam Spiritu sancto regam, ut in eis incoëntur nova iusticia, et vita aeterna.

Non mitto vos ad imperia occupanda, sed plerumque imperia in vos, et Ecclesiam exercebunt saevitiam, imo hic ipse populus Israël, qui gloriatur titulo populi Dei, vobis adversabitur: Eiiciet vos extra Ecclesiam suam, tanquam hostes Dei. Sed nunc praemoneo vos, ut sciatis veram Ecclesiam ibi esse, ubi Evangelium meum erit, et invocatio Dei, per nomen meum, sicut aliquanto ante dixerat: Si manseritis in me, et verba mea in vobis manserint, quicquid volueritis, petetis, et fiet vobis. Item: In hoc glorificatur pater meus coelestis, ut fructum multum feratis, et fiatis mei discipuli. Nihil tristius est, quam eiici ex Ecclesia, quae vere sic dicitur. Ideo discamus quae sit vera Ecclesia: deinde etiam repetamus doctrinam generalem de cruce, quare Deus ante resurrectionem velit Ecclesiam subiectam esse cruci, videlicet, quia manet peccatum in hac imbecilla natura, quod vult agnosci, coërceri calamitatibus, et aboleri morte, ut Paulus inquit: Corpus destinatum est morti, propter peccatum, scilicet, haerens in carne.

Vult afflictiones assidua exercitia esse poenitentiae et invocationis, vult item eas esse testimonia doctrinae, cum Prophetae et Apostoli malunt mori, quam abiicere doctrinam, ostendunt se vere sentire, quod docent. Vult item testimonia esse, quod aliud iudicium restet. Quia hic videntur in morte neglecti, Esaias, Ieremias, Paulus, quos Deus ostendit antea sibi curae esse. Necesse est igitur aliud iudicium restare, in quo punientur tyranni, qui in eos saevierunt, ubi Deus discrimen ostendet suae Ecclesiae et impiorum.

## 16:5 Dominica Cantate
Dominica Cantate.

Gospel of John 16.

But now I go to him who sent me, and none of you asks me, whither I go.

But because I have spoken these things to you, sadness has filled your heart. But I tell you the truth, it is expedient for you that I go.

For if I do not go, that Comforter will not come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you. that I will send him to you. And when he comes, he will convict the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment. Of sin indeed, because they do not believe in me; of righteousness, however, because I go to the Father, and you will see me no more. But of... judgment, because the prince of this world is already judged.

I have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all truth. For he will not speak on his own authority, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will announce to you things to come. He will glorify me, for he will take of what is mine and announce it to you. All things that the Father has are mine. Therefore I said that he will take of what is mine and announce it to you.

Summary of the Gospel.

It is a description of the kingdom of Christ, namely, of the office of teaching, of the sum of the Gospel, and of persecution. First he says: The Holy Spirit will convict the world. Here Christ shows that his kingdom is not a worldly polity to be established by human counsels and strengths, or by arms, but that it is a gathering over which the Son of God presides, giving the Holy Spirit, who convicts individuals and all, namely, through the ministry of the Gospel.

And although there is nothing more despised than the office of teaching the Gospel, yet he attributes great power to it here. For to convict is the act of a superior, and of one who has authority. And it is a reproof of human errors and sins, and it is an effective rebuke; it impels hearts so that they may recognize the wrath of God, it wounds minds, and converts some to God, but it curses the impious, so that they may rush into eternal destruction.

Just as from the beginning in the Church the Holy Spirit has convicted the world. Noah convicted his age. Moses convicted Pharaoh. Elijah and Elisha convicted the kings of Israel. Daniel the Babylonian kings. The Baptist the high priests, Herod, and others. Then Christ, the Apostles, and their successors convicted the men of all nations, converted many, gathered the Church, and cursed tyrants. And the Holy Spirit was effective in helping the believers and in punishing the impious; great changes of the world followed, and this office remains in the Church, which is at times more, at times less pure, at times has larger congregations, as now the flame of the Gospel has been stirred up again, by which the Holy Spirit convicts the idolatries of the world and shows the saving doctrine, by which many are converted to God, and changes of things occur.

This word 'to convict' or 'to reprove' encompasses all these things. Therefore, let us individually yield to this authority and power: and let us ask the Son of God that the Holy Spirit may be effective in us too, that he may convict perverse opinions and sins, in us and in others, and impel hearts so that they may recognize the wrath of God.

Thus also Paul says in Rom. 1: The wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness.

On the second. On the distinction of doctrines.

On sin, Because they do not believe etc. The world knows civil or external sins, such as murders, adulteries, thefts: but it does not know the root of sin, namely, the contempt of God, and the contempt of the Son of God who was given so that he might be the propitiator. Therefore, this sin is entirely unknown to reason, namely, that our nature is under sin, and all our things are guilty, but that we are only freed from sin in this way, if we believe that the Son of God is the propitiator. These things are not judged by reason, but are only revealed in the Gospel, therefore human judgments resist them. It seems absurd that the Son of God should be crucified; it seems a useless and fabricated thing to promise a liberator from sin and eternal death through faith in this crucified one. The Gospel therefore convicts these darknesses of the human mind.

On righteousness, Because I go to the Father etc. The world understands righteousness to be obedience to laws, but Christ here proposes another righteousness, namely, his passion, resurrection, perpetual intercession, and efficacy. For he encompasses all these things when he says: I go to the Father, I will die, I will rise again, I will reign, I will be a mediator before the Father, I will be a savior. We are therefore righteous, that is, accepted, not by our own virtues, but because of Christ the mediator, who suffered and reigns. This righteousness is to be distinguished far from the righteousness of the law. For although works have their place, yet they are not that thing because of which we are reconciled and accepted by God, but because of the mediator Christ we are righteous, that is, accepted by faith, and we are gifted with eternal life because of Christ going to the Father, raising us from the dead, and establishing an eternal kingdom.

But the world is ignorant of both, sin and righteousness; it is ignorant of the Son of God, and true invocation, therefore it fashions worship by its own audacity. Hence are the idolatries of all nations. These the voice of the Holy Spirit condemns and refutes, which cries out that it is sin not to believe in the Son of God, and that we are righteous, that is, accepted on account of the mediator Christ, and are gifted with eternal life, because Christ went to the Father, etc. When in this way we have acknowledged the Son, we can truly call upon the Father, and we are freed from false worships, etc.

Concerning judgment.

He spoke concerning the sum of the Gospel, namely, that our nature is under sin, and that we are freed from sin only by faith in Christ: likewise, that we are righteous and saved by the passing of Christ; now he adds a third point concerning judgment, that is, concerning persecution. The world, offended by the appearance of the weakness of Christ and the Gospel, denies that this voice is the word of God, and the devil, the enemy of the Son of God, impels his members so that with all cruelty they might destroy the Gospel, and in such great power of the ungodly it seems from time to time that the whole Church is about to perish, but it emerges nevertheless, and resists the power of the devil and the world, and remains not by human strength or counsels, but because Christ restrains the devil, who is already judged and condemned. The devil, therefore, cannot rage as much as he wants, nor destroy the Church, which will be glorified in its own time; indeed, he cannot even destroy it utterly in this life.

Thus, in this sermon, a picture of the Church is, as it were, proposed, when he says: He will reprove the world, he testifies that it is truly established, then he distinguishes doctrine from the law, that we are not freed from sin except by faith in the Son of God. Likewise, that we are righteous on account of Christ the mediator, and that eternal life is given by his going to the Father, that is, by his reigning and raising us up, etc.

Now when the Church professes these things, the devil excites huge struggles, and the world defends its own opinions, idolatries, and other errors: therefore the Church is meanwhile under the cross, but it conquers nevertheless, and will be glorified, because the devil is condemned.

Let us diligently remember these consolations, so that we may learn how liberation from sin happens, namely, by faith in the Son of God. Let us learn also that we are not righteous on account of our own virtues, but on account of the Son, who goes to the Father, that is, intercedes for us, justifies, and gives life, etc. Let us learn also that in such great dangers the Church will not perish, even if the madness of the ungodly, and the Turkish power, and many confusions of affairs

Latin:

Dominica Cantate.

Evangelium Iohannis 16.

Nunc autem vado ad eum, qui misit me, et nemo ex vobis interrogat me, quo vadam.

Sed quia haec locutus sum vobis, moestitudo implevit cor vestrum. Sed ego veritatem dico vobis, expedit vobis, ut ego vadam.

Si enim non abiero, Consolator ille non veniet ad vos. Sin autem abiero, mittam eum ad vos. Et cum venerit ille, arguet mundum de peccato, et de iusticia, et de iudicio. De peccato quidem, quia non credunt in me, De iusticia vero, quia ad patrem vado, et posthac non videtis me. De iudicio autem, quia princeps huius... mundi iam iudicatus est.

Ad haec multa habeo quae vobis dicam, sed non potestis portare nunc. Cum autem venerit ille Spiritus veritatis, ducet vos in omnem veritatem. Non enim loquetur a semetipso, sed quaecunque audierit loquetur, et quae futura sunt annunciabit vobis. Ille me glorificabit, quia de meo accipiet, et annunciabit vobis. Omnia quaecunque habet pater, mea sunt. Propterea dixi, quod de meo accipiet et annunciabit vobis.

Summa Evangelii.

Descriptio est regni Christi, videlicet officii docendi, summae Evangelii, et persecutionis. Primum ait: Spiritus sanctus arguet mundum. Hic ostendit Christus regnum suum non esse mundanam politiam, humanis consiliis et viribus, aut armis constituendam, sed esse coetum, cui praeest Filius Dei, dans Spiritum sanctum, arguentem singulos et omnes, scilicet, per ministerium Evangelii.

Etsi autem nihil est contemtius munere docendi Evangelii, tamen hic magnam potentiam ei tribuit. Nam arguere, est superioris, et habentis autoritatem. Estque reprehensio errorum et peccatorum humanorum, et est efficax obiurgatio, impellit corda, ut agnoscant iram Dei, vulnerat mentes, et convertit aliquos ad Deum, impiis vero maledicit, ut ruant in perpetuum interitum.

Sicut ab initio in Ecclesia Spiritus sanctus arguit mundum. Nohae arguit suum seculum. Moises arguit Pharaonem. Elias, Elisaeus arguerunt reges Israël. Daniel reges Babylonicus. Baptista pontifices, Herodem, et alios. Deinde Christus, Apostoli et successores arguerunt omnium gentium homines, multos converterunt, Ecclesiam collegerunt, et tyrannis maledixerunt. Et fuit efficax Spiritus sanctus in credentibus iuvandis, et in impiis puniendis, magnae mutationes mundi secutae sunt, et manet hoc officium in Ecclesia, quae alias est magis, alias minus pura, alias maiores coetus habet, ut nunc rursus excitata est flamma Evangelii, qua Spiritus sanctus arguit idololatrias mundi, et ostendit salutarem doctrinam, qua multi convertuntur ad Deum, et fiunt mutationes rerum.

Haec omnia complectitur verbum arguendi, seu reprehendendi. Quare singuli cedamus huic autoritati et potentiae: et rogemus Filium Dei, ut in nobis quoque Spiritus sanctus sit efficax, arguat pravas opiniones, peccata, in nobis et aliis, impellat corda, ut agnoscant iram Dei.

Sic et Paulus Rom. 1. inquit: Revelatur ira Dei de coelo super omnem impietatem.

De secundo. De distinctione doctrinarum.

De peccato, Quia non credunt etc. Mundus novit peccata civilia, seu externa, ut caedes, adulteria, furta: sed radicem peccati non novit, videlicet contemtum Dei, et contemtum Filii Dei donati, ut sit propiciator. Itaque hoc peccatum prorsus ignotum est rationi, videlicet, quod nostra natura sit sub peccato, et omnia nostra sint rea, sed sic tantum liberemur a peccato, si credamus Filium Dei esse propiciatorem. Haec non iudicantur a ratione, sed tantum sunt revelata in Evangelio, ideo refragantur humana iudicia. Videtur absurdum Filium Dei crucifigi, videtur res inutilis, et commentitia, promittere liberatorem a peccato et morte aeterna, per fiduciam huius crucifixi. Arguit igitur has tenebras humanae mentis Evangelium.

De iusticia, Quia vado ad patrem etc. Mundus intelligit iusticiam esse obedientiam legum, sed Christus hic aliam iusticiam proponit, scilicet suam passionem, resurrectionem, perpetuam intercessionem, et efficaciam. Nam haec omnia complectitur, cum ait: Vado ad patrem, moriar, resurgam, regnabo, ero mediator coram patre, ero salvator. Sumus igitur iusti, id est, accepti, non nostris virtutibus, sed propter Christum mediatorem, passum, regnantem. Haec iusticia longe discernenda est a legis iusticia. Etsi enim opera habent suum locum, tamen non sunt illa res, propter quam sumus reconciliati, et accepti Deo, sed propter mediatorem Christum sumus iusti, id est, accepti fide, et donamur vita aeterna propter Christum euntem ad patrem, resuscitantem nos a mortuis, et constituentem regnum aeternum.

Utrumque autem ignorat mundus, peccatum et iusticiam, ignorat Filium Dei, et veram invocationem, ideo fingit cultus sua audacia. Hinc sunt omnium gentium idololatriae. Has damnat et arguit haec vox Spiritus sancti, quae clamat peccatum esse, non credere in Filium Dei, et nos iustos, id est, acceptos esse propter mediatorem Christum, et donari vita aeterna, quia Christus abiit ad patrem etc. Cum hoc modo agnovimus Filium, vere possumus invocare patrem, et liberamur a falsis cultibus etc.

De iudicio.

Dixit de summa Evangelii, videlicet, quod natura nostra sit sub peccato, et quod tantum fide in Christum a peccato liberemur: item, quod iusti et salvi simus transitu Christi, nunc addit tertium de iudicio, id est, de persecutione. Mundus offensus specie imbecillitatis Christi et Evangelii, negant hanc vocem esse verbum Dei, et diabolus hostis Filii Dei impellit sua membra, ut omni saevitia deleant Evangelium, et in tanta potentia impiorum videtur subinde interitura tota Ecclesia, sed emergit tamen, et resistit potentiae diaboli et mundi, et manet non humanis viribus, aut consiliis, sed quia Christus reprimit diabolum iam iudicatum et condemnatum. Non potest igitur diabolus grassari quantum vult, nec perdere Ecclesiam, quae glorificabitur suo tempore, imo neque in hac vita funditus eam delere potest.

Ita in hac concione quasi pictura Ecclesiae proponitur, cum inquit: Arguet mundum, testatur eam vera condi, deinde discernit doctrinam a lege, quod non liberemur a peccato, nisi fide Filii Dei. Item, quod iusti simus propter Christum mediatorem, et quod detur vita aeterna ipso eunte ad patrem, id est, regnante et resuscitante nos, etc.

Iam haec cum profitetur Ecclesia, diabolus excitat ingentia certamina, et mundus defendit suas opiniones, idololatrias et alios errores: ideo Ecclesia interim sub cruce est, sed vincit tamen, et glorificabitur, quia diabolus condemnatus est.

Has consolationes diligenter meminerimus, ut discamus, quomodo contingat liberatio a peccato, scilicet, fide in Filium Dei. Discamus item, nos non esse iustos propter nostras virtutes, sed propter Filium, qui vadit ad patrem, id est, intercedit pro nobis, iustificat et vivificat etc. Discamus item in tantis periculis non interituram tamen esse Ecclesiam, etiam si rabies impiorum, et potentia Turcica, et multae confusiones rerum

## 16:19 Dominica Iubilate
Dominica Iubilate.

Gospel of John 16.

Jesus said to his disciples: A little while, and you shall not see me, and again a little while and you shall see me, because I go to the Father.

Then some of his disciples said among themselves: What is this that he says to us, a little while and you shall not see me, and again, a little while and you shall see me, and because I go to the Father?

They said therefore: What is this that he says, a little while? We do not know what he is talking about. But Jesus knew that they wanted to ask him, and said to them: Do you inquire among yourselves about this, that I said, a little while, and you shall not see me, and again a little while, and you shall see me.

Amen, amen I say to you, you shall lament and weep, but the world shall rejoice. You shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy.

A woman when she is in labor has sorrow, because her hour has come. But when she has brought forth the child, she no longer remembers the anguish for joy, because a man is born into the world. And you therefore now indeed have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your joy no one shall take from you.

And in that day you shall not ask me anything. There are two topics.

I. Preaching concerning the afflictions of the Church.

II. Consolation in these afflictions.

Latin:

Dominica Iubilate.

Evangelium Iohannis 16.

Dixit Iesus discipulis suis: Modicum, et non videtis me, et iterum modicum et videtis me, quia vado ad patrem.

Dixerunt ergo quidam ex discipulis eius inter se: Quid est hoc, quod dicit nobis, modicum et non videtis me, et rursus, modicum et videbitis me, et quia ego vado ad patrem?
